records.s: is_taken_from Tin Woodman [by an unseen person behind him] The Tin Woodman uses his axe to frighten the guards at the gateway and clear a path into the Emerald City. In the throne room, someone behind him snatches the axe from his grasp, leaving him disarmed.

records.l: revolution, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: establishes women's rule of the Emerald City [after Scarecrow leaves the city] The revolution placed the women in control of the Emerald City after the Scarecrow left. Men are described as performing housework and minding children while the women run things to suit themselves.

records.l: capture of the Scarecrow's party, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: occurs_in throne room [when the Army of Revolt surrounds the travelers] The Army of Revolt captures the Scarecrow's party in the throne room after General Jinjur signals the rebels and the Tin Woodman's axe is snatched away. General Jinjur then announces that the prisoners will be destroyed, except for Tip, who will be returned to old Mombi.

records.l: mouse panic, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: causes Army of Revolt [the girls flee in terror] The mouse panic begins when the Scarecrow releases several mice from inside his jacket. The mice cause the Army of Revolt and General Jinjur to flee the throne room and abandon the palace.

records.l: mice, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: are_frightening_to Army of Revolt [when released in the throne room] The Scarecrow releases a succession of tiny grey mice from his bosom. Their presence terrifies the Army of Revolt and General Jinjur, enabling the prisoners to escape.

records.l: women's rule of the Emerald City, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: requires housework and childcare [for the men] Under the women's rule, men in the Emerald City sweep, dust, wash dishes, and mind children while women sit gossiping and laughing. The women and the Army of Revolt show little concern when the Scarecrow's party enters the city.

records.l: prisoners' planned destruction, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: General Jinjur plans to chop up the Saw-Horse and Jack Pumpkinhead's body for kindling, use the pumpkin to make tarts, burn the Scarecrow, cut the Tin Woodman into pieces for the goats, and make the Woggle-Bug into soup or goulash. Tip is excluded from this plan because he belongs to old Mombi and is to be returned to her.

records.l: Pastoria, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Pastoria, former King of the Emerald City, was displaced by the Wizard of Oz, died, and was succeeded in rightful claim by his daughter Ozma.

records.l: girl soldiers, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: surround Jinjur’s palace [in a double row] The girl soldiers surround Jinjur’s palace in a double row. Their presence makes the group prisoners and prevents them from escaping through the palace doors.

records.l: captivity, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: imprisons the party of prisoners [inside Jinjur’s palace] The group recognizes that it remains in captivity because Jinjur’s girl soldiers surround the palace. The companions decide that staying inside is untenable because the palace may eventually be breached and some members may starve or decay.

records.l: escape from the palace, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: requires aerial machine [because the doors and ground are unavailable] The group concludes that escape through the palace doors would result in capture and that escape through the ground is impossible. The Scarecrow therefore proposes escaping through the air with a living winged machine.

records.l: construction of the aerial machine, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_assigned_to Nick Chopper [as a skillful mechanic] Nick Chopper is assigned to construct the aerial machine from materials found throughout the palace. The companions separate to search for suitable materials and carry them to the roof, where construction will begin.

records.l: sofas, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Two large sofas are brought to a roof, placed edge to edge as Gump's protective body, and firmly bound with ropes and clothes-lines for flight.

records.l: the roof, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_part_of the palace [site of the construction and first flight] The roof is where the adventurers gather materials and construct the flying machine. The Thing rises from it, flies above it, and later settles back onto it at Tip’s command.

records.l: the Gump's first flight, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: The Gump's first flight begins from the roof after animation, rises slowly with furiously flapping wings, circles back on Tip’s command, and lands on the roof.

records.l: the Gump's animation, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Tip sprinkles magic powder and speaks three cabalistic words with hand gestures, animating the assembled Thing as the Gump’s head screeches and four wings flap.

records.l: Jackdaws, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: The Jackdaws are numerous, brave birds living as a colony in Jackdaw’s Nest, a hollow-ledge nest filled over years with stolen household articles and money. Fond of pumpkins, they return angrily when intruders occupy it, attack the Tin Woodman, Gump, Saw-Horse, and Scarecrow, strip and drop the Scarecrow’s straw into the gulf, then flee when the Gump breaks free into their nest.

records.l: Jackdaw’s Nest, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Jackdaw’s Nest is an inaccessible nest on a hollow ledge beneath a mountain cliff, hundreds of feet above a great gulf, occupied by Jackdaws. It cushions the travelers’ fall after a crash and holds leaves, papers, valuables, stolen money, and stolen articles, including a diamond necklace. The party is attacked there; after the Scarecrow’s straw is thrown into the gulf, he is restuffed. The party searches for treasures, takes objects, and escapes by Gump at daylight as the Jackdaws return.

records.l: Glinda’s palace, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Glinda’s palace is the travelers’ intended destination, but they never reach it. The Woggle-Bug compares their mountain nest to the palace and considers the nest a worse prison.

records.l: mountain range, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: has deep gorges and steep cliffs [along the travelers’ route] The Gump reaches a mountain range containing high peaks, deep gorges, steep cliffs, and a level rock surface. The travelers attempt to land there after discovering that they are lost.

records.l: Gump’s flight, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Gump’s flight unintentionally leaves Land of Oz, carrying travelers south in sofas; after rising slowly and speeding through the night, it passes South Country unseen.

records.l: Gump’s crash, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Gump misjudges a landing on a level rock, breaks both right wings, tumbles down a cliff, and is left suspended upside down after dumping travelers into the Jackdaw’s Nest.

records.l: counting seventeen by twos, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Counting seventeen by twos starts at one-half, then proceeds through odd numbers to seventeen; the Saw-Horse discovers the method and Woggle-Bug confirms it.

records.l: wishing, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Wishing, granted by Dr. Nikidik’s Famous Wishing Pills after required counting, can immediately alter events, even undoing earlier actions. Though travelers doubt the pills are usable, Tip reverses swallowing one and the Woggle-Bug repairs the Gump.

records.l: stolen money, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Stolen bills of various denominations, collected by the Jackdaws from villages and cities, are cleaned and used to fill the Scarecrow’s legs and body.

records.l: Jackdaw attack, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Jackdaw attack targets Scarecrow and threatens the party, nearly damaging Tin Woodman before his axe, Saw-Horse’s kicks, and Gump’s movement force retreat.

records.l: Scarecrow’s restuffing, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: The Scarecrow is restored after Jackdaws destroy his straw, with stolen bills of various denominations stuffed into his legs and body.

records.l: Tip’s first wish, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Tip’s first wish is never to have swallowed the pill; it restores Dr. Nikidik’s Famous Wishing Pills to the box, though Tip still insists he experienced dreadful pain.

records.l: Gump’s repair, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Woggle-Bug uses wishing to restore Gump’s broken wings to perfect repair, enabling Gump to fly as well as before.

records.l: Scarecrow's throne, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: The Scarecrow says that Jinjur stole his throne in the Emerald City. Glinda questions his claim because he received the throne from the Wizard of Oz, who had taken it from Pastoria, and concludes that the throne belongs to Ozma.

records.l: search for Ozma, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_pursued_by Glinda the Good [through the Wizard’s records] Glinda begins a search for Ozma by examining a book recording the Wizard's observable actions. The suspicious clues are that he ate beans with a knife, visited Mombi secretly three times, and limped slightly, with the visits to Mombi seeming most significant. Glinda concludes that finding Mombi may reveal where Ozma is hidden.

records.l: Glinda's march on the Emerald City, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_planned_by Glinda the Good [to take Mombi prisoner] Glinda decides to march with her army on the Emerald City at daybreak. Her immediate purpose is to take Mombi prisoner and force her to disclose the location of Ozma, while also opposing Jinjur's rule.

records.l: Army of Glinda the Good, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: A group of girl soldiers assembles at daybreak, surrounds and enters Emerald City searching for Mombi, then marches back to its tents.

records.l: Mombi’s enchantment, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: causes Jellia’s transformation into Mombi Mombi performs a magical rite that makes Jellia resemble her while making herself resemble Jellia. Glinda later breaks the enchantment on Jellia, causing Mombi to resume her own crooked form in the palace.

records.l: Jellia’s transformation into Mombi, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_reversed_by Glinda the Good [through magic] Through Mombi’s enchantment, Jellia takes on the form and features of the old witch. She is led before Glinda as if she were Mombi until Glinda recognizes and reverses the transformation.

records.l: Mombi’s transformation into a rose, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Mombi transforms into a red rose in the palace garden to hide, fooling Glinda’s searchers until the Tin Woodman plucks her.

records.l: Mombi’s capture, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Mombi’s capture begins when she becomes a rose and the Tin Woodman unknowingly carries her from the Emerald City to Glinda’s camp. Glinda captures her in the desert with a golden magical thread, returns her by Gump, and questions her about Ozma.

records.l: search for Mombi, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_conducted_in royal palace (Emerald City) [by Glinda and her companions] Glinda and her companions search the Emerald City after Jinjur agrees to let them enter. They spend several hours searching without finding Mombi because she is disguised as a rose, and Glinda orders the army to leave at sundown.

records.l: Mombi’s deception, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Mombi deceives Glinda by having Jellia impersonate her, then transforms into a rose; Glinda discovers the first ruse, while the second succeeds until the Tin Woodman removes her.

records.l: surrender of Mombi, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_demanded_by Glinda the Good [as a condition for peace] Queen Jinjur refuses to surrender the real Mombi. Instead, she offers Jellia in disguise and later permits Glinda to search the city, while Mombi escapes discovery by becoming a rose.

records.l: Griffin (Mombi's transformation), The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Mombi transforms into a Griffin with exceedingly fleet legs and enduring strength, escapes through a tent wall, outruns the Saw-Horse, then collapses in desert sands and changes back into Mombi.

records.l: Mombi's transformations, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: are_easy_for Mombi Mombi first takes the form of a rose, then changes into a Shadow and a Black Ant while trying to escape Glinda. She finally becomes a Griffin, but Glinda’s golden thread destroys the magic of the transformation.

records.l: rescue and restoration of Ozma, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_needed Ozma [to restore her to her rightful position] Glinda says that their assistance is necessary for little Ozma to be rescued and restored to her rightful position as Queen of the Emerald City. The unit does not describe Ozma’s rescue or restoration taking place.

records.l: Mombi's transformation spell, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: Mombi's transformation spell changed infant Princess Ozma into the boy Tip, who was raised as Tip; Mombi later reversed it with a potion, burning herbs, magical powder, an incantation, and “Yeowa!”

records.l: Tip's transformation into Princess Ozma, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: restores Princess Ozma [to her proper form] Tip's transformation into Princess Ozma occurs when Mombi reverses the enchantment that made Ozma appear to be a boy. Tip sleeps through the process and rises from the couch as a young girl, while retaining Tip's memories and relationships.

records.l: Ozma's disappearance, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: is_explained_by Mombi [as an enchantment into a boy] Ozma's disappearance is explained when Mombi reveals that the Wonderful Wizard of Oz brought the infant Ozma to her and asked her to conceal the child. Mombi hid Ozma by transforming her into a boy who became known as Tip.

records.l: the truth about Princess Ozma, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: reveals Princess Ozma [as Tip in enchanted form] The truth about Princess Ozma is that she is Tip, the child Mombi raised after transforming her from a girl into a boy. She is the rightful ruler of the Emerald City and is restored to her original female form.

records.l: the conquest of Jinjur, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: results_in Ozma's accession The conquest of Jinjur is achieved when the Gump lands in the Emerald City's courtyard and soldiers take her prisoner. Heralds proclaim the victory, Glinda's army enters the city, and Princess Ozma succeeds to the throne.

records.l: Ozma's accession, The Marvelous Land of Oz
records.s: places Princess Ozma [on the throne of her royal ancestors] Ozma's accession follows Jinjur's capture and the surrender of the Army of Revolt. As Queen, Ozma restores the stolen jewels, brings peace to the Emerald City, and rules with wisdom and justice.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz
records.s: the Nine Tiny Piglets is a nine tiny ones

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz
records.s: the Gargoyles is a wooden people (also called creatures)
records.q: There were odd wooden houses, with carved wooden flowers in the front yards. The tree-trunks were of coarse wood, but the leaves of the trees were shavings. The patches of grass were splinters of wood, and where neither grass nor sawdust showed was a solid wooden flooring. Wooden birds fluttered among the trees and wooden cows were browsing upon the wooden grass; but the most amazing things of all were the wooden people--the creatures known as Gargoyles.
records.t:
the Gargoyles is a wooden people (also called creatures), 1908, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz
There were odd wooden
houses, with carved wooden flowers in the front yards.  The tree-trunks
were of coarse wood, but the leaves of the trees were shavings.  The
patches of grass were splinters of wood, and where neither grass nor
sawdust showed was a solid wooden flooring.  Wooden birds fluttered
among the trees and wooden cows were browsing upon the wooden grass;
but the most amazing things of all were the wooden people--the
creatures known as Gargoyles.

records.s: the Swedish widow lives in the widow's home (with her four children)
records.q: She took the gown and the four children to her home, where she lost no time in trying on the costume, which fitted her as perfectly as a flour-sack does a peck of potatoes.

records.q: For the wily widow, wishing to escape her admirer, had sprinkled the door-step and the front walk with insect Exterminator, and not even the Woggle-Bug's love for the enchanting checked gown could induce him to linger longer in that vicinity.

records.s: the Woggle-Bug's money amounts to eight silver dollars (earned from ditch-digging)
records.q: It was just after noon that the Woggle-Bug hired as a ditch-digger in order to win his heart's desire; so at noon on the second day he quit work, and having received eight silver dollars he put on his coat and rushed away to the store that he might purchase his intended bride.

records.s: Mr. H. M. Woggle-Bug, T. E. wears gorgeous multicolored clothing (reds, yellows, blues, and greens)
records.q: Being about as big, in his magnified state, as a man, the Woggle-Bug took care to clothe himself like a man; only, instead of choosing sober colors for his garments, he delighted in the most gorgeous reds and yellows and blues and greens; so that if you looked at him long the brilliance of his clothing was liable to dazzle your eyes.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note
records.s: L. Frank Baum introduces Ozma of Oz as a record of Dorothy Gale's adventures with the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and others. He explains that children asked for more about Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, and what Ozma did after becoming ruler of Oz. Baum says the book includes old friends as well as new characters, including Billina, Tiktok, and the Hungry Tiger. He hopes his young readers will find the story "real Ozzy."

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note
records.s: Ozma of Oz is presented as a book recording Dorothy Gale's adventures with the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and other characters.

records.l: L. Frank Baum, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note
records.s: L. Frank Baum wrote Ozma of Oz and explains that children’s letters inspired him to write more about Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, and Ozma. He says he enjoys writing the stories and hopes children will approve of the new book.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note
records.s: Ozma became the Ruler of Oz, and children asked what she did afterward. Some readers also asked Baum to have Ozma and Dorothy meet and enjoy themselves together.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note

records.l: children, Ozma of Oz, front matter .. Author's Note
records.s: The children’s letters and requests inspired L. Frank Baum to write Ozma of Oz and ask for more about Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, and Ozma. They also suggested that Dorothy return to the Land of Oz and meet Ozma, and Baum hopes they will write to tell him how they like the story.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: A fierce wind creates a terrible storm on the ocean while Dorothy Gale and her Uncle Henry travel by ship toward Australia. Dorothy leaves the cabin to search for Uncle Henry and is carried away when the wind lifts a chicken-coop from the deck. She survives on the coop as it floats across the waves, and after the storm subsides, she falls asleep beneath the moon and stars.

records.l: wind, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: The wind grows from a strong breeze into a violent force that creates huge waves and a terrible storm. It tears the ropes from the chicken-coop, lifts it into the air with Dorothy clinging to it, and later stops blowing.

records.l: the ocean, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: The ocean is violently disturbed by the wind, producing waves as high as houses and trees. It carries the chicken-coop far from the ship, then becomes calmer after the wind stops.

records.l: the storm, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: The storm makes the day dark, tosses the ship dangerously, and forces the passengers to remain in the cabin. It eventually subsides, allowing Dorothy to float more gently and rest.

records.l: the ship, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: The ship carries Dorothy Gale and Uncle Henry toward Australia. During the storm it rolls, tips, and is violently jostled, and Dorothy is blown away from it in the chicken-coop.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: Dorothy Gale is a little Kansas girl traveling with Uncle Henry to Australia. Worried that he has gone onto the dangerous deck, she searches for him, but the wind carries her away in a chicken-coop; she remains calm, uses the coop as a raft, and falls asleep after the storm quiets.

records.l: Uncle Henry, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: Uncle Henry is traveling with Dorothy Gale to Australia to visit relatives and recover from poor health caused by hard work on his Kansas farm. He goes to lie down in his sleeping-berth while Dorothy mistakenly searches for him on deck.

records.l: chicken-coop, Ozma of Oz, 1. The Girl in the Chicken Coop
records.s: The chicken-coop is lashed to the ship's deck until the wind tears away its ropes and carries it into the sea with Dorothy clinging to it. Its thick wooden bottom supports Dorothy like a raft, and it later floats gently enough for her to sleep inside it.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: Dorothy Gale awakens in a hen-coop drifting on the ocean and discovers that a yellow hen can talk. The hen, whom Dorothy renames Billina, explains how she survived the storm, and she and Dorothy drift toward an unknown land. After reaching the shore, Dorothy dries her shoes while Billina searches for food and argues that humans also eat animals. Billina finds a golden key buried in the sand, and Dorothy decides to explore the land for breakfast.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: Dorothy Gale awakens in the hen-coop after the storm and speaks with the yellow hen, whom she renames Billina. She reaches the unknown shore, dries her wet shoes and stockings, and finds a golden key after digging it out of the sand.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: Billina is a yellow hen who survives the storm by clinging to the corner of the hen-coop. She begins speaking to Dorothy, accepts the name Billina, eats ants, sand-bugs, and a tiny crab, and discovers the golden key buried in the sand.

records.l: the ocean, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: The ocean is calm and placid after the storm, but the hen-coop continues drifting across it. The ocean carries Dorothy and Billina toward an unknown shore, where the coop finally reaches the beach.

records.l: the unknown land, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: The unknown land has a broad beach of white sand and gravel, rocky hills, and a strip of green trees marking the edge of a forest. No houses or people are visible, and Dorothy plans to explore it for food.

records.l: the hen-coop, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: The hen-coop blows away from the ship during the storm and floats with Dorothy and Billina across the ocean. It eventually grates gently onto the sandy beach, allowing them to reach the shore.

records.l: the golden key, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: The golden key is found buried in the sand near the water's edge after Billina strikes it with her bill. It is large, somewhat old, bright, and still in perfect shape, but its lock and purpose are unknown.

records.l: Billina's egg, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: Billina lays a morning egg in the hen-coop and offers it to Dorothy as food. Dorothy refuses because she cannot eat it unless it is cooked, while Billina explains that she does not hatch eggs without a snug nest and thirteen eggs.

records.l: the storm, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: The storm leaves Dorothy and Billina wet and adrift after the hen-coop is blown away from the ship. Billina nearly drowns but clings to the coop, and the sunshine later dries their clothing and feathers.

records.l: Dorothy and Billina's voyage, Ozma of Oz, 2. The Yellow Hen
records.s: Dorothy and Billina's voyage begins when the storm carries their hen-coop away from the ship and leaves them adrift on the ocean. They survive the dangerous night, drift toward land, and end the voyage when the coop reaches the beach.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: Dorothy and Billina find the warning “BEWARE THE WHEELERS!” written in the beach sand and discover trees bearing lunch-boxes and dinner-pails. After Dorothy picks and eats a lunch-box and takes a dinner-pail, a Wheeler pursues her, followed by many others. Dorothy and Billina escape onto a rocky hill, where the Wheelers cannot follow because their wheels cannot roll over the jagged rocks. The Wheelers surround the hill and threaten Dorothy because she picked their food containers, invoking a law that demands death for anyone who picks a dinner-pail without permission.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: Dorothy reads the words “BEWARE THE WHEELERS!” in the sand and searches the forest for food. She picks and eats a lunch-box, takes a dinner-pail, and is chased by the Wheelers until she and Billina take refuge on a rocky hill.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: Billina cannot read but discusses what the warning might mean and suggests the Wheelers could be automobiles. She recognizes the approaching creatures as Wheelers, warns Dorothy to run, leads her to the rocky hill, and helps her understand that the Wheelers cannot follow among the rocks.

records.l: the Wheelers, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The Wheelers are strange, humanlike creatures who move on four wheels instead of hands and feet. They chase Dorothy and Billina, surround the rocky hill, threaten to tear Dorothy into pieces, and claim ownership of the lunch-boxes and dinner-pails.

records.l: Wheeler (first pursuer), Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The first Wheeler Dorothy sees emerges from a forest path and rolls swiftly after her when she runs. It reaches the rocky hill but stops when Dorothy climbs among the loose, jagged rocks.

records.l: the beach sand, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The beach sand contains large, widely spaced signs that Dorothy eventually reads as “BEWARE THE WHEELERS!”

records.l: the rocky hill, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The rocky hill provides refuge for Dorothy and Billina. Its loose, jagged rocks prevent the Wheelers from rolling after them, although the Wheelers surround the hill and trap them there.

records.l: the fairy country, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: Dorothy believes she is in a fairy country because lunch-boxes and dinner-pails grow on trees and Billina can talk. She concludes that it is not the Land of Oz because the Land of Oz has no nearby seashore.

records.l: the warning in the sand, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The warning says, “BEWARE THE WHEELERS!” It proves accurate when the Wheelers appear and chase Dorothy and Billina.

records.l: the lunch-box tree, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The lunch-box tree bears square paper boxes in clusters throughout the year. Its blossoms and unripe fruit are lunch-boxes, and its leaves are paper napkins.

records.l: the dinner-pail tree, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The dinner-pail tree bears tin dinner-pails on stout branches. The pails range from small and dark brown to large dull-tin and bright-tin colors as they ripen.

records.l: lunch-boxes, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The lunch-boxes grow on trees and contain food wrapped in white paper, including a ham sandwich, sponge-cake, pickle, new cheese, and an apple. Dorothy picks a ripe lunch-box and eats everything inside.

records.l: dinner-pails, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The dinner-pails grow on trees and are treated by the Wheelers as their property. Picking one without permission is said to be punishable by death under the Wheelers’ law.

records.l: Dorothy's picked dinner-pail, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: Dorothy picks a bright, pretty dinner-pail with a stout handle and carries it toward the seashore. The Wheelers accuse her of stealing it and use it as the reason for threatening her.

records.l: the Wheelers' law, Ozma of Oz, 3. Letters in the Sand
records.s: The Wheelers’ leader declares that anyone who picks a dinner-pail without permission must die immediately. The law is cited against Dorothy after she takes a dinner-pail without knowing that the trees are claimed by the Wheelers.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Dorothy and Billina discover a hidden rock door on a hill and use a golden key to enter a small rocky chamber. Inside they find Tiktok, a copper mechanical man made by Smith & Tinker, and wind his clock-work mechanisms so that he can think, speak, and move. Tiktok tells them that the cruel King of Ev, Evoldo, sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King before locking Tiktok away and drowning himself. Tiktok then becomes Dorothy's obedient servant, provided she keeps him wound up.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Dorothy follows a hidden path to the top of the rocky hill with Billina, unlocks the rock door with the golden key, and discovers Tiktok inside. She reads the instructions attached to him, winds his thinking, speaking, and action mechanisms, and accepts him as her obedient servant.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Billina discovers the hidden path and recognizes the crack in the rock as a door with a keyhole. She encourages Dorothy to wind Tiktok and questions him about his abilities and history.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Tiktok is a copper mechanical man made by Smith & Tinker. After Dorothy winds his mechanisms, he thinks, speaks in a monotonous voice, walks stiffly, and tells how Evoldo locked him away after selling his family to the Nome King.

records.l: King of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The King of Ev is described as a cruel ruler who beat his servants until they died. He had a lovely wife and ten children, whom he sold to the Nome King, and later tried unsuccessfully to recover them.

records.l: King Evoldo, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Evoldo is the name Tiktok gives for the cruel King of Ev. After regretting the sale of his family, he locked Tiktok inside the rock, threw the key into the ocean, jumped in after it, and drowned.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The Nome King bought Evoldo's wife and ten children after Evoldo sold them. Using magic, he changed them into other forms and placed them in his underground palace as decorations.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The Land of Ev is identified as the place where Smith & Tinker manufactured Tiktok. Dorothy concludes that it is a fairy land.

records.l: the rocky hill, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The rocky hill contains a smooth path winding from its base to its top. Rocks at the bottom conceal the path and prevent the Wheelers from using it, while the top holds the solitary rock containing Tiktok.

records.l: the rocky chamber, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The rocky chamber is a small, dark room inside the large rock on the hill. Tiktok remained imprisoned there after Evoldo locked him inside, until Dorothy opened the rock door and wound him up.

records.l: the rock door, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: The rock door is formed by the face of a large round rock and has a crack outlining it and a keyhole at one side. The golden key unlocks it, causing the door to swing outward on hinges.

records.l: the golden key, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Dorothy finds the golden key on the shore. She uses it to unlock the rock door and gain access to Tiktok.

records.l: Tiktok's clock-work mechanism, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Tiktok's clock-work has separate controls for thinking, speaking, and walking or action. It is said to be guaranteed to work perfectly for a thousand years, but each function must be wound up to operate.

records.l: Evoldo's bargain with the Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: In a fit of anger, Evoldo sold his wife and ten children, five boys and five girls, to the Nome King. The Nome King's magic changed them into other forms and placed them in his underground palace.
records.t: In a fit of anger, Evoldo sold his wife and ten children—five boys and five girls—to the Nome King. The Nome King's magic changed them into other forms and placed them in his underground palace.

records.l: Tiktok's awakening, Ozma of Oz, 4. Tiktok the Machine Man
records.s: Tiktok awakens when Dorothy winds his clock-work mechanisms. His thoughts, speech, and movement return in sequence, and he explains that his functions had previously run down after his long imprisonment.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Dorothy rewinds Tiktok after he runs down and asks him about the Wheelers, who threaten to kill them below the rocks. While Tiktok thinks of a way to escape, Dorothy eats from her dinner pail and learns about the Land of Ev, its royal family, and Tiktok's makers. Tiktok explains that the Land of Oz is near the Land of Ev and tells Dorothy that Ozma of Oz now rules there after a revolution. Tiktok then leads Dorothy and Billina toward the town of Evna, promising to protect them from the Wheelers.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Dorothy discovers that Tiktok has run down, finds his lost clock-key in a crack in the rocks, and rewinds his voice and action machinery. She eats dinner, learns about the Land of Ev and the Land of Oz, and follows Tiktok toward Evna.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Tiktok runs down while explaining that the Wheelers are harmless, but Dorothy rewinds him and restores his ability to speak and think. He explains the Wheelers, the royal family of Ev, his makers, and the Land of Oz, then devises a route to Evna and offers to protect Dorothy.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Billina helps Dorothy look for Tiktok's lost key and searches the cracks for food. She refuses Dorothy's turkey and other food because she prefers bugs and ants, though she later eats the crumbs.

records.l: the Wheelers, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The Wheelers are below the rocks and threaten to kill Dorothy and Tiktok. Tiktok says they are mischievous and harmless to anyone who dares to fight them, while Billina says they claim the lunch-box and dinner-pail trees for themselves.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The Land of Ev is separated from the Land of Oz by a broad desert. The Wheelers inhabit only a small portion of it, while the town of Evna contains the royal palace.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The royal family of Ev owns the lunch-box trees and dinner-pail trees. There is no one ruling the Land of Ev because King Evoldo's wife and ten children were transformed by the Nome King.

records.l: King Evoldo, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: King Evoldo ruled the Land of Ev and used to carry a whip to keep the Wheelers in order. He jumped into the sea, leaving no royal family to rule the land.

records.l: Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The Land of Oz is a wonderful fairy country separated from the Land of Ev by a broad desert. Tiktok says a revolution occurred there, after which Ozma of Oz became its ruler.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The Scarecrow traveled with Dorothy to the city of the great Wizard of Oz to get brains, although Dorothy thought he thought just as well before receiving them. He had been king of the Land of Oz but was deposed by General Jinjur.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Ozma of Oz is described as the rightful heir to the throne of the Land of Oz. She deposed General Jinjur and now rules the land.

records.l: the rocks, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The rocks trap Dorothy and Tiktok while the Wheelers remain below them. Dorothy searches the rocks and finds Tiktok's clock-key in a crack.

records.l: Dorothy's picked dinner-pail, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The dinner pail contains lemonade, turkey, cold tongue, lobster salad, bread and butter, custard pie, an orange, strawberries, nuts, and raisins. Its bottom bears the royal E of the royal family of Ev, and Dorothy packs the unused food back into it.

records.l: the Wheelers' threat to kill Dorothy and Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The Wheelers are down below the rocks and threaten to kill Dorothy and Tiktok. Tiktok says they are not truly dangerous and would run away if he had a club.

records.l: the revolution in the Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: The revolution in the Land of Oz deposed the Scarecrow, after which General Jinjur ruled briefly. Ozma of Oz then deposed Jinjur and became ruler as the rightful heir.

records.l: escape from the rocks, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Tiktok tries to think of a way to escape from the rocks. After thinking, he leads Dorothy and Billina toward Evna, where he says they will be more comfortable and protected from the Wheelers.

records.l: Tiktok's clock-work mechanism, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Tiktok's voice, action, and thought machinery must be wound with a key. He says he is complicated and may be difficult to repair because his maker, Mr. Tinker, is gone.

records.l: Dorothy's dinner, Ozma of Oz, 5. Dorothy Opens the Dinner Pail
records.s: Dorothy's dinner consists of food from the dinner pail, including lemonade, meat, lobster salad, bread and butter, custard pie, fruit, nuts, and raisins. She offers some to Tiktok and Billina, finishes part of it, and saves the rest.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina enter the Land of Ev after Tiktok defeats and questions the Wheelers. They reach the royal palace of Ev, where they meet Princess Langwidere, who has thirty interchangeable heads and demands Dorothy’s head for her collection. When Dorothy refuses, Langwidere orders her army to imprison Dorothy, while Tiktok runs down during the fight and Billina is sent to the chicken-house. The Nome King is identified as the captor of the royal family of Ev.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Dorothy travels with Tiktok and Billina into the Land of Ev and helps keep the Wheelers’ weakness secret. At the royal palace, Princess Langwidere offers her head No. 26 in exchange for Dorothy’s head, but Dorothy refuses and is ordered imprisoned.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Tiktok uses the dinner-pail to frighten away the Wheelers and captures their leader, who tells him about the Land of Ev and Princess Langwidere. He fights Langwidere’s soldiers to protect Dorothy, but his action runs down, leaving him motionless in the drawing-room.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Billina praises Tiktok after he drives away the first Wheelers and accompanies Dorothy into the palace. She forces her way past the servant, is found in Langwidere’s work-basket, and is ordered to be put in the chicken-house.

records.l: the Wheelers, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The Wheelers attack Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina, but Tiktok frightens them with the dinner-pail. Their leader reveals that the Wheelers are physically helpless because their wheels prevent them from using fists, scratching, pulling hair, or kicking, and promises to stop frightening children.

records.l: Princess Langwidere, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Princess Langwidere lives in the royal palace of Ev and spends much of her time admiring herself in mirrored rooms. She owns thirty beautiful heads, demands Dorothy’s head for her collection, and orders Dorothy imprisoned when she refuses.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The Nome King has imprisoned every member of the royal family of Ev, leaving the Land of Ev without a ruler.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The Land of Ev contains the Wheelers, the royal palace, and a beautiful vale of farms, roads, fruit trees, and fields. It currently has no ruler because the Nome King has imprisoned the royal family, although Princess Langwidere lives in part of the palace and spends money from the royal treasury.

records.l: palace of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The royal palace of Ev stands in the center of a beautiful vale and is surrounded by gardens, fountains, walks, and marble statuary. Dorothy, Tiktok, and Billina enter its grounds and are brought to a drawing-room before Dorothy is taken to the North Tower.

records.l: Dorothy's picked dinner-pail, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The dinner-pail serves as Tiktok’s weapon against the Wheelers and Langwidere’s soldiers. Its loud blows frighten or knock down his opponents, although Tiktok eventually stops when his action runs down.

records.l: the ruby key, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: The ruby key is carved from a single blood-red ruby and hangs from a chain attached to Princess Langwidere’s left wrist. It unlocks the velvet-lined cupboards containing her heads and allows her to change from one head to another.

records.l: Princess Langwidere's collection of heads, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Princess Langwidere’s collection contains thirty heads kept in separate velvet-lined cupboards numbered with gold. The heads vary in hair, eyes, noses, mouths, and other features, and she changes them to alter her appearance.

records.l: Princess Langwidere's army, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Princess Langwidere’s army consists of a large colonel and ten lean soldiers who appear sad and discouraged. They are ordered to carry Dorothy to the North Tower, but Tiktok knocks down the colonel and seven soldiers before running down.

records.l: the head exchange, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: Princess Langwidere proposes exchanging Dorothy’s head for head No. 26 because she wants Dorothy’s unusual prettiness for her collection. Dorothy refuses, and Langwidere responds by ordering her imprisonment.

records.l: Dorothy's imprisonment, Ozma of Oz, 6. The Heads of Langwidere
records.s: After Dorothy refuses the head exchange, Langwidere’s soldiers carry her to a high tower at the north of the palace and lock her securely inside.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Dorothy Gale looks out from her tower prison in the Land of Ev and sees Ozma of Oz arriving across the desert with the Scarecrow, Nick Chopper, the Cowardly Lion, Tiktok, and soldiers. Ozma confronts Princess Langwidere and agrees to help free the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, but first requires Langwidere to release Dorothy. Langwidere unlocks Dorothy, who returns to Ozma and her friends. While Ozma and Langwidere are away, the Scarecrow and Nick Chopper learn that Tiktok is a wind-up machine with mechanical brains but no conscience or heart.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Dorothy Gale is imprisoned in a tower by Princess Langwidere after refusing to exchange her head for one from Langwidere's collection. She sees Ozma of Oz and her friends arrive, calls to them for help, and is released by Langwidere.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Ozma of Oz crosses the desert in a golden chariot drawn by a Lion and a Tiger, leading a procession from the Land of Oz. She tells Langwidere that she is powerful enough to destroy her kingdom but has come to free the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, and she orders Langwidere to release Dorothy.

records.l: Princess Langwidere, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Princess Langwidere imprisons Dorothy because Dorothy will not give her a head for her collection. She initially threatens Ozma and her company, but becomes eager to receive help freeing her aunt and cousins and readily releases Dorothy.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The Scarecrow arrives with Ozma, riding a Saw-Horse, and responds when Dorothy calls to him from the tower. He later speaks with Tiktok about brains and says that the brains given to him by the Wizard of Oz work splendidly.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Nick Chopper arrives on foot with Ozma's company, carrying his axe and leading twenty-seven soldiers. He listens to Tiktok's conversation with the Scarecrow and says that Tiktok is inferior because Tiktok has no heart or conscience.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The Cowardly Lion helps draw Ozma's golden chariot across the desert, standing shoulder to shoulder with the Tiger.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Tiktok is found in the palace and explains that he is a machine who can think, speak, and act when properly wound. His action has run down because Dorothy has the key, and he says he has Smith & Tinker's Improved Combination Steel Brains but no conscience or heart.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The Nome King is holding the Queen of Ev and her ten royal children prisoner, according to the news that reached Ozma.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The Land of Ev contains the palace, the tower prison, and the desert route toward the Land of Oz. Its royal family is imprisoned by the Nome King, while Princess Langwidere rules the kingdom and finds its affairs burdensome.

records.l: Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The Land of Oz is separated from the Land of Ev by a dangerous desert. Ozma and her companions travel from it to rescue Dorothy and seek the release of Ev's royal family.

records.l: palace of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The palace is Princess Langwidere's residence, where Ozma and her company enter without invitation to demand Dorothy's release. Ozma, Langwidere, and Dorothy later meet there after Dorothy is freed.

records.l: the North Tower, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The tower prison holds Dorothy in a room above the trees and farm houses. Dorothy looks out from its window, sees Ozma's procession, and calls down to the Scarecrow before Langwidere releases her.

records.l: the desert surrounding Oz, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The desert stretches westward from the Land of Ev toward the Land of Oz and is described as dangerous, deadly, and too wide to cross by ordinary means. Ozma's procession crosses it on a magic carpet.

records.l: the magic carpet, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The magic carpet unrolls across the desert beneath Ozma's procession, providing a safe surface above the life-destroying sands. It rolls itself up behind the procession and disappears after they reach the grassy meadows of the Land of Ev.

records.l: the golden chariot, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The golden chariot carries Ozma across the desert and is drawn by a Lion and a Tiger. Ozma stands inside it holding the ribbons and an ivory wand marked with diamond letters O and Z.

records.l: Princess Langwidere's collection of heads, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Princess Langwidere's heads collection is the reason she demands Dorothy's head in exchange for an old, cast-off head. Dorothy refuses because she does not want to exchange her own head for one she is not used to.

records.l: the prisoners' enslavement and imprisonment, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: The royal family's imprisonment concerns the Queen of Ev and her ten royal children, whom the Nome King is holding captive. Ozma offers to seek a way to free them, and Langwidere welcomes the possibility because their restoration would relieve her of ruling the kingdom.

records.l: Dorothy's rescue, Ozma of Oz, 7. Ozma of Oz to the Rescue
records.s: Dorothy's rescue begins when Ozma and her companions cross the desert and arrive at Langwidere's palace. Ozma makes Langwidere release Dorothy, and Dorothy returns to the company in Ozma's care.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Dorothy reunites with the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Cowardly Lion, and Billina after Ozma sets them free. She meets the Hungry Tiger, who explains that he refuses to eat living creatures despite his constant hunger. Billina is found fighting a speckled rooster and is brought back to the palace. Ozma announces a solemn conference to determine how to liberate the royal family of the Land of Ev from imprisonment.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Dorothy greets the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, winds Tiktok so he can bow, and asks about Billina. She reunites with the Cowardly Lion, meets the Hungry Tiger, rescues Billina from the chicken house, and carries her back to the palace.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Scarecrow joyfully embraces Dorothy and thanks Tiktok for protecting her. He tells Dorothy that he does not know where Billina is.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Tin Woodman gently embraces Dorothy and thanks Tiktok for protecting her. He explains that his Army of Oz consists of eight Generals, six Colonels, seven Majors, five Captains, and one private.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Dorothy winds Tiktok's action so that he can bow properly when introduced to the others. He is thanked by the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman for protecting Dorothy and later sits between them in the drawing-room.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Billina is found in the chicken house fighting a speckled rooster and leaves victorious, though she has lost many feathers, nearly lost an eye, and has a bleeding comb. Dorothy carries her back to the palace, where the Hungry Tiger says she looks appetizing but refuses to eat her because it would be wrong.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Cowardly Lion is found hitched to the chariot beside the Hungry Tiger and reunites happily with Dorothy. He introduces the Hungry Tiger and insists that, despite seeming brave to others, he has always been afraid when in danger.

records.l: Hungry Tiger, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Hungry Tiger explains that he is constantly hungry and craves living creatures, including fat babies, but refuses to eat them because his conscience tells him it is wrong. He says this makes him a good beast but a disgracefully bad tiger, and he has joined the Cowardly Lion after leaving the forest.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Ozma has set Dorothy and her friends free and invites Tiktok to sit in the drawing-room. She announces that a solemn conference will decide how to liberate the royal family of the Land of Ev.

records.l: Princess Langwidere, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: Princess Langwidere tells Dorothy that Billina is in the chicken house because her drawing-room is no place for hens. She sits opposite Tiktok in the drawing-room beside Ozma during the gathering.

records.l: Ozma's army, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Army of Oz is present in the drawing-room wearing handsome uniforms. It consists of twenty-seven members: eight Generals, six Colonels, seven Majors, five Captains, and one private.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The royal family of the Land of Ev is described as having endured a long imprisonment. Ozma and the others are preparing to determine how to liberate them.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The Land of Ev is described as a fair land whose royal family has been imprisoned for a long time.

records.l: solemn conference, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: A solemn conference is announced by Ozma to decide the best manner of liberating the royal family of the Land of Ev.

records.l: the liberation of the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 8. The Hungry Tiger
records.s: The liberation of the royal family is the purpose of the solemn conference announced by Ozma. The conference will determine the best manner of freeing them from their long imprisonment.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Ozma of Oz organizes an expedition from the Land of Ev to the Kingdom of the Nomes to free the former royal family of Ev, who are imprisoned by Roquat of the Rocks. The group learns that Evoldo sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King in exchange for a long life, then drowned himself. Ozma, Dorothy, the Army of twenty-seven, and their companions prepare for the dangerous journey, while Princess Langwidere stays behind. At daybreak, the party leaves the palace in a procession headed toward the Nome King's palace.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Ozma learns that Evoldo sold his family to the Nome King and decides that the prisoners must still be liberated. She consults Glinda the Good, receives a magic carpet, assembles an army, and leads the expedition toward the Kingdom of the Nomes.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Dorothy argues that imprisoning a queen mother and her ten children is wrong and agrees to join Ozma's expedition. She looks after Billina, talks with the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman, meets the Sawhorse, and rides in the golden chariot as the party departs.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Tin Woodman explains the purpose of Ozma's expedition and says that he and the army will fight the Nome King if necessary. He joins the journey despite fearing that the Nome King's furnaces may melt his tin.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Scarecrow agrees to undertake the rescue mission but worries that a spark from the Nome King's furnaces could destroy his straw body. He rides the Sawhorse during the procession and advises Ozma about the journey.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Tiktok points out that the Nome King did not wrongfully obtain the royal family because Evoldo sold them to him. As Dorothy's slave, Tiktok says he will go wherever she goes and marches behind the Scarecrow.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Billina agrees to join the expedition and is carried by Dorothy in the golden chariot. She spends part of the palace stay smoothing her feathers and later picks up scraps around the dining room.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Cowardly Lion rules the great forest as the King of Beasts and joins Ozma's expedition after learning that she intends to free Ev's royal family. He is unharnessed to roam through the palace before being harnessed to the chariot for the departure.

records.l: Hungry Tiger, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Hungry Tiger accompanies the Cowardly Lion and frightens the palace servants without harming anyone. He jokes with Nanda about eating her, explains that his appetite is too large for his body, and later helps pull the chariot.

records.l: Princess Langwidere, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Princess Langwidere says that Evoldo was wicked and explains that he sold his family to the Nome King for a long life before drowning himself. She refuses to join the expedition because she cannot bear heat, returns to her cabinet to change heads, and remains at home.

records.l: King Evoldo, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Evoldo, the former King of Ev, sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King in exchange for a long life. After realizing what he had done, he jumped into the sea and drowned himself.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Roquat of the Rocks is the Nome King's name and he rules the Underground World. He holds Evoldo's wife and children in his palace, where they have been transformed into ornaments and bric-a-brac.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The royal family of Ev consists of Evoldo's wife and ten children, five boys and five girls. The Nome King has enslaved them, imprisoned them in his underground palace, and transformed them into decorations.

records.l: Queen of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The queen of Ev, wife of Evoldo, was sold to the Nome King along with her ten children. She is imprisoned underground and has been transformed into an ornament.

records.l: Ozma's army, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Ozma assembles an Army of twenty-seven from the finest soldiers of Oz for the rescue mission. The army is housed and fed at the palace, then marches in formation behind the principal members of the expedition.

records.l: the Kingdom of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Kingdom of Oz is Ozma's country and supplies the army and several companions for the expedition. Its people obtain precious metals and stones from the earth, which the Nomes hide underground.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Land of Ev is the country whose former royal family was sold to the Nome King. Ozma's party stays in its palace and begins traveling through it toward the Nome King's domain.

records.l: underground kingdom of the Nomes, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Kingdom of the Nomes is the underground realm ruled by Roquat of the Rocks. It is rich in gold, silver, diamonds, rubies, and emeralds, and Ozma's party plans to enter it to rescue the prisoners.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Nome King's palace lies beneath the great mountain at the north end of Ev. The palace contains the transformed members of Ev's royal family as decorations and is the destination of Ozma's dangerous expedition.

records.l: the desert surrounding Oz, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The great desert separates the Land of Ev from Oz. Ozma initially cannot find a way across it until Glinda the Good provides the magic carpet.

records.l: the magic carpet, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Glinda the Good gives Ozma a magic carpet that continually unrolls beneath the travelers' feet, creating a comfortable path across the great desert.

records.l: the prisoners' enslavement and imprisonment, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The queen of Ev and her ten children have been enslaved and held prisoner by the Nome King in his underground palace. They have also been transformed into ornaments and bric-a-brac.

records.l: the liberation of the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Ozma organizes the expedition to liberate the royal family of Ev. Dorothy, the army, and the other companions agree to undertake the dangerous mission, which begins at daybreak.

records.l: Evoldo's bargain with the Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: Evoldo sold his wife and ten children to the Nome King in exchange for a long life. He later destroyed that life by jumping into the sea and drowning himself.

records.l: Nomes, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Nomes are powerful, strangely shaped sprites who serve the Nome King. They labor at furnaces and forges, produce metals and precious stones, and hide their treasures in rocks and underground.

records.l: the golden chariot, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The golden chariot carries Ozma, Dorothy, and Billina at the front of the departing procession. The Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger are harnessed to it.

records.l: Sawhorse, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The Sawhorse is a living wooden creature animated by magic powder. It does not tire or need food, carries the Scarecrow, and has gold plates on its feet so its legs will not wear out.

records.l: the journey to the Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 9. The Royal Family of Ev
records.s: The journey is undertaken by Ozma, Dorothy, their companions, and the Army of twenty-seven to rescue Ev's royal family. The procession leaves the palace at daybreak and makes good progress toward the valley leading to the Nome King's domain.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Dorothy, Ozma, Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Cowardly Lion, Tiktok, Sawhorse, Billina, and the army travel through a rocky valley toward the Land of Ev and the Nome King's underground palace. They cross a gulf on the magic carpet but are stopped by a giant iron man who pounds the narrow road with an immense iron mallet. The travelers pass beneath the hammer one by one, while the Cowardly Lion and the Tiger repeatedly carry the twenty-six officers to safety. Sawhorse is struck and damaged, the Scarecrow's foot is smashed, and the private is rescued after landing on the giant's arm.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Dorothy explains Billina's daily egg-laying habit and rides the Hungry Tiger beneath the Giant with the Hammer. She later helps with the rescue and continues the journey after the Sawhorse is repaired.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Ozma stops the chariot for Billina, uses the magic carpet to cross a deep gulf, and questions Tiktok about the iron giant. She rides the Cowardly Lion beneath the hammer and later helps oversee the rescue of the private.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The Scarecrow retrieves Billina's egg, thinks of a way to pass beneath the giant's hammer, and helps organize the crossing. He rescues the private by having him jump onto his straw-filled body, but the hammer smashes his left foot.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The Tin Woodman urges Billina to hurry, helps direct the procession, and crosses beneath the raised hammer. He later fits new ears to the Sawhorse.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The Cowardly Lion is frightened by the giant's hammer but bravely carries Ozma beneath it. He and the Tiger make twelve return trips to carry the twenty-six officers to safety before he becomes too tired to return for the private.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Tiktok explains that the iron giant was made for the Nome King by Smith & Tinker to prevent people from finding the underground palace. He says the giant cannot think or speak and that only the Nome King has the key to stop its machinery. Tiktok calmly walks beneath the raised hammer.

records.l: Sawhorse, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The Sawhorse retrieves Billina's egg and carries the Scarecrow through the mountain passage. It is struck by the hammer while attempting to carry the private, losing both ears and suffering a cracked left knee.

records.l: twenty-six officers, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The twenty-six officers are too frightened to walk or run beneath the hammer, despite their claimed courage in battle. The Cowardly Lion and the Tiger carry them across in pairs, and they insist that the private must also be rescued so they will have someone to command.

records.l: Omby Amby, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The private initially remains on the far side to guard the chariot. After the Sawhorse is struck, he lands on the Giant with the Hammer's arm and clings there until he drops onto the Scarecrow's body, escaping without broken bones.

records.l: the Giant with the Hammer, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The Giant with the Hammer is a huge man made of cast-iron plates, standing across the narrow road and towering more than a hundred feet above it. Made for the Nome King by Smith & Tinker, it has no thinking or speaking attachment and is designed to pound the road to keep travelers from finding the underground palace.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The third great mountain blocks the valley and forms the northern edge of the Land of Ev. The Nome King's palace is said to lie beneath this mountain.

records.l: the valley, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The valley lies between two high mountains and ends at a third mountain near the Land of Ev. Its path becomes rocky and narrow, eventually forcing the travelers to confront the Giant with the Hammer.

records.l: the magic carpet, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Ozma throws a small square of green cloth onto the ground, and it becomes a magic carpet that unrolls across a deep gulf. It protects the travelers from dangers beneath their feet but cannot shield them from the hammer above.

records.l: the iron mallet, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The iron mallet is larger than a barrel and fills the narrow road whenever it strikes. It rises and falls repeatedly, creating the brief openings through which the travelers pass.

records.l: the journey to the Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The journey through the mountains takes the procession over a gulf and along an increasingly rocky, constricted path. The travelers must abandon the chariot and use the backs of the Cowardly Lion and the Tiger, as well as the other available means, to continue.

records.l: passing beneath the giant's hammer, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: Passing beneath the giant's hammer requires each traveler to move when the hammer rises and reach the other side before it falls. The Cowardly Lion, the Tiger, Tiktok, the Tin Woodman, the Scarecrow, Billina, and the officers cross, though the Sawhorse is struck during the rescue of the private.

records.l: the giant's pounding, Ozma of Oz, 10. The Giant with the Hammer
records.s: The giant's pounding produces deep thumping sounds that echo through the mountains like cannon fire. It blocks the road and continues behind the travelers after they finally pass beyond it.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: Ozma of Oz, Dorothy, and their companions reach the mountain at the edge of the Kingdom of Ev and enter the Nome King's palace. The Nome King explains that the King of Ev exchanged the Queen of Ev and her ten children for a long life, and that he transformed them into bric-a-brac and ornaments. Ozma's attempt to negotiate their release fails until the Nome King offers a dangerous guessing challenge involving eleven objects in his palace. If Ozma identifies none of the royal transformations, she will herself become an ornament or article of bric-a-brac.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King receives Ozma of Oz and her companions in his underground palace and claims that the Queen of Ev and her children are his slaves because he purchased them from the King of Ev. He refuses to release them, displays the strength of his vast army, and offers Ozma a challenge in which she may identify their transformations.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: Ozma of Oz leads her companions to the Nome King's palace to rescue the Queen of Ev and her ten children. She first demands and requests the Nome King's appearance, then offers replacements for the royal family and threatens to conquer his kingdom before agreeing to his guessing challenge.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: Dorothy encourages Ozma to plead with the Nome King and successfully calls him by saying, "PLEASE Mr. Nome King, come here and see us." She argues that the King of Ev did not receive a long life because he drowned, but accepts the Nome King's explanation of the bargain.

records.l: Queen of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Queen of Ev was sold by the King of Ev to the Nome King and is held as one of his slaves. The Nome King says that he transformed her into an article of ornament or bric-a-brac in his palace.

records.l: King of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The King of Ev exchanged the Queen of Ev and their ten children to the Nome King for a long life. He then jumped into the sea and was drowned, which the Nome King says destroyed the long life he had provided.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Queen of Ev's ten children were sold with her to the Nome King and are held as his slaves. Like their mother, they were transformed into articles of ornament and bric-a-brac and scattered throughout the Nome King's palace.

records.l: Nomes, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nomes are rock-fairies who serve the Nome King and move across the mountain's rocky surface. They mock Ozma's party with laughter, vanish when the Nome King growls, and include both workers and soldiers in the Underground World.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Kingdom of Ev lies beyond the mountain that blocks the travelers' path. Its royal family is needed to govern it, according to Ozma, but the Queen of Ev and her children are being held by the Nome King.

records.l: underground kingdom of the Nomes, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Underground World is a vast cavern beneath the mountain, filled with furnaces, forges, Nomes, and thousands of silver and gold doors. The Nome King shows Ozma that it contains a very large, well-equipped force of Nome soldiers.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King's palace is entered through a door in the mountain and a jewel-lit passage. It contains a domed cavern with a jeweled rock throne and rooms where the Queen of Ev and her children have been scattered as ornaments and bric-a-brac.

records.l: Nome King's army, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King's army emerges from thousands of silver and gold doors in the Underground World. Its rock-colored soldiers wear jeweled steel armor, carry bronze weapons, and stand in disciplined ranks; the Nome King says this is only a small part of his army.

records.l: Queen of Ev and her children's transformations, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King transformed the Queen of Ev and her ten children into articles of ornament and bric-a-brac rather than making them perform hard labor as slaves. He scattered their transformed forms throughout the rooms of his palace.

records.l: King of Ev's bargain, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The King of Ev exchanged the Queen of Ev and his ten children to the Nome King for a long life. The Nome King insists that he fulfilled the bargain, even though the King of Ev destroyed that life by drowning himself.

records.l: Ozma's rescue mission, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: Ozma's rescue mission brings her, Dorothy, and their companions to the Nome King's dominions to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children. She abandons the idea of fighting the Nome King's army and seeks a peaceful way to restore the royal family.

records.l: Nome King's challenge, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King permits Ozma to enter his palace alone and touch eleven different objects while saying the word "Ev." Any objects that are members of the royal family will be restored, but if none is correct, Ozma herself will be transformed into bric-a-brac or an ornament.

records.l: bric-a-brac and ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 11. The Nome King
records.s: The Nome King uses bric-a-brac and ornaments as transformed forms for the Queen of Ev and her ten children, scattering them throughout his palace. He also threatens to transform Ozma into one if she fails to identify any of the royal family correctly.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: Ozma accepts the Nome King's challenge to identify members of the royal family of Ev among the ornaments in his palace, risking enslavement if she guesses incorrectly. She uses all eleven guesses without success, and her final blind guess transforms her into an emerald grasshopper ornament. The Nome King then invites another attempt, offering twelve guesses because twelve people are now transformed into ornaments. Dorothy volunteers, but the Tin Woodman claims the privilege of going next as commander of Ozma's army.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: Ozma accepts the Nome King's offer and enters his royal palace to identify the royal family of Ev among its ornaments. After ten unsuccessful guesses, she makes an eleventh guess blindly and is transformed into a pretty grasshopper formed from a single emerald.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The Nome King imposes the guessing challenge, leads Ozma to his royal palace, and waits outside while she guesses. After Ozma fails, he cheerfully announces that another person may try with twelve guesses because twelve people are now transformed into ornaments.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: Dorothy warns Ozma not to accept the challenge because a wrong guess would enslave her. After Ozma is transformed, Dorothy volunteers to make the next attempt, but the Tin Woodman goes instead.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The Scarecrow worries about failing the challenge and becoming a piece of bric-a-brac. After Ozma's failure, he encourages the Tin Woodman to be careful.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The Tin Woodman claims the privilege of following Ozma as commander of her army and enters the Nome King's royal palace to attempt her rescue.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The royal family of Ev has been transformed into ornaments in the Nome King's palace. Ozma tries to identify its members but fails.

records.l: the Nome King's underground palace, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The palace is a splendid underground structure filled with rooms, marble, carpets, draperies, carved furniture, and many ornaments. The transformed members of the royal family of Ev are hidden among its ornaments, and Ozma and then the Tin Woodman enter it through an opening in the cave wall.

records.l: eleven guesses, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: Ozma is allowed eleven guesses to identify an object that is a transformed member of the royal family of Ev. She makes all eleven guesses unsuccessfully.

records.l: guessing challenge, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The challenge requires a person to touch an ornament and say the word "Ev" in an attempt to restore a transformed member of the royal family. A wrong guess results in the guesser becoming an ornament and being enslaved.

records.l: Queen of Ev and her children's transformations, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The royal family of Ev and unsuccessful guessers are transformed into ornaments. After Ozma's failure, the Nome King says that twelve persons are now transformed into ornaments.

records.l: the prisoners' enslavement and imprisonment, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The challenge threatens to enslave anyone who guesses incorrectly. Ozma risks her freedom and is no longer free after her final guess.

records.l: bric-a-brac and ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: The palace contains many ornaments made from metals, glass, china, stones, marbles, and precious gems, among them the transformed members of the royal family of Ev. Ozma becomes a new ornament.

records.l: emerald grasshopper, Ozma of Oz, 12. The Eleven Guesses
records.s: Ozma's final guess transforms her into a pretty grasshopper that seems to have been formed from a single emerald. It rests on the edge of a small round table in the palace.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The Nome King laughs as the Tin Woodman and the twenty-six officers become ornaments after failing to guess correctly in his palace. Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Tiktok, and a private remain, while the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger sleep and Billina hides beneath the King’s throne. The King sends the survivors to sleeping rooms after the private is transformed, planning to continue the guessing challenge the next day. Dorothy later discovers that Billina is missing, but she cannot reopen the locked doorway to the throne room.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The Nome King laughs at the Tin Woodman’s transformation and threatens reluctant officers with his fiery furnaces. He orders refreshments and sleeping rooms for the surviving guests, then plans to continue transforming them into ornaments the next day.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: Dorothy is disheartened by the loss of her friends but eats the cakes and drinks the clay coffee served by the Nome King’s Chief Steward. She worries when Billina is missing and cannot get back into the locked throne room, then goes to sleep.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The Scarecrow is saddened that the Tin Woodman has become an ornament and worries that the Nome King’s laughter will hurt his friend’s pride. He remains with Dorothy, Tiktok, and the private and is taken to a sleeping room.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The Tin Woodman becomes an ornament after making an unsuccessful guess in the Nome King’s palace. The Nome King considers him a particularly funny ornament, which causes the King to laugh.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
