records.s: Tiktok remains with Dorothy and the Scarecrow after the others are transformed. He observes that the Tin Woodman was always an ornament to society and predicts that he and the Scarecrow will become absurd ornaments the next day.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: Billina gathers the crumbs of cake and then hides in a hollow beneath the Nome King’s rocky throne. She falls asleep there, unnoticed by the others, and is missing when Dorothy later looks for her.

records.l: little band of adventurers, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The little band is greatly disheartened after its girl Ruler and Tin Woodman are lost as ornaments. By the end of the unit, only Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Tiktok, the private, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, the Sawhorse, and the hidden Billina remain from the group waiting outside the palace.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The Nome King’s palace is described as magnificent but dreadful and creepy. Its rocky portal leads to rooms where those who guess incorrectly are transformed into ornaments, and its sleeping apartments are plain but comfortable.

records.l: Queen of Ev and her children's transformations, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: Those who enter the Nome King’s palace and guess incorrectly are transformed into ornaments. The Tin Woodman, all twenty-six officers, and the private undergo this transformation in the unit.

records.l: guessing challenge, Ozma of Oz, 13. The Nome King Laughs
records.s: The guessing challenge requires each entrant to make guesses inside the Nome King’s palace, with failure resulting in transformation into an ornament. The officers and private fail, while the Nome King postpones dealing with the remaining guests until the next day.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The Nome King reveals that the Queen of Ev and her children have been transformed into royal-purple ornaments, while people from Oz have been changed into green ornaments. Dorothy enters the palace to wind Tiktok and make guesses, but Tiktok fails to identify the correct ornament. Dorothy succeeds in restoring Evring, a prince of Ev who had been changed into the image of a purple kitten, though her other guesses fail. She returns to the throne room with Evring.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: Dorothy enters the palace to wind Tiktok and attempt the guessing task. After several failures, she correctly identifies the image of a purple kitten as Evring and restores him, then returns to the throne room with him.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The Nome King reveals that the Queen of Ev and her children are all hidden among the royal-purple ornaments. He plans to transform Dorothy into a gray ornament and the Scarecrow and the machine man into solid-gold ornaments, but Dorothy instead returns with Evring.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: Tiktok stands motionless in the palace after using all but one of his allowed guesses. Dorothy winds him up, and he makes his final guess by touching a yellow vase and saying "Ev," but he disappears without being identified.

records.l: Prince Evring, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: Evring is a prince of Ev who had been transformed into the image of a purple kitten. Dorothy correctly guesses his hiding place and restores him, after which he accompanies her back to the throne room.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The royal family of Ev, including Evring, has been transformed into ornaments by the Nome King. They are all hidden among the ornaments that are royal purple.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The palace contains many ornaments of different colors, shapes, and sizes, including the enchanted members of the royal family of Ev. Dorothy searches its rooms, restores Evring, and then exits through its massive rock doors.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: Ev is the kingdom whose royal family has been transformed into ornaments and hidden in the Nome King's palace. Evring identifies himself as a prince of Ev and says that his father sold his mother and siblings to the cruel ruler of the Nomes.

records.l: the purple ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The purple ornaments are the transformed Queen of Ev and her children. They are scattered throughout the palace in many shapes and sizes, and Dorothy restores at least one of them.

records.l: the image of a purple kitten, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The image of a purple kitten stands on the corner of a mantel in the palace. When Dorothy touches it and says "Ev," it disappears and Evring appears in its place.

records.l: guessing challenge, Ozma of Oz, 14. Dorothy Tries to be Brave
records.s: The guessing task requires the visitors to identify which palace ornaments are the transformed people of Ev. Tiktok fails on his final guess, while Dorothy makes several unsuccessful guesses before correctly identifying Evring.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Billina lays an egg under the Nome King's throne and uses the King's fear of eggs to secure permission to guess enchantments. Dorothy returns safely with Prince Evring after correctly guessing one enchantment, but the Scarecrow fails and is transformed into a solid gold card-receiver. Billina then enters the enchanted palace to guess, despite Dorothy's warning, while the Nome King worries about the talking hen.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Dorothy correctly guesses one of the Nome King's enchantments and returns safely to the throne room with Prince Evring. She warns Billina that guessing the ornaments is difficult, but Billina enters the enchanted palace anyway.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Billina lays an egg under the Nome King's throne and bargains for the right to enter the palace and guess the enchantments. She insists on going despite Dorothy's concern and enters the enchanted palace, confident that she may guess correctly.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: The Nome King is terrified because eggs are poisonous to Nomes, and he allows Billina to guess in exchange for having the egg removed. He celebrates the Scarecrow's transformation but becomes increasingly nervous about Billina's presence and talking.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: The Scarecrow is distressed by the danger facing Dorothy and the others. He fails to guess any of the enchantments and is transformed into a solid gold card-receiver.

records.l: Prince Evring, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Prince Evring returns with Dorothy and offers Billina and Dorothy a home in the Land of Ev. He is shy around the Scarecrow but speaks with dignity when he makes his offer.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: The enchanted palace receives the Scarecrow after Dorothy's return and awaits Billina as its next visitor. Those who fail to guess its objects' enchantments are transformed into ornaments.

records.l: Billina's eggs, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Billina's egg is laid under the Nome King's throne, where it frightens him because eggs are poisonous to Nomes. The Scarecrow removes it and places it in a pocket.

records.l: ornament, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: The Nome King turns those who fail his guessing challenge into ornaments. The Scarecrow becomes a solid gold card-receiver, and the King plans to make Billina an ornament if she fails.

records.l: guessing, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: Guessing the enchantments is dangerous and difficult, but Dorothy succeeds once while the Scarecrow fails every time. Billina insists on trying and claims she may succeed.

records.l: the Nome King's enchantments, Ozma of Oz, 15. Billina Frightens the Nome King
records.s: The Nome King's enchantments transform visitors who guess incorrectly into objects. Dorothy breaks one enchantment by guessing correctly, while the Scarecrow fails to break any.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Billina uses her knowledge of the Nome King's transformations to restore the Queen of Ev, her nine children, the people of Oz, Ozma of Oz, the Scarecrow, and Tiktok. She recognizes the emerald grasshopper as Ozma and finds the Scarecrow and Tiktok among the gold ornaments, but no transformation that could be the Tin Woodman. The group returns toward the Nome King to demand information about the Tin Woodman, only to find the cavern filled with his motionless warriors and the enraged King waiting on his throne.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Billina surveys the underground palace, identifies the purple and green transformations, and restores the Queen of Ev, her nine children, the people of Oz, Ozma of Oz, the Scarecrow, and Tiktok. She recognizes the emerald grasshopper as Ozma and leads the group back toward the Nome King to ask about the Tin Woodman.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Nome King’s transformations are identified and reversed by Billina. He is waiting on his rocky throne surrounded by his warriors, with his face distorted by rage, after the group decides to demand information about the Tin Woodman.

records.l: Queen of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Queen of Ev is restored from a purple footstool by Billina and gratefully embraces her nine recovered children. She helps identify the grasshopper as the transformation Billina is seeking for Ozma.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The royal family of Ev is restored from the Nome King’s transformations. The Queen and her nine children are reunited, and they prepare to return to their own country.

records.l: Princes and Princesses of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Five Princesses and four Princes of Ev are restored by Billina and stand beside their mother. The Princesses are Evanna, Evrose, Evella, Evirene, and Evedna; the Princes are Evrob, Evington, Evardo, and Evroland.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Ozma of Oz has been transformed into an emerald grasshopper, but Billina restores her to her lovely and dainty form. Ozma helps search for the Scarecrow, Tiktok, and the Tin Woodman and decides that the group must make the Nome King explain what happened to their friend.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Scarecrow has been transformed into a solid-gold ornament and is restored by Billina. He declares that the Nome King is a villain and joins the group’s return to confront him.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Tin Woodman has been transformed into something the Nome King described as funny, but no such ornament is found in the palace. Ozma and the others return to the Nome King to learn what has become of him.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Tiktok has been transformed into a gold ornament and is restored with the Scarecrow. He admits that he thought the Nome King was honest and says that Smith & Tinker are responsible when his thoughts do not work properly.

records.l: people of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The people of Oz are represented among the twenty-six officers and the private, who have been changed into green ornaments. Billina restores them, and they thank her for freeing them from the Nome King’s magic.

records.l: Nome King's warriors, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Nome King’s mail-clad warriors fill the domed cavern in orderly ranks. They stand motionless with battle-axes poised, awaiting the King’s command.

records.l: the Nome King's underground palace, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The underground palace is described as one of the most splendid and beautiful places in fairyland, with rich velvet carpets and magnificent rooms. Its purple, green, and gold ornaments conceal many of the Nome King’s transformed captives.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Ev is the country of the Queen and her nine children. Evardo, the eldest prince, is to inherit his father’s throne and become King of Ev when he returns.

records.l: Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Oz is the homeland of Ozma, the Scarecrow, Tiktok, and the officers and private who are restored in the palace. Ozma is identified as green because she is from Oz.

records.l: the purple ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Billina counts ten purple ornaments scattered throughout the palace. She identifies them as transformations of the Queen of Ev and her nine children and restores all of them.

records.l: the green ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The green ornaments are transformations of the people of Oz. Billina finds and restores the twenty-six officers and the private, then continues searching for Ozma among the remaining green objects.

records.l: gold ornaments, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The gold ornaments include the transformations of the Scarecrow and Tiktok. Billina and Ozma find these ornaments and restore both companions.

records.l: emerald grasshopper, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The emerald grasshopper is a hard, lifeless transformation that Billina briefly mistakes for food. After the Queen suggests it may be the object Billina seeks, Billina restores it and reveals Ozma of Oz.

records.l: Queen of Ev and her children's transformations, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Nome King’s transformations include the purple ornaments containing the royal family of Ev, the green ornaments containing people of Oz, the gold ornaments containing the Scarecrow and Tiktok, and the emerald grasshopper containing Ozma. The Tin Woodman’s transformation remains unidentified.

records.l: the Nome King's enchantments, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: The Nome King’s enchantment has changed people into ornaments and other objects, leaving them unable to move. Billina breaks the enchantment by correctly guessing which objects were once living beings.

records.l: release of the transformed people, Ozma of Oz, 16. Purple, Green, and Gold
records.s: Billina’s successful guesses release the Queen of Ev, her children, the people of Oz, Ozma, the Scarecrow, and Tiktok from their transformations. Thirty-seven people are alive in the palace after the releases and credit Billina with saving them from the Nome King’s magic.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Billina’s restoration mission succeeds, breaking the Nome King’s enchantments and restoring the royal family of Ev, Ozma, and their companions. The Nome King summons his warriors and attempts to seize Dorothy, but the Sawhorse protects her and cannot be stopped by the King’s magic. When the Scarecrow throws Billina’s eggs at the Nome King, the warriors flee in terror, leaving the King blinded and helpless. Billina then tells Dorothy to take the Nome King’s jeweled belt.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Dorothy waits with Prince Evring for Billina’s restoration mission to succeed and rejoices whenever the bell announces that another enchantment has been broken. She stands protected by the Lion, the Tiger, and the Sawhorse when the Nome King orders his warriors to seize her. At Billina’s urging, she prepares to take the Nome King’s jeweled belt.

records.l: Prince Evring, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Prince Evring waits with Dorothy for Billina’s mission to succeed. When the Nome warriors enter, he remains beside Dorothy while she holds his hand.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Nome King becomes increasingly furious as the bell announces that his enchantments are being broken. He summons his warriors, tries to seize Dorothy, and attempts to enchant the Sawhorse, but the magic does not work on wood. Billina’s eggs strike and blind him, causing him to stand helplessly in fear while his warriors flee.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Billina successfully guesses which palace ornaments contain enchanted people and restores them to their natural forms. She tells the Scarecrow how to use her eggs against the Nome King and then tells Dorothy to take the King’s jeweled belt.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Ozma is restored to her natural form during Billina’s mission. She orders her army to fight the Nome warriors, and the generals pass the order down until a private soldier attacks.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Scarecrow fears that the Nome King’s underground dungeons and volcanic fires would reduce him to an ash-heap. Following Billina’s whispered advice, he throws one of her eggs into the Nome King’s left eye and a second into his right eye, blinding him.

records.l: Sawhorse, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Sawhorse kicks the Nome King when he tries to act against Dorothy. The King’s magic cannot stop the wooden Sawhorse, which kicks him again and then stands beside Dorothy and the Hungry Tiger.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Lion crouches beside Dorothy and Prince Evring when the Nome warriors enter. It snarls and bares its teeth so fiercely that the warriors retreat, and Billina later perches on its back.

records.l: Hungry Tiger, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Tiger crouches on Dorothy’s other side and threatens the Nome warriors with fierce snarls and bared teeth. It later stands beside the Sawhorse when the restored people enter.

records.l: Nome King's warriors, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Nome warriors enter the throne room after the Nome King summons them and prepare to seize Dorothy. They are briefly knocked down by Ozma’s private soldier, but flee in terror when Billina’s eggs strike the Nome King.

records.l: people of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The people of Ev are restored from their enchanted forms during Billina’s mission. They appear with the people of Oz in the palace doorway and witness the Nome King and his warriors.

records.l: people of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The people of Oz are restored during Billina’s mission. They enter with the people of Ev after the palace doors open and find the Nome King’s warriors gathered in the throne room.

records.l: the Nome King's underground palace, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Nome King’s palace contains the enchanted ornaments and the rooms where Billina restores the royal family of Ev, Ozma, and their followers. Its doors open to reveal the restored people, while the Nome King’s warriors gather inside.

records.l: throne room, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The throne room fills with Nome warriors after the King summons them. The warriors later flee from it after the Scarecrow’s eggs blind the Nome King.

records.l: the magic belt, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Nome King’s magic belt fails to stop the wooden Sawhorse because the creature is made of wood. Billina tells Dorothy that the jeweled belt unbuckles in the back and urges her to take it.

records.l: Billina's eggs, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Billina’s eggs are treated by the Nome warriors as deadly poison. The Scarecrow throws two of them at the Nome King, blinding him and causing the warriors to flee.

records.l: the Nome King's enchantments, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The bell rings whenever an enchantment is broken. Billina breaks many of the Nome King’s enchantments, restoring the royal family of Ev, Ozma, and their companions to their natural forms.

records.l: conquest of the Nome Kingdom, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: The Nome King’s defeat begins when the Scarecrow blinds him with Billina’s eggs and his warriors flee. The King remains unable to see or escape while Billina directs Dorothy to take his jeweled belt.

records.l: Billina's restoration mission, Ozma of Oz, 17. The Scarecrow Wins the Fight
records.s: Billina’s restoration mission succeeds as she correctly identifies enchanted ornaments and transforms them back into living people. The mission restores the royal family of Ev, Ozma, and their followers and leads to the Nome King’s helplessness.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Dorothy takes the Nome King's magic belt after Billina blinds him with broken eggs, and she uses it to open the passage out of his palace. Dorothy, Ozma, Billina, the Scarecrow, and the others search the palace for the transformed Tin Woodman but cannot find him. The Nome King claims he knows what ornament the Tin Woodman became, yet the ornament is gone when he searches for it. During the escape, Dorothy turns pursuing warriors into eggs and later stops the giant man of iron so the group can reach Ev safely.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Dorothy takes the Nome King's jeweled magic belt and fastens it around her waist. She commands the belt to open the passage, attempts to restore the Tin Woodman, turns pursuing warriors into eggs, and stops the giant man of iron so the group can pass safely.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The Nome King is blinded by broken eggs and loses his magic belt. He tries unsuccessfully to transform the group, agrees to search for the Tin Woodman, and later attempts to stop their escape by sending warriors after them.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Ozma welcomes the rescued people and refuses to leave without finding the Tin Woodman. She leads the returning party and orders the march through the passage after the search fails.

records.l: Queen of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The Queen of Ev is welcomed back to the land of the living and leaves the Nome King's palace with her children. She rides the Tiger during the journey toward Ev and worries about her children's safety near the giant man of iron.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Billina saves the captives by using eggs against the Nome King, but she has no clue for identifying the Tin Woodman's transformed form. She warns Dorothy not to return the magic belt and supports threatening the Nome King with transformation.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The Scarecrow taunts the Nome King after the eggs blind him and suggests making him a goose-egg unless he finds the Tin Woodman. He believes the belt must be kept and later commands the army while the group travels without the Tin Woodman.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The Tin Woodman remains missing after the Nome King transformed him into an ornament. Dorothy and the others search the palace for him, but even the Nome King cannot find the ornament he says was the Tin Woodman's form.

records.l: Ozma's army, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The army leaves the Nome King's palace ahead of the royal family and the other travelers. The Scarecrow commands it during the journey because the Tin Woodman is absent.

records.l: Nome King's warriors, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: A large number of the Nome King's warriors chase the escaping party with swords, spears, and axes. Dorothy uses the magic belt to turn the foremost warriors into eggs, causing the rest to flee.

records.l: the royal family of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The royal family of Ev leaves the Nome King's palace with the rescuing party, although the Nome King had claimed they were his slaves. The Queen of Ev and her children travel together toward Ev.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The party intends to return to Ev after escaping the Nome King's underground cavern. The road to Ev lies plainly before them once they emerge from the passage.

records.l: Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The palace contains many rooms and thousands of ornaments, among which the transformed Tin Woodman is believed to be hidden. The group searches it without success before leaving through the passage.

records.l: passage, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The passage out of the Nome King's palace has been closed and cannot be found by ordinary searching. Dorothy commands it to open with the magic belt, allowing the party to escape into the outer air.

records.l: the magic belt, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The magic belt is taken from the Nome King by Dorothy and obeys her commands. It opens the hidden passage, is used in the unsuccessful search for the Tin Woodman, turns warriors into eggs, and stops the giant man of iron.

records.l: Billina's eggs, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Eggs are poisonous to Nomes and blind the Nome King when Billina uses them against him. Dorothy later transforms pursuing warriors into eggs, which block the passage and frighten the remaining warriors away.

records.l: escape from the Nome King's palace, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: The group escapes after Dorothy uses the magic belt to reopen the passage. The Nome King's warriors pursue them, but Dorothy defeats the pursuit by turning the foremost warriors into eggs, and the party reaches the outer path safely.

records.l: search for the Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 18. The Fate of the Tin Woodman
records.s: Dorothy, Ozma, Billina, and the others search every room of the palace for the Tin Woodman's transformed form. The Nome King also searches, but the ornament is gone, so the party leaves without rescuing him.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Ozma and the others return to Ev in her golden chariot after the defeat of the Nome King, while the royal children and Queen mother are welcomed home. Evring reveals that he picked up a tin whistle in the Nome King's palace, and Billina uses it to restore the enchanted Tin Woodman. At the palace of Ev, the Queen mother presents her eldest son as King Evardo Fifteenth, and the people approve his succession. The people celebrate the royal family's return, and Billina receives a necklace of pearls and sapphires.

records.l: Nome King, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Nome King has been defeated, and the Nomes no longer laugh impudently at the returning adventurers. His palace is where Evring found the tin whistle that had concealed the Tin Woodman.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Ozma returns to Ev in her golden chariot with the Queen mother, the royal children, and their companions. She welcomes the Tin Woodman when Billina restores him and is splendidly entertained by the Queen mother at the palace.

records.l: Queen of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Queen mother returns joyfully to Ev with her children and welcomes them at the royal palace. She permits Princess Langwidere to keep her rooms and cabinet of heads, and she proclaims her eldest son King Evardo Fifteenth.

records.l: the ten royal children of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The royal children of Ev return safely to their country and cheer when the palace comes into view. They are splendidly entertained by the Queen mother after their arrival.

records.l: Prince Evring, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Evring rides with Dorothy on the Sawhorse and has become fond of her after she rescued him. He reveals that he picked up a tin whistle in the Nome King's palace and put it in his pocket, unintentionally carrying the Tin Woodman inside it.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Dorothy rides with Evring on the Sawhorse and is pleased when Billina restores the Tin Woodman. She embraces the Tin Woodman and tells him that his enchantment is over.

records.l: Sawhorse, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Sawhorse carries Dorothy, Evring, and Billina toward Ev. It leaps and prances in alarm when Evring blows the tin whistle.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Billina rides on the Sawhorse and notices that Evring's tin whistle explains why the Tin Woodman could not be found or summoned by the magic belt. She touches the whistle and says "Ev," restoring the Tin Woodman, and later receives a necklace of pearls and sapphires from the new King.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Scarecrow wishes that the Tin Woodman were with the returning party and says that leaving him behind breaks his heart. He is delighted when Billina restores the Tin Woodman and embraces his old comrade.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Tiktok says that the Tin Woodman was a fine fellow, though tin was not very durable. Tiktok also wishes sometimes to be stuffed with straw instead of being made of copper, and later squeezes the Tin Woodman's hand so earnestly that some fingers are dented.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Tin Woodman has been enchanted and concealed inside Evring's tin whistle, so the magic belt could not make him appear and the Nome King could not find him. Billina restores him by saying "Ev," after which he rejoins his friends and is welcomed by the army and the people.

records.l: Ev, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: Ev is reached by the returning party after they cross the gulf and pass through countryside filled with birds, flowers, farms, and new-mown hay. Its people celebrate the return of the Queen mother and the royal children and accept Evardo as their new ruler.

records.l: palace of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The palace of Ev comes into view as the royal party returns, and a large crowd gathers there to welcome the Queen mother and her ten children. Princess Langwidere is found in her mirrored chamber, and Evardo is proclaimed king from a balcony overlooking the subjects.

records.l: King Evardo Fifteenth, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: King Evardo Fifteenth is the Queen mother's eldest son and is fifteen years old. He has fifteen silver buckles, is proclaimed king by his mother, receives a gold crown and ermine robe, and then goes to look for cake in the royal pantry.

records.l: people of Ev, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The people of Ev gather to welcome the Queen mother and her children, shouting, cheering, and throwing flowers. They shout their approval fifteen times when Evardo is proclaimed king, and some Wheelers promise to obey him.

records.l: tin whistle, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The tin whistle is shaped like a small fat pig, painted green, with the whistle in its tail. Evring finds it in the Nome King's palace, and when Billina touches it and says "Ev," the Tin Woodman appears.

records.l: conquest of the Nome Kingdom, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The defeat of the Nome King leaves the Nomes silent and respectful instead of laughing at the adventurers. It also allows Ozma, the Queen mother, the royal children, and their companions to return safely toward Ev.

records.l: proclamation of Evardo as king, Ozma of Oz, 19. The King of Ev
records.s: The Queen mother proclaims Evardo Fifteenth as the future ruler of Ev from a balcony overlooking the gathered subjects. She crowns him with gold and rubies and places an ermine robe over his shoulders, while the people approve the proclamation.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Dorothy accepts Ozma's invitation to return from Ev to the Land of Oz, traveling across the desert with Ozma, Tiktok, Billina, and the others on a magic carpet. They enter the Land of Oz, travel by yellow brick road to the Emerald City, and receive a joyful welcome. At a grand reception, the adventurers are honored with gifts, Dorothy is made a Princess of Oz, and Tiktok receives emerald bracelets. During the royal feast, Ozma promotes the private Omby Amby to Captain General and Commander of her Body Guard, while the Hungry Tiger consumes all the food and then loses his appetite.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Dorothy accepts Ozma's invitation to return to the Land of Oz because she is anxious to see it again. She travels with Ozma's party, is welcomed by people who remember her, receives a coronet, and is made a Princess of Oz.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Ozma leads the return journey from Ev to the Land of Oz on her magic carpet. She is welcomed as the ruler of Oz, receives a grand reception, honors the adventurers, and promotes Omby Amby to command the armies and her Body Guard.

records.l: Tiktok, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Tiktok joins Ozma's party as Dorothy's faithful follower because he belongs to her. Dorothy winds up his machinery before the journey, and he later receives bracelets set with eight rows of sparkling emeralds.

records.l: Billina, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Billina accepts Ozma's invitation to visit the Land of Oz and crosses the desert with the party. She lays her daily egg during the journey and sits on a golden roost at the royal feast, eating from a jeweled platter.

records.l: Scarecrow, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The Scarecrow returns to the Emerald City with Ozma's party and is joyfully greeted by the people. He receives a silver jar of complexion powder and sits at the royal feast with flowers before him because he does not require food.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The Tin Woodman returns to the Emerald City and is welcomed as a popular favorite. He receives a new axe studded with diamonds and helps answer Ozma's question about the number of privates in the armies.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The Cowardly Lion is joyfully greeted during the procession into the Emerald City. He attends the royal feast and is served on a golden platter.

records.l: Omby Amby, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Omby Amby is the private summoned from the barracks during the feast. Ozma promotes him to Captain General of all the armies of her kingdom and Commander of her Body Guard, and she promises to supply his uniforms from the royal treasury.

records.l: Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The Land of Oz is ruled by Ozma, who governs the four regional kings and lives in the Emerald City at the center of the four kingdoms. Dorothy and the others enter it safely after crossing the desert and are welcomed by its people.

records.l: the Emerald City, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The Emerald City is Ozma's royal city in the exact center of the four kingdoms of the Land of Oz. Dorothy and the returning adventurers travel to it by yellow brick road, where they receive a joyful procession, reception, and feast.

records.l: the magic carpet, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Ozma throws down the magic carpet at the edge of the dangerous desert, and it unrolls far enough for the entire party to walk on it without being crowded. It carries them safely across the desert to the Land of Oz.

records.l: magic journey to Oz, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The magic journey to Oz begins when Dorothy accepts Ozma's invitation to leave Ev. Ozma, Dorothy, Tiktok, Billina, and the others cross the desert on the magic carpet and reach the Land of Oz before sunset.

records.l: Ozma's rescue mission, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The royal reception celebrates Ozma's successful rescue mission to save the royal family of a neighboring kingdom. Jack Pumpkinhead reads an address congratulating her for its success.

records.l: grand reception, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: The grand reception in the royal palace is attended by important persons of Oz. The adventurers are honored with gifts, including medals, a diamond-studded axe, complexion powder, Dorothy's coronet, and Tiktok's emerald bracelets.

records.l: royal feast, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: At the royal feast, Ozma seats Dorothy at her right and Billina at her left, while the other adventurers and officials receive places at the table. The Hungry Tiger consumes all the food and then declares that he has lost his appetite.

records.l: private's military promotion, Ozma of Oz, 20. The Emerald City
records.s: Ozma summons the private during the feast and learns that his name is Omby Amby. She promotes him to Captain General of all the armies and Commander of her Body Guard, providing royal funds for his uniforms.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Dorothy uses Ozma's magic picture to see Aunt Em on the Kansas farm and Uncle Henry in Australia, where he appears ill and lonely. Glinda the Good explains that the magic belt can transport Dorothy out of a fairy country but would be lost when she arrived, so Dorothy gives it to Ozma and arranges a way to return. Dorothy says farewell to her friends in the Land of Oz and is transported to Uncle Henry, promising to care for him. Uncle Henry says he is already feeling better.

records.l: Dorothy, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Dorothy spends several happy weeks in the Land of Oz as Ozma's guest. After seeing that Uncle Henry is ill and lonely in Australia, she decides to return to him, gives the magic belt to Ozma, and says farewell to her friends. She is transported to Uncle Henry and promises to nurse and care for him.

records.l: Ozma, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Ozma entertains Dorothy in the Land of Oz and lets her use the magic picture. She agrees to help Dorothy return to Uncle Henry and accepts the magic belt so it will not be lost. She is to watch for Dorothy's signal in the magic picture and use the belt to bring Dorothy back to Oz.

records.l: Uncle Henry, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Uncle Henry is shown in a room in Sydney, Australia, looking sad and lonely, with white hair and thin, wasted hands and face. Dorothy believes that worry about her is harming him, so she returns to care for him. He smiles, cuddles Dorothy, and says he is already feeling better.

records.l: Glinda the Good, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Glinda the Good listens to Dorothy's concern about Uncle Henry and advises her about the magic belt. She confirms that the belt could take Dorothy to Australia but would be lost there, and agrees that giving it to Ozma is a wise plan.

records.l: Land of Oz, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: The Land of Oz is where Dorothy spends several happy weeks among old and new friends. It is a fairy country in which the magic belt retains its powers, and Dorothy leaves it to return to Uncle Henry in Australia.

records.l: the Emerald City, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: The Emerald City is where Dorothy and Ozma return after visiting Glinda the Good. Dorothy says goodbye to her friends there and stands on an emerald in the palace courtyard before being transported away.

records.l: Australia, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Australia is where Uncle Henry is staying in a pleasant room in Sydney. Dorothy is transported there to nurse him and take care of him.

records.l: the magic picture, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: The magic picture hangs in Ozma's private room and constantly changes its scenes. It can show any part of the world or any living person when Ozma expresses a wish, allowing Dorothy to see the Kansas farm and Uncle Henry in Australia. Ozma is to look at Dorothy in it every Saturday and watch for a signal that Dorothy wants to return to Oz.

records.l: the magic belt, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: The magic belt can transport Dorothy to Uncle Henry when Ozma uses it, but Dorothy gives it to Ozma before leaving the Land of Oz. Ozma will use it to return Dorothy to the Land of Oz if Dorothy makes the agreed signal.

records.l: Dorothy's return to Uncle Henry, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Dorothy's return to Uncle Henry is arranged after she sees that he is ill and lonely in Australia. She gives the magic belt to Ozma, waves her handkerchief as the agreed signal, and is transported to Australia, where she promises to care for him.

records.l: Dorothy's farewell from Oz, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: Dorothy's friends in the Land of Oz gather to bid her sorrowful good-bye and wish her long life and happiness. She kisses Ozma, says she is sorry to leave her many friends, and hands Ozma the Nome King's magic belt before departing.

records.l: the magic belt's powers, Ozma of Oz, 21. Dorothy's Magic Belt
records.s: The magic belt has magical powers only while it is in a fairy country such as the Land of Oz or the Land of Ev. It can fulfill a wish to transport Dorothy to Australia, but it would be lost when she arrived there and could not bring her back. By remaining with Ozma in Oz, it can later be used to return Dorothy to the Land of Oz.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: L. Frank Baum explains that children have persuaded him to write another story about the Land of Oz. The current book follows Dorothy on another adventure and includes the Wizard, Princess Ozma, Jim the Cab-Horse, the Nine Tiny Piglets, and Eureka the Kitten. Baum says the children’s suggestions helped shape the book, and he considers it partly theirs. He also expresses gratitude for their letters, friendship, and support.

records.l: L. Frank Baum, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: L. Frank Baum says that the children have compelled him to continue writing tales of the Land of Oz. He explains that their suggestions helped shape the current book, and he expresses deep pride and gratitude for having pleased and befriended his young readers.

records.l: the children/readers, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: The children/readers demand more stories about Oz, especially stories including Dorothy and the Wizard. They send Baum thousands of suggestions and letters, and their requests influence the contents of the current book.

records.l: the Land of Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: The Land of Oz remains the setting and subject of the stories that the children want Baum to continue telling. The current book returns to this world and its characters.

records.l: Oz stories, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: The Oz stories continue because the children will not let Baum stop writing them. Dorothy has become a regular and beloved figure in the stories, and the current book also revisits the Wizard and other familiar characters.

records.l: the current book, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: The current book is described as a shared work belonging to Baum and the children because their suggestions helped shape it. It presents Dorothy in another strange adventure and introduces or includes the Wizard, Princess Ozma, Jim the Cab-Horse, the Nine Tiny Piglets, and Eureka the Kitten.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: Dorothy appears again as the heroine of the current book and is described as sweet, gentle, and innocent. Because she is in California while Toto is in Kansas, she begins this adventure with her kitten, Eureka, instead of her dog.

records.l: the Wizard, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, To My Readers
records.s: The Wizard returns in the current book because readers wanted to know what happened to him after he rose into the sky in a balloon. He remains the same jolly old humbug who had frankly acknowledged that he was a humbug.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Dorothy Gale arrives at Hugson's Siding from San Francisco with her kitten Eureka and is met by Zebediah, who takes her toward Hugson's Ranch in a buggy. The train was delayed because repeated earthquakes made the engineer fear the rails would spread apart. As Dorothy and Zebediah travel, a powerful earthquake opens cracks in the earth, frightening them and stopping Jim. A second crack opens beneath the horse, pulling Jim, the buggy, Dorothy, and Zebediah into a pit.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Dorothy arrives at Hugson's Siding carrying a suit-case, a covered bird-cage containing her kitten Eureka, and a parasol. Zebediah takes her toward Hugson's Ranch, but an earthquake opens a crack beneath the buggy and pulls her into a pit, where she briefly loses consciousness.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Zebediah waits five hours at Hugson's Siding to take Dorothy to Hugson's Ranch. He drives the buggy and is frightened when the earthquake opens cracks beneath them; he clings to the buggy seat as they fall into a pit.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Jim is a large, thin, bony horse with damaged harness. He carries Dorothy and Zebediah in the buggy, becomes tense and frightened during the earthquake, and falls into the pit when the earth cracks open beneath him.

records.l: Uncle Henry, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Uncle Henry is visiting Uncle Hugson at Hugson's Ranch. He and Dorothy are scheduled to start back for Kansas the next day.

records.l: the train from Frisco, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: The train from Frisco arrives at Hugson's Siding at about five o'clock in the morning instead of midnight. It travels slowly because earthquakes shake the earth and the engineer fears the rails may spread apart.

records.l: Hugson's Siding, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Hugson's Siding has a bare shed serving as a station-house, an old wooden bench, and no nearby houses or people visible at dawn. Dorothy arrives there and meets Zebediah near a horse and buggy.

records.l: Hugson's Ranch, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: Hugson's Ranch is where Uncle Henry is visiting Uncle Hugson and where Zebediah works for Uncle Hugson. Zebediah takes Dorothy there from Hugson's Siding.

records.l: the earthquake, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: The earthquake repeatedly shakes the ground during the train journey and later causes the buggy to sway and the earth to split open. It frightens Dorothy, Zebediah, and Jim and ultimately sends them into a pit.

records.l: the buggy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: The buggy is standing near trees at Hugson's Siding and has a shiny top and side curtains. Zebediah drives Dorothy in it until an earth crack opens beneath it and pulls it downward.

records.l: the great crack in the earth, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: An earth crack opens beside Dorothy and Zebediah during the earthquake and then closes again. Another great crack opens directly beneath Jim, causing the horse, buggy, and passengers to fall.

records.l: the pit, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 1. The Earthquake
records.s: The pit opens beneath Jim when the earth splits apart. It receives Jim, the buggy, Dorothy, and Zebediah as they fall into darkness.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim fall through a great crack in the earth with the buggy and land safely on the roof of a glass city. They discover six colored suns, talking animals, and air that supports people and animals as they walk through it. The expressionless people of the Glass City blame the newcomers for the Rain of Stones and send them to the House of the Sorcerer to prove their innocence.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Dorothy survives the fall into the inner world and realizes that she has begun another strange adventure. She discovers that Eureka can talk and that people and animals can walk on the air. The man with the star holds her and her companions responsible for the Rain of Stones, so she goes with him toward the House of the Sorcerer.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Zeb falls with Dorothy, Jim, and the buggy and remains frightened by the strange events. He cautiously learns to walk on the air and helps Dorothy and the animals reach the street. The man with the star questions him about the Rain of Stones.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Jim is frightened and struck by falling stones during the descent, but he lands safely on the roof. He unexpectedly begins speaking and complains about the danger, his hunger, and his former work drawing a public cab in Chicago. After hesitating, he walks off the roof and floats safely down to the glass pavement.

records.l: Eureka, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Eureka escapes from her overturned bird-cage and is revealed to be able to talk. She explains that the air supports her and walks through it without falling. She joins Dorothy and Zeb on their way to the street and complains that she wants milk.

records.l: The Glass City, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The Glass City lies in the inner world and has clear glass houses, buildings, roofs, streets, domes, and spires. It is illuminated by six colored suns and has suffered damage from the Rain of Stones. A glass palace with a central dome and four corner spires stands in an open square.

records.l: the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The people of the Glass City are beautifully formed, attractively dressed, and have handsome but expressionless faces. They have never seen a horse or a cat and gather to stare at Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka. They follow the man with the star in a procession.

records.l: the Prince of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The man with the star appears to be an authority among the people of the Glass City. He questions Zeb and Dorothy about the Rain of Stones, declares that they will be held responsible unless they prove their innocence, and leads them toward the House of the Sorcerer.

records.l: Gwig, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The Sorcerer is said to be able to discover the truth about whether Dorothy, Zeb, and their companions caused the Rain of Stones.

records.l: the House of the Sorcerer, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The House of the Sorcerer is the place where Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka are ordered to go so that the Sorcerer can determine the truth about the Rain of Stones.

records.l: the Rain of Stones, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The Rain of Stones damages the Glass City by breaking roofs and steeples and cracking or chipping buildings. The man with the star accuses Dorothy, Zeb, and their companions of causing it.

records.l: the earthquake, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The earthquake opens a large crack in the earth through which Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and the buggy fall. Zeb and Dorothy explain that the earthquake, rather than them, caused the stones to come loose.

records.l: the six colored suns, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The six colored suns hang far below the falling travelers, with one large white sun surrounded by rose, violet, yellow, blue, and orange suns. Their rays illuminate the inner world and cast changing rainbow colors over the travelers and the Glass City. The suns produce bright light but no heat.

records.l: the buggy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: The buggy slows the fall by catching the air like a parachute or umbrella. It lands on a broad glass roof, and Zeb accidentally kicks over Dorothy's bird-cage while getting out. Dorothy later climbs back into it with Eureka, and Jim pulls it through the Glass City.

records.l: walking on air, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 2. The Glass City
records.s: Walking on air is possible in the country beneath the earth because the air supports the weight of people and animals. Eureka demonstrates it first, then Dorothy and Zeb walk through the air, and Jim floats down from the roof to the street.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: Dorothy and Zeb arrive with their horse and buggy in the Land of the Mangaboos, where the Prince questions them about the Rain of Stones. The thorn-covered Sorcerer Gwig claims the newcomers caused the damage, but the man with the star challenges his predictions. A balloon brings Oz, the Great and Terrible, who explains that an earthquake opened a crack through which he descended from the surface of the earth. Oz defeats Gwig in a contest of magic, but Gwig tries to stop Oz's breath, prompting Oz to cut him in two; the Prince then explains that the Mangaboos are vegetable beings.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: Dorothy arrives in the Land of the Mangaboos with Zeb, the horse, and the buggy. She denies causing the Rain of Stones and tells the Sorcerer that an earthquake caused it. She recognizes Oz when he descends in the balloon and watches him defeat Gwig.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: Zeb drives the horse and buggy through the doorway of the glass palace and enters the hall with Dorothy. He follows Dorothy outside to watch the descending balloon and later into the hall to see Oz meet Gwig. He has lost his hat during the flight through the air.

records.l: Gwig, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: Gwig is the thorn-covered Sorcerer of the Mangaboos. He insists that his sorcery is always correct and argues that Oz's arrival does not disprove his prediction because only one person descended from the sky. After losing the magical contest, he attempts to stop Oz's breath, but Oz cuts him in two; Gwig is declared dead and is to be planted so other Sorcerers can grow from his bush.

records.l: the Prince of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The Prince questions Dorothy, Zeb, and Oz about their arrival and challenges Gwig's inaccurate predictions. He offers to make Oz the Chief Wizard if Oz proves superior to Gwig, while threatening to stop Oz from living if he fails. After Oz defeats Gwig, the Prince explains that the Mangaboos are vegetable beings and invites Oz to the public gardens.

records.l: the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The Mangaboos gather around the horse and buggy, watch the descending balloon, and observe the contest between Oz and Gwig. They are vegetable beings rather than flesh-and-blood people, and their dead Sorcerers can be planted so that other Sorcerers grow from their bushes.

records.l: the Land of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The Land of the Mangaboos contains a glass palace with a lofty domed hall and glass pavement. It is located beneath the earth and is inhabited by vegetable Mangaboos, including a Sorcerer who can be grown from a bush.

records.l: the balloon, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The balloon slowly descends from high in the air into the great square of the Land of the Mangaboos. It carries Oz in a basket and comes to rest on the glass pavement.

records.l: the Rain of Stones, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The Rain of Stones damages and cracks the Mangaboos' houses and injures some of their people. Gwig claims that a second fall was actually a Rain of People-and-Horse-and-Buggy, with some stones accompanying it. Dorothy states that the damage was caused by the earthquake rather than by her and Zeb.

records.l: the earthquake, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: The earthquake causes a large crack in the earth. Oz falls into the crack after descending in his balloon, and the earth closes over him, carrying him down to the Land of the Mangaboos.

records.l: the Wizard and Sorcerer contest, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 3. The Arrival Of The Wizard
records.s: Oz and Gwig compete to prove whose powers are greater. Gwig creates the sound of unseen bells, while Oz produces a piglet from his hat, multiplies it into nine piglets, and makes them disappear. The Prince judges Oz superior, but Gwig attacks Oz with a spell that stops his breath, leading Oz to cut Gwig in two.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Prince leads Dorothy, Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and Eureka through the glass city’s gardens in the Land of the Mangaboos. The Mangaboos plant the two halves of the Sorcerer in a planting-ground, expecting him to sprout into a bush producing more sorcerers. The travelers learn that Mangaboos grow on plants, become alive when picked, and usually live about five years without eating. The Prince reveals that the Royal Princess will succeed him, but he plans to destroy the strangers rather than let them remain in his country.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: Dorothy travels with Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and Eureka through the gardens of the glass city. She learns how Mangaboos grow on bushes and objects that the Royal Princess is already ripe, while the Prince plans to have the strangers destroyed.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: Zeb travels through the gardens with Dorothy and the others and asks questions about Mangaboo growth and eating. He becomes hungry and notices strawberries and melons that might provide food.

records.l: the Wizard, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Wizard rides in the buggy, explains the changing colors of the grass to Jim, and questions the Prince about the Royal Princess. The Prince considers keeping him until a new Sorcerer is ready because he may be useful.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: Jim rides in the procession with the kitten on his back and eats the rainbow-colored grass. He refuses to leave the field because he is busy eating.

records.l: Eureka, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: Eureka rides on Jim and later follows the Wizard, Dorothy, and Zeb through the folk gardens. She complains that she is starving and says she would not eat milk-weeds.

records.l: the Prince of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Prince leads the travelers through the gardens and explains the Mangaboos' vegetable way of growing and living. He says the Royal Princess will succeed him but delays picking her because he does not want to give up power, and he plans to destroy the strangers.

records.l: Gwig, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The two halves of the Sorcerer are carried to the planting-ground, placed in a hole, covered with earth, and watered. The Prince expects him to sprout into a large bush that will produce several sorcerers.

records.l: the Royal Princess, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Royal Princess grows on the Royal Bush of the Mangaboos and is described as beautifully formed and dressed. She is destined to succeed the Prince, although he claims she is not quite ripe and need not yet be picked.

records.l: the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Mangaboos live without eating and grow on bushes in the folk gardens. They become fully alive when they are ripe and picked, usually live about five years if kept cool and moist, and must be planted again if they sprout.

records.l: the Land of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Land of the Mangaboos contains the glass city, broad garden plains, brooks, glass bridges, planting-grounds, and folk gardens. Its people move mainly on the ground even though they can walk through the air.

records.l: The Glass City, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The glass city has fine streets, towers, and roofs that grow rather than being built. A Rain of Stones can break or crack these structures, which eventually grow together again.

records.l: the planting-ground, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The planting-ground is a freshly plowed field where the Mangaboos bury and water the two halves of the Sorcerer. The Prince expects the buried Sorcerer to sprout soon.

records.l: the folk gardens, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The folk gardens contain rows of broad-leaved plants bearing Mangaboos at every stage from bud and blossom to ripe adult. The growing Mangaboos remain motionless until they are picked.

records.l: the Royal Bush of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Royal Bush of the Mangaboos is a large, beautiful bush enclosed by a smaller hedge. All Mangaboo Princes and Rulers have grown on it from time immemorial, including the Royal Princess.

records.l: the vegetable kingdom, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The vegetable kingdom is represented by the Mangaboos' way of growing on plants, becoming alive when picked, and returning to the ground if they sprout. The Prince regards this vegetable existence as unpleasant because mature rulers must give way to new ones.

records.l: the Rain of Stones, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Rain of Stones breaks the towers and cracks the roofs of the glass city. The damaged glass eventually grows together again, but the Mangaboos must wait for this repair.

records.l: the Sorcerer's planting, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Sorcerer's planting occurs when the two halves of the Sorcerer are buried and watered in the planting-ground. The Prince expects the planting to produce a large bush bearing several sorcerers.

records.l: the Mangaboo life cycle, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Mangaboo life cycle begins with buds and blossoms on bushes, followed by babies, partly grown people, and ripe adults. A Mangaboo becomes alive when picked, can live for about five years under good conditions, and must be planted if it begins to sprout.

records.l: the Royal succession, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Royal succession passes from the Prince to the Royal Princess when she becomes fully ripe and is picked. The Prince delays this change because he does not want to abandon the sovereignty of the Mangaboos.

records.l: the Prince's proposed destruction of the strangers, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 4. The Vegetable Kingdom
records.s: The Prince says the strangers must be destroyed because they do not belong inside the earth and cannot be planted as Mangaboos. He considers keeping the Wizard but intends to destroy Dorothy, Zeb, Jim, and Eureka, then orders them to follow him to meet their doom.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Dorothy and the Wizard pick the Royal Princess of Mangaboo, who receives the Star of Royalty and becomes the ruler after accusing the Prince of selfishly delaying her picking. Dorothy, Zeb, the Wizard, Eureka, and Jim explore the vegetable gardens, where they eat fruits and discover that the Wizard's tiny piglets can talk. The Wizard catches a fish for the hungry Eureka, then the group returns to the city and takes shelter in the House of the Sorcerer. They find that the people of Mangaboo walk in the air and that the country has no apparent night or need for stairs.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Dorothy helps the Wizard pick the Royal Princess before the man with the star returns. She explores the vegetable gardens, eats fruit, protects the tiny piglets from Eureka, and returns with the others to stay in the House of the Sorcerer.

records.l: the Wizard, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Wizard suggests picking the Royal Princess and helps Dorothy lift her from the bush. He admits that he is a humbug and that the piglet trick was sleight of hand, catches a fish for Eureka, and decides to take possession of the House of the Sorcerer.

records.l: the Royal Princess, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Royal Princess is picked by Dorothy and the Wizard and immediately comes to life. She accuses the Prince of leaving her unpicked to preserve his unlawful rule, receives the Star of Royalty, and is escorted to the glass city as the new ruler.

records.l: the Prince of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Prince returns with his people and trembles when he sees that the Royal Princess has been picked. He gives her the Star of Royalty, after which he walks away alone; his later fate is unknown.

records.l: people of Mangaboo, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The people of Mangaboo bow to the Royal Princess after she receives the Star of Royalty. They form a procession to escort her to the glass city, walking on the ground while she walks in the air above them.

records.l: the Land of Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Mangaboo has vegetable people, vegetable gardens, brooks, and a glass city. Its inhabitants can walk in the air, and it appears to have no night because the colored suns do not move.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Zeb explores the vegetable gardens with Dorothy and the Wizard and eats their fruits. He learns that the Wizard's piglets are real and can talk, then returns to the House of the Sorcerer and sleeps on a glass bench.

records.l: Eureka, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Eureka complains about the lack of milk or meat and questions whether the Wizard is truly a wizard. She eats the fish he catches, refuses the crackers, and sleeps beside Jim after the group returns to the city.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Jim continues eating the pink grass while the others explore the gardens. After returning to the city, he is unharnessed, rolls over, and goes to sleep with Eureka beside him.

records.l: the Nine Tiny Piglets, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Wizard reveals that the tiny piglets have been in his inside pocket and explains that their apparent separation and joining were a trick. They can talk, fear Eureka, eat Dorothy's crackers, and are returned to the Wizard's pocket to sleep.

records.l: The Glass City, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The people of Mangaboo escort the new Royal Princess toward the glass city for her palace ceremonies. The travelers later return there and enter the domed hall containing the House of the Sorcerer.

records.l: the House of the Sorcerer, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Wizard decides to use the House of the Sorcerer as a place for the travelers to stay. Inside, they find a bare domed hall, high doorways reachable by walking through the air, furnished glass rooms, and no beds.

records.l: Star of Royalty, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: The Prince removes the Star of Royalty from his brow and places it on the Royal Princess's brow. The people then bow to her as their ruler.

records.l: the Land of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 5. Dorothy Picks the Princess
records.s: Dorothy identifies the land as a fairy country because it has vegetable people and allows Eureka and Jim to talk. The Wizard suggests that its weak gravitational attraction may explain why they can walk in the air.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Wizard, Zeb, and Dorothy learn that the Princess intends to destroy them for trespassing in the Land of the Mangaboos, while sending Jim the cab-horse and Eureka to the Black Pit. The Wizard uses lanterns and kerosene oil to create a fire test that scorches the Mangaboo advisors and convinces the Princess to spare the three humans. For several days they remain undisturbed in the House of the Sorcerer, until the Mangaboos drive Jim, Eureka, and the nine tiny piglets toward the mountain. Jim and Eureka fight back, but the numerous Mangaboos eventually force them to continue toward the Black Pit.

records.l: the Wizard, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Wizard retrieves his satchel, two lanterns, and a can of kerosene oil from his balloon's basket-car. He performs tricks for the Princess, then uses the lanterns and kerosene oil to create a fire test that scorches her advisors and saves himself, Zeb, and Dorothy from destruction.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: Zeb fetches the Wizard's satchel, two lanterns, and a can of kerosene oil from the balloon's basket-car. He is spared from the Mangaboo destruction decree along with the Wizard and Dorothy.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: Dorothy says she dislikes the cold, flabby Mangaboos and wishes there were another place to go. She helps the Wizard present his magic and is spared from being thrown into the Garden of the Clinging Vines.

records.l: the Royal Princess, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Princess declares that the Wizard, Zeb, and Dorothy must be destroyed and that their animals must be sent to the Black Pit. After seeing the Wizard's fire test scorch her advisors, she recognizes him as greater than any Sorcerer the Mangaboos have known and spares the three humans.

records.l: the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Mangaboos are described as cold, flabby, heartless vegetable people. They are impressed by the Wizard's lanterns but are frightened and scorched by the fire test; later, they use thorn branches to drive Jim, Eureka, and the piglets toward the mountain, though many are smashed or disabled when the animals resist.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: Jim protests being sent to the Black Pit and tries to protect the nine tiny piglets while the Mangaboos drive the animals away. He kicks and scatters many Mangaboos, but eventually becomes too tired to resist and is driven toward the mountain.

records.l: Eureka, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: Eureka plays with the nine tiny piglets and later tries to protect them from the Mangaboos by snarling, biting, scratching, and attacking the enemies' faces. She helps Jim fight back but is eventually forced toward the mountain.

records.l: the Land of the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Land of the Mangaboos has six colored suns and no night, so periods between sleep are used to describe days. It contains the city, gardens, the House of the Sorcerer, the Garden of the Clinging Vines, and the mountain with the Black Pit.

records.l: the House of the Sorcerer, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Wizard, Zeb, and Dorothy are permitted to occupy the House of the Sorcerer peacefully for several days after the Princess spares them. The nine tiny piglets later wander from the Wizard's room into the dome's lower part, where they play with Eureka beside Jim.

records.l: the Garden of the Clinging Vines, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Garden of the Clinging Vines contains tough green vines that writhe together like great snakes. The vines crush everything they touch, and the Wizard, Zeb, and Dorothy are threatened with being thrown into the garden before the fire test saves them.

records.l: the Black Pit, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Black Pit is in the mountain and is designated as the place where the Mangaboos intend to send Jim and Eureka, along with the other animals. The Mangaboos begin driving the animals toward it after the Princess spares the three humans.

records.l: the lanterns, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The two lanterns are brought from the balloon's basket-car and placed on Dorothy's and Zeb's heads. When the Wizard lights them, they appear to the Mangaboos as two unfamiliar suns.

records.l: kerosene oil, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The kerosene oil is retrieved from beneath the balloon-car's seat. The Wizard pours it onto the glass floor and lights it, producing a broad pool of flame for the fire test.

records.l: the Nine Tiny Piglets, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Wizard produces the nine tiny piglets as one of his magic tricks and later lets them exercise in his room. They wander into the dome, play with Eureka beside Jim, and are driven toward the mountain by the Mangaboos.

records.l: the thorn branches, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Mangaboos carry branches covered with sharp thorns and thrust them toward Jim, Eureka, and the piglets. The thorns force the animals out of the House of the Sorcerer and down the street toward the mountain.

records.l: the Mangaboo destruction decree, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The decree calls for the Wizard, Zeb, and Dorothy to be thrown into the Garden of the Clinging Vines and for their animals to be driven to the Black Pit. After the fire test, the Princess withdraws the part concerning the three humans but maintains the order against the animals.

records.l: the fire test, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 6. The Mangaboos Prove Dangerous
records.s: The Wizard claims that the fire will reveal which advisors gave the Princess bad advice. The advisors are ordered into the flames and are badly scorched and withered, convincing the Princess that the Wizard is a powerful Sorcerer.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: The Mangaboos imprison Jim and the piglets in the Black Pit by blocking its entrance with glass rocks. Eureka escapes and alerts Dorothy and the Wizard, who return with Zeb to attempt a rescue but become trapped inside the mountain with the prisoners. They use lanterns to guide Jim and the buggy through a steep tunnel, eventually emerging into a bright and charming new country.

records.l: Jim, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: Jim is driven into the Black Pit with the piglets and later becomes trapped inside when the Mangaboos rebuild the barrier. He is harnessed to the buggy and cautiously pulls it through the dark, steep tunnel, stopping at times to rest before finally emerging into the new country.

records.l: Eureka, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: Eureka escapes through the remaining opening of the Black Pit while the Mangaboos pursue her. She flies higher and faster than they can, reaches the House of the Sorcerer, and awakens Dorothy to tell her what happened.

records.l: the Nine Tiny Piglets, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: The piglets are driven into the Black Pit with Jim and are trapped behind the glass-rock barrier. The Wizard later picks up all nine piglets and places them carefully in his inside pocket.

records.l: the Mangaboos, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: The Mangaboos imprison Jim and the piglets by piling glass rocks at the Black Pit's entrance. They pursue Eureka, follow Dorothy, the Wizard, and Zeb to the mountain, and attack them with sharp thorns while rebuilding the barrier.

records.l: the Wizard, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: The Wizard is awakened by Dorothy and joins the effort to rescue Jim and the piglets. He pulls down the glass rocks but becomes trapped inside the cavern, then agrees to follow the tunnel and travels with Dorothy and Zeb while carrying a lantern.

records.l: Dorothy, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: Dorothy is awakened by Eureka and helps prepare to rescue Jim and the piglets. She enters the Black Pit to avoid the Mangaboos' thorns, accepts the possibility of dying there, and travels through the mountain holding a lantern.

records.l: Zeb, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
records.s: Zeb joins Dorothy and the Wizard in going to the rescue and carries the lanterns and oil can. After being wounded by the Mangaboos' thorns, he drives the buggy through the tunnel while the others hold lanterns.

records.l: the Black Pit, Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz, 7. Into the Black Pit and Out Again
