At the end, the Wonderful Wizard of Oz restores her from stone; she recognizes Dr. Pipt and runs into his outstretched arms.

records.l: Unc Nunkie's house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_located_in the surrounding woods [in the middle of] The house is a lonesome, round house where Ojo and Unc Nunkie have lived for as long as Ojo can remember. It has a little garden behind it and thick woods all around.

records.l: the mountain containing the radium mines, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A rocky mountain at Oz’s edge, home to Hoppers and Horners and the Horners’ radium mine; a winding path climbs its steep rocks and enters a hidden inner passage.

records.l: the bread tree, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_the_only_thing_that_grows_in the yard and garden The bread tree is the only thing growing in Ojo and Unc Nunkie's yard. It has only two more loaves, and those loaves are not yet ripe.

records.l: bread, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: grows_on the bread tree Bread is the only food in the cupboard, and Ojo eats the last ripe loaf while setting aside Unc Nunkie's share. The remaining loaves on the bread tree are not ripe yet.

records.l: food, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Food is plentiful and available to everyone in the Land of Oz, though Ojo's house has only bread, prompting a possible search elsewhere.

records.l: poverty, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: describes Ojo and Unc Nunkie [as they understand their situation] Ojo believes that he and Unc Nunkie are poor because they have only a house and bread, while other people in the Land of Oz have access to plenty. Unc Nunkie denies that they are poor but does not explain why.

records.l: leaving home to seek food, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_necessary_for Ojo and Unc Nunkie [because their local food supply is running out] Ojo proposes that he and Unc Nunkie leave their house and visit the Munchkin Country because their food is running out. Unc Nunkie questions where they would go and says that Ojo is too little, so no departure occurs in this unit.

records.l: Mombi the Witch, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Mombi, an old Witch, stole baby Ozma and transformed her into a boy, received Powder of Life from Dr. Pipt to give life to Jack Pumpkinhead, then lost it when Ozma escaped.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead is a remarkable living pumpkin-headed man with a wooden body, a carved pumpkin head, and pumpkin seeds for brains. Created through Ozma’s childhood transformation and brought to life when Mombi used the Powder of Life, he fled with Ozma and became her companion. He lives near Emerald City in his preferred pumpkin house, where he grows replacement heads for when one spoils. He welcomes travelers with food and directs them toward a naturally dark well in the Quadling Country.

records.l: Emerald City, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Emerald City is a wonderful, strange, and exceptionally splendid Fairy City at the center of Oz, ruled by Ozma, the kind girl Ruler. It is surrounded by green country and a high, thick, polished green marble wall set with emeralds, with four gates barred in gold. At its center are Ozma’s royal gardens, and its royal palace contains the Throne Room; it also has the only prison in Oz. The city’s inhabitants are polite and respectful toward the unfortunate, though prisoners are so rare that many gather to watch a trial. Travelers repeatedly follow the yellow brick road toward Emerald City, seeking a six-leaved clover from its surrounding fields and later Ozma’s help. Ojo and his companions reach its gate at sunset, but Ojo is arrested for unlawful magic before entering. He enters as a prisoner, is tried, forgiven, and housed for the night. Later the party returns to ask Ozma how to save Unc Nunkie, receives an immediate welcome, and Ozma gives Ojo and Unc Nunkie a house just outside the city walls.

records.l: the Magician's house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A large, round, blue house in a mountain clearing in the Country of the Gillikins, surrounded by forest; Dr. Pipt and Margolotte live there amid an abundant garden and a workshop with bubbling kettles.

records.l: Powder of Life, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Powder of Life is a wonderful magic substance, a fine white powder made by Dr. Pipt from four boiling kettles. He alone knows its recipe, and it is said to be worth a kingdom. Stored in a small gold bottle with a pepper-box top in his locked cabinet, it brings to life anything upon which it is sprinkled. A previous supply given to Mombi awakened Jack Pumpkinhead; it also brought the Sawhorse to life, and Ozma's possession of it helped her escape Mombi and become ruler of Oz. Dr. Pipt prepares a batch for the Patchwork Girl, sprinkles it on her head and arms, and awakens her. Soon afterward, the remaining powder accidentally falls on a phonograph, bringing it to life and exhausting the supply. Dr. Pipt says another lot would take six years, but later Ozma says he will make no more because his kettles and recipe book have been destroyed.

records.l: the creation of the Powder of Life, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The creation of the Powder of Life is Dr. Pipt's nearly completed process for Margolotte's purpose. Over nearly six years, he stirs a compound in four kettles with both feet and hands. When the contents boil away, he and Margolotte collect, mix, cool, and lock the remaining grains in a gold bottle.

records.l: Ojo and Unc Nunkie's journey to Dr. Pipt's house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo and Unc Nunkie journey at dawn from Unc Nunkie's house, through Munchkin Country and over a mountain into the Country of the Gillikins, eating their remaining bread before reaching Dr. Pipt's house.

records.l: the Patchwork Girl's creation and awakening, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Patchwork Girl is a servant intended for Dame Margolotte. Assembled from scraps and fitted with brains, she lies lifeless on a bench after being brought into Dr. Pipt's workshop. Dr. Pipt prepares music and sprinkles Powder of Life over her; the records do not state the result.

records.l: Glass Cat, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Glass Cat is a living, transparent cat made entirely of brittle glass, a curious creation of Dr. Pipt. Her pink brains are visible through her body, along with her finely polished ruby heart and glass paws; she sees poorly by day and fears hard knocks. Made alive by an early batch of the Powder of Life, she enters Dr. Pipt's home, hides during an accident, mocks others, and joins Ojo and the Patchwork Girl. She is rescued after a monstrous plant traps her in a leaf, then boasts of her visible brains and beauty, comparing herself favorably to Scraps. She follows the Woozy through an optical-illusion barrier and refuses to remain at a farmhouse as children's plaything, preferring Ojo's adventures because children might smash her. At the end, her pink brains are replaced by transparent brains, changing her from conceited and disagreeable to modest and well behaved. Ozma keeps her as a palace pet.

records.l: the Liquid of Petrifaction, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Liquid of Petrifaction is a liquid that turns whatever it touches into solid marble. Unlawfully kept on Dr. Pipt's shelf, it is accidentally knocked down and immediately petrifies Margolotte and Unc Nunkie. Their transformation prompts Ojo to search for materials to reverse its effect.

records.l: the Patchwork Girl's brains, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Patchwork Girl's brains are stored and sewn inside her head before animation. Margolotte chooses Obedience, Amiability, Truth, and Cleverness; Ojo secretly adds powders granting many other qualities.

records.l: magic, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Magic is an interesting but dangerous practice in the Land of Oz. Wicked Witches and Magicians used it for evil, causing trouble, so Princess Ozma forbids most of it. She permits Glinda the Good and the Wizard of Oz because she trusts them to benefit the people, while Dr. Pipt has limited permission for his own purposes. Dr. Pipt uses magic to create and give life to the Glass Cat and hopes to bring the Patchwork Girl to life, though he says it cannot make creatures grow like Nature's more wondrous magic.

records.l: the Blue Forest, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A solitary, forgotten thick forest on the mountainside along the path into Munchkin Country, gloomy to Ojo but lovely to Scraps, is crossed and left near sundown.

records.l: Victor Columbia Edison, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Victor Columbia Edison, or Vic, is a phonograph made living and mobile by Powder of Life. It names itself when asked by Patchwork Girl. Later, its varnished wooden case is damaged by thrown objects; it plays “My Lulu,” angers the Shaggy Man, and runs away to avoid being taken apart.

records.l: magic charm, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The magic charm is a scarce, hard-to-get object that Ojo seeks to make to undo the Liquid of Petrifaction’s marble transformation and restore Unc Nunkie and Margolotte to life. Dr. Pipt says the compound can restore them instantly if its five ingredients are obtained: a six-leaved clover, the left wing of a yellow butterfly, water from a dark well, three hairs from the tip of a Woozy’s tail, and one drop of oil from a live man’s body. The charm also contains a flesh-wound charm. Ozma permits Dr. Pipt to make it, on condition that his magic powers are removed afterward. By the end, the Crooked Magician has sent for the ingredients and Ojo has obtained four, but cannot obtain the yellow butterfly’s left wing.

records.l: the six-leaved clover, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The six-leaved clover is a very scarce tiny green plant, a clover with six spreading leaves, found in the green country and fields around the Emerald City. Though neglected and trampled under foot, it is protected by the Law of Oz: picking it is forbidden without Ozma’s consent. It is one of five required things for the restoring compound, needed to restore the petrified victims and to restore Unc Nunkie to life. Ojo searches for it, discovers one beside the road of yellow bricks, plucks it, and hides it in his basket. Suspected of breaking the law, he gives it to Scraps, who hides it in a golden vase so it cannot prove his offense. Before the court it grows from the vase, and Ozma forgives Ojo and permits him to keep it.

records.l: yellow butterfly, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A yellow butterfly is sought in the yellow Winkie Country west of the Emerald City. Its left wing is required for a restoring compound and is one of five things required by the Crooked Magician; Ojo is directed there to find it.

records.l: Unc Nunkie's transformation into a marble statue, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a petrification by magic The marble transformation occurs when the Liquid of Petrifaction strikes Margolotte and Unc Nunkie. They become motionless, stiff, cold, and hard like marble statues.

records.l: the accident involving Margolotte and Unc Nunkie, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A magical accident petrifies Unc Nunkie and Margolotte. It begins when the Patchwork Girl knocks the Powder of Life from Dr. Pipt's hand, startling them; Unc Nunkie's movement upsets the Liquid of Petrifaction, which falls on both and turns them into marble statues. The accident is later linked to Dr. Pipt's unlawful keeping of the liquid. Ojo undertakes a quest for ingredients, including three tail hairs, for a magic charm to restore them to life, accompanied or aided by Scraps, the Woozy, and the Glass Cat. Ozma later has the statues brought to the palace.

records.l: Ojo's search for the magical ingredients, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo's search for magical ingredients is a rescue mission to save Unc Nunkie and Margolotte by obtaining Dr. Pipt's restoring compound ingredients. Traveling with the Patchwork Girl and Bungle, he gathers three Woozy-tail hairs, a six-leaved clover, water from a dark well, and oil from a live man's body. The journey leads from the Emerald City toward the Quadling Country, but it ends unresolved when the Tin Woodman refuses to allow harm to a yellow butterfly for its left wing.

records.l: the journey through the mountains, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The journey through the mountains is an adventure undertaken by Ojo, Scraps, and the Glass Cat toward the Emerald City and the Country of the Winkies. After leaving the advisers, they cross lonely routes, rivers, and dark forests, spend a night at a roadside house, seek directions from the Foolish Owl and Wise Donkey, leave the Tottenhot, climb rough rocks, and pass Mister Yoop’s cave through a narrow passage.

records.l: the path, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The path, initially the travelers' only forest route, broadens after they leave the woodchopper, becomes hard for Ojo and Scraps to see at night, and leads downhill to Munchkin Country.

records.l: the woodchopper, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The woodchopper is a Munchkin man with bushy blue whiskers who lives alone in a small leaf-covered house at the forest’s edge. He advises Scraps about illegal magic, explains dangers ahead, tells of Dorothy and the Tin Woodman, and offers lodging.

records.l: the roadside house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: contains the mysterious lodging [with three beds] The roadside house is dark and silent, with three prepared beds. Its unseen occupant allows Ojo, Scraps, and the Glass Cat to enter only if they make no noise and go directly to bed. Scraps is thrown out when she refuses to keep quiet, and the door is locked behind her.

records.l: the yellow butterfly's left wing, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The yellow butterfly's left wing is an ingredient Ojo seeks for a magic charm in the Country of the Winkies, but the Tin Woodman forbids taking it because doing so would torture and kill the butterfly, preventing Ojo from saving Unc Nunkie.

records.l: the unseen voice, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: An unseen voice in the roadside house admits travelers for the night, commands strangers to be quiet and sleep, and remains invisible even to the Glass Cat.

records.l: classical music, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Classical music is highly puzzling music people are supposed to like; a phonograph plays it, but Ojo and the Glass Cat dislike it, prompting laughter and its stoppage.

records.l: rag-time, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Rag-time is music presented as the opposite of classical; a phonograph plays its jerky, confusing sounds until Patchwork Girl silences it with her apron.

records.l: music, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Music is intended to amuse and soothe, but the phonograph’s music is dismissed by Ojo, the Glass Cat, and Patchwork Girl as a nuisance.

records.l: phonograph's escape, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_from Dr. Pipt [after a quarrel and threat of destruction] The phonograph escapes from Dr. Pipt's house while the Magician is stirring his four kettles. It runs after Ojo and his companions throughout the night because it wants pleasant company and freedom to talk and play tunes.

records.l: journey to the Emerald City, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A journey toward the Emerald City begins when Ojo, the Glass Cat, and Patchwork Girl leave the Munchkin house and take the widest, best path. Later, the party travels sadly from the Winkie Country to the Emerald City without important adventure.

records.l: the Wise Donkey, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Wise Donkey is a wise public adviser, born in the Land of Mo and obliged to remain in the Land of Oz after it was shut off. Dressed in a blue apron and cap, he partners with the Foolish Owl. He welcomes travelers, offers advice, and directs them along the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City.

records.l: the Foolish Owl, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Foolish Owl, an unusually foolish public adviser, sits on a shelf in a blue sunbonnet and composes rhyming nonsense poems about Scraps, Ojo's charm search, and the travelers' uncertain journey; the Wise Donkey admires her unusual foolishness.

records.l: the road of yellow bricks, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The road of yellow bricks is a broad, winding road paved with smooth, bright yellow bricks, the only yellow thing in the blue country. It follows an easy route over hills and dales and leads west, directly toward the Emerald City through the Munchkin Country. Ojo and his companions seek it, find it, and travel on it. On one section, the landscape and road slide backward while the bricks remain still, forcing them to walk backward before continuing forward.

records.l: the Foolish Owl and Wise Donkey's house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a house [roadside residence and shop] The house stands beside the roadside and bears a sign identifying the Foolish Owl and Wise Donkey as public advisers. Inside, the Wise Donkey dusts the furniture while the Foolish Owl sits on a shelf.

records.l: advice, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Wise Donkey says advice is free unless it is followed. He advises the travelers to follow their current path to the yellow brick road and to move on so they will reach the Emerald City sooner.

records.l: Munchkin farmers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: keep honey-bees [to make honey] The Munchkin farmers kept honey-bees to make honey and tried to destroy the Woozy because it ate their bees. When they could not hurt it, they drove it into a forest and built a fence around it.

records.l: forest (Woozy's forest), The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: contains Woozy's cave [near the center of the forest] The Woozy's forest is enclosed by a high fence and contains tall, closely set trees and a rocky cave where the Woozy lives. Ojo, Scraps, and the Glass Cat enter it and later leave with the Woozy through an opening burned in the fence.

records.l: fence around Woozy's forest, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: contains the Woozy [to keep it imprisoned] The Munchkin farmers built the high fence around the Woozy's forest to imprison the creature because it ate their honey-bees. The fence is too tall for the Woozy to climb or jump over, but the Woozy's eye fire burns through one of its boards and creates an opening.

records.l: three hairs from a Woozy's tail, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Woozy's three tail hairs, its only hairs and ornaments, are needed for the Crooked Magician's charm to restore Unc Nunkie and Margolotte; Ojo cannot remove them and plans to bring the Woozy to the magician.

records.l: Unc Nunkie and Margolotte's restoration to life, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Unc Nunkie and Margolotte's restoration to life is sought by Ojo, who gathers materials and fears the effort will fail without the Woozy's three tail hairs. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, using magic taught by Glinda the Good, ultimately frees both from the Liquid of Petrifaction and returns them to life.

records.l: Woozy's imprisonment, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_caused_by Munchkin farmers [because the Woozy ate their honey-bees] The Munchkin farmers imprisoned the Woozy in a fenced forest after failing to destroy it. The Woozy says it has lived there for years without food because there are no honey-bees and the leaves, mosses, and vines do not suit its taste.

records.l: Woozy's escape, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_enabled_by Woozy's eye fire [which burns through the fence] The Woozy escapes its fenced forest after its eyes flash fire and burn through a fence board. It leaves with Ojo, Scraps, and the Glass Cat after promising not to eat honey-bees while traveling with them.

records.l: honey-bees, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Woozy enjoys eating honey-bees and had eaten the bees kept by the Munchkin farmers for honey. Ojo makes the Woozy promise not to eat any honey-bees while it travels with their group.

records.l: Krizzle-Kroo, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: angers the Woozy [terribly] "Krizzle-Kroo" is a phrase that makes the Woozy terribly angry, although the Woozy does not know what it means. Ojo, Scraps, and the Glass Cat shout it together, causing the Woozy's eyes to flash fire and burn the fence.

records.l: Woozy's eye fire, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Woozy's eyes flash real fire when it becomes very angry. The eye fire burns the wooden fence after the group shouts "Krizzle-Kroo!," allowing the Woozy to escape.

records.l: monstrous plants, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Monstrous plants grow in rows beside the yellow brick road, twice as high as the Patchwork Girl’s head, with swaying broad leaves that change color and bend down to fold around, capture, and imprison travelers.

records.l: capture by the monstrous plants, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Monstrous plants capture Ojo, Scraps, Glass Cat, and Woozy by enclosing them in leaves, holding them in darkness until the Shaggy Man intervenes and enables their escape.

records.l: Shaggy Man's rescue, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Shaggy Man rescues Ojo, then frees Scraps and the Glass Cat by cutting down their enclosing leaves, and frees the Woozy by slicing off the leaf’s stem.

records.l: whistling that charms the plants, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Shaggy Man’s whistling charms monstrous plants, making their leaves straighten and remain still; he habitually uses it when passing them.

records.l: drop of oil from a live man's body, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A drop of oil from a live man's body is one of five ingredients required by the Crooked Magician's magic charm. Though the Shaggy Man considers it improbable to find, Ojo keeps searching and captures a drop from the Tin Woodman's knee joint in a crystal vial, fulfilling the requirement.

records.l: Winkie Country, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Winkie Country is Oz’s yellow country, ruled by the Tin Woodman. As travelers follow the river toward it, they hope to continue Ojo’s search for a yellow butterfly. The beautiful land has yellow buttercups, dandelions, and splendid lilies, the Tin Woodman’s castle, abundant tin, and skilled Winkie tinsmiths. It is the only place in Oz with yellow butterflies, which the Tin Woodman can protect through his authority.

records.l: Sawhorse, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Sawhorse is a rudely made wooden horse, a living animal brought to life by the Powder of Life. Ozma’s favorite steed since then, it has gold-plated legs and a jeweled cloth-of-gold saddle. Swift, untiring, and kind to friends, it kicks the Woozy, carries the Scarecrow rapidly toward Jinjur’s home, and returns him to the Emerald City in one day.

records.l: royal palace, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_home_to Dorothy Gale [as Ozma's companion] The royal palace is where Dorothy Gale lives and where she receives the Shaggy Man, Scraps, the Woozy, and the Glass Cat. Scraps hides the six-leaved clover in a golden vase there.

records.l: Law against picking six-leaved clovers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: protects Land of Oz [by suppressing wicked sorcery] The law against picking six-leaved clovers was created because Witches and Magicians used them in potions and charms for harmful magic. Ozma explains its purpose to Ojo and forgives his violation of it.

records.l: Square Meal Tablets, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: contain a complete meal [each tablet] Square Meal Tablets contain the equivalent of several foods, including soup, fried fish, mutton pot-pie, lobster salad, charlotte russe, and lemon jelly. The Scarecrow uses six tablets to persuade the lazy Quadling man to help build the raft and gives him two additional tablets afterward.

records.l: five things required by the Crooked Magician, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: restore marble figures to life [when made into a charm] The five things required by the Crooked Magician are three hairs from a Woozy's tail, a six-leaved clover, the left wing of a yellow butterfly, a gill of water from a dark well, and a drop of oil from a live man's body. Ojo and his companions continue toward the Emerald City while searching for them.

records.l: Chiss, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Chiss is an overgrown giant porcupine in Oz, regarded as an evil spirit because sharp arrowlike quills cover its body and it throws them in any direction. Dangerous to road travelers and said to resist ordinary killing, it attacks the travelers until the Shaggy Man imprisons it and Ojo and Scraps remove all its quills.

records.l: the road's backward-sliding trick, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: slides_backward the road of yellow bricks [carrying walkers backward] The road's backward-sliding trick carries anyone walking upon that section back toward where they started. The Shaggy Man knows that walking backward lets travelers gain ground and pass safely beyond the troublesome section.

records.l: Chiss's quill attack, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a shower of quills [fired toward the travelers] Chiss's quill attack sends a shower of quills toward the travelers when they come too near. Scraps shields Ojo and is pierced by many quills, the Shaggy Man is wounded in the leg, and the Glass Cat and the Woozy remain unharmed.

records.l: the Law of Oz, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Law of Oz is a body of rules meant to protect the people and guard their welfare, with willful violation risking arrest. It includes a prohibition on picking six-leaved clovers. Ojo the Unlucky is accused of breaking the Law by picking one, despite Scraps's objection, after being warned by the Shaggy Man. He is arrested and is to be tried and required to make amends if guilty. Ozma says even seemingly foolish laws should not be disobeyed.

records.l: the Soldier with the Green Whiskers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Soldier with the Green Whiskers is a tall soldier with a long green beard who faithfully serves Princess Ozma as her Body-Guard, the Royal Army of Oz, and the Emerald City Police Force. On Ozma’s orders, he identifies and arrests Ojo for allegedly wilfully breaking a Law of Oz, possibly by picking a six-leaved clover. He puts gold, jewel-set handcuffs on Ojo, leads him into the Emerald City, places him in prison clothing, delivers him to Tollydiggle with a receipt, reports his duty complete, and later escorts him from prison to the royal palace.

records.l: South Country of the Quadlings, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: South Country of the Quadlings is a wild, secluded southern country with mountains, rocks, caverns, forests, and secluded peoples. Travelers enter seeking a dark well, then pass through a peaceful, lonely area of red houses, fences, and wildflowers, reaching a river and a Quadling man's home.

records.l: Ojo's arrest, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo's arrest is his detention at the Emerald City gate for allegedly breaking the Law of Oz by picking a six-leaved clover. Acting under Ozma of Oz's order, the Soldier with the Green Whiskers handcuffs Ojo, promises him a fair trial and an opportunity to prove innocence, and takes him to the Emerald City prison. His imprisonment is comfortable and nonviolent. The arrest leads to Ojo's trial and judgment before Ozma of Oz, with freedom possible if innocence is proved.

records.l: Ojo's trial, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo's trial concerns his unlawful picking of a six-leaved clover; before Ozma, he confesses, regrets it, explains his motive, and is released after she deems him sufficiently punished.

records.l: Tollydiggle, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Tollydiggle, the Emerald City prison’s official jailer with no prior experience, kindly receives Ojo, removes his restraints, feeds and houses him comfortably, reads to him, and explains humane treatment.

records.l: the prison (Emerald City), The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a prison [the only one in the Land of Oz] The prison in the Emerald City is described as the only prison in the Land of Oz. It is intended to help prisoners become strong and brave, rather than to punish them harshly.

records.l: the prison house (Emerald City), The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A pretty, well-kept house beside the great city wall, guarded by Tollydiggle, holds Ojo; though unlocked and comfortable, it keeps him through trust and kind treatment.

records.l: the prisoner's robe (Ojo's robe), The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo's white prisoner robe covers him from head to foot, with eye holes; it marks him as a prisoner and makes him appear quaint while led through the Emerald City.

records.l: kindness toward prisoners, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Kindness toward prisoners is a principle of Ozma's prison system, treating unfortunate prisoners kindly to prevent bitterness and make them strong and brave.

records.l: Toto, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Toto is a little, black, shaggy-coated, non-fairy dog, Dorothy Gale's pet, usually well behaved, and able to understand her without speaking. He travels beside Dorothy, sleeps near her, drives off Tottenhots, and watches for trouble. Frightened in a canyon, he returns to Dorothy, who carries him during escape. He later barks at and attacks Hip Hopper, causing him to fall. On a raft he cannot swim well enough to help reach shore, then is welcomed by the Tin Woodman at his castle.

records.l: Ozma's transformation and accession, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ozma escapes Mombi with Jack Pumpkinhead and the Powder of Life; Glinda recognizes and restores her, enabling her accession as Oz's rightful ruler.

records.l: Ozma's childhood transformation, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: transforms Ozma of Oz [from a baby girl into a boy] When Ozma was a baby girl, Mombi stole her and transformed her into a boy. Ozma did not know who she was and was forced to serve Mombi until she grew old enough to run away.

records.l: Ojo's traveling party, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ojo's traveling party includes Ojo, Dorothy, the Scarecrow, and Scraps, who join to help Ojo. Though planned with them, the Glass Cat and Woozy remain in the Emerald City by choice and Ozma's decision.

records.l: the adventurers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The adventurers include Dorothy and Ojo, leave Jack Pumpkinhead’s home, travel south toward the Quadling Country for two days, meet the Tottenhots, and sleep in their circular houses until daylight.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead's pumpkin house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A house made from an immense pumpkin shell, with door, windows, stove, steps, and furniture, stands in a pumpkin-field and shelters travelers for one night.

records.l: the Tottenhots' circular houses, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a circular pot-like dwellings [with closable tops] The Tottenhots' circular houses are black, pot-like dwellings scattered beneath palm trees. Their tops open and close when the Tottenhots enter or leave, and one house contains soft cushions where the travelers sleep.

records.l: the Tottenhots' attack, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Tottenhots attack the adventurers by roughly tossing the Scarecrow and Patchwork Girl and trying to toss Ojo, until Dorothy and Toto stop them and they retreat into circular houses.

records.l: journey to obtain the dark-well water, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The journey to obtain dark-well water is a search for a gill of magic water. The Scarecrow seeks Jack Pumpkinhead’s advice, Dorothy brings a gold flask, and Ojo with companions travels through a great cave and slippery mine tunnel, obtains the water, and returns safely to Horner city.

records.l: the gold flask, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A gold flask holding a pint is given to Ojo, who fills it with water from the dark well, seals it, and pockets it.

records.l: water from the dark well, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Water from the dark well, kept in Dorothy's gold flask, must never see daylight for a magic charm. The travelers need only a gill; Ojo collects it, carries it safely in his jacket pocket, and returns with the group to the Horner city.

records.l: the mountain rift, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The mountain rift is a great rock split with high walls and a narrow, twisting passage, easier than sharp uneven rocks, eventually leading to Mister Yoop’s cave.

records.l: Mister Yoop's cave, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Mister Yoop’s cave is a cavern hollowed into a mountain-rift wall, holding Mister Yoop captive; marked as a dangerous giant’s dwelling, it warns strangers away.

records.l: the iron bars, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_fixed_in the rock walls [tops and bottoms firmly fixed in solid rock] A row of thick iron bars blocks the front of Mister Yoop’s cave, with their tops and bottoms fixed firmly in the rock. Yoop shakes them and reaches his long arms through them, but cannot quite touch the travelers.

records.l: Mister Yoop's captivity, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: confines Mister Yoop [inside his cave behind iron bars] Mister Yoop is held captive behind the iron bars of his cave. His captivity prevents him from catching the travelers, and they are relieved that he is still caged.

records.l: the escape past Mister Yoop, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a escape [past the Giant's cave] The Scarecrow proposes that he be seized first so Dorothy, Ojo, Scraps, and Toto can run beyond Yoop’s reach. The plan succeeds, although Yoop throws the Scarecrow and Scraps at the escaping group.

records.l: the Hoppers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Hoppers are a people and one of two nations on the mountain, living in their own country and marble city. Each has one leg, moves by hopping, and balances easily; their arms are longer than the Horners’ in combat. They fear the Horners’ sharp forehead horns. After Diksey’s joke angers them, they prepare for and declare war on the Horners. Dorothy persuades them to act as though they appreciate the joke, and they return laughing, tell Diksey it is good for a Horner, and ask him not to repeat it.

records.l: Country of the Hoppers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_on mountain The Country of the Hoppers is located on the mountain and contains a great city where Hip Hopper's people live. A path through the mountain leads toward it.

records.l: Hopper Country, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Hopper Country, separated from Horner Country by a gated fence, lies on one side of the mountain and occupies half of the great cave. While its Hoppers war with the Horners, travelers are directed there; it contains Hopper village, about fifty artistic marble houses.

records.l: Horner Country, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Horner Country lies beyond the mountain from Hopper Country, called by Hip Hopper a black spot. A path from rocky lowlands may lead to a dark well at its entrance. It occupies half the great cave, with dull gray rock, square houses, crowded streets of Horners, and a city larger than Hopper village.

records.l: the mountain path, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: leads_to Country of the Hoppers [ascending the mountain] The rock path winds among the mountain's rocks and provides a smoother, easier route upward. It ends at a large rock that swings backward to reveal the tunnel entrance.

records.l: tunnel, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A mountain tunnel behind a movable rock glows rosy, with a high arched roof and one winding passage without side passages.

records.l: fence between the Hopper Country and the Horner Country, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The marble dividing fence separates Hopper Country from Horner Country and the Hoppers from the Horners before peace. Very high, with a locked central gate marked “WAR IS DECLARED,” it later holds the Scarecrow atop a picket until Diksey, Ojo, and Dorothy rescue him.

records.l: the proposed war between Horners and Hoppers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A dangerous war between the Hoppers and Horners is proposed after the Hoppers misunderstand a Horner joke criticizing their one leg as an insult. Though Hip Hopper expects victory, both sides fear fighting, especially the Horners' sharp horns. Dorothy persuades the Hoppers to laugh at Diksey's joke and ask him not to repeat it, preventing the war.

records.l: the Hoppers and the Horners' cave, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A vast, softly lit marble cave, nearly reaching the mountain’s top, contains the Hopper village and the Horner city at its farther end. Its colored walls surround round dark holes; beyond the city, one hole leads to the mine.

records.l: the Chief of the Horners, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Jak, the Chief of the Horners, is a respected Horner who lives in the Chief Horner's dwelling, wears a jeweled star above his horn, and has nineteen daughters. During a dispute with the Hoppers, he insists the Horners are safe behind a locked gate, explains the joke involved, and waits for Diksey. After the joke is explained, he ends the war and restores peace.

records.l: Diksey, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Diksey is a good-natured Horner man and expert guide in the Horners' radium mine. He jokes with the Hoppers and helps Ojo and Dorothy rescue the Scarecrow by bringing a ladder. He tells Ojo of the mine's dark well, then leads Ojo and companions safely through the cave and tunnel to it and back.

records.l: Diksey's under-standing joke, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Diksey Horner's joke compares the Hoppers' one leg with the Horners' two, saying the Hoppers have less “under-standing” or “standundering,” while denying it means less understanding. Jak praises it, but the Hoppers misunderstand it and pretend to laugh to prevent war, causing tension between the groups.

records.l: the misunderstanding between the Hoppers and Horners, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: caused the war between the Hoppers and the Horners The Hoppers interpreted Diksey’s joke about their single legs as an insult, while the Horners treated it as harmless humor. Scraps says that the Hoppers’ understanding of the Horners’ intended understanding caused the misunderstanding.

records.l: the Horners' radium mine, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Horners' radium mine, Diksey Horner's workplace beneath their mountain, is entered through a dark slanting hole in the great cave. Its smooth tunnel descends to a vast cave containing a very dark well, which Diksey leads the group to investigate.

records.l: the Champion's throwing attempt, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The Champion balances the very light Scarecrow and throws him toward the top of the marble fence. The Scarecrow does not clear it and instead lands on a picket.

records.l: the Scarecrow's entrapment on the fence, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A sharp picket catches the Scarecrow in the middle of his back and holds him on top of the fence. His hands wave over Horner Country and his feet kick over Hopper Country, while his companions try to find a way to rescue him.

records.l: Scraps's arrival in Horner Country, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_a arrival The Champion throws Scraps toward the fence, but she sails over it and lands in Horner Country. Her stuffed body knocks over two men and a woman, and after the crowd returns she identifies herself to Jak and begins discussing the conflict.

records.l: the Horner city, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Horner city, at the farther end of the great cave, has unpaved streets and Chief Horner's dwelling; after obtaining water, the group returns safely.

records.l: radium, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Radium is a translucent, frosted-silver metal found as tiny grains among loose rocks in a great cave. It gives off soft light, decorates Horner homes and furniture, is abundant, and is medicine preventing sickness for people living near it.

records.l: peace between Horners and Hoppers, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Peace is restored after the Hoppers accept Diksey's explanation and joke; Diksey promises restraint, the gate opens, and the Horners, Hoppers, and travelers reunite.

records.l: the Quadling house, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Small, round, bright-red Quadling home beside the river; travelers stay overnight with the family after the raft is completed.

records.l: raft, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: The raft is a log craft made of logs bound with the Quadling woman's clothesline and reinforced by wooden strips. Completed by evening, it begins carrying the travelers the next morning down the Trick River. Reversing currents impede it, but a fish, a pole, and holds on a tree and rock help it survive a steep wave and reach the Winkie Country safely.

records.l: raft construction, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Raft construction is performed by the Quadling man with travelers' help: he chops logs, Ojo fastens them, others carry materials, and the raft is completed by evening.

records.l: the travelers' river voyage, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_planned next morning [on the river] The travelers have not yet begun their river voyage by the end of the unit. After spending the night at the Quadling house, they plan to set out on the completed raft the next morning.

records.l: fish, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: A great fish, a strong swimmer, is caught by Ojo, pulls his raft against the current, weakens and drags it shoreward, then is freed when Ojo cuts the line.

records.l: Tin Woodman's tin castle, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Tin Woodman's tin castle stands in southern Winkie Country, built entirely of brightly polished tin from ground to tallest turret. Its glittering turrets, walls, gates, grounds, and furnishings are tin; its grounds hold statues of Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, the Wizard, the Shaggy Man, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Ozma.

records.l: yellow butterflies, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Yellow butterflies are among the prettiest created things, very sensitive to pain, and found only in the Winkie Country; the Tin Woodman protects them from harm because tearing a wing causes torture and death.

records.l: marble statues of Unc Nunkie and Margolotte, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: are_brought_to Emerald City [to Ozma's palace] Ozma has the marble statues of Unc Nunkie and Margolotte brought to the Emerald City palace. She says they are standing in the next room and leads the party toward them.

records.l: luck, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: is_associated_with number thirteen [according to the Tin Woodman] The Tin Woodman tells Ojo that Friday, the number thirteen, being left-handed, and having a wart are not signs of bad luck. He urges Ojo to call himself Ojo the Lucky and says that people who fear bad luck may fail to notice good fortune.

records.l: the statue of Unc Nunkie, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: depicts Unc Nunkie [before restoration] The statue of Unc Nunkie stands in the room until the Wonderful Wizard of Oz makes a magic pass and speaks a magic word before it. Unc Nunkie immediately comes to life.

records.l: the statue of Margolotte, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: depicts Margolotte [before restoration] The statue of Margolotte is present in the room until the Wonderful Wizard of Oz makes a magic pass and speaks a magic word before it. Margolotte then moves, comes to life, and runs to Dr. Pipt.

records.l: the nice house outside the Emerald City, The Patchwork Girl of Oz
records.s: Ozma gives the nice house outside the Emerald City to Ojo and Unc Nunkie as their future home. They will live there under her protection.

Sky Island is L. Frank Baum’s fairyland adventure about Trot, Cap’n Bill, and Button-Bright, continuing Trot and Cap’n Bill’s earlier adventures. Button-Bright arrives beside the Pacific Ocean from Philadelphia after traveling by his family’s Magic Umbrella, which flies to any named destination but cannot be redirected or stopped. Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap’n Bill test it, then fly toward Sky Island and become stranded there when the umbrella is seized. On the Blue side of the island, the travelers are captured by Quitey Righty Boolooroo, ruler of the Blueskins. Trot is made servant to the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Cap’n Bill is assigned as Royal Nectar Mixer, and Button-Bright as Royal Bootblue. With help from Ghip-Ghisizzle, who believes the Boolooroo has illegally prolonged his rule by hiding the Royal Record Book, they seek the umbrella. Button-Bright retrieves the Record Book but not the umbrella, and the three escape through the Great Fog Bank into the sunny Pink Country. The Pinkies treat them more comfortably but debate whether outsiders must be thrown from Sky Island. Rosalie the Witch confirms their story yet supports expelling them. At the island’s edge, Polychrome, the Rainbow’s Daughter, arrives and interprets the laws to make Trot the rightful Queen of the Pink Country. Trot, Cap’n Bill, and Button-Bright resolve to recover the umbrella, while Rosalie proposes an army to confront the Boolooroo. Cap’n Bill commands the Pinkies’ march through the fog against the Blues. During the conflict he is captured, and Trot uses Rosalie’s invisibility ring to enter the Blue City. She disrupts the planned patching punishment, helps Ghip-Ghisizzle escape, and ultimately saves Cap’n Bill. The Boolooroo is defeated by the very punishment intended for Cap’n Bill, aided by Trot and a billygoat. Trot takes control of both countries, ends the war, makes Ghip-Ghisizzle the new Boolooroo, banishes the former Boolooroo and the Princesses, and destroys the Great Knife. After finding the umbrella on a rubbish heap, the party returns through the Fog Bank, where the umbrella briefly becomes an elephant. Trot reforms Pink Country rule, appoints Rosalie Queen, and then flies home with Cap’n Bill and Button-Bright. Button-Bright safely reaches Philadelphia, and his father locks the Magic Umbrella away.

Sky Island is an English eBook by L. Frank Baum, the second story in the adventures of Trot and Cap'n Bill. Available through Project Gutenberg as eBook 4356, it was released August 1, 2003, and updated December 27, 2020. Baum introduces it as his present story, centered on Button-Bright and his Magic Umbrella, and invites readers' responses.

publishes Sky Island [as an eBook] Project Gutenberg distributes Sky Island for use at no cost and with almost no restrictions in the United States and most other parts of the world. It provides the Project Gutenberg License and advises users outside the United States to check the laws of their own countries.

L. Frank Baum is identified as Sky Island’s author and writes its introductory talk, linking it with The Sea Fairies and earlier characters while inviting children to write to him at Ozcot in Hollywood, California.

Sky Island is a book, following Trot and Cap'n Bill's visit to The Sea Fairies, and is dedicated to Mary Louise Brewster. Its story begins when Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright are carried by the Magic Umbrella toward an island suspended in the sky. The island is surrounded by sky rather than water; its edges are guarded in places by bushes or fences because anyone who steps beyond them tumbles away. It has trees, ponds, houses, and three countries: the Blue Country, the Fog Country, and the Pink Country. The travelers first reach the blue part, where gardens, buildings, vegetation, paths, and water are blue. The Blue Country is ruled by the Boolooroo, whose palace adjoins their landing place. Though he calls the government a republic, he directs elections and punishes disobedience. He and his court call Sky Island the Center of the Universe. The island is a fairy country whose people do not visibly age and cannot die before six hundred years. The Great Fog Bank separates the equal-sized Blue and Pink Countries. Trot and her companions, initially seeking to escape, become involved in the conflicts of both lands. The narrative proceeds through the Pink Country, its queens and tribes, the arrival of Polychrome, war between Pinks and Blues, Cap'n Bill's capture, Trot's invisible adventure, and the conquest of the Blues. After victory, Trot becomes Queen of Sky Island except the Fog Bank, while the Blue and Pink Countries retain separate rulers. Before leaving, she regulates the Pinkies by leaving Rosalie to rule the Pink Country. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright then say goodbye to their friends and fly upward from Sky Island in the Magic Umbrella to return home.

Trot is a little girl from Earth, the daughter of Mrs. Griffith and Cap'n Griffith, who lives in a frame cottage and is Cap'n Bill's close companion and friend. She meets Button-Bright near the Pacific Ocean, believes his account of the Magic Umbrella, and eagerly joins him and Cap'n Bill on an air-ride intended for a picnic. The umbrella instead carries them to Sky Island. There Trot repeatedly resists unjust treatment. In the Blue Country, the Boolooroo imprisons the travelers, and the Six Snubnosed Princesses seize Trot as their maid and slave. Though shaken and slapped, she refuses inwardly to accept slavery, wins the protection of the princesses' pets, reunites with her companions, and escapes through the Fog Bank. In the Pink Country, she and her friends face possible expulsion, but Polychrome identifies Trot as the lightest-skinned person present, making her Queen under the country's succession law. Trot accepts the Pinkies' support while keeping return to Earth and recovery of the Magic Umbrella as central goals. When Cap'n Bill is captured, she uses Rosalie's ring to enter the Blue City invisibly, frees Tiggle, searches the palace, and repeatedly risks herself to rescue Cap'n Bill. She uses a rope to save him from the Great Knife, helps overthrow the Boolooroo, and ends patching and the Great Knife's threat. After the victory, Trot rules the Pink and Blue Countries as Queen of Sky Island, appointing Cap'n Bill and later Ghip-Ghisizzle to govern the Blues, protecting the Pinkies, and banishing the former Boolooroo and the princesses. She delays departure until she has arranged affairs responsibly. Back in the Pink Country, she makes a law granting the Queen equal conditions, appoints Rosalie Queen, orders a palace and statues, and then returns home with Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright in the Magic Umbrella.

Cap'n Bill is an old, retired, one-legged sailor from Earth who lives with Trot and her mother. Friendly, cheerful, honest, knowledgeable, and meek, he is Trot's close chum and devoted protector, caring for her exceptionally well. Though skeptical of Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella, he builds seats for it, joins Trot and Button-Bright on its flight, and becomes both frightened and resourceful when they reach Sky Island. Captured by the Boolooroo of the Blues, Cap'n Bill is made a palace slave and Royal Nectar Mixer. He explores the Blue City, escapes with Trot and Button-Bright, and endures the Fog Bank before the group reaches the Pink Country. There he favors the Pinkies over the Blues, supports Trot after she becomes Queen, and urges a campaign to recover the Magic Umbrella and confront the Boolooroo. As Commander in Chief of Trot's Army of Conquest, he leads the Pinkies through the Fog Bank and against the Blue City. During the fighting he directs the Pinkies but is captured after falling when his wooden leg enters a hole. The Boolooroo plans to patch him to Tiggle, but Trot repeatedly saves him from the Great Knife and frees him. He then helps bind the Boolooroo, supports Trot's rule, and becomes her General and Royal Manager of the Blue Country. After the victory, Cap'n Bill helps find the discarded umbrella, seats, and lunch basket. He travels back through the Fog Bank, prepares the equipment, pilots the return journey with Trot and Button-Bright, and regards getting back to Earth as the best part of the adventure.

Magic Umbrella is an old, large, strong but disreputable-looking family relic, handed down through Button-Bright's family. Its thick brown cloth has faded to dull drab, and its wooden handle is carved as an elephant's head with red-stone eyes and tiny ivory tusks. It has ropes, two wooden seats, and a wicker basket or lunch-basket attached, allowing it to carry as many as three passengers. Found by Button-Bright in his attic, it is magical through fairy enchantment rather than power of its own. When Button-Bright or another rightful family member holds it open and speaks a destination, it flies rapidly and safely there, obeying the destination but neither stopping nor changing course beforehand. It cannot grant wishes for ice-cream soda or money, and it refuses to return early when Button-Bright changes his mind. It carries Button-Bright, Trot, and Cap'n Bill on journeys over land, ocean, clouds, and an arched path through the heavens, including travel to Sky Island and the Blue Country. On Sky Island, the Boolooroo repeatedly takes the umbrella to prevent the travelers' escape. Though it belongs to Button-Bright's family and will not work for the Boolooroo, he has it carried to the Royal Treasury, tests it, and throws it beneath a cabinet. It disappears from the Treasure Chamber and remains missing despite extensive searches. Eventually Tiggle recalls throwing it from beneath the cabinet onto a rubbish heap, where Cap'n Bill finds it and Button-Bright recovers it. When rejected by the Frog King, it transforms into a huge elephant, leads the travelers through the Fog Bank, and becomes an umbrella again at the Pink Country's edge. Finally, commanded to take the travelers to Trot's house, it carries Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright safely from Sky Island to Earth. Button-Bright later flies to Philadelphia with it, after which his father locks it in a strong chest in the attic.

Blue City is a blue city in Blue Country, inhabited by Blueskins and extending a half mile in every direction from its center. Broad blue-marble streets run among blue buildings, castles, shops, spires, and turrets. It contains the Royal Palace, the Boolooroo's palace, and the Room of the Great Knife; its city wall surrounds it, connects with the palace-garden wall, and has a principal gate. Outer walls protect it against the country beyond. At first, Button-Bright and Cap'n Bill tour the city with Ghip-Ghisizzle. Later, fugitives find it deserted, but an alarm brings lights, shouts, angry citizens, guards, and pursuers. As the Pinkies approach, Blueskins rush inside, the Boolooroo closes and locks the gates, and Cap'n Bill's army halts outside the wall. The Blueskins capture Cap'n Bill within the city, while Trot secretly climbs over the wall. At night the city is quiet and blue-lit but joins the pursuit of Ghip-Ghisizzle; finally it wakes as Cap'n Bill tries to escape and soldiers pursue him along the wall, while Ghip-Ghisizzle plans an attack on it.

The Pink Country, also called the Sunset Country, is a pink country forming one half of Sky Island, separated from the Blue Country by the Fog Bank. About two square miles in area, it borders the fog and has a dangerous outer edge dropping into the gulf below. It is a land of sunrises and sunsets, with pink grass, trees, paths, sky, clouds, sunlight, marble public spaces, and round buildings without corners or angles; its neat, garden-like landscape ranges from faint rose to deep pink. It contains the City and Tourmaline's palace, and is inhabited by several hundred Pinkies, including the eastern Sunrise Tribe and western Sunset Tribe. Its prosperity, color uniformity, and laws matter greatly. Under Tourmaline, the Pinkies initially have no established place for outsiders and consider expelling Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill after they emerge from the Fog Bank. Polychrome interprets the laws to protect the travelers and make Trot Queen. Tourmaline is relieved, Trot is received as the new Queen, and the customs require a poor plain dress and little pleasure. After Trot and her companions return from the Blue Country, the country welcomes them; Trot leaves Rosalie the Witch to rule under the new law.

The Boolooroo, Quitey Righty, is the sky-blue king and elected monarch of Sky Island, also called the Blue Country and the country of the Blueskins. He has a round body and long neck, blue skin, eyes, hair, and clothing, and wears a star-shaped jewel with blue stones. Though elected for a three-hundred-year term, he claims to have reigned not quite two hundred years; the Royal Book of Records shows that he has completed, and exceeded, his lawful term. He keeps that book and the Royal Treasury locked up, with the key in his pocket, apparently to conceal his fraud and retain power. What matters most is his cruel, deceitful rule. He steals Button-Bright's Magic Umbrella, enslaves Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright, and assigns them work in Sky Island. He threatens punishment by “patching,” a punishment he invented, and uses the Great Knife against prisoners. He is feared, hated, and friendless; he hates everyone, treats the strangers cruelly, and is afraid of the Pinkies. He is father of the Six Snubnosed Princesses and married to the Queen, but even his household brings him anger and demands. As the travelers seek escape and the Book of Records threatens his position, he suspects Ghip-Ghisizzle, orders him bound and scheduled for patching, and tries to hold his rule during the Pinkies' invasion. He imprisons Cap'n Bill and repeatedly orders him patched, eventually proposing to join him to a billygoat. When he tries to operate the Great Knife, the goat knocks him down, and Trot and Cap'n Bill bind him beneath it. Trot takes control, keeps him locked in the Room of the Great Knife, and removes him from rule because he has ruled beyond his lawful term. He loses the palace and treasure and must leave with the Six Snubnosed Princesses, saying he will reform and become a model private citizen.

The Blueskins are blue, long-legged people of the Blue City and soldiers of the Boolooroo, serving under the Captain of the Guards. Their only arms are cords until they use bluewood lances. They attack the Pinkies, retreat from sharp sticks, are defeated by enchanted weapons, and capture Cap'n Bill. After returning cautiously, they obey Trot, imprison the princesses, and prepare the Blue City for the Pinkies' arrival.

records.l: the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island
records.s: The Six Snubnosed Princesses are six sister princesses of Sky Island, daughters of the Boolooroo and Queen, and royal daughters of the Revered and Resplendent Royal Ruler of the Blues. They are gorgeously dressed Blueskin girls with blue gowns and hair, huge towers of hair, long thin necks, and snub noses regarded as high breeding. Haughty, cruel, and vindictive, they habitually mistreat their favored animal and bird pets. They claim Trot as their maid, slave, and living pincushion, fasten six ribbons to her, and drag her into the Blue Palace, where they order her to serve them and seek harsh punishment for her after their pets rebel. They also quarrel over marrying Ghip-Ghisizzle to become Queen, free him from the Room of the Great Knife, and confine him until he chooses one of them. When the billygoat attacks during Cap'n Bill's patching, they are thrown into the corridor in terror. Later they reject Trot's rule and each demands the kingdom, but Trot has them locked under guard, making them meek and mild. After Trot's victory, they and their parents are expelled from the palace and escorted, screaming and hysterical, to Ghip-Ghisizzle's small cabin.

Ghip-Ghisizzle is a Blueskin royal officer, Majordomo, and Master of Ceremonies in the Blue Country, marked by a blue-gold chain and expected to become the Boolooroo. He is friendly and protective toward Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the other strangers, guiding them through the Blue City, explaining its customs, giving them rooms, and trying to shield them from hostile servants, soldiers, and the Boolooroo's plan to send them through the Arch of Phinis. He sympathizes with the prisoners because he disapproves of their treatment. His central concern is the succession. Though the current Boolooroo dislikes him and conceals the length of his reign, Ghip-Ghisizzle believes the Royal Record Book can establish whether he is the lawful ruler. After the Book disappears, he denies taking it and suspects Button-Bright. The Boolooroo has him bound and schedules him to be patched with Tiggle. The Six Snubnosed Princesses rescue him only to confine him and demand that he marry one of them; he refuses. He escapes over the City Wall, reaches the Pinkies' camp, and is captured by Captain Coralie. With the Royal Record Book, Ghip-Ghisizzle learns that the Boolooroo has ruled beyond the lawful three hundred years and that he has been the rightful ruler since Thursday. He seeks the former Boolooroo's resignation and agrees to help Button-Bright and the Pinkies recover the Magic Umbrella if they help him. Trot appoints him Boolooroo, and he becomes ruler of the Blue Country. He opposes patching, agrees to destroy the Great Knife and care for the billygoat, offers his little cabin to the former royal family, refuses to marry the former Princesses because he judges them wicked, and is ordered by Trot to treat the people of the Blue City nicely while she is away.

Button-Bright is a boy from Philadelphia, an Earth person whose formal name is Saladin Paracelsus de Lambertine Evagne von Smith. He is a descendant and member of the family that rightfully owns the old Magic Umbrella, a precious family relic with an elephant-head handle. After finding it in an attic, he discovers that it can carry him through the air and flies from Philadelphia across several places to the Pacific Ocean, arriving by parachute-like descent and meeting Trot and Cap'n Bill. Though he says he dislikes most girls and boys, he considers Trot one of the good ones and becomes her companion. The umbrella matters most to Button-Bright: it enables the journey, is repeatedly lost or sought, and is his means of returning home. He directs it toward Sky Island, but its literal obedience brings the travelers into danger. In the Blue Country, the Boolooroo takes the umbrella, enslaves Button-Bright, and makes him Royal Bootblue, responsible for blueing and shining royal footwear. Button-Bright plans an escape, steals the Treasure Chamber key, enters the chamber despite the Blue Wolf, fails to find the umbrella, and escapes with the Royal Record Book concealed in his blouse. With Trot, Cap'n Bill, and later the parrot, he crosses the Fog Bank into the Pink Country. He tells their story, fears their uncertain fate, wants to return to Earth, and recognizes Polychrome as an old friend when she helps save them. During the conflict with the Boolooroo, he leads the Pinkies, supports Ghip-Ghisizzle if he will rule, and makes return of the Magic Umbrella a condition of his help. The Royal Record Book establishes that the Boolooroo has completed his lawful reign. After the victory, Button-Bright searches for and recovers the umbrella, carries it through its brief transformation involving its elephant head, and finally travels with Trot and Cap'n Bill back to Earth. He stays at Trot's house, flies home to Philadelphia, and reports that he arrived safely.

The Blue Wolf is a monstrous, ravenous animal in the Blue City, terrible and fearful in aspect, with a lion-sized head, powerful shoulders and front legs, flashing blue eyes, and needle-sharp foot-long teeth. Crouching near the Treasure Chamber entrance, it guards the Royal Treasure Chamber. It attacks Button-Bright, who jams a sofa pillow in its jaws; the wolf cannot free its teeth and struggles to remove it with its claws.

Fog Bank is a thick, heavy, blue-grey fog bank across the center of the island, between the Blue Country and the Pink Country. It is an impassable-seeming barrier around the Blue Country: blinding, wet, clinging, sticky, and unhealthy for humans to remain in. Its dampness soaks clothes and hair, and those who enter are said to lose their six hundred allowed years and become liable to die at any time. Yet its pebbled ground can be seen, and it is the Paradise of Frogs, home to common frogs and giant frogs. It has no parsnips. It first separates the Blue Country from the Pink Country and from the travelers' approach. Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, Trot, and the blue parrot plunge into it to escape the Blueskins, who will not follow. A common frog guides them through its moist gray mist; near the Pink Country it turns soft rose, and they eventually emerge soaked, chilled, and with wrinkled, discolored clothing. Later, with a big frog, they escape through it again. Though a law sends Blueskins who break through it back with sharp sticks, it does not apply to the strangers. The Pinkies later cross it in about a dozen jumps with giant frogs and enter the Blue Country. Ghip-Ghisizzle fears Button-Bright may be lost in it. The fog remains the only part of Sky Island outside Trot's kingdom. It is crossed again with frogs and under the transformed elephant's guidance; its pink glow continues to signal the Pink Country. Trot and her companions plan to dive into it when leaving for the Land of Sunrise and Sunset.

Tourmaline is the young, beautiful, light-pink Queen of the Pinkies and sole ruler of the Pink Country. About seventeen, slender and rosy-complexioned, she wears a plain coarse pink robe and a rose-gold brow band bearing a luminous pink jewel. Though her word is law and she holds absolute authority, including the power to enforce laws and decree death when punishment is merited, she is modest, plain, and poor by principle. Living in a plain stone palace, she darns her own stockings and believes a ruler should be a public servant, not rich or falsely admired. As queen, Tourmaline consults the Great Book of Laws when strangers arrive, convenes the twelve Counselors, and seeks a decision on whether the travelers should remain as guests or be thrown over the island’s edge. When the Council divides evenly, she will not cast the deciding vote because she finds it impolite to oppose Counselors, instead asking Rosalie the Witch to decide. She orders the strangers cast away because they do not harmonize with the Pink Country’s color scheme, pressing for immediate execution even in rain. Later, she accepts Polychrome’s reading of the protection law and yields her circlet when Trot is identified as the rightful Queen. After losing the throne, Tourmaline appears in fine robes but declines restoration, saying queenship brought want and misery and that she prefers freedom. Trot orders a pink marble statue of her placed in the Court of the Statues after her death.

Poverty Queen is Trot’s regulation of the Queen of the Pinkies: she receives the same food, dresses, good times, housing, and spending money as the people, cannot take more, and faces being pushed off the edge if she does.

The Sunrise Tribe occupies the eastern half of the Pink Country, claims importance because the sun greets it first, lives at peace with the Sunset Tribe, and has six members on Tourmaline’s Council questioning strangers’ fit.

The Sunset Tribe occupies the western half of the Pink Country, claims importance because the sun reaches it after leaving the Sunrise Tribe, gathers nightly to watch sunset, and has six Council members including its leader, Coralie.

Rosalie the Witch is a famous, wise, honest, rosy-pink witch, somewhat taller than most Pinkies, with a slender staff tipped by a lustrous pink jewel. Though not very obliging and prone to headaches from witchcraft, she has useful but limited powers: only one magic charm every three days. She has no power over frogs, keeps Ghip-Ghisizzle prisoner in her tent, and is friends with giant frogs. Summoned as the wise and honest deciding voter, she uses a vision to confirm the Earth people's account, votes to throw them from the island, and expects fairies to protect them through the Magic Umbrella. She advises the Army of Conquest's size, secures the frogs' help across the Fog Bank, sees events in the Blue City, enchants the Pinkies' sticks, and helps the rescue effort with a rope ladder and the invisibility ring she lends Trot. After victory, she urges the group to return before conflict between Pinkies and Blueskins. She refuses queenship under an old law that would make its ruler poor and miserable, but after Trot changes it, accepts appointment as Queen of the Pinkies. Loved and respected, she rules and protects them, cares for a parrot given by Trot, and remains on Sky Island with Coralie and Tourmaline when Trot leaves because they have no Magic Umbrella.

Rosalie the Witch pledges to protect and serve Trot while Trot rules the Pink Country, proposing to lead the Pinkies through the Fog Bank against the Boolooroo to recover the Magic Umbrella and assist the campaign.

Polychrome is the Rainbow's Daughter, a fairy of the sky who lives in sky country and has powers far stronger than Rosalie the Witch's. She arrives by descending from the Rainbow to aid her old friend Button-Bright and the travelers, protecting Trot from threatened execution. Challenging Tourmaline, she interprets the Great Book of Laws in the travelers' favor, makes Trot Queen by placing Tourmaline's circlet on her, and leads her before the Pinkies. After asking Rosalie to protect Trot and promising to watch over Button-Bright, Polychrome leaves with her sisters on the Rainbow.
is_a queen Mayre is named in the contents as Queen of the Pink Country.

records.l: Queen of the Pink Country, Sky Island
records.s: The Queen of the Pinkies is an office regulated by Trot under a new law: its holder has the same food, dresses, good times, money, and no better home than the people. Trot holds it temporarily, then appoints Rosalie the Witch.

The Pinkies are the several hundred short, round, chubby, wholly pink people of Pink Country, with pink hair, eyes, cheeks, complexions, clothing, and a pink color scheme. Wealthy, polite, strong, and devoted to their laws, they regard wealth and honor as their due. Their society includes the Sunrise and Sunset Tribes, treats women as important as men in work and war, and uses long sharp-pointed sticks as weapons. They are ruled first by Tourmaline, whom they acknowledge as Queen, and regard the Blueskins as natural enemies. At first suspicious of outsiders, Pinkies capture and escort the travelers to Tourmaline, fearing enemies, magicians, or sorcerers. Although they do not hate the strangers, they have never admitted outsiders and support an order to execute them. Rosalie's explanation and Polychrome's interpretation of the laws change their response: they kneel to Trot, recognize her as Queen, and spread news of her rule. Eager for relief from monotonous lives, they form a two-hundred-warrior army and invade Blue Country across the Fog Bank on giant frogs. They camp outside Blue City, repel an attack, and, after Rosalie enchants their sticks, destroy the Blueskins' longer lances. They suffer setbacks in attempts to save Cap'n Bill, capture Ghip-Ghisizzle, and prepare to assault the City. Instead, Trot orders peace and they enter Blue City as welcomed conquerors. They celebrate but refuse to dance with the Blues and quarrel with them. Anxious to return home, the Pinkies travel back through the Fog Bank. They welcome Trot's return, accept her new law granting the Queen equal conditions as just, accept Rosalie as Queen, and promise her a palace and statues. They give Trot the royal pink-gold band with its pink jewel. At the end, their Pink Band plays while they gather in the Court of the Statues to bid Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright farewell.

records.l: the War of the Pinks and Blues, Sky Island
records.s: The War of the Pinks and Blues is listed as the title of chapter 19.

records.l: the amazing conquest of the Blues, Sky Island
records.s: Trot, supported by the Pinkies and aided by the billygoat, completes the conquest of the Blue Country, becoming Queen of the Blues; Ghip-Ghisizzle becomes Boolooroo and is ordered to rule kindly and avoid trouble.

records.l: the capture of Cap'n Bill, Sky Island
records.s: Cap'n Bill is captured after he pursues the retreating Blueskins alone and falls when his wooden leg steps into a hole. The Blueskins seize him, carry him into the Blue City, and bind him while the Pinkies are unable to reach him.

records.l: the tribulation of Trot, Sky Island
records.s: is_planned_by Six Snubnosed Princesses The Princesses punish Trot by shaking, slapping, pushing, and otherwise mistreating her after she refuses to act as their slave. Later they argue over harsher punishments, including beating her with knotted cords, locking her in a dark room, feeding her sand, or binding her to a windmill, but none of these proposed punishments occurs in this unit.

The Treasure Chamber is a dark, crowded, guarded room in the palace, holding the Boolooroo's accumulated riches, the Book of Records, and the Magic Umbrella. The Boolooroo keeps its key, Jimfred Jinksjones guards outside, and the Blue Wolf guards inside. Jimfred guards the entrance until Button-Bright deceives him into leaving; Button-Bright then unlocks and enters the chamber. Among gold, jewels, ornaments, cloths, furniture, vases, and bric-a-brac, he searches for the Magic Umbrella but does not find it.

The journey home takes Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright from Sky Island through the clouds and open sky to Earth. They encounter a Rainbow, stars, and a huge bird, eat food from the lunch basket, and land safely near Trot's house.
is_a friend [old, old] Dorothy is described as an old, old friend of Baum's readers. Readers compared Trot favorably to her, and Button-Bright previously had an adventure with Dorothy in Oz.
is_a fair land [remarkable] The sky country is described as a remarkable and fair land. Baum says that experiencing it makes him and the readers appreciate Mother Earth as a very good place to live.

Earth is a good place to live upon, beneath Sky Island, with ocean and mainland. It is home to Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill when they are at home, and the intended destination of the strangers. Though the Boolooroo calls it an uninhabited, round, cold, barren ball of mud and water, the travelers contradict him. Unable to return without the Magic Umbrella, they eventually see Earth below, fly over its ocean, reach the mainland, and arrive at the high bluff near Trot's house.

write_to L. Frank Baum [about how they like Sky Island] Baum's former readers approved of The Sea Fairies and wrote that they liked Trot almost as well as Dorothy. Their letters are Baum's greatest treasures, and he invites them to write and tell him how they like Sky Island.
Mrs. Griffith, Trot’s mother, lives in a frame cottage and is motherly and good, welcoming and feeding Button-Bright while often scolding Cap’n Bill and Trot.

Trot's house, home of Trot and Cap'n Bill, is a white cottage near a giant acacia on a high bluff, with a shed. Trot breakfasts there before flying, returns from town by Magic Umbrella, and comes home at dusk to find her mother cooking.

The Pacific Ocean is the world's biggest lot of water, beyond the high bluff near Trot's house, with Sky Island on its horizon. Trot and Button-Bright meet beside it; later three voyagers fly over it toward Sky Island.
Philadelphia is a big city and Button-Bright's distant home, at the other end of America from Trot's home; he lives there and finds an old umbrella that carries him toward Germantown.
A bay-shore fishing town with a store; the Magic Umbrella brings Trot and Button-Bright there, Trot trades yarn inside while Button-Bright draws a crowd outside.

Trot and Cap'n Bill infer that Button-Bright came down from the sky using his umbrella like a parachute. Button-Bright confirms that this was how he arrived, but the unit does not explain how he first got into the air.

records.l: Button-Bright's journey from Philadelphia, Sky Island
records.s: Button-Bright reaches the Pacific coast from Philadelphia by parachute descent with an umbrella, denying common travel methods and promising a later explanation.

records.l: frame cottage (Mrs. Griffith's cottage), Sky Island
records.s: is_a frame cottage [neat, on a high bluff, a little back from the sea, and covered with green vines] The frame cottage stands on a high bluff a little back from the sea and is covered with pretty green vines. It provides Button-Bright with food, shelter, and a place to stay overnight.
Magic is a lost art from before the characters’ births, associated with the Dark Ages; Button-Bright believes his flying umbrella proves it still exists, leading Cap’n Bill to reconsider.
Rosalie the Witch believes fairies, powerful and living in Pink Country, enchant the Magic Umbrella and defend Earth people from Pinkies’ injury.

records.l: flight of the Magic Umbrella, Sky Island
records.s: The flight of the Magic Umbrella is a swift, unfaltering air journey triggered when Button-Bright holds the umbrella open and speaks a destination or wishes to travel. It carries Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Trot faster than railroad trains, amazing villagers because it flies without visible power. On a trial trip it passes over Smuggler's Cove, circles, and returns without stopping for a drifting boat. Later it crosses the Pacific toward Sky Island, through clouds and down in an arching descent.
A seat suspended by six ropes: Cap'n Bill makes a broad board for Trot and Button-Bright, adds a second seat for himself, and all three ride safely in a trial flight.

records.l: flight from Sky Island to Earth, Sky Island
records.s: The air-ride is an exhilarating journey using the Magic Umbrella. It carries Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill quickly and comfortably; Cap'n Bill overcomes his fear during a trial ride. The flight home begins at Sky Island, passes clouds and Polychrome, and gently lands on a bluff near Trot's house on Earth.

takes_place_at Sky Island [planned destination] Trot proposes a picnic on Sky Island because it is too far to reach by sailing or rowing. She packs a basket of food, which Cap'n Bill fastens beneath his seat for the journey.

The island, whose right name is too hard to say, contains the Pink Country. As travelers approach, it grows larger, but the Magic Umbrella passes over it; later it shrinks behind them. Its rain-accustomed inhabitants and the Pinkies threaten strangers from its edge.

Clouds are vaporous, changeable formations that can appear as ships, trees, castles, palaces, dragons, and giants; travelers pass through black rain and white misty clouds before reaching clear blue sky.

records.l: the landing on Sky Island, Sky Island
records.s: The landing on Sky Island is a sudden, rough arrival: the basket thuds, Cap'n Bill lands forcefully, Trot and Button-Bright fall on him, and an angry voice protests.

The Blueskins are a people and citizens of the Blue Country, especially the Blue City, and inhabitants of Sky Island. Blue-skinned, tall, lanky, large compared with the Pinkies, and described as ugly and fierce, they have egg-shaped heads, long thin necks, short round bodies, and exceptionally long legs. They wear blue silk liveries as palace servants and use long winding-up cords weighted at the ends as weapons. Every man and woman is a voter under the government of Sky Island.
