Each is allowed exactly six hundred years of life; at that term's end they pass away rather than die and enter the Great Blue Grotto. Jealous of strangers and possible royal favor, the Blueskins dislike, threaten, and often pursue unfamiliar visitors, including Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright. They particularly hate the Six Snubnosed Princesses and are the Pinkies' natural enemies. They fear the Fog Bank above all else: no Blueskin has entered it, and pursuers stop when the travelers reach it. Their conflict with the Pinkies includes capturing prisoners in weighted cords, patching captured Pinkies, defending the City, and fighting with their cords, although several flee toward the Blue City when the Pinkies arrive. Many resent the Boolooroo, believing his treatment of the Earth people brought on the invasion. During the events, Blueskin soldiers capture the prisoners, carry out the Boolooroo's orders, chase escaping travelers, and later recapture Cap'n Bill. After Trot's conquest and the Boolooroo's defeat, they rejoice that the war is over, welcome Trot and the Pinkies, celebrate the destruction of the Great Knife, and receive Ghip-Ghisizzle as their new Boolooroo. Trot orders them to stop quarreling with the Pinkies and welcome them to the Blue City; she is also identified as their queen. Under Ghip-Ghisizzle after the conquest, they are secretly glad when Trot, the Pinkies, and the other strangers depart, and remain sullen during the departure.

The Royal Palace is a magnificent blue palace in Blue City, on Sky Island: the Boolooroo's royal residence and a building of six hundred tall towers and turrets, lofty rooms, broad corridors, passages, and superb blue furnishings. It contains royal apartments, servants' quarters and hall, the Royal Treasure Chamber, the Room of the Great Knife, prisoners' rooms, and areas for former Princesses. Richly blue-clad servants and guards at its entrance serve and protect it. For the strangers, it is safer than the City because servants and soldiers fear harming prisoners without the Boolooroo's permission. Trot is dragged there while Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright are assigned to servants' quarters; Button-Bright later steals the Treasure Chamber key and reaches the chamber. After an alarm fills it with guards, soldiers, and servants, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Trot escape through a little door. Trot returns at night, finds Cap'n Bill's hidden prison location, and Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes. Following the conquest, the palace hosts a feast and ball, its treasure and authority pass to Ghip-Ghisizzle, and the Boolooroo's family is expelled. A search there fails to find the Magic Umbrella, later said to have been discarded behind it.

records.l: the travelers' journey to Sky Island, Sky Island
records.s: Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright travel by Magic Umbrella to Sky Island, but after lunch, blue cords prevent their attempted journey home.

records.l: the capture of Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill, Sky Island
records.s: The Blueskins capture Cap'n Bill, Trot, and Button-Bright in a garden, creeping behind their bench and throwing thin, weighted blue cords around them and the Magic Umbrella. The cords pin each traveler's arms to their sides, leaving the three prisoners helpless under the Boolooroo and his people. After arranging for the Magic Umbrella to be secured, the Boolooroo releases them.

Princess Indigo, one of the Six Snubnosed Princesses and the Boolooroo’s daughter, owns a blue dog. She declares Trot a slave and mistreats her, but Trot’s pets drive Indigo away; rescued by her sisters, she avoids her room because Trot is inside.

is_mixed_by Tiggle [in the royal pantry] Royal nectar is a drink for which the Boolooroo is very particular. Cap'n Bill is assigned to carry it, while Ghip-Ghisizzle arranges for Tiggle to mix it so that it will suit the Boolooroo and the royal household.
Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill are captured, released because escape seems impossible without the Magic Umbrella, then condemned, threatened with patching, and assigned separate slavery.
The Boolooroo declares Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill slaves, assigning Trot to the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Cap'n Bill as Royal Nectar Mixer, and Button-Bright as Royal Bootblue.

Patching is the Boolooroo’s severe punishment in Sky Island and the Blue Country. Using the Great Knife or slicing machine, prisoners are cut in two and mismatched halves are joined, causing the resulting person to lose individuality and potentially have conflicting desires. The Boolooroo threatens Ghip-Ghisizzle, guards, and strangers with patching, including a proposed head-rearranging variant. Ghip-Ghisizzle is to be joined with Tiggle but is rescued before it happens. After his escape, Cap’n Bill is scheduled for patching with Tiggle, and later the Boolooroo plans to join him to the billygoat. Trot prevents these punishments, turns the threat back on the Boolooroo, and finally forbids any further patching, choosing exile and loss of status instead.

Jimfred Jonesjinks is a patched Blueskin and patched man, one half of a mismatched paired body with Fredjim Jinksjones. Joined from two people’s halves, he has mismatched features and a limp, guards the palace entrance, and is more intelligent than Fredjim. He says patching destroys individuality while Fredjim guards the Treasure Chamber.

Tiggle is a servant and prisoner of the Boolooroo who works in the royal pantry mixing royal nectar. Bound captive in the Room of the Great Knife, he is meant to be patched to Cap'n Bill, but Ghip-Ghisizzle replaces him and Trot frees him. Tiggle hides in a cellar of a deserted house to evade the Boolooroo's soldiers. A former servant of the former Boolooroo, he later returns after hearing the new Boolooroo wants him and recalls discarding the Magic Umbrella behind the palace.

The Earth travelers, wearing Boolooroo uniforms, are enslaved by Blueskins in Blue Country but escape through the Fog Bank. In Pink Country, Pinkies capture them as suspected enemies. After they tell the truth about their adventures, Tourmaline and the Counselors judge them; despite support for honoring them, the order is to throw them into the sky.
Earth people are strangers in the Pink Country: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill, whose truth Rosalie confirms before concluding fairies protect them unknowingly.

The Royal Record Book is a small light-blue leather book kept locked in the Treasure Chamber by the Boolooroo. It records the Pink Country as the Sunset Country and contains the terms of the Boolooroo’s rule and Ghip-Ghisizzle’s lawful succession. The Boolooroo hides it because it proves his permitted reign has expired. When it goes missing, he fears exposure. Button-Bright has taken it; Ghip-Ghisizzle reads it, learns the reign ended on Thursday, and recovers evidence that establishes his succession.

The Boolooroo's reign is supposed to last three hundred years, but Ghip-Ghisizzle suspects that the current Boolooroo has already ruled for three hundred years and claims it has lasted only two hundred. If so, the Boolooroo is five hundred years old and is trying to gain another hundred years of rule.

is_a high official position [in Sky Island] Royal bootblue duty requires Button-Bright to apply a finely perfumed blue paste to the royal boots and shoes and shine them. It is considered a high official position in Sky Island, and he is expected to perform it in the evening or early morning.

The Blue Country is the blue half of Sky Island, beyond the Fog Bank. It has no sun, but moonlight every night; its fields are blue, and it contains Blue City, a mountain, the Great Blue Grotto, the Arch of Phinis, and plentiful blue goats. It is inhabited by nervous, restless Blueskins and is less delightful and less comfortable than the Pink Country. For three hundred years it was ruled by Boolooroo, whose cruel treatment of Earth people helped bring the Pinkies through the Fog Bank to threaten and conquer the country. Earlier, travelers were enslaved after Boolooroo stole their Magic Umbrella, but escaped through the Fog Bank; they also could not remain because the people hated them. After Trot and Cap'n Bill overpower Boolooroo, Trot takes the Blue Country into her kingdom, appoints Cap'n Bill Royal Manager, removes the former ruling family, and appoints Ghip-Ghisizzle Boolooroo. She plans peace with the Pinkies and a celebration in Blue City.

records.l: the Great Blue Grotto, Sky Island
records.s: The Great Blue Grotto is a fatal place at the foot of the mountain in the Blue Country, beyond the Arch of Phinis outside the City gates. When Blueskins' six hundred years end, they march into it and never return; the Boolooroo expects it to destroy three strangers sent there.

records.l: the Arch of Phinis, Sky Island
records.s: The Arch of Phinis is a grim blue-marble archway at the entrance to the Great Blue Grotto outside the Blue City. Marked "Phinis," it is the required passage for Blueskins when they reach six hundred years, though the Boolooroo plans to send three strangers through early. Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Trot consider it for refuge but do not enter.

is_a celebration [held after the conquest] The grand feast takes place in the palace after the Pinkies and Blueskins enter the City together. Trot, Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, Rosalie the Witch, Captain Coralie, and Ghip-Ghisizzle dine in the Royal Banquet Hall with service from a hundred servants.

records.l: the apartments occupied by the Six Snubnosed Princesses, Sky Island
records.s: The exceptionally magnificent apartments contain reception room, six bedchambers, marble baths, and lavish blue-and-gold furnishings; Trot is kept there, befriends pets, then occupies Princess Indigo's room.

records.l: blue dog (Princess Indigo's pet), Sky Island
records.s: A blue dog crows like a rooster, receives Trot's care, then follows her and bites Princess Indigo's ankle defending her.

records.l: blue cat (Princess Azure's pet), Sky Island
records.s: sings_like a bird The blue cat sings like a bird and is fed milk by Trot. It follows Trot with the other pets and scratches Princess Indigo's leg when she tries to drive Trot away.

records.l: blue lamb (Princess Cobalt's pet), Sky Island
records.s: Princess Cobalt's blue lamb is a pet with larkspur-blue fleece that chatters gratefully; Trot feeds and pets it, and it follows her and butts Princess Indigo defending her.

The parrot is a talking, jolly bird and pet that barks like a dog, recites rhymes, sings, and imitates sounds. It travels through the Fog Bank with Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright, riding on Button-Bright's shoulder and later perching on Trot. In the Fog Bank it complains about being wet, warns the group about a giant frog, and emerges into sunshine with them. In the Pink Country it dries its feathers, alerts the travelers to the Pinkies, and frightens the Pinkies by speaking. After the Pinkies and Blueskins meet peacefully, it celebrates with verses and barking, then joins Trot at the feast, where she feeds it.

records.l: blue peacock (Princess Cerulia's pet), Sky Island
records.s: Princess Cerulia's pet blue peacock mews like a cat, is fed by Trot, loves and follows her, then joins the pets' rebellion against Princess Indigo.

records.l: blue rabbit (Princess Turquoise's pet), Sky Island
records.s: The fuzzy blue rabbit, a Princess’s pet, roars like a lion, eats Trot’s blue carrot, follows and plays with pets, then trips Princess Indigo.
Six pets rebel after Princess Indigo mistreats Trot and throws water on them, attacking and frightening her, forcing other Princesses to rescue.

records.l: the Treasure Chamber key, Sky Island
records.s: belongs_to the Boolooroo [kept in his pocket] The Treasure Chamber key is attached to a blue-gold chain and is kept in the Boolooroo's clothing. Button-Bright steals it from the sleeping king after searching the royal pockets and uses it to unlock the Royal Treasure Chamber.

records.l: the Great Blue Grotto expedition, Sky Island
records.s: The Boolooroo plans to march Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill through the Arch of Phinis into the Great Blue Grotto to destroy them, despite Ghip-Ghisizzle's age warning.

records.l: the Room of the Great Knife escape, Sky Island
records.s: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill plan to return to Earth using the Magic Umbrella; Button-Bright steals the Treasure Chamber key, deceives Jimfred, and enters the guarded chamber while the others wait.
A blue, unusually bright parrot, formerly Princess Cerulia’s pet, escapes the palace, follows Trot, lands on her shoulder, speaks in rhyme and barks like a dog, repeatedly criticizing Boolooroo.

The friendly frog is a common, very small frog living in the Fog Bank who hopes to grow larger. It meets Trot, Cap'n Bill, and Button-Bright, dislikes the Blueskins, and considers the Pinkies decent neighbors. Swiftly guiding the travelers with grunts, croaks, and enormous leaps, it helps them escape by carrying each on its back in a final leap to the Fog Bank border before attending the King's Court.

records.l: King of the Giant Frogs, Sky Island
records.s: King of the Giant Frogs is a king of the frogs in the Fog Bank, about ten times larger than a common frog. He leads giant frogs, rules Frog King's kingdom, and has frogs as subjects. He helps Rosalie the Witch's party cross the Fog Bank, but later bars travelers over an umbrella and flees when it becomes an elephant.

Pink City is a city in Pink Country, enclosed by a strong high pink marble wall and entered through pink metal bars. Its circular street winds past round domed houses toward central Tourmaline, alongside the Pinkies' humble, uncomfortable palace and Court of the Statues.

records.l: the travelers' escape from the Blue Country, Sky Island
records.s: The travelers escape the Blue Country after the Boolooroo makes them slaves. Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill cross the wet, sticky Fog Bank with a big frog's help, reach the Pink Country, and are captured by the Pinkies and taken to Tourmaline.

Coralie is a prominent Pinkie woman of the Sunset Tribe who serves as captain, Commander in Chief, and spokesperson. She hosts Trot and other prisoners kindly, argues to the Council that they are harmless and deserve a chance to return home, and later captures Ghip-Ghisizzle after his flight from the City.

records.l: the Great Book of Laws, Sky Island
records.s: The Great Book of Laws contains Pink Country protection and succession rules; Polychrome examines its wording to protect travelers and establish Trot as Queen under equal conditions.

The palace of Tourmaline is a small, plain, low-domed building made of coarse pink stone. It has simple furnishings and no ornamentation, banners, or nearby flowers, reflecting Tourmaline's lack of wealth and special privilege.

express the Will of the People The Pink Country laws are treated as the Will of the People, and Tourmaline has the authority to enforce them, adjust grievances, compel order, and decree death when punishment is merited. No known law covers the arrival of strangers, so Tourmaline searches the Great Book and may have to create a new law.

records.l: the Council of twelve, Sky Island
records.s: The Council of twelve is a council summoned by Tourmaline to advise on the strangers' fate in the Pink Country. After examining and conferring, it must choose whether to honor them as guests or throw them over the island’s edge. Its vote ends evenly divided, six to six.

records.l: the enchanted Pinkies' weapons, Sky Island
records.s: deflect the Blueskins' bluewood lances [by whirling in swift circles] The enchanted Pinkies' sharp sticks whirl in swift circles when the Blueskins attack. They deflect the Blueskins' longer lances, breaking them or sending them through the air and causing the Blueskins to flee.

records.l: the setting of the sun, Sky Island
records.s: is_visible_from the Sunset Tribe [in magnificent splendor] The setting of the sun draws the Sunset Tribe and neighboring households onto balconies and roofs. Trot considers its orange, red, and yellow splendor even greater than any sunset seen on the Earth.

records.l: the Pinkies' tribal rivalry, Sky Island
records.s: exists_between the Sunrise Tribe [and the Sunset Tribe] The rivalry between the Sunrise Tribe and Sunset Tribe concerns which side the sun favors. The tribes argue that being greeted first or receiving the sun after it leaves the other tribe proves greater importance or attractiveness, and they have sometimes fought with sharp sticks.

has_alternatives remaining as honored guests or being thrown from the island [as decided by the Pinkies] The strangers’ fate is undecided after Tourmaline’s Council examines them. They may remain as honored guests, or they may be taken to the edge of Sky Island and thrown over the bushes into the sky.

The Rainbow is immense, with vivid, blended colors. It appears through breaks in clouds near the Pink Country or over the Court of the Statues, descending to a field and bearing Polychrome and her sisters. After Polychrome departs or they are carried skyward, its colors fade and the arch rises, dissolves, and disappears.

shows the adventures of the Earth people [as Rosalie the Witch sees them] The vision shows the Earth people's adventures, including Button-Bright's discovery and flights with the Magic Umbrella, their journey to Sky Island, meeting the Boolooroo, and passage through the Fog Bank. It enables the Pinkies to confirm that the strangers have told the truth.

The deciding vote is needed because the twelve Counselors divide evenly over the strangers' fate. Tourmaline asks Rosalie the Witch to cast it, and Rosalie votes to have the strangers thrown from the island.

records.l: expedition through the Fog Bank, Sky Island
records.s: An Army of Conquest commanded by Cap'n Bill crosses the Fog Bank with the King of the Giant Frogs and giant frogs, arriving safely in the Blue Country.

enchants the Magic Umbrella [enabling it to fly and carry passengers] Fairy power is said to enchant the Magic Umbrella, giving it the ability to fly and carry passengers through the air. Rosalie believes this power will protect the Earth people from harm.

records.l: Daughters of the Rainbow, Sky Island
records.s: Fairies of the sky dance along the Rainbow in rainbow-tinted robes, arriving with Polychrome and allowing her to remain behind as it rises.

records.l: the Pink Country protection law, Sky Island
records.s: The Pink Country protection law grants the Ruler’s protection, a house, and a good living to everyone in the Pink Country except Blueskins, who must be driven back across the Fog Bank; it consequently protects Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap’n Bill.

records.l: the Pink Country succession law, Sky Island
records.s: selects_ruler_by lightest skin [for life unless someone lighter is found] The Pink Country succession law states that the person with the lightest skin in the Pink Country shall be King or Queen for life, and that everyone must obey the ruler's commands. Polychrome determines that Trot is lighter in color than Tourmaline, making Trot the rightful Queen.

records.l: the travelers' threatened execution, Sky Island
records.s: Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill face a decreed death sentence by being thrown over the Pink Country's edge, but Polychrome invokes its protection law, prevents it, and makes Trot Queen.

records.l: the arrival of Polychrome, Sky Island
records.s: Polychrome arrives by Rainbow near travelers and Pinkies, helps overturn their threatened execution, and changes Pink Country rule by installing Trot as Queen.

Trot is uncertain how she will rule the Pink Country and asks the people to enjoy a holiday while she considers it. She learns that the Pinkies expect their Queen to be poor and without fun, making the position potentially tiresome.

makes Trot [the new Queen of the Pinkies] Trot's coronation takes place when Polychrome leads her before the assembled Pinkies. The people are impressed by Trot's friendship with Polychrome and Rosalie's humble deference, and they kneel to her and kiss her hand.

records.l: the planned campaign against the Boolooroo, Sky Island
records.s: seeks_to_recover Magic Umbrella [by force if necessary] Trot, Button-Bright, Cap'n Bill, and Rosalie plan to enter the Blue Country, recover the Magic Umbrella, and possibly replace the Boolooroo with Ghip-Ghisizzle without fighting. They nevertheless intend to proceed prepared for a struggle and expect to begin after assembling the army in two or three days.

The Army of Conquest is a Pinkie army formed to fight the Blueskins and support Ghip-Ghisizzle in his struggle for rule of the Blue Country. Rosalie proposes gathering it and marching through the Fog Bank against the Boolooroo. It consists of two hundred Pinkies, one hundred Sunsets and one hundred Sunrises, with men and women equally divided, and is commanded and led by Cap'n Bill. Expected to be ready within days, it relies on sharp sticks as an advantage over Blueskin weapons. The army rides giant frogs across the Fog Bank, reaches the City wall, and must halt before its locked gates. Its aid depends on return of the Magic Umbrella and permission for the adventurers to fly home.
records.t: The Army of Conquest is a Pinkie army formed to fight the Blueskins and support Ghip-Ghisizzle in his struggle for rule of the Blue Country. Rosalie proposes gathering it and marching through the Fog Bank against the Boolooroo. It consists of two hundred Pinkies—one hundred Sunsets and one hundred Sunrises—with men and women equally divided—and is commanded and led by Cap'n Bill. Expected to be ready within days, it relies on sharp sticks as an advantage over Blueskin weapons. The army rides giant frogs across the Fog Bank, reaches the City wall, and must halt before its locked gates. Its aid depends on return of the Magic Umbrella and permission for the adventurers to fly home.

records.s: Giant frogs are gigantic, large frogs that help the Army of Conquest through the Fog Bank. They form a barrier, carry Pinkies and travelers on their backs, and leap across the fog to Blue Country. Later, an umbrella’s transformation into a huge elephant makes them flee and hide in moist banks.

records.l: war between the Pinkies and Blueskins, Sky Island
records.s: The war begins when the Pinkies enter the Blue Country to fight the Blueskins, believing themselves braver and better armed. It ends after the Boolooroo's defeat, when the Blueskins peacefully receive the Pinkies and Trot calls for sociability and happiness.

The Great Knife is a dreadful, immense cutting machine and instrument of punishment, a huge blade mounted in a derrick-like framework. Used to patch prisoners, it is released by a cord to split a person in two before halves are joined. It is prepared for Ghip-Ghisizzle and Tiggle, then twice misses Cap'n Bill when Trot pulls his frame away. Afterward, it is broken into pieces and burned, and the Blueskins celebrate its destruction.

records.l: the Room of the Great Knife, Sky Island
records.s: The Room of the Great Knife is a large palace execution room centered on the Great Knife, with spectator benches, a royal platform, and a cutting machine used to patch prisoners. It holds bound prisoners including Ghip-Ghisizzle and Tiggle, and later receives Cap'n Bill for punishment. During the conquest, attackers drive out the soldiers and royal family. After the former Boolooroo is removed, its knife and terrible furnishings are destroyed, and Trot orders the room converted into a skating rink.

is_a invasion [of the Blue Country] The Pinkie invasion interrupts the Boolooroo's attempt to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched. It causes the City to shut its gates and forces the Blueskins to prepare for battle.

is_limited_to one every three days [for Rosalie] Rosalie explains that she is allowed to work only one magic charm every three days. She uses the available charm to enchant the Pinkies' weapons, leaving her unable to use another charm immediately to rescue Cap'n Bill.

reaches the Blue City wall [from the ground to the top] Rosalie knots ropes into a ladder long enough to reach the top of the Blue City wall. After seven attempts, she catches it on a broken flagstaff, allowing Trot to climb up and then descend into the City.

records.l: ring of Rosalie the Witch, Sky Island
records.s: Rosalie the Witch’s witchcraft treasure is a magic ring worn by Trot. It makes its wearer invisible to Blueskins, Pinkies, and Earth people, allowing Trot to enter the Blue City unseen. Touching another person or living creature makes Trot visible while contact lasts, and Rosalie requires the ring’s return.

records.l: the Blueskins' attack on the Pinkies, Sky Island
records.s: The Blueskins' first attack fails when the Pinkies form a line with their sharp sticks and drive them back. During a second attack, the Blueskins' longer lances are destroyed or thrown aside by the enchanted weapons, causing another retreat.

records.l: Trot's secret entry into the Blue City, Sky Island
records.s: Trot secretly enters the Blue City at night, using Rosalie’s magic ring to become invisible and a rope ladder to climb the wall, then passes a guard and searches for Cap’n Bill.
is_outside the City The Pinkies' camp lies outside the City near the City wall. Ghip-Ghisizzle leaps toward it for protection, and Captain Coralie captures him there.

records.l: Ghip-Ghisizzle's flight from the City, Sky Island
records.s: ends_with capture by the Pinkies [after reaching the Pinkies' camp] Ghip-Ghisizzle escapes through a window, runs along the palace garden wall and the City wall, and leaps into the field outside the City near the Pinkies' camp. The Blueskins pursue him but stop when he reaches the Pinkies.

Being patched is a punishment and means of control in which the Boolooroo uses the Great Knife to split two people and join them into a strange combination. Jimfred and Fredjim found it less painful than expected but confusing. The Boolooroo plans to patch Cap'n Bill with Tiggle, though Tiggle is hiding.
Cap'n Bill's capture occurs in Blue City after his attempted escape, when Blueskins overtake him on the wall, bind him, and carry him down, disappointing his companions.

records.l: Cap'n Bill's escape attempt, Sky Island
records.s: is_an escape attempt [from the Blue City] Trot helps Cap'n Bill escape from the Boolooroo's apartments by lowering him from a window on a sheet and directing him to a rope ladder. He crosses the wall but cannot outrun the Blueskins, who head him off and recapture him.

is_held_by Ghip-Ghisizzle [with Rosalie, Button-Bright, and the others] Ghip-Ghisizzle, Rosalie the Witch, Button-Bright, and the others hold a council of war in Rosalie's tent after Cap'n Bill's recapture. They discuss how to take the Blue City and capture the Boolooroo.

records.l: the Boolooroo's unlawful rule, Sky Island
records.s: is_recorded_in Royal Record Book [the book provides legal proof] The Royal Record Book states that the Boolooroo had already completed three hundred years of rule by Thursday and therefore no longer had the right to govern. He has continued ruling and has also tried to have Ghip-Ghisizzle patched to prevent him from becoming Boolooroo.

records.l: the Captain of the Guards, Sky Island
records.s: Captain of the Blue guards commands soldiers, returns after Trot threatens the Boolooroo, obeys Trot as ruler, escorts the princesses, guards the palace, and reports a Pinkie attack threat.

A blue billygoat is obstinate and dangerous. First encountered by soldiers, it attacks the Boolooroo, soldiers, and Six Snubnosed Princesses, clearing the Room of the Great Knife; Trot ties it to a doorway pillar. Later released and locked with the Boolooroo, it serves as a feared guard. It helps Trot defeat and dethrone the Boolooroo, becoming an honored hero promised a fenced yard, food, and lifelong honor from the Blueskins.

records.l: the Pinkies' attack on the City, Sky Island
records.s: is_preparing the City [according to the Captain of the Guards] The Captain of the Guards reports that the Pinkies are preparing to attack the City. Trot responds by ordering the City to open its gates and welcome them rather than resist them.

is_planned the Blue City [for the Pinkies and Blues] Trot orders a grand celebration for the Pinkies' arrival in the Blue City. It is to include music, dancing, eating, and royal neckties to drink, with the bands, soldiers, and people taking part.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's rule of the kingdom, Sky Island
records.s: includes the Blue Country [jointly] Trot and Cap'n Bill take control of the kingdom after the Boolooroo is overthrown. Trot claims authority over both the Pinkies and the Blues, while Cap'n Bill is made her General of the Army and Royal Manager of the Blue Country.

records.l: the destruction of the Great Knife, Sky Island
records.s: removes the Great Knife [the knife and its furniture are broken up and burned] The destruction of the Great Knife is ordered by Trot and carried out after the former Boolooroo is removed. The Knife, frames, and benches are broken up and burned while the Blueskins dance and sing in celebration.

records.l: the Boolooroo's lawful succession, Sky Island
records.s: is_established_by the Book of Royal Records [the record shows Ghip-Ghisizzle is lawful] The Book of Royal Records establishes that the former Boolooroo is no longer lawful because he has ruled beyond three hundred years. Ghip-Ghisizzle therefore becomes the lawful Boolooroo of the Blue Country, though Trot remains Queen of Sky Island.

records.l: search for the Magic Umbrella, Sky Island
records.s: The search begins throughout the palace with the help of many people and the palace's full liberty. After Indigo's false claim is exposed, Trot questions the servants and learns that Tiggle may know what happened to the umbrella.

records.l: departure of the Pinkies, Sky Island
records.s: The Pinkies depart Blue City, led by Captain Tintint with Coralie in their ranks and the Pinkie Band marching, leaving through the blue-barred gateway toward the Fog Bank.

records.l: return of Trot and her companions to Earth, Sky Island
records.s: The return of Trot, Button-Bright, and Cap'n Bill to Earth is planned after they leave the Pink Country. Although the recovered Magic Umbrella allows them to go home whenever they wish, Trot delays until fulfilling duties in Sky Island and helping the Pinkies, then announces their departure after arranging a new Queen.
The Magic Umbrella transforms into an elephant with a living carved head, trunk, ears, and frame-tail; it charges frogs, leads travelers through fog, then shrinks back.

records.l: umbrella's transformation into an elephant, Sky Island
records.s: The umbrella's transformation into an elephant begins when it trembles, shakes, and sends red sparks from the carved elephant head's eyes. After Button-Bright drops it, it becomes a complete elephant of monstrous size and later changes back into the Magic Umbrella.
Button-Bright stays overnight at Trot's house, uses the Magic Umbrella to return safely to Philadelphia, and his father locks it away.

This document is a sequence of six Oz adventures centered on familiar inhabitants of the Emerald City and the wider Land of Oz. It begins with the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger setting out to behave ferociously, only to rescue a lost baby and injured mother; her praise makes them reject cruelty. Dorothy and Toto then face the giant Crinklink while traveling alone, but Crinklink proves to be the Wizard of Oz in disguise, teaching Dorothy to return safely to the Emerald City. Tiktok seeks repairs from the Nome King, is smashed after insulting him, and is restored by Kaliko; Tiktok’s apparent return as a phantom frightens the King into apologizing and sending jewels to Princess Ozma. Ozma and the Wizard next tour the Land of Oz to ensure that people are happy and wrongs are corrected. They stop three Imps from tormenting travelers and a family, ultimately confining their spirits in buttons until they repent. Ozma later uses the Magic Picture to discover two lost children, and Jack Pumpkinhead and the Sawhorse rescue them from the King of all the Squirrels. When Jack’s head is smashed, the little Wizard saves the children and gives Jack a new pumpkin head. Finally, the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman suffer a river accident, are trapped by crows, and are rescued by the Wizard, who restores the Tin Woodman with oil. Across the episodes, Oz’s friends repeatedly turn danger into rescue, correction, repair, and safe return.

records.l: Emerald City, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Emerald City is a beautiful fairy city of great grandeur at the center of the Land of Oz. It contains the Royal Palace, where Princess Ozma rules, and where the Wizard of Oz lives in a cozy suite. Its quiet streets are walked by the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger; Dorothy and Toto live there and return there; and Jack Pumpkinhead begins his journey there to rescue the children.

records.l: Land of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Land of Oz is a beautiful fairy country ruled by Princess Ozma. It contains magical places, creatures, things, Tiktok’s home, southeast wooded hills, a black-water lake, and the supposed Crinklink. Though solitary travel can be dangerous, Ozma and the Wizard journey through it seeking problems to correct so inhabitants are happy and contented.

records.l: Throne Room, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Throne Room, a great royal audience room in the palace in Emerald City, is where Princess Ozma daily hears her people’s troubles, guarded by the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger.

records.l: Princess Ozma, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Princess Ozma is the beautiful, powerful princess and ruler of Oz, living in Emerald City and governing from a glistening-emerald throne in the Throne Room, where the Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger serve as chief guardians. Concerned above all with her people’s happiness, she holds a daily audience to hear their troubles and uses the Magic Picture in the Royal Palace to learn of events across Oz. She is Tiktok’s favorite ruler, studies Tiktok, and is feared by the Nome King. With the Wizard, she journeys through Oz to investigate complaints, confronts mischievous Imps, and approves keeping their spirits in buttons in hopes of reforming them. When the Magic Picture reveals lost children, she sends her friend Jack Pumpkinhead with a map; after Jack is harmed, she sends the little Wizard, riding the Cowardly Lion, to rescue Jack and the children.

records.l: Scarecrow, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow is an important personage of Oz, a queerly made straw man in blue Munchkin clothes, with a bran-filled cloth head and painted features. Though unsuccessful at scaring crows, he considers himself superior to man, feels no pain, never tires, and needs neither food nor drink. Given sharp brains by the Wizard of Oz, he lives in his palace by a river and is best friends with the Tin Woodman. While steering his corncob boat, he repeatedly mishaps but saves his friend and is freed by the Wizard.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead, an active, good-natured, popular inhabitant and important personage of Oz, has a rough-stick body and carved pumpkin head. Living in a hollow pumpkin in his pumpkin field, he grows replacement heads. Riding the Sawhorse, he rescues two children from squirrels; after a falling limb destroys his head, the little Wizard replaces it.

records.l: Tiktok the Clockwork Man, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Tiktok the Clockwork Man is an entirely metal personage of the Land of Oz, powered by separate keyed motion, speech, and thought machinery and favored by Princess Ozma of Oz. Seeking new springs and a cog-wheel from the Nome King, he is smashed into pieces, reconstructed and repaired by Kaliko, briefly speaks gruffly, asserts that he is real, and prepares to return with jewels.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Tin Woodman is an important personage of Oz, a man made entirely of tin and formerly a woodchopper, with freely movable jointed arms, legs, and head. Given a red-plush heart by the Wizard of Oz, he lives in Tin Woodman's castle in Winkie Land and is Scarecrow's best friend. After falling overboard and rusting, crows pull him out; Scarecrow and the Wizard restore his movement.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Wizard of Oz is a little, withered old Wizard and important personage of Oz who lives in Princess Ozma’s palace in Emerald City. Kind and loved by the people of the Land of Oz, he serves Princess Ozma as an attendant, accompanies her on journeys, and carries a bag of magic tools. He can do many queer things with magic: he changes the Imps, dries his clothes after the river, and puts their spirits into three buttons so they may repent. Sent to rescue Jack Pumpkinhead and the children, he rides the Cowardly Lion, returns the children, and gives Jack a new pumpkin head. He also rescues the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman, freeing the Scarecrow, drawing a boat to shore, and helping restore the Tin Woodman’s joints. He gives the Scarecrow sharp brains and the Tin Woodman a red-plush heart. Faithful to Dorothy, he disapproves of her traveling alone, disguises himself as Crinklink and a ferryman to teach her why, then takes her toward Emerald City.

records.l: Dorothy, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Dorothy is a Kansas girl living in the Land of Oz by invitation, often seated at Ozma's feet, and a faithful friend of the Wizard of Oz. Traveling with Toto through southeastern Oz, she is captured by the disguised Wizard and made to wash dishes. Frightened by Crinklink, she learns it was a lesson, becomes angry, and returns to the Emerald City.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Cowardly Lion is an enormous, habitually tame and peaceable beast, born in the jungle with the Hungry Tiger and serving as one of Princess Ozma's chief guardians. Though named for cowardice and armed with powerful teeth and sharp claws, he rejects cruelty: after wishing to inspire fear, he carries an injured baby's mother home and concludes that cowardice is better than wrongdoing.

records.l: Hungry Tiger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Hungry Tiger is an enormous beast and one of Ozma's chief guardians, born in the jungle with the Cowardly Lion and continually hungry. He leaves the palace to prove power, longs to eat fat babies, but comforts and carries a lost baby, choosing hunger over cruelty.

records.l: Ozma's chief guardians, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a guardians [of Princess Ozma] The Cowardly Lion and Hungry Tiger are Ozma's chief guardians. They are more ornamental than useful because the people of Oz are seldom naughty and no one disturbs Princess Ozma's audiences.

records.l: lost baby, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: A baby, lost from its mother, cries in the street until the Hungry Tiger comforts and carries the baby safely back to its mother; the baby kisses the Tiger’s nose.

records.l: baby's mother, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The baby's mother rushes out to rescue her lost baby, trips and is injured; the Cowardly Lion takes her home as the Hungry Tiger carries baby.

records.l: fat babies, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Hungry Tiger claims to be hungry for fat babies and imagines that eating one would make people fear him. When he encounters a real baby, he cannot bring himself to eat the child and instead protects it.

records.l: hunger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: concerns fat babies [the Hungry Tiger's desire to eat them] The Hungry Tiger repeatedly complains of hunger, especially for fat babies. After choosing not to eat the lost baby, he remains hungry but decides that going hungry is better than being cruel.

records.l: cowardice, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_better_than cruelty [according to the Cowardly Lion] The Cowardly Lion openly identifies himself as cowardly and imagines attacking someone only to flee before anyone can punish him. After helping the baby's mother, he concludes that cowardice is preferable to doing wrong.

records.l: cruelty, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_worse_than hunger [according to the Hungry Tiger] Cruelty is rejected by both beasts when they choose to help the lost baby and the injured mother instead of harming them. The Hungry Tiger specifically concludes that it is better to remain hungry than to be cruel to a child.

records.l: Toto, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Toto, a small black, fuzzy, curly-haired Kansas dog with bright black eyes, understands Dorothy but cannot speak. He accompanies her, growls at threats, is frightened when carried away, then attacks sleeping Crinklink to save Dorothy and reveal Crinklink as the Wizard of Oz.

records.l: Crinklink, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Crinklink is a fictional, changeable-sized monster presented as a terrifying giant. He carries Dorothy and Toto across a black-water lake to his log castle, threatens punishment and dishwashing, and may enslave captives, before being revealed as the Wizard of Oz in disguise.

records.l: the wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Wild wooded hills at the southeast of Oz, usually avoided because many magical things abound, are entered and crossed by Dorothy and Toto to a log castle.

records.l: the black-water lake, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The black-water lake is a big, deep barrier without a bridge or boat; it blocks Dorothy and Toto until a tiny ferryman offers passage and the disguised Wizard carries them across in one giant step.

records.l: the ferryman, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The ferryman is a three-inch man with blue hair, small eyes, a big nose, a sharp chin, scarlet clothes, and an animal-buttoned jacket. He says he carries people across the black-water lake by a spoken word, then is revealed as the Wizard of Oz in disguise.

records.l: Crinklink's log castle, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Crinklink's log castle, perched on the highest hill peak, is a one-room home with a table, chair, tiny bed, and soiled dishes scattered throughout.

records.l: the dishes, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The dishes in Crinklink's log castle are soiled, piled everywhere, and needed clean; left unwashed for years, they are ordered cleaned before a heap falls and breaks during Toto's attack.

records.l: washing the dishes, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Washing the dishes is a task Crinklink assigns Dorothy; she carefully washes for hours without breakage until Toto attacks and knocks the dishes down.

records.l: the Wizard's lesson about traveling alone, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: teaches traveling alone is dangerous [in a fairy country] The Wizard's lesson is that it is dangerous for a little girl to wander alone in a fairy country. He creates the false ferryman and Crinklink and makes Dorothy believe she has been captured, hoping to teach her to be more careful.

records.l: Nome King, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Nome King is a Nome who rules the Nome kingdom from an underground palace, with a bad temper and a heavy mace. When annoyed, he smashes Tiktok, then feels ashamed, fears Princess Ozma of Oz, is forgiven by Kaliko, and promises jewels as compensation.

records.l: Kaliko, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Kaliko, the Nome King’s clever Chief Steward and mechanic, repairs destroyed Tiktok with replacement parts, confirms he is real, seeks forgiveness, and is forgiven and rewarded with higher wages.

records.l: Tiktok's destruction, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_caused_by Nome King's mace [the blow burst Tiktok's body apart] Tiktok's destruction occurs when the Nome King hurls his heavy mace at him, bursting the bolts that hold his metal body together. His wheels, pins, cogs, and springs scatter across the floor, leaving only a scrap-heap.

records.l: Tiktok's repair, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_performed_by Kaliko [by replacing worn or imperfect parts] Tiktok's repair is completed by Kaliko over two weeks of steady work. Kaliko fits the pieces together, replaces worn or imperfect parts, and restores Tiktok's motion, thought, and speech machinery.

records.l: the Nome King's anger, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Nome King's anger, sparked by a bitten tongue and Tiktok's insults, drives an impulsive mace blow that destroys Tiktok; afterward he regrets his unreasoning temper and resolves to avoid anger unless annoyed.

records.l: Ozma and the Wizard's journey through the Land of Oz, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Ozma and the Wizard journey from the Emerald City through the Land of Oz for many days, reach unfamiliar mountains and a valley, and try to protect travelers from three mischievous Imps.

records.l: valley in the mountains, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a pretty valley The valley lies beyond a rocky path and contains three caves where the Imps live. The Imps harass travelers and a family in a nearby cottage, so Ozma and the Wizard enter the valley to find them.

records.l: three mischievous Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Three small, lively Imps, Olite, Udent, and Ertinent, live in a mountain valley, tormenting travelers by jeering, calling names, pushing, and throwing stones; later they attack Ozma and the Wizard even after being transformed.
records.t: Three small, lively Imps—Olite, Udent, and Ertinent—live in a mountain valley, tormenting travelers by jeering, calling names, pushing, and throwing stones; later they attack Ozma and the Wizard even after being transformed.

records.l: Imp Olite, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a Imp [mischievous] Imp Olite is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Olite's spirit is contained in a tin button.

records.l: Imp Udent, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a Imp [mischievous] Imp Udent is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Udent's spirit is contained in a brass button.

records.l: Imp Ertinent, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a Imp [mischievous] Imp Ertinent is one of the three mischievous Imps who torment travelers and attack Princess Ozma and the Wizard of Oz. After several transformations, Ertinent's spirit is contained in a lead button.

records.l: thorny bushes transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a bushes [thorny and stubby] The Wizard first transforms the three Imps into thorny, stubby bushes rooted in the ground. The bushes soon move across the earth and prick the Wizard while trying to injure Ozma, so he transforms them again.

records.l: white pigs transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_a pigs [white, fat, roly-poly, and cute] The Wizard accidentally transforms the thorny bushes into three fat, roly-poly white pigs instead of mice. The pigs continue the Imps' mischief by tripping Ozma and the Wizard and pushing the Wizard into the river.

records.l: blue doves transformed from the Imps, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Wizard transforms white pigs into three blue doves, which attack Ozma and him by pecking eyes, biting fingers, and tweaking Ozma's ear.

records.l: three buttons containing the Imps' spirits, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Three buttons, tin, brass, and lead, contain the spirits of the mischievous Imps Olite, Udent, and Ertinent after the Wizard transforms blue doves. He boxes them, intending to sew them onto his coat until repentance changes them into silver, gold, and aluminum and restores the Imps.
records.t: Three buttons—tin, brass, and lead—contain the spirits of the mischievous Imps Olite, Udent, and Ertinent after the Wizard transforms blue doves. He boxes them, intending to sew them onto his coat until repentance changes them into silver, gold, and aluminum and restores the Imps.

records.l: magic, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_used_by Wizard of Oz [to transform creatures and objects] The Wizard uses magic to transform the Imps from living creatures into bushes, pigs, doves, and finally buttons. His magic also dries his clothes after the river incident, and he explains that the Imps' spirits can change the buttons when they repent.

records.l: Sawhorse, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Sawhorse is a remarkable wooden animal, made from a log with four stick legs, a branch tail, knot eyes, and gold plates on its feet. Swift, untiring, intelligent, and Ozma's favorite steed, it carries Jack Pumpkinhead and children through danger, gets lost, is led out, and brings Jack home.

records.l: the little girl, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The little girl becomes lost and hungry in the western forest with the little boy, is imprisoned by squirrels, then freed by Jack and rides the Sawhorse out to her anxious friends.

records.l: the little boy, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The little boy is a lost, hungry child in the western forest with the little girl. After they eat squirrels' stored nuts, squirrels bind him to a tree, but he explains their hunger and is returned to his friends.

records.l: King of all the Squirrels, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: King of all the Squirrels is a king who wears a gold circle with a central diamond and rules forest squirrels, ordering two children imprisoned for taking nuts before Jack frees them.

records.l: the squirrels, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: store nuts [for winter in the squirrels' storehouse] The squirrels bind the two children to a tree after they eat nuts saved for winter. They throw nuts at Jack and rejoice when a fallen limb smashes his pumpkin head.

records.l: the forest, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: A great, gloomy forest in the far west of Oz, filled with branching paths, where Jack finds children and the Sawhorse is lost after Jack’s head is smashed before the Cowardly Lion guides it out.

records.l: the Magic Picture, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The Magic Picture in the Royal Palace constantly changes scenes, showing important events throughout Oz; Ozma uses it to find lost children and see the forest’s events.

records.l: Ozma's map, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: shows the forest's paths [and the location of the children] Ozma's map shows Jack the forest's location, the route to it, and the paths leading to the children. Jack consults it repeatedly because the forest paths branch in many directions, but it is no longer useful after his head is destroyed.

records.l: the children's rescue, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: The children's rescue is carried out first by Jack Pumpkinhead, who frees them from the squirrels, and then by the Sawhorse, which carries them from the forest. The little Wizard ultimately returns them to their anxious friends.

records.l: Jack's head being smashed, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Jack's head being smashed occurs when a dead tree limb falls on him as squirrels throw nuts, destroying his pumpkin head and leaving Jack Pumpkinhead unable to see or speak.

records.l: Jack's restoration, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: At Jack's pumpkin field, the little Wizard brings Jack Pumpkinhead home, carves and attaches a new pumpkin head, restoring him to good condition.

records.l: crows, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: Crows are black birds usually friendly to Scarecrow, but they laugh when he loses an eye, then carry Scarecrow and Tin Woodman from the river to a dead tree and abandon them suspended.

records.l: river, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: has_branch smaller river [flowing from a deep forest] The river carries the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman in the Scarecrow's boat. A smaller stream flows from the forest, and the boat travels up it until it becomes narrow and crooked. The Tin Woodman sinks to its bottom after the boat collides with a rock.

records.l: forest, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is deep forest The forest surrounds the smaller river and provides a cool, shady route for the boat. Its trees conceal a tall dead tree where the crows suspend the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman. A bramble-bush in the forest traps the Scarecrow after he falls.

records.l: Scarecrow's corncob boat, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: A jeweled, hollowed, pointed corncob boat with a glittering purple silk sail carries the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman up the river, bumps a rock, floats midstream after crows lift them away, and is magically drawn to shore.

records.l: anchor, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_onboard Scarecrow's corncob boat [an extra anchor was also aboard] The Scarecrow throws out the boat's anchor after the accident to keep the boat in place. He considers tying an extra anchor around his waist to sink, then later clings to that anchor while the crows lift him and the Tin Woodman. When he drops it, he falls into a bramble-bush while the Tin Woodman falls safely onto dry leaves.

records.l: oil-can, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_used_for Tin Woodman's rescue [to oil his joints] The oil-can is left back in the boat while the Tin Woodman hangs suspended and his joints rust. The Wizard of Oz draws the boat to shore so the Scarecrow can retrieve the oil-can. The Scarecrow uses it to oil each of the Tin Woodman's joints.

records.l: boat accident, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: involves Tin Woodman [he fell overboard and sank] The boat accident occurs when the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman become distracted while sailing up the forest stream and fail to notice a large rock ahead. The boat strikes the rock, causing the Tin Woodman to fall overboard and sink. The accident leaves the Tin Woodman at risk of rusting and leads to the crows' unsuccessful rescue attempt.

records.l: Tin Woodman's rescue, Little Wizard Stories of Oz
records.s: is_performed_by Scarecrow [with help from the Wizard of Oz] The Tin Woodman's rescue begins when the Scarecrow tries to dive for him and then uses a fishline and hook. The King Crow has the crows pull the line, but they lift both friends into a tree and abandon them. The Wizard of Oz later helps free the Scarecrow and retrieve the oil-can, and the Scarecrow oils the Tin Woodman's joints while the Wizard moves them until the Tin Woodman can walk again.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann Soforth, Queen of Oogaboo, becomes dissatisfied with her small kingdom and decides to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz. Salye's taunt inspires Ann to raise an army of Oogaboo's eighteen men, most of whom she assigns high military ranks. Jo Candy refuses to join, while Jo Files agrees to serve as the sole Private and promises to find a gun-tree. Ann's Army is assembled with four Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, four Captains, two prospective Lieutenants, and Jo Files as Private, though only sixteen men have joined.

records.l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann Soforth is the eldest daughter of Oogaboo's royal family and acts as Queen after her mother leaves in search of King Jol Jemkiph Soforth. Dissatisfied with ruling a tiny, poor kingdom, she decides to conquer the world and organizes an army of Oogaboo's men.

records.l: Salye, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Salye, Ann Soforth's younger sister, refuses to sweep the palace floor and taunts Ann by suggesting that she raise an army and conquer the Land of Oz. She then goes into the back yard to swing in a hammock.

records.l: Queen Ann of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Queen of Oogaboo is Ann Soforth, who rules eighteen men, twenty-seven women, and forty-four children. She decides that conquering the peaceful Land of Oz will allow her to replace Princess Ozma as ruler.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Princess Ozma rules the Land of Oz from the Emerald City and is loved and obeyed by her people. Her army is said to consist of twenty-seven unarmed officers, and she once made her only private soldier a Captain-General and took away his gun.

records.l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Oogaboo is a small, poor valley in a remote mountainous corner of the Land of Oz. It has a royal family for pride, while its people remain under Princess Ozma's overall rule.

records.l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Land of Oz is a beautiful fairyland ruled by Princess Ozma from the Emerald City. Ann considers it peaceful and believes its unarmed officers and gentle people will be easy to overcome.

records.l: world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann declares that she intends to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz. She later imagines conquering other lands and possibly even the moon.

records.l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann's Army is formed from the men of Oogaboo for her planned conquest. Four men become Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, and four Captains; Jo Files becomes the sole Private, while Jo Candy refuses to join.

records.l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Jo Files is a young, intelligent, ambitious man whose orchards produce steel files and story-books. He refuses the officer ranks and volunteers to be the sole Private in Ann's Army, claiming that he will do the fighting; he also knows where to find a gun-tree and plans to pick a musket.

records.l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann plans the conquest of Oz because she believes Princess Ozma's peaceful, unarmed forces can be defeated through surprise and intimidation. She expects to set herself up as ruler in Ozma's place without shedding blood.

records.l: Ann's venture, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ann's venture begins when she leaves the palace to organize an army for her proposed conquest. She believes the venture cannot make her less happy than remaining in Oogaboo and accepts the risks in hopes of gaining greater power.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Three days after Queen Ann Soforth's decision to conquer the world, the Grand Army of Oogaboo assembles outside the royal palace. Ann orders the protesting women to be silent and leads her sixteen officers and the Private, Files, in the army's departure. The officers and Files pass orders down the ranks until Files begins marching, followed by the officers and then Queen Ann. The procession leaves Oogaboo through a narrow mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz, seeking plunder and fame.

records.l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Oogaboo's Grand Army assembles in the square before the royal palace. The army then marches out of Oogaboo through a narrow mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz.

records.l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Grand Army of Oogaboo consists of sixteen officers and the Private, Files. Its members wear impressive uniforms and carry weapons, but General Bunn says they seek plunder rather than trouble and prefer to avoid fighting.

records.l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Queen Ann Soforth appears in a green and gold uniform, commands the protesting women to keep silent, and orders her Army to form ranks. She leads the army out of Oogaboo, expecting it to return rich and famous through conquest, plunder, and heroism.

records.l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Files is the Private in the army and carries a gun, which he has picked. He looks fierce enough to make his commanding officers secretly afraid of him, and he begins the march after receiving the order passed down through the ranks.

records.l: plunder, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Plunder is the main objective of Queen Ann Soforth's campaign. General Bunn says the army wants as much plunder and as little fighting as possible, while Ann connects securing plunder with conquest and becoming heroes.

records.l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Fairyland of Oz lies beyond the narrow mountain pass leading out of Oogaboo. The army takes this pass as it begins its campaign.

records.l: army departure and march, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The army departs after the Generals, Colonels, Majors, and Captains pass the command "For-ward March!" down the ranks to Files. Files marches first, the officers follow, and Queen Ann comes last as the procession enters the mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Princess Ozma is unaware that Ann Soforth and the Army of Oogaboo intend to invade and conquer the Land of Oz. Glinda the Good learns of the plan through her Magic Record Book and uses magic to redirect the mountain pass, sending the army into an adjoining territory instead of Oz. Lost and hungry, the army encounters a Rak, which Private Files wounds with his gun before leading Queen Ann away from it. The army later reaches a valley, camps beside a brook, and continues to claim that it has begun the conquest of the world.

records.l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Princess Ozma is busy caring for her subjects and is unaware of Ann Soforth's plan to invade the Land of Oz.

records.l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Land of Oz is protected from the Army of Oogaboo's intended invasion when Glinda redirects the mountain pass into another territory.

records.l: Glinda the Good, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Glinda the Good, the Official Sorceress of the Kingdom, guards the peace of the Land of Oz. After learning of the army's plan, she uses magic to alter the mountain pass so the army does not enter Oz.

records.l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Ann Soforth, Queen of Oogaboo, leads her army toward the Land of Oz intending to conquer it and the world. When the army reaches an unknown territory instead, she decides to conquer whatever land they find and later praises Private Files for his courage.

records.l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Army of Oogaboo consists of sixteen officers and one private soldier under Ann Soforth. It becomes lost in an unknown, barren country, grows hungry and discouraged, encounters a Rak, and eventually camps beside a brook.

records.l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Oogaboo is the army's homeland, a pretty valley with orchards. After the army passes through the altered mountain route, its members cannot find their way back there.

records.l: magic Record Book of the Sorceress Glinda, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Glinda's Magic Record Book records every event that takes place anywhere, from small incidents to great disasters. By reading it, Glinda learns that Ann Soforth has assembled an army to invade the Land of Oz.

records.l: mountain pass from Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Glinda performs a magical ceremony that causes the mountain pass from Oogaboo to make several turns and twists. After the army emerges into the adjoining territory, the pass disappears behind it.

records.l: adjoining territory, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The adjoining territory is distinct from the Land of Oz and separated from it by an invisible barrier. The Army of Oogaboo enters it without realizing at first that it has failed to reach Oz.

records.l: the officers of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The sixteen officers travel with Ann Soforth through the strange country and become hungry, fretful, and disloyal. When the Rak appears, they panic, fall to the ground, and later run away when it rolls off them.

records.l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Private Files remains cheerful during the army's hardships and becomes a trusted adviser to Queen Ann. He recognizes the approaching cloud as possibly the breath of a Rak, shoots the creature with his gun, and leads the Queen away after the officers flee.

records.l: Rak, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Rak is described as a huge flying, running, and swimming beast that breathes smoke, has a furnace-like body, and feeds on living things. Private Files's bullets break its jaw, left wing, and right leg, but it says that its injuries will heal and that it bears a charmed life.

records.l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Ann Soforth says that the army has started out to conquer the world and treats the unknown territory as part of that objective. Private Files refuses to remain with the Rak because he has an engagement to help Queen Ann achieve the conquest.

records.l: invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Ann Soforth assembles the Army of Oogaboo for an invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz. Glinda prevents the army from reaching Oz by changing the route through the mountain pass.

records.l: the Army's journey, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The army's journey takes it through a barren, rocky country where it finds little food and becomes hopelessly lost. On the third day it encounters the Rak, then travels beyond the creature's smoky breath and camps by a brook.

records.l: the Rak's attack, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Rak's smoky breath darkens the sky and envelops the army, while its body falls upon the sixteen officers after Files shoots it. The Rak tries to crush and eat the army, but it rolls away from the officers, allowing them to escape.

records.l: magic, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Glinda uses magic to alter the mountain pass and divert the Army of Oogaboo from the Land of Oz. The army also possesses magical travel equipment, including tents and a table that grow when placed on the ground.

records.l: gun (Files's gun), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Files's gun is loaded with large, hard bullets gathered from a bullet-tree in Oogaboo. He fires it at the Rak, breaking the creature's jaw, left wing, and right leg.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Betsy Bobbin and Hank, a thin, sad-faced mule, are thrown into the sea when their ship strikes a rock during a storm. Betsy grabs Hank's tail, then helps him climb onto a floating hatch-cover that becomes their raft after the ship catches fire, explodes, and sinks. They endure the night on the raft, and Hank stays awake to guard Betsy while she sleeps. At dawn, they see a beautiful, apparently uninhabited land ahead.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Betsy is thrown from the ship into the sea when it strikes a rock. She grabs Hank's tail, helps him aboard a floating hatch-cover, and rides with him through the storm. After sleeping on the raft, she wakes at dawn and sees land ahead.

records.l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Hank, a thin, sad-faced mule, is thrown into the sea with Betsy. He swims to the raft, and Betsy helps him climb aboard. He comforts Betsy, promises to protect her, and stays awake through the night while she sleeps.

records.l: ship, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The ship strikes a rock during the storm. After Betsy and Hank are thrown overboard, it catches fire, blows up, and sinks beneath the waves.

records.l: storm, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The storm brings waves, lightning, and thunder while the ship is wrecked. It continues after the ship sinks, then wears itself out and passes away with distant growls.

records.l: sea, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Betsy and Hank fall into the dark blue sea after the ship strikes a rock. They float on the raft through the night, while the waves gradually become smaller and easier to ride.

records.l: raft (Betsy's and Hank's raft), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The raft is a hatch-cover torn from the ship's deck. Betsy pulls herself onto it, and Hank swims to it and climbs aboard with her help. It keeps them from drowning and carries them toward land.

records.l: shipwreck, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The shipwreck occurs when the ship strikes a rock during the storm. The ship catches fire, explodes, and sinks, leaving Betsy and Hank on a floating hatch-cover.

records.l: adjoining territory, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: At dawn, Betsy sees land ahead. It appears to be a very beautiful country with banks of flowers between leafy trees, but no people are visible.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Betsy and Hank reach shore on a raft and discover a greenhouse in the Rose Kingdom. Inside, they find rosebushes bearing Roses with girls’ faces, who are frightened by Hank’s braying and demand that the refugees leave. The Roses explain that only Roses are allowed in the kingdom and that the Royal Gardener may cast strangers back into the sea. When the Royal Gardener arrives, he panics at Hank, invokes the Law of the Rose Kingdom, and is interrupted when a man crashes through the greenhouse roof.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Betsy wades ashore from the raft with Hank and enters the greenhouse seeking people, food, and shelter. She explains that she and Hank survived a shipwreck by floating ashore on a raft, and she defends Hank when the Roses and the Royal Gardener are frightened by him.

records.l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Hank follows Betsy ashore and into the greenhouse. His loud braying startles the Roses and causes the Royal Gardener to throw a watering pot over his head; Hank becomes angry and backs toward the Gardener threateningly.

records.l: raft (Betsy's and Hank's raft), Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The raft carrying Betsy and Hank gently reaches the sandy beach. Betsy and Hank had caught hold of it after their ship was wrecked and floated ashore.

records.l: greenhouse, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The greenhouse is a large, splendid structure with thousands of crystal panes. It is filled with potted rosebushes bearing magnificent Roses with girls’ faces, and a man later falls through its roof.

records.l: Roses of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The Roses awaken when Hank brays and are frightened by his harsh voice. They tell Betsy that only Roses are allowed in the Rose Kingdom and urge her and Hank to leave before the Royal Gardener finds them.

records.l: Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The Rose Kingdom is devoted to cultivating the rarest and fairest Roses. Only Roses are allowed there, according to the Roses and the Royal Gardener.

records.l: Royal Gardener, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The Royal Gardener enters the greenhouse carrying a spading fork and a watering pot. Hank’s bray frightens him so badly that he throws the watering pot over Hank’s head, falls down, and hides behind the Roses before shouting that Betsy and Hank are breaking the law.

records.l: Law of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The Law of the Rose Kingdom forbids strangers from entering its domains. The Royal Gardener says that the law makes no exception for shipwrecks.

records.l: shipwreck, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Betsy tells the Roses that she and Hank were on a big ship when a storm wrecked it. They survived by catching hold of a raft and floating ashore.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Shaggy Man falls into the Rose Kingdom while searching for his lost brother, and he, Betsy, and Hank are threatened with death for entering the kingdom. Shaggy uses the Love Magnet to win the Royal Gardener's affection, but it has no effect on the Roses because they have no hearts. Betsy and Shaggy pick the ripe Princess Ozga from the Royal Gardens, but the Roses reject her because they want a male Ruler. The Gardener and the Roses drive Shaggy, Betsy, Hank, and Ozga out of the Rose Kingdom, after which they agree to travel together in search of Shaggy Man's lost brother and the Nome King's cavern.

records.l: Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Shaggy Man falls through the glass roof of the Rose Kingdom's greenhouse after an apple-tree branch breaks. He explains that he is searching for his lost brother and is seeking the hidden passage to the Nome King's underground cavern. He helps Betsy pick Princess Ozga, is driven out of the Rose Kingdom with her, and continues traveling with Betsy, Hank, and Ozga.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Betsy meets Shaggy Man after his fall and learns that he comes from the Land of Oz and knows Ozma and Dorothy. She helps pick Princess Ozga from the Royal Gardens and correctly observes that the Roses have no hearts, so the Love Magnet cannot affect them. After being driven from the Rose Kingdom, she agrees to help Shaggy Man find his lost brother.

records.l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Hank eats Shaggy Man's apple core and kicks the Royal Gardener out of the greenhouse. He is affectionate toward Shaggy Man when he sees the Love Magnet and helps resist the Gardener and the Roses during the expulsion. He leaves the Rose Kingdom with Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Princess Ozga.

records.l: Royal Gardener, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Royal Gardener declares that the strangers have broken the Law and must die, but the Love Magnet makes him affectionate toward Shaggy Man. He explains that the Rose Kingdom has no current Ruler because the previous one withered and no male rose is ripe enough to pick. After Betsy and Shaggy pick Princess Ozga, he tries to drive the group out with a garden fork and finally lets them cross the drawbridge before returning to the greenhouse.

records.l: Rose Princess, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Princess Ozga is a ripe Royal Princess growing on a bush in the Royal Gardens and is a distant cousin of Ozma of Oz. Betsy and Shaggy pick her so that she can rule the Rose Kingdom, but the Roses reject her because she is a girl and they want a King. She is exiled with Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Hank and agrees to help search for Shaggy Man's lost brother.

records.l: the Ugly One, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Shaggy Man's lost brother was a miner in Colorado who entered a gold mine and never came out. He disappeared about ten years earlier, and Shaggy Man suspects that the Nome King captured him.

records.l: Nome King, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Nome King, also called the Metal Monarch and named Ruggedo, lives in an underground cavern and claims to own all the metals hidden in the earth. Shaggy Man suspects that he captured Shaggy Man's brother because he becomes angry when people dig gold from the earth.

records.l: Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Rose Kingdom is a flower-strewn territory surrounded in part by a deep gulf and governed temporarily by the Royal Gardener. Its rulers grow on Royal Bushes, and the kingdom's subjects want a male rose to become King. Shaggy Man, Betsy, Hank, and Princess Ozga are expelled from it.

records.l: Royal Gardens, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Royal Gardens are enclosed by a tall hedge and contain enormous rosebushes on which the members of the Royal Family grow in various stages of maturity. The growing people appear green, lifeless, and unseeing until they are ripe and picked. Princess Ozga is found there fully ripe.

records.l: Roses of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Roses follow the Royal Gardener into the Royal Gardens and insist that the Rose Kingdom must have a male Ruler. They reject Princess Ozga because she is a girl and refuse to respond to the Love Magnet because, as Betsy observes, they have no hearts. Their hidden thorns help drive the group out of the kingdom.

records.l: Love Magnet, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Love Magnet is a small silver horseshoe-shaped enchantment that wins the heart of everyone who looks at it. Shaggy Man uses it to make the Royal Gardener and Hank affectionate toward him, but it has no effect on the Roses because they have no hearts.

records.l: Law of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Law of the Rose Kingdom states that strangers who enter the kingdom must be condemned by the Ruler and put to death. It also treats breaking the greenhouse glass and intruding into any part of the kingdom as violations, although the strangers leave before any Ruler formally condemns them.

records.l: Shaggy Man's search for his lost brother, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Shaggy Man has been searching for his lost brother since learning from the magic Record Book of Glinda that the brother disappeared. He believes the brother may be in the Nome King's underground cavern and plans to keep traveling until someone can direct him there. Betsy, Hank, and Princess Ozga agree to help him.

records.l: exile from the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Royal Gardener and the Roses force Shaggy Man, Betsy, Hank, and Princess Ozga out of the greenhouse and across the drawbridge. The group then enters the bleak, stony country beyond the Rose Kingdom and continues traveling together.

records.l: death sentence for strangers, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Royal Gardener announces that the Law requires every stranger entering the Rose Kingdom to be condemned to death. Because the kingdom has no current Ruler, no formal condemnation occurs, and the strangers ultimately escape by being expelled.

records.l: Tik-Tok of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Polychrome becomes stranded on earth when the Rainbow rises and disappears before she can climb back onto it. She joins Betsy Bobbin, Hank, the Princess, and Shaggy Man as they search for Shaggy Man's brother, who is imprisoned by Ruggedo. At an old well, the travelers recover Tik-Tok, who explains that Ruggedo threw him there after he was sent from Oz to help the search. The reunited party prepares to choose a road toward Ruggedo's hidden cavern when an army approaches.

records.l: Polychrome, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Polychrome is stranded on a rock when the Rainbow disappears before she can return to it. She joins the travelers and says that, as a Daughter of the Rainbow and a sky fairy, she does not fear Ruggedo, although she cannot tell them how to reach his cavern.

records.l: Rainbow, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Rainbow appears over the barren country after rain, carrying its Daughters. It lifts into the sky before Polychrome can climb back aboard, leaving her stranded on earth.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Betsy discovers Polychrome and invites her to join the group. With Shaggy Man, she investigates the old well, helps pull out Tik-Tok, reads the inscriptions on his body, and winds his thought, speech, and action mechanisms.

records.l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Hank travels with the group and carries Betsy when she becomes tired. At the crossroads he investigates the old well by looking into it and braying, helping draw attention to something at its bottom.
