records.l: the rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 17. A Remarkable Journey
records.s: The rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill begins when the travelers reach the river opposite the Magic Isle. The Wizard promises to do his best, sends the Glass Cat to reassure them, and starts preparing his magic, but no rescue method has yet been found.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The Wizard tries many spells and tools to free Trot and Cap'n Bill from the Magic Isle, but none succeeds. He and Dorothy cross to the island on the raft, where the prisoners warn that cutting or pulling up their flesh roots would hurt them. Trot and Cap'n Bill continue shrinking, and they fear that they will soon disappear. Trot asks Dorothy to tell Ozma that they were captured while seeking a birthday present for her.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The Wizard uses powders, liquids, magic words, a pistol, sparks, and nearly every tool in his black bag in an unsuccessful effort to free Trot and Cap'n Bill. He believes he can break enchantments made by ordinary witches and magicians and says that, if necessary, he can make the right key. He takes Dorothy across the river on the raft and tries a magic axe and silver pincers, but abandons both plans when he learns they would injure the prisoners.

records.l: Trot, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: Trot remains rooted in the ground of the Magic Isle despite the Wizard's attempts to free her. She and Cap'n Bill shrink to about half their natural sizes and fear that soon nothing will be left of them. She explains that cutting or pulling up their flesh roots would be like cutting off fingers and toes or pulling teeth, and asks Dorothy to tell Ozma why they were captured.

records.l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: Cap'n Bill remains rooted beside Trot on the Magic Isle and becomes about half his natural size. He warns the Wizard that their roots are flesh roots and that cutting or pulling them up would hurt terribly. He believes that their situation is hopeless and asks that Dorothy tell Ozma what happened if they are destroyed.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: Dorothy suggests going to Glinda when the Wizard's efforts fail and accompanies him across the river on the raft. She is shocked by how small Trot and Cap'n Bill have become and listens as Trot asks her to explain their fate to Ozma.

records.l: the Cowardly Lion, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The Cowardly Lion is afraid that the Magic Isle will capture him, but he volunteers to retrieve the raft. He swims to the island, drags the raft from the beach, and brings it back to the Wizard.

records.l: the Magic Isle, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The Magic Isle holds Trot and Cap'n Bill by roots that have grown from their feet into the ground. It causes them to shrink while also serving as a trap connected to the Magic Flower, which Trot says lures people onto the island and destroys them.

records.l: the raft, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The raft used by Trot and Cap'n Bill remains on the beach of the Magic Isle. The Cowardly Lion brings it across the river, and the Wizard uses it to take himself and Dorothy to the island without stepping onto the island.

records.l: the magic of the Wizard, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The Wizard's magic includes powders, liquids, magic words, explosive sparks, a magic axe, and silver pincers that can grow or shrink. Although he says he can break enchantments known to ordinary witches and magicians, his attempts do not free Trot and Cap'n Bill.

records.l: the island's enchantment trapping people, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The enchantment of the Magic Isle roots Trot and Cap'n Bill to the ground and makes them shrink continuously. The Wizard does not know who created it or what powers that magician possessed, and he is unable to break it with the magic he tries.

records.l: the rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: The rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill is unsuccessful in this unit. The Wizard tries many methods, but cutting or pulling up their roots would cause severe pain, so the prisoners remain trapped and continue shrinking.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's shrinking, The Magic of Oz, 18. The Magic of the Wizard
records.s: Trot and Cap'n Bill shrink every minute while they are trapped on the Magic Isle. When the Glass Cat reports their condition, they are only about half their natural sizes, and Trot warns that soon nothing will be left of them.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Dorothy suggests that the Wizard transform Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees so they can escape the Magic Isle. The transformation succeeds, and although the Hungry Tiger and the Cowardly Lion claim to have eaten the bees, Trot and Cap'n Bill land safely on Dorothy's shoulder and are restored to their normal forms. Cap'n Bill then uses a wooden bark sole to avoid the island's enchantment and retrieves the Magic Flower in its golden flower-pot as a birthday present for Ozma. The Glass Cat receives credit for discovering the flower and leading the others to it.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Dorothy is distressed when Trot and Cap'n Bill become trapped and suggests that the Wizard transform them into bumblebees. She is relieved when they survive and later supports Cap'n Bill's plan to retrieve the Magic Flower for Ozma.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Wizard uses the Magic Word to transform Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees and later restores them to their normal forms. He explains that the island's enchantment affects things made of meat, while wooden and glass objects are not held by it.

records.l: Trot, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Trot is transformed into a bumblebee with Cap'n Bill to escape the Magic Isle, then safely returns and is restored to her normal form. She is happy about the Magic Flower becoming a birthday present for Ozma and promises to tell Ozma how helpful the Glass Cat was.

records.l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Cap'n Bill is transformed into a bumblebee and safely escapes the Magic Isle before being restored to his usual form. He binds a broad piece of bark to his good foot, returns to the island, and retrieves the golden flower-pot containing the Magic Flower for Ozma.

records.l: the Cowardly Lion, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Cowardly Lion says that he ate one of the bees, not knowing that Trot and Cap'n Bill had escaped and that other bees were present.

records.l: the Hungry Tiger, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Hungry Tiger says that he ate one of the bees because the bees were the only food he and the Cowardly Lion could find. He did not know that Trot and Cap'n Bill had transformed into bees.

records.l: the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Glass Cat is credited with discovering the Magic Flower, leading Trot and Cap'n Bill to it, and bringing the Wizard to save them. Its glass feet are noted as unaffected by the Magic Isle's enchantment.

records.l: Ozma, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Ozma is intended to receive the Magic Flower as a birthday present from Trot and Cap'n Bill. Dorothy and Trot expect the unusual flower to surprise her and everyone in the Emerald City.

records.l: the Magic Isle, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Magic Isle traps Trot and Cap'n Bill by causing their feet to take root in the ground. Cap'n Bill later carries away the Magic Flower after protecting his foot with wood.

records.l: the Magic Word, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Magic Word transforms people into other forms and restores them to their former shapes and sizes. The Wizard uses it to change Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees and then back again.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill as bumblebees, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Trot and Cap'n Bill fly from the Magic Isle to the riverbank after the Wizard transforms them into bumblebees. They avoid being eaten by the Hungry Tiger and the Cowardly Lion, land on Dorothy's shoulder, and speak to her in tiny voices.

records.l: Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Magic Flower grows different flowers in succession, including daffodils, tulips, gladioli, yellow roses, and violets. Cap'n Bill retrieves it as a birthday present for Ozma.

records.l: Golden Flower-pot, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The golden flower-pot holds the Magic Flower on the Magic Isle. Cap'n Bill lifts it from the ground, carries it to the raft, and brings it to the riverbank.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's transformation into bumblebees, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The Wizard successfully transforms Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees so they can fly away from the Magic Isle. He later reverses the transformation, restoring their natural forms and sizes and making the roots on their feet disappear.

records.l: Cap'n Bill's retrieval of the Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: Cap'n Bill retrieves the Magic Flower by covering his good foot with wood so the island's enchantment cannot hold it. He removes the golden flower-pot, carries it to the raft, and brings it safely to the riverbank.

records.l: the island's enchantment trapping people, The Magic of Oz, 19. Dorothy and the Bumble Bees
records.s: The island's magic takes root in the feet of people and beasts because they are made of meat and holds them to the ground. Wooden legs, wooden soles, and glass feet are not affected, while leather shoes and wool stockings do not prevent the enchantment.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Wizard's party prepares to carry the Magic Flower to the Emerald City, using a magically made board secured to the Cowardly Lion's back. During the journey, the Glass Cat repeatedly pulls the monkeys' tails, until the monkeys escape their damaged cage and cover her in blue mud. The Wizard decides the Glass Cat deserves this punishment, though Dorothy helps clean her eyes and ears so she can travel. The Glass Cat later runs away to wash herself and is found clean at the Royal Palace, where she ignores the travelers.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Wizard uses his Little Saw to make a fitted board for carrying the Magic Flower and creates tents and supper by magic. He says the Glass Cat deserves punishment for teasing the monkeys, refuses to punish the monkeys for their revenge, and allows the Glass Cat to remain covered in blue mud until the Emerald City.

records.l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: Cap'n Bill plans to make a board for the Cowardly Lion and holds the Magic Flower's pot during the journey. He later bends the golden wires of the monkeys' cage back into position.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: Dorothy helps arrange for the Cowardly Lion to carry the Magic Flower and rides the Hungry Tiger with Trot while carrying the monkeys' cage. She is horrified by the Glass Cat's condition, washes the cat's eyes and ears, and agrees that the punishment is probably enough.

records.l: Trot, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: Trot warns that the Magic Flower could be smashed if it fell from the Cowardly Lion's back. She rides the Hungry Tiger with Dorothy and helps carry the monkeys' cage.

records.l: the Cowardly Lion, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Cowardly Lion agrees to carry the Magic Flower if it can be fastened securely. The Little Saw makes a board fitted to his back, and the flower-pot is placed on it.

records.l: the Hungry Tiger, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Hungry Tiger carries Dorothy and Trot during the journey. When the Glass Cat disturbs the sleeping monkeys, he strikes at her, misses, and bends two bars of the monkeys' cage.

records.l: the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Glass Cat repeatedly pulls the monkeys' tails for amusement, causing them to retaliate by covering her in dark blue mud. The mud makes her dull blue and prevents her from seeing or hearing until Dorothy cleans her eyes and ears. She later runs away to a nearby lake, washes herself clean, and is found at the Royal Palace pretending not to notice the travelers.

records.l: the twelve cake monkeys, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The monkeys are carried in their cage during the journey and are tormented by the Glass Cat pulling their tails. After the Hungry Tiger bends two cage bars, they use the opening to surround the Glass Cat, smear her with blue mud, and return to their cage.

records.l: Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Magic Flower is too heavy for Cap'n Bill to carry all the way, so it is placed in its flower-pot on a specially fitted board tied to the Cowardly Lion's back. Cap'n Bill walks beside the Lion and holds the flower-pot to prevent accidents.

records.l: the cage of monkeys, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The monkeys' cage is carried between Dorothy and Trot on the Hungry Tiger. The Hungry Tiger bends two of its bars, allowing the monkeys to squeeze out, and Cap'n Bill later repairs the bars.

records.l: the blue mud, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The blue mud lies along the banks of a stream and is thick and slimy. The monkeys smear it over the Glass Cat, including her eyes and ears, and it dries hard on her body like paint.

records.l: Emerald City, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The party travels toward the Emerald City with the Magic Flower and their companions. The Wizard intends the Glass Cat to arrive there still covered in blue mud, but she escapes and washes herself before the travelers reach the Royal Palace.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The journey proceeds slowly because the Wizard and Cap'n Bill walk while the others carry the Magic Flower and the monkeys. The party camps beside a brook, resumes traveling the next day, and eventually arrives at the Royal Palace.

records.l: the monkeys' revenge on the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The monkeys take revenge after the Glass Cat repeatedly pulls their tails. They escape through the bent cage bars, seize the Glass Cat, cover her in blue mud, and return to the cage.

records.l: the Glass Cat's punishment, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Wizard considers the Glass Cat's blue-mud covering a punishment for teasing the monkeys and plans to let her be seen that way in the Emerald City. Dorothy cleans the mud from the cat's eyes and ears, but the Glass Cat must continue traveling with the mud on her body until she runs away to wash.

records.l: teasing the monkeys, The Magic of Oz, 20. The Monkeys Have Trouble
records.s: The Glass Cat teases the monkeys by slyly pulling their tails through the bars of their cage. Her teasing causes the monkeys to retaliate, and the Wizard says the punishment is deserved.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Dorothy and her friends arrive at the Royal Palace while Ozma hears Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., appeal for punishment of students from the Royal Athletic College. The students rebelled after Professor Wogglebug tried to feed them Square-Meal Tablets instead of ordinary food, and the Senior Class threw him into a river. While Ozma considered the case, Cap'n Bill secretly carried the Magic Flower to Trot's room and the Wizard of Oz moved a cage of monkeys to his tower room. Trot cared for the Magic Flower, while the Wizard trained the intelligent monkeys for Ozma's birthday.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Dorothy arrived at the Royal Palace with her friends. She was among the friends who knew that the Magic Flower had been brought safely to the palace.

records.l: Royal Palace, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Royal Palace was where Ozma held high court in her Throne Room. Its top towers included a private room belonging to the Wizard of Oz, and its marble stables housed the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger.

records.l: Ozma, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Ozma heard Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., appeal for punishment of the rebellious Senior Class. She had refused to eat Square-Meal Tablets in place of ordinary food, so she was probably not severe with the students.

records.l: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., was Principal of the Royal Athletic College and the inventor of the Tablets of Learning and the Square-Meal Tablet. After insisting that students eat the Square-Meal Tablets instead of ordinary food, he was seized by the Senior Class and thrown into a river, where he remained helpless for three days before a fisherman dragged him out. He then brought the Senior Class to the Emerald City and appealed to Ozma for punishment.

records.l: College of Athletic Arts, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The College of Athletic Arts is located in the Munchkin Country, not far from the Emerald City. Its students use Tablets of Learning so they can devote their time to athletic exercises and sports.

records.l: Royal Athletic College, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Royal Athletic College is the college of which Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., is Principal. Its Senior Class rebelled against his attempt to replace ordinary meals with Square-Meal Tablets.

records.l: Emerald City, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Emerald City was where Ozma heard Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E.'s, appeal against the Senior Class.

records.l: Tablets of Learning, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Tablets of Learning instantly teach subjects such as mathematics, geography, spelling, handwriting, history, mechanics, home cooking, and agriculture. They allow students of the Royal Athletic College to spend their time on athletic exercises and sports instead of studying from books.

records.l: Square-Meal Tablet, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Square-Meal Tablet is a tiny tablet containing the condensed equivalent of soup, fried fish, a roast, a salad, and a dessert, with the nourishment of a full meal. Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., fed it to his students instead of ordinary food, but they refused it because they wanted to enjoy the taste of their meals.

records.l: Senior Class, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Senior Class of the Royal Athletic College seized Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., and threw him into a river after he insisted that the students eat Square-Meal Tablets. The class was brought to the Emerald City so Ozma could decide how to punish its rebellion.

records.l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Cap'n Bill secretly carried the golden flower-pot containing the Magic Flower to Trot's room. He succeeded without being seen by anyone except Jellia Jamb.

records.l: Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Magic Flower was moved from its island to Trot's room in the Royal Palace. It did not seem to lose any of its magic after being moved, and Trot believed Ozma would prize it as a delightful treasure.

records.l: Trot, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Trot kept the Magic Flower in her room, watered it every day, and allowed only Betsy Bobbin and Dorothy to see its blossoms. She was sure that Ozma would value the magical plant.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The Wizard of Oz carried the cage of monkeys to a private room in one of the top towers of the Royal Palace. He began training the monkeys, treating them kindly and gently as he prepared them for Ozma's birthday.

records.l: the monkeys, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: The twelve tiny monkeys were kept in a cage in the Wizard of Oz's tower room. They were intelligent, learned every trick the Wizard taught them, and promised to do their best for Ozma's birthday.

records.l: Ozma's birthday, The Magic of Oz, 21. The College of Athletic Arts
records.s: Ozma's birthday was the great occasion for which the Wizard of Oz trained the twelve tiny monkeys.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma, the beloved fairy Ruler of the Fairyland of Oz, celebrates her birthday with festivities throughout the land and a grand feast at her palace. Her guests include many trusted friends, while her animal friends sit at a separate table. Dorothy presents Ozma with a Surprise Cake containing twelve performing monkeys, and other guests give her remarkable gifts, including the Magic Flower and an emerald gown made by Glinda. Ozma examines and gratefully accepts her birthday gifts after the banquet.

records.l: Ozma, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma is the beautiful fairy Ruler of the Fairyland of Oz and is greatly beloved for being sweet, gentle, and fair. She celebrates her birthday with a feast, welcomes friends and animals, receives many gifts, and is especially delighted by the Magic Flower and an emerald gown.

records.l: Oz, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The Fairyland of Oz is ruled by Ozma and contains four countries, the Winkie, Gillikin, Munchkin, and Quadling Countries, as well as the Emerald City. Its people prepare widespread celebrations for Ozma's birthday.
records.t: The Fairyland of Oz is ruled by Ozma and contains four countries—the Winkie, Gillikin, Munchkin, and Quadling Countries—as well as the Emerald City. Its people prepare widespread celebrations for Ozma's birthday.

records.l: Ozma's birthday, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma's birthday is treated as an occasion for feasting and rejoicing. Celebrations, decorations, processions, games, plays, and other festivities are prepared throughout the Land of Oz.

records.l: Ozma's birthday feast, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma holds a grand birthday feast in her palace for her closest friends and their animal companions. The guests dine at a long table, while the animals are seated at a smaller table and the birthday gifts are arranged on another table.

records.l: Emerald City, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The Emerald City is Ozma's magnificent capital, where her palace stands and where Aunt Em and Uncle Henry have a cozy home. Its people often visit Ozma's gardens and palace, and they prepare birthday celebrations for her.

records.l: Royal Palace, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma's palace stands in the center of an extensive garden containing trees, flowering shrubs, statuary, fountains, an aquarium, birds, and the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion. Its gates remain open, and it hosts Ozma's birthday feast.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Dorothy attends Ozma's birthday feast and sits next to the Scarecrow of Oz. She gives Ozma the Surprise Cake, urges Ozma to cut it, and is delighted when the twelve monkeys emerge and perform.

records.l: Trot, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Trot attends Ozma's birthday feast and sits opposite the Tin Woodman, next to Cap'n Bill. She tells Ozma the story of the adventures involved in obtaining the Magic Flower.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Betsy Bobbin attends Ozma's birthday feast and is seated next to Aunt Em and before the Shaggy Man.

records.l: the Scarecrow of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The Scarecrow of Oz sits at Ozma's right during the birthday banquet. Although his straw-stuffed body is not beautiful, his happy nature and shrewd wit make him a general favorite, and he politely entertains the guests without eating.

records.l: the Tin Woodman, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The Tin Woodman sits at Ozma's left at the birthday banquet and has his metal body brightly polished for the occasion. He is Emperor of the Winkie Country and, like the Scarecrow, does not eat but helps entertain the guests.

records.l: Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Cap'n Bill attends Ozma's birthday feast beside Trot. He is credited with bravely carrying the golden flower-pot containing the Magic Flower away from the enchanted Isle.

records.l: Glinda the Good, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Glinda the Good sits at the foot of the banquet table in the place of honor facing Ozma. She leads Ozma to the table of gifts and has woven an exquisite gown from strands drawn from pure emeralds with the help of her maidens.

records.l: Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The Magic Flower blooms gloriously during the banquet, producing mammoth blossoms that fill the room with delicate fragrance. Ozma receives it as a birthday gift and says she will place it in her boudoir.

records.l: Ozma's birthday gifts, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma's birthday gifts are placed on a large table in the Banquet Hall. They include the Magic Flower and a marvelous gown woven by Glinda and her maidens from strands drawn from pure emeralds, and Ozma examines them all before thanking the donors.

records.l: Dorothy and the Wizard's Surprise Cake, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Dorothy and the Wizard's Surprise Cake is a huge frosted cake decorated with candy flowers and candles, bearing the words "OZMA'S Birthday Cake from Dorothy and the Wizard." When Ozma cuts it, it releases twelve tiny monkeys and their golden band instruments.

records.l: the twelve cake monkeys, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The twelve cake monkeys leap from the Surprise Cake and bow to Ozma while congratulating her. They dance, perform acrobatic feats, and play a jolly tune on golden band instruments before the banquet ends.

records.l: Ozma's birthday celebrations, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: Ozma's birthday celebrations take place throughout the Land of Oz. Brass bands prepare processions in the four countries and the Emerald City, while homes and buildings are decorated and people hold games, plays, and other festivities.

records.l: the birthday banquet, The Magic of Oz, 22. Ozma's Birthday Party
records.s: The birthday banquet includes Ozma's closest friends, royal courtiers, and animal companions. Ozma enters to an orchestra's march and a great cheer, enjoys the guests' company, and later watches the twelve cake monkeys perform before the banquet concludes.

records.l: The Magic of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Dorothy, the Wizard, and Ozma decide to restore two enchanted nuts to their natural forms beside the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion. The Wizard transforms the hickory-nut into Kiki Aru, who drinks the Water of Oblivion and forgets everything, including his identity and magic. The walnut becomes Ruggedo, who threatens to conquer Oz before drinking the water and losing his memories. Ozma keeps both Kiki Aru and the now-innocent Ruggedo in the Land of Oz so they cannot return to their former wicked ways.

records.l: Dorothy, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Dorothy suggests using the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion to make the transformed magicians forget all the magic they know. She helps restore Kiki Aru and Ruggedo by arranging for them to drink the water, and she leads the memoryless Kiki Aru to a seat beside her.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Wizard explains that the two nuts contain the beast magicians and worries that restoring them could be dangerous. He uses the Magic Transformation Word to turn the hickory-nut into Kiki Aru and the walnut into Ruggedo, making each one very thirsty so that each drinks the Water of Oblivion.

records.l: Ozma, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Ozma insists that the enchanted magicians should be freed from their unnatural forms, despite the danger they may pose. After Kiki Aru and Ruggedo lose their memories, she decides to keep them in the Land of Oz and teach them to be true and considerate of others.

records.l: Kiki Aru, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Kiki Aru is restored from the hickory-nut to his natural form as a Hyup boy. He drinks the Water of Oblivion and forgets his name, history, magic, and everything else he knew, becoming an innocent and pleasant boy whom Ozma decides to keep in the Land of Oz.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Ruggedo is restored from the walnut to his natural form as the Nome King. Before drinking the Water of Oblivion, he recognizes his enemies and threatens to conquer Oz, but afterward he forgets his identity, his plans, and all other knowledge, becoming harmless and innocent.

records.l: Oz, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: Oz is the land Ruggedo threatens to conquer and the place whose people he once sought to rule. Ozma and the Wizard decide that Ruggedo must remain in the Land of Oz so he cannot return to his former evil ways.

records.l: Land of Oz, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Land of Oz becomes the new home for Kiki Aru and the memoryless Ruggedo. Ozma believes that by keeping them there, they can learn no evil and remain innocent.

records.l: the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Fountain of the Water of Oblivion is beside the marble bench where Dorothy, the Wizard, and Ozma discuss the two enchanted magicians. It provides the water that Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink after being restored to their natural forms.

records.l: the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Water of Oblivion causes anyone who drinks it to forget everything previously known. Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink it after their transformations and lose their identities, memories, and knowledge of magic.

records.l: the Magic Word, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Magic Transformation Word is the powerful word used to restore the two enchanted nuts to their natural forms. The Wizard says that its power depends not only on the word itself but also on how it is pronounced, and he uses it in the form "Pyrzqxgl."

records.l: the transformation of the magicians, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The Wizard transforms the hickory-nut into Kiki Aru, a Hyup boy, and the walnut into Ruggedo, the Nome King. He makes both newly restored beings very thirsty so they will drink the Water of Oblivion.

records.l: the Water of Oblivion's memory-erasing effect, The Magic of Oz, 23. The Fountain of Oblivion
records.s: The memory-erasing effect removes a drinker's memories, identity, knowledge of magic, and understanding of personal history. It makes Kiki Aru innocent and makes Ruggedo forget his anger and plans to conquer Oz, leaving both harmless.

The document is a fantasy adventure in which Princess Ozma, ruler of Oz, vanishes along with crucial magical objects: her Magic Picture, Glinda the Good’s Great Book of Records, and the Wizard of Oz’s magic tools. Dorothy, Betsy Bobbin, Trot, Scraps, the Wizard, and many friends organize searches across Oz, while Cayke the Cookie Cook and the Frogman separately pursue Cayke’s stolen diamond-studded gold dishpan, a family heirloom that helps its owner cook well. Dorothy’s party travels through the Winkie Country and dangerous unknown lands, crossing the Merry-Go-Round Mountains, entering the illusory City of Thi, passing the Great Orchard, and visiting Herku. There they learn that Ugu the Shoemaker, a powerful magician in a wickerwork castle, may be responsible. Meanwhile, Cayke and the Frogman follow clues through the Winkie Country and Bear Center. The Lavender Bear King and the truth-telling Little Pink Bear identify Ugu as the thief and join their expedition. Near Ugu’s castle, the two parties unite. Ugu has used Cayke’s dishpan and inherited magic to steal the magical possessions and abduct Ozma, intending to become master of Oz. The rescuers overcome his defenses, a ring of fire, a steel wall, and illusory girl-soldiers, and enter the castle. Ugu traps them in an upside-down rotating hall, but Dorothy uses the Magic Belt’s daily wish to free them. When Ugu threatens them, Dorothy transforms him into a dove; he escapes briefly in Cayke’s dishpan. The Magic Picture initially suggests that Ozma has become a black spot, but the Little Pink Bear reveals that she is hidden as a golden peach pit in Button-Bright’s pocket. The Wizard opens the pit, freeing Ozma. The party returns to the Emerald City, Toto regains his growl, and Ozma restores the stolen items. Ugu, still a dove, repents and is forgiven by Dorothy. Finally, Cayke receives her jeweled dishpan back from Ozma.

records.l: Ozma, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Ozma is the lovely, beautiful, beloved girl ruler, princess, and powerful fairy who is the Supreme Ruler and protector of the Emerald City and all the Land of Oz. She lives in her royal palace, rules its people, loves Dorothy, values Glinda the Good as a servant, and is guarded by the Cowardly Lion on state occasions. Her treasures include the Magic Picture, which can reveal people approaching her palace with intent to conquer it, and she wears a chain of emeralds. She forbids magic to all subjects except Glinda and the Wizard of Oz. She cannot be destroyed by any magic, though she can be overpowered and confined. Ozma disappears suddenly from her royal apartments in the Emerald City without telling Dorothy or her friends. Her loss causes widespread grief, and friends and travelers search for her through places including the City of Thi, where she is not found. They suspect she has been stolen, eventually believing that Ugu the Shoemaker took her along with magic from the Emerald City. Ugu confronts Ozma in her apartments, takes her magical possessions, binds her in the Magic Dishpan, carries her to the Wicker Castle, and imprisons her. Although she remains the ruler of Oz despite Ugu's claim, he hides her so completely that even the Magic Picture shows only a round black spot. At last, Ozma is discovered confined within a golden peach pit in Button-Bright's pocket. The Wizard opens the pit, and she emerges from a pink cloud-like haze, freed from enchantment. After hearing how her friends conquered Ugu, she thanks those who helped, invites the Bear King to visit her palace, confiscates Ugu's magical possessions, and returns triumphantly to the Emerald City. Restored before the dishpan is returned, she gives Cayke the Cookie Cook the diamond-studded gold dishpan.

records.l: Dorothy, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Dorothy is a mortal Earth and Kansas girl who lives in a delightful suite in Ozma’s royal palace as a Princess of Oz and Ozma’s dearest, devoted friend. When Ozma disappears, Dorothy searches the palace, helps use the Magic Picture, and becomes deeply determined to find her, convinced that a wicked person is responsible. She leads and joins a traveling search party with Betsy, Trot, the Wizard, Toto, and other companions through the Winkie Country and toward Ugu the Shoemaker’s castle. Loyal to Ozma as ruler, she repeatedly defends Ozma’s authority, refuses unsuitable food and offers, protects and scolds her companions, and persists through dangers including mountains, thistles, traps, and hostile-looking soldiers. Wearing the Magic Belt, she is protected during the journey and later secretly learns its powers. She uses it to reverse a rotating-room trap, freeing her companions, then confronts Ugu and transforms him into a dove, defeating the magician who stole Ozma and magic from the Emerald City. After Ozma is released, Dorothy embraces her, recounts the victory, and keeps Ugu transformed until he reforms. When Ugu expresses sorrow, Dorothy forgives him, saying that anyone who is sorry has to be forgiven.

records.l: Betsy, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Betsy Bobbin is a little, young mortal girl from the outside world who lives in Ozma’s royal palace, is Dorothy’s friend and one year older than her, and has the mule Hank as her mount. She suggests a trip to the Munchkin Country and using the Magic Picture to find Ozma. Alarmed by Ozma’s disappearance and stolen magical possessions, she joins the search, brings and rides Hank, questions reports of an unknown country, agrees to enter it, identifies thistles hurting the Lion and Hank, and reaches the city with the group. She supports Ugu’s forgiveness because he seems sorry and good.

records.l: Trot, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Trot is a young mortal girl from the outside world who lives in Ozma’s royal palace and is Dorothy’s friend, one year younger than Dorothy. When Ozma is missing, she joins Dorothy, Betsy Bobbin, and the others in searching through the Munchkin Country. Troubled that Oz lacks effective soldiers or policemen, she travels in the Red Wagon and on the Woozy’s back, questioning uncertain stories of the Thistle-Eaters, Herkus, and giants. She observes that appearances may deceive, that crossing the thistle field strains the Wizard, and that the journey has not yet found Royal Ozma. She continues through Thi, the City of Herku, and toward the western mountains. She also supports Ugu’s forgiveness because he seems truly sorry and good.

records.l: Scraps, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Scraps is a magically alive Patchwork Girl: a soft-bodied, cotton-stuffed person made from a quilt cut and stuffed into shape, with a round quilt head, brown-yarn hair, and two black button eyes. Daffy, dancing, clever, and a favorite of Oz’s subjects, she has much brains despite her stuffing. She never sleeps at night, sees well in darkness, cannot get lost, and is proud to be Oz’s unique Original and Only Cotton-Stuffed person. She is friends with the Woozy, rides it during the search for Ozma, and spends a sleepless night talking with it and the Sawhorse. From the start she suspects Ozma was stolen and presses the group to confront wickedness. She repeatedly leads through danger: devising a harness-strap crossing of a gulf, surviving the whirling mountains, recognizing and dancing through the Wall of Illusion, questioning the High Coco-Lorum, finding fruit and the lost Button-Bright, and bringing the Frogman to the others. Immune to Ugu’s actions, she mocks fear and helps expose another illusion by dancing through apparent soldiers. At Ugu’s, she urges action; when the room is restored, she falls from a chandelier and is rolled and patted back into shape.

records.l: Button-Bright, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Button-Bright is a venture-some boy, described as an American boy from Philadelphia and as coming from Emerald City. What matters most about him is his repeated habit of getting lost, then being found again, alongside his curious, skeptical questions and his unwitting role in carrying Ozma. Traveling with the Wizard on the Wooden Sawhorse and later in the Red Wagon, he supports entering dangerous country, notices the reappearing mysterious city, and argues that what can be seen and heard must exist somewhere. He follows Scraps through a wall, becomes invisible until entering the city, and asks about its dragon, the Herkus, and its music. In the Great Orchard he wanders away, eats an enchanted peach, and keeps its golden pit. He questions claims about Herku's strength and Ugu the Shoemaker. Lost again while the travelers prepare for Ugu's castle, he falls into a deep hole while wandering in moonlight and is rescued by Dorothy and the others; he jokes that he has been found again. Finally, while emptying his pocket of a peg top, string, rubber ball, and the golden pit, he reveals the pit that had unknowingly carried Ozma. Ozma emerges, and Button-Bright recalls the peach as the best he ever ate and tries to tell how he rescued her.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Wizard of Oz is a wizard and magician who lives in Ozma's palace, has learned powerful magic from Glinda the Good, and owns a black bag of wizardry tools. When Ozma disappears, along with the Magic Picture and the Great Book of Records, his bag is stolen as well. Deprived of his wizardry, he seeks Glinda's aid and joins Dorothy's party, becoming a principal problem-solver and leader in the search for Ozma. He travels on the Wooden Sawhorse, helps organize the Red Wagon expedition and supplies, and argues that the party must investigate dangerous unknown places. Although he repeatedly admits that he can do little without his tools, he protects and guides the travelers: he crosses last with blankets fastened around himself, makes a blanket path across thistles, questions people in Thi and Herku, gathers food, searches for missing companions, and presses the group onward. Learning of Ugu the Shoemaker, he proposes joining forces with Frogman's party and explains that Ugu has the stolen magical objects, Glinda's recipes for sorcery, and the Great Book of Records. Approaching Ugu's castle, he helps assess its defenses and rescue companions. He destroys a circle of fire with a lighted match, explains how to remove a steel wall with a pin, and recognizes girl-soldiers as an optical illusion. Inside the wicker castle he challenges Ugu and organizes an unsuccessful effort to recover the stolen magic. Finally, he questions the little Pink Bear, correctly reasons about its answer, and opens a golden peach pit to find Ozma inside. After Ozma's return, he helps recount the adventure, restore the Magic Picture to her boudoir, and again performs tricks with his recovered tools.

records.l: Woozy, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: Woozy is a peculiar, square-bodied animal and thick-skinned creature with tough, leather-like skin. Though its movements seem clumsy, it travels with remarkable swiftness, eats fruit readily, and can stay awake for a month; when asleep, it snores loudly. A great friend of Scraps, it joins the search party, carries Scraps through the Emerald City and into the Winkie Country, then follows her across the gulf to protect her despite first suggesting they turn back. Bounced across mountains, it reaches safety unharmed. It fearlessly crosses thistles, carries companions and Hank, and later discusses beauty, insisting loveliness includes inward as well as outward qualities.

records.l: Land of Oz, The Lost Princess of Oz
records.s: The Land of Oz is a wonderful, astonishing fairyland ruled by Princess Ozma, its girl and supreme ruler. It is divided into four great countries, Munchkin, Quadling, Gillikin, and Winkie, with the Emerald City at their meeting place; the Winkie Country occupies a quarter of its territory. Oz is large, with remote cracks, corners, regions, and queer people, some of whom may never visit the Emerald City. Its inhabitants generally live under Ozma’s rule and are considered good and considerate, though unexplored regions may contain wicked creatures. No one can die or be killed there, and it has no soldiers or policemen apart from one soldier. Animals, birds, and fishes can speak the human language. The action begins with Ozma’s rule over this deathless land. After Glinda’s magical supplies are stolen and Ozma disappears, inhabitants search through Oz’s countries while the Wizard and others refuse to seek a new ruler. Ugu steals magic from the Emerald City, Glinda’s castle, and the Yip Country, seeks Oz’s magical possessions, and plans to master the realm. Expeditions oppose him, and the Wizard maintains that Ozma remains ruler wherever she is hidden. The whole land ends by celebrating Ozma’s safe return with cheering, decorations, feasting, and a week of festivities.
