After fleeing giant soldiers, they return, recognize the giants as transformed friends and relatives, and gather. Twelve intelligent, good-tempered monkeys volunteer to accompany the Wizard of Oz to the Emerald City for Ozma's birthday. Temporarily three inches high and confined in a golden cage, they learn and perform the Wizard's tricks.

records.l: the forest, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The forest is a place ruled by Gugu, containing clearings, a hollow tree, monkeys, and a vast assemblage of animals. Kiki's transforming power scatters its inhabitants through the jungles. Ruggedo searches there, conspirators meet, and the Wizard hides. Trees imprison giant soldiers, and the animals later welcome the Wizard and Dorothy as trusted friends.

records.l: the black bag, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Wizard’s black bag holds the magic tools needed to break transformations. Kiki Aru steals it, hides it hanging from a tree branch, and it is not found during the search. The Glass Cat later finds it, hides it under leaves, guides the Wizard to it, and enables its recovery.

records.l: Magic Tools, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Magic Tools inside the black bag can break enchantments when used properly. Kiki cannot identify their uses; when the Wizard regains them with the bag, they restore his confidence to rescue Trot and Cap'n Bill.

records.l: the enchantments, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Enchantments transform the Wizard of Oz into a Fox and Dorothy into a Lamb. Though the Wizard says they are easy to break with known methods and tools, Kiki's taking the black bag leaves the needed magic tools unavailable.

records.l: the search for the Black Bag, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_undertaken_by the Wizard of Oz [after the bag is lost] The Wizard, Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, the Hungry Tiger, and Gugu search the clearing and surrounding forest for the missing black bag. After the Glass Cat arrives, they decide to search for the Goose first, believing he may help them find the Magician and recover the bag.

records.l: the monkeys, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The monkeys, fifty in a clearing, gather in trees and are chosen for Ruggedo’s giant army; Kiki Aru transforms at least six into uniformed giant men carrying sharp swords.

records.l: the giant army, The Magic of Oz
records.s: A planned army of fifty monkeys transformed into uniformed, sword-carrying fifty-foot men begins with six giants created before the Wizard stops Kiki Aru; they remain standing in the forest.

records.l: the hollow tree, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The hollow tree provides hiding places for the Wizard of Oz in Fox form and later Kiki Aru when he whispers the Magic Word; through its opening, the Wizard hears the word and uses it for transformations.

records.l: the hickory-nut, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a transformed form of Kiki Aru [created by the Wizard] The hickory-nut is the form into which the Wizard transforms Kiki Aru. The Wizard picks it up and places it in his pocket as proof of what happened.

records.l: the walnut, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a transformed form of Ruggedo [created by the Wizard] The walnut is the form into which the Wizard transforms Ruggedo after correctly recalling the Magic Word. The Wizard picks up the walnut and places it in his pocket.

records.l: the Lonesome Duck, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Lonesome Duck is the only duck in the Land of Oz, a uniquely colored, immortal bird living alone in its diamond palace a little way up the river, with food supplied by magic. It has no family, relations, friends, or occupation, dislikes everyone it meets, and is lonesome. Its simple magic serves its needs: when it cannot free Trot and Cap'n Bill, it performs an incantation to create each of them a comfortable, sturdy toadstool, then leaves.

is_caused_by lack of friends [and lack of family or occupation] Loneliness is described by the Lonesome Duck as existing for years without family, friends, or anything to do. The Duck claims that its disagreeable nature prevents it from making friends, while Trot argues that helping others could end its loneliness.

records.l: six giant soldiers, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Six giant soldiers, enchanted former monkeys, are made fifty-foot-tall men by Kiki Aru. Trapped among forest trees, they cannot move, raise their arms, or draw their sharp swords. They wear caps with red and yellow plumes until the Wizard of Oz breaks the enchantment and restores their natural monkey forms.

records.l: enchantment of the giant soldiers, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_broken_by Wizard of Oz [restoring the soldiers to their natural forms] The enchantment turns six monkeys into enormous soldiers and leaves them helpless among the forest trees. The Wizard breaks it after Rango agrees to let twelve monkeys accompany him to the Emerald City.

records.l: golden cage, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_made_from silver-and-gold dish [transformed by magic] The Wizard creates a golden cage with silver bars by using powder and fire in a silver-and-gold dish. The twelve selected monkeys are reduced to about three inches high and placed safely inside it.

records.l: the Magic Plant, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Magic Plant, called the world's most beautiful by the Cowardly Lion, grows in a golden flower-pot on the Magic Isle. It rapidly produces hundreds of varied flowers: picked blooms remain perfect a long time, while unpicked ones soon disappear and are replaced.

records.l: the rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The rescue of Trot and Cap'n Bill begins when travelers reach the river opposite the Magic Isle. The Wizard promises help, sends the Glass Cat to reassure them, and prepares magic. His attempts fail because cutting or pulling their roots would cause severe pain, leaving them trapped and shrinking.

records.l: the cage of monkeys, The Magic of Oz
records.s: A cage made with golden wires holds the monkeys until the Hungry Tiger bends two bars; they escape, and Cap'n Bill later repairs the bars.

records.l: the twelve cake monkeys, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The twelve cake monkeys are small, long-tailed monkeys kept and carried in a cage. After the Glass Cat teases them by pulling their tails, and the Hungry Tiger bends two bars, they escape briefly to surround her and smear her with blue mud before returning to the cage. At Ozma's birthday party, they leap from a Surprise Cake, bow, dance, perform acrobatics, and play golden instruments.

records.l: the magic of the Wizard, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_not_equal_to the magic of the Magic Isle [according to the Wizard's embarrassment] The Wizard's magic includes powders, liquids, magic words, explosive sparks, a magic axe, and silver pincers that can grow or shrink. Although he says he can break enchantments known to ordinary witches and magicians, his attempts do not free Trot and Cap'n Bill.

records.l: the island's enchantment trapping people, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Magic Isle’s enchantment takes root in the feet of people and beasts made of meat, trapping them in the ground and making them shrink continuously. It roots Trot and Cap’n Bill when they walk on the island. Wood and glass, including wooden legs or soles and glass feet, are unaffected; leather shoes and wool stockings fail. The Wizard cannot break the magic or identify its creator.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's shrinking, The Magic of Oz
records.s: reduces half their natural sizes [at the time the Glass Cat reports it] Trot and Cap'n Bill shrink every minute while they are trapped on the Magic Isle. When the Glass Cat reports their condition, they are only about half their natural sizes, and Trot warns that soon nothing will be left of them.

records.l: the birthday banquet, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Ozma's birthday banquet gathers her closest friends, royal courtiers, and animal companions, with Ozma at the head table. She enters to an orchestra's march and cheering, enjoys the company, then watches twelve cake monkeys perform before it ends.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill as bumblebees, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Transformed into bumblebees, Trot and Cap'n Bill fly from the Magic Isle to the riverbank, avoid the Hungry Tiger and Cowardly Lion, then speak to Dorothy.

records.l: Trot and Cap'n Bill's transformation into bumblebees, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Wizard transforms Trot and Cap'n Bill into bumblebees to escape the Magic Isle, then reverses it, restoring their natural forms, sizes, and root-free feet.

records.l: Cap'n Bill's retrieval of the Magic Flower, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Cap'n Bill retrieves the Magic Flower from the Magic Isle by covering his good foot with wood, removing its golden pot, and carrying it safely to the riverbank.

records.l: the blue mud, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The blue mud is thick, slimy, dark blue, and paintlike when dry; from stream banks, monkeys smear it over the Glass Cat until it hardens on her body, eyes, and ears, then she washes it off.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_slow slow journey [because the Wizard and Cap'n Bill travel on foot] The journey proceeds slowly because the Wizard and Cap'n Bill walk while the others carry the Magic Flower and the monkeys. The party camps beside a brook, resumes traveling the next day, and eventually arrives at the Royal Palace.

records.l: the monkeys' revenge on the Glass Cat, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a revenge [tit-for-tat for teasing] The monkeys take revenge after the Glass Cat repeatedly pulls their tails. They escape through the bent cage bars, seize the Glass Cat, cover her in blue mud, and return to the cage.

records.l: the Glass Cat's punishment, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a punishment [being covered in blue mud and publicly shamed] The Wizard considers the Glass Cat's blue-mud covering a punishment for teasing the monkeys and plans to let her be seen that way in the Emerald City. Dorothy cleans the mud from the cat's eyes and ears, but the Glass Cat must continue traveling with the mud on her body until she runs away to wash.

records.l: teasing the monkeys, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a tail-pulling [done by the Glass Cat] The Glass Cat teases the monkeys by slyly pulling their tails through the bars of their cage. Her teasing causes the monkeys to retaliate, and the Wizard says the punishment is deserved.

records.l: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., The Magic of Oz
records.s: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., Principal of the Royal Athletic College, invented the Tablets of Learning and Square-Meal Tablet. After forcing students to eat the tablets rather than ordinary food, the Senior Class threw him into a river; unable to swim, he was rescued after three days and appealed to Ozma for their punishment.

records.l: College of Athletic Arts, The Magic of Oz
records.s: is_a college [athletic] The College of Athletic Arts is located in the Munchkin Country, not far from the Emerald City. Its students use Tablets of Learning so they can devote their time to athletic exercises and sports.

records.l: Royal Athletic College, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Royal Athletic College, an athletic college in Munchkin Country near the Emerald City, is led by Professor H. M. Wogglebug; its Senior Class rebels over Square-Meal Tablets.

records.l: Tablets of Learning, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Tablets of Learning, patented in Land of Oz by Professor Wogglebug, instantly teach mathematics, geography, spelling, handwriting, history, mechanics, home cooking, and agriculture, freeing Royal Athletic College students from book study for athletic exercises and sports.

records.l: Square-Meal Tablet, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Square-Meal Tablet is a tiny tablet containing condensed soup, fried fish, roast, salad, and dessert, providing a full meal’s nourishment. Professor H. M. Wogglebug fed it to students instead of ordinary food, but they refused it for lack of meal taste.

records.l: Senior Class, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Senior Class of the Royal Athletic College refuses Square-Meal Tablets, seizes Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T.E., and throws him into a river; afterward, it is brought to the Emerald City for Ozma to decide punishment.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Betsy Bobbin attends Ozma's birthday feast and is seated next to Aunt Em and before the Shaggy Man.

records.l: the Fountain of the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Fountain of the Water of Oblivion, on the palace grounds beside a marble bench, contains water causing forgetfulness; restored Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink from it.

records.l: Ozma's birthday celebrations, The Magic of Oz
records.s: Ozma's birthday celebrations span the Land of Oz, beginning with bands preparing processions and continuing with decorations, games, plays, and festivities in four countries and Emerald City.

records.l: the Water of Oblivion, The Magic of Oz
records.s: causes_forgetting all previously known memories [after a person drinks it] The Water of Oblivion causes anyone who drinks it to forget everything previously known. Kiki Aru and Ruggedo drink it after their transformations and lose their identities, memories, and knowledge of magic.

records.l: the transformation of the magicians, The Magic of Oz
records.s: The Wizard transforms a hickory-nut into Kiki Aru and a walnut into Ruggedo, then makes them thirsty to drink the Water of Oblivion.

records.l: the Water of Oblivion's memory-erasing effect, The Magic of Oz
records.s: makes_harmless Ruggedo [after he drinks the Water of Oblivion] The memory-erasing effect removes a drinker's memories, identity, knowledge of magic, and understanding of personal history. It makes Kiki Aru innocent and makes Ruggedo forget his anger and plans to conquer Oz, leaving both harmless.

records.s: Ervic promises to help Adepts at Magic (faithfully and truly)
records.q: "We are the three Adepts whom Queen Coo-ee-oh betrayed and wickedly transformed," said the goldfish, its voice low and soft but distinctly heard in the stillness of the night. "I know of our Queen's treacherous deed," replied Ervic, "and I am sorry for your misfortune. Have you been in the lake ever since?" "Yes," was the reply. "I--I hope you are well--and comfortable," stammered Ervic, not knowing what else to say. "We knew that some day Coo-ee-oh would meet with the fate she so richly deserves," declared the bronzefish. "We have waited and watched for this time. Now if you will promise to help us and will be faithful and true, you can aid us in regaining our natural forms, and save yourself and all your people from the dangers that now threaten you." "Well," said Ervic, "you can depend on my doing the best I can. But I'm no witch, nor magician, you must know." "All we ask is that you obey our instructions," returned the silverfish. "We know that you are honest and that you served Coo-ee-oh only because you were obliged to in order to escape her anger. Do as we command and all will be well." "I promise!" exclaimed the young man. "Tell me what I am to do first."

"We are the three Adepts whom Queen Coo-ee-oh betrayed and wickedly
transformed," said the goldfish, its voice low and soft but distinctly
heard in the stillness of the night.

"I know of our Queen's treacherous deed," replied Ervic, "and I am
sorry for your misfortune. Have you been in the lake ever since?"

"Yes," was the reply.

"I--I hope you are well--and comfortable," stammered Ervic, not knowing
what else to say.

"We knew that some day Coo-ee-oh would meet with the fate she so richly
deserves," declared the bronzefish. "We have waited and watched for
this time. Now if you will promise to help us and will be faithful and
true, you can aid us in regaining our natural forms, and save yourself
and all your people from the dangers that now threaten you."

"Well," said Ervic, "you can depend on my doing the best I can. But I'm
no witch, nor magician, you must know."

"All we ask is that you obey our instructions," returned the
silverfish. "We know that you are honest and that you served Coo-ee-oh
only because you were obliged to in order to escape her anger. Do as we
command and all will be well."

"I promise!" exclaimed the young man. "Tell me what I am to do first."

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Glinda, the good Sorceress of Oz, learns from Glinda's Great Book of Records that the Skeezers have declared war on the Flatheads, two previously unknown peoples in the Land of Oz. Glinda discovers that the Skeezers live on the Magic Isle in a lake and that the Flatheads inhabit a hollow-topped mountain nearby, but she cannot learn much more because both peoples use magic to shield themselves. Ozma, Ruler of Oz, decides that it is her duty to visit them and settle their dispute, and Princess Dorothy agrees to accompany her. Glinda gives Dorothy a protective alarm ring, and Ozma and Dorothy return to the Emerald City to prepare for their journey.

records.l: Glinda, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Glinda learns through her Great Book of Records that the Skeezers and Flatheads are preparing for war. Using her magic, she discovers that the Skeezers live on a Magic Isle and that the Flatheads inhabit a mountain south of the Skeezers' lake, but she cannot learn their appearances or the cause of their quarrel. She gives Dorothy a ring that will summon her aid if Dorothy faces serious danger.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ozma learns that the Skeezers and Flatheads are her subjects and decides that her duty is to prevent them from fighting. She rejects sending the Wizard of Oz to threaten them and chooses to travel peacefully with Dorothy to settle their dispute.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Dorothy discovers the report of war between the Skeezers and Flatheads in Glinda's Great Book of Records. She insists on accompanying Ozma to help prevent the war and receives a protective alarm ring from Glinda; she also plans to wear the Magic Belt she took from the Nome King.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Skeezers are a previously unknown people in the Land of Oz who have declared war on the Flatheads. They number one hundred and live on a Magic Isle in a great lake, where they use magic to prevent outsiders from learning much about them.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Flatheads are a previously unknown people in the Land of Oz who are involved in a war with the Skeezers. They number about one hundred and live in a basin-like hollow atop a mountain south of the Lake of the Skeezers; they also work magic and generally keep themselves isolated.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Land of Oz includes the Gillikin Country, the Quadling Country, the Winkie Country, the Munchkin Country, and the Emerald City. Ozma regards the Skeezers and Flatheads as subjects of the Land of Oz and resolves to protect them from war.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The war is revealed when Glinda's Great Book of Records reports that the Skeezers have declared war on the Flatheads. The cause of the conflict is unknown, and Ozma decides to intervene before fighting and further trouble occur.

records.l: Ozma and Dorothy's mission to prevent the war, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy plan to travel to the Magic Isle of the Skeezers and the enchanted mountain of the Flatheads. They intend to approach the two peoples peacefully, learn about their dispute, and persuade them to stop fighting.

records.l: Glinda's Great Book of Records, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: Glinda's Great Book of Records continually prints a truthful, brief record of every event occurring anywhere in the world at the moment it happens. While visiting Glinda, Dorothy sees it record that the Skeezers have declared war on the Flatheads.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter One
records.s: The Magic Isle is an island in a great lake in the Skeezer Country. The Skeezers live there and use magic that prevents Glinda from learning much about them.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy leave the Emerald City in the Red Wagon with the Sawhorse to travel toward the Skeezer Country, while the Scarecrow temporarily rules the Land of Oz. They are trapped by a strong purple web woven by enormous purple spiders led by the Spider King, who intends to make them servants. Dorothy's Magic Belt protects her from the Spider King's attack, and Ozma's Silver Wand repels him. A green crab agrees to cut the web after Ozma changes its color to white, allowing Ozma and Dorothy to escape.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Ozma asks the Scarecrow to rule the Land of Oz while she travels with Dorothy toward the Skeezer Country. She uses her Silver Wand to repel the Spider King and change a green crab white, and escapes the purple spiders with Dorothy.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Dorothy travels with Ozma toward the Skeezer Country while wearing the Nome King's Magic Belt and carrying Glinda's Magic Ring. She discovers that a crab can cut the purple web, carries the crab to the web, and escapes with Ozma.

records.l: Scarecrow, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Scarecrow is a live, intelligent creature who once briefly ruled the Land of Oz and is loved and respected by its people. Ozma asks him to rule the Land of Oz during her absence, and he agrees.

records.l: Spider King, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Spider King leads the enormous purple spiders that trap Ozma and Dorothy in their web. He wants them to keep house for his people, but Ozma's magic and Dorothy's Magic Belt prevent him from harming them.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Land of Oz is surrounded by a Deadly Desert and is large enough that traveling from the Emerald City to the Skeezer Country is a considerable journey. Its distant regions are less populated and less well known, and Ozma feels it is her duty to learn about every part of it.

records.l: the Emerald City, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Emerald City is at the center of the Land of Oz and is surrounded by densely settled country. Ozma and Dorothy leave it at sunrise to travel toward the Skeezer Country.

records.l: the Gillikin Country, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Gillikin Country is the least known part of the Land of Oz. It contains mountains, valleys, forests, streams, and strange bands of people, and the Skeezer Country lies in its farthest northwestern part.

records.l: Skeezer Country, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Skeezer Country is in the farthest northwestern part of the Land of Oz, bordering the north desert. Ozma and Dorothy travel toward it to learn about the Skeezers and Flatheads.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Skeezers are associated with the Skeezer Country, and Ozma and Dorothy intend to learn about them during their journey. Ozma tells Dorothy to keep their plans concerning the Skeezers secret until they return.

records.l: purple spiders, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The purple spiders are enormous creatures with sharp claws, small eyes, fuzzy hair, and purple bodies. They weave a powerful web to imprison Ozma and Dorothy, but flee after the girls resist the Spider King and later pursue them unsuccessfully.

records.l: green crab, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: A green crab with two sharp claws agrees to cut the purple spiders' web in exchange for becoming white. Ozma changes its color to snow-white, and the crab cuts enough strands for Ozma and Dorothy to escape.

records.l: Silver Wand, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Silver Wand is Ozma's weapon of offense and defense. She holds it over the Spider King to drive him back and uses it to change the green crab's color to white.

records.l: purple magic web, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The purple magic web is woven by enormous purple spiders and forms a circular barrier that traps Ozma and Dorothy. It is too strong for them to break, but the green crab cuts through it with its claws.

records.l: journey to Skeezer Country, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The journey to Skeezer Country begins when Ozma and Dorothy leave the Emerald City in the Red Wagon with the Sawhorse. They abandon the wagon when the route becomes too brush-covered for it to pass, then continue on foot and are briefly trapped by the purple spiders.

records.l: Ozma and Dorothy's imprisonment, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: The Spider King's imprisonment begins when his spiders surround Ozma and Dorothy with a purple web. He plans to force them to perform household work, but they escape after the green crab cuts the web.

records.l: magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Two
records.s: Magic protects Ozma and Dorothy from the Spider King and helps them escape his trap. The Spider King acknowledges that their magic is greater than his, while Ozma realizes that other magical beings and forces exist in the Land of Oz beyond her control.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy reach a valley filled with dense, smoke-like mist and consider how to cross it. Ozma calls for the Mist Maidens, believing they live in the Mist Valley and will answer because they are fairies. The Mist Maidens carry Ozma and Dorothy safely over the mist to the opposite hillside, then disappear back into the mist.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Ozma looks down into the mist-filled valley with Dorothy and decides they must venture into the mist if they wish to continue. She calls for the Mist Maidens and asks them to take her and Dorothy to the opposite hillside. The Mist Maidens carry her across, and she thanks them.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: Dorothy worries that the dense mist may cause them to get lost or step on something dreadful. She follows Ozma into the mist when the Mist Maidens come, is carried safely across, and thanks them.

records.l: Mist Maidens, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Mist Maidens live in the Mist Valley and answer Ozma's call. They appear from the mist in gray, mist-like garments, carry Ozma and Dorothy over the billows to the opposite hillside, and then return into the mist.

records.l: Mist Valley, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The Mist Valley is filled with rolling waves of dense mist that remain even in the sunshine. Ozma believes the Mist Maidens live there.

records.l: opposite hillside, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The opposite hillside is grassy and appears beautiful from across the valley. The Mist Maidens carry Ozma and Dorothy there and set them on the grass.

records.l: mist, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Three
records.s: The mist fills the valley like dense smoke and hides everything within it. The Mist Maidens float on its surface and carry Ozma and Dorothy swiftly above its billows.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Dorothy and Ozma cross a flower-filled plain toward the flat mountain where the Flatheads live, but stop to camp when night overtakes them. Ozma uses her silver wand and fairy magic to create a striped tent filled with food, beds, and other comforts. Dorothy reflects that everyone having such magic might remove work and worry, but Ozma explains that striving, helping others, and having things to marvel at make life worthwhile. After dinner, the table and its contents disappear by magic, and Dorothy and Ozma sleep in the tent.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Dorothy travels with Ozma across a broad plain toward the flat mountain where the Flatheads live. She becomes tired from the journey, enjoys the magical feast and comfortable bed, and wishes that everyone could use magic to avoid work and worry.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Ozma travels with Dorothy and uses her silver wand to create a handsome, well-appointed tent for their night’s camp. She explains that unlimited magic would remove the pleasure of striving and earning, and says that using her powers to make others happy gives her happiness.

records.l: fairies, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Fairies can possess different kinds of magic, and not all fairies know how to create a tent and its provisions. Their magic arts are divided among them, which gives them reason to remain modest and to marvel at nature and wit.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Oz is described as the realm ruled by Ozma. Ozma is a more powerful fairy than any other inhabitant of Oz, although the Wizard of Oz can accomplish some things she cannot.

records.l: the plain, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The plain is broad, beautiful, and covered with fragrant wild flowers, flowering bushes, fruit, and groups of trees. It has no dwellings or signs of life, is bordered by palms on one side, and takes Dorothy and Ozma longer to cross than they expect.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The Lake of the Skeezers is believed by Ozma and Dorothy to lie just beyond the line of palm trees near the flat mountain.

records.l: Silver Wand, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Ozma’s silver wand has a large sparkling emerald at one end. She waves it and chants mystic words to create the magic tent and everything the travelers need.

records.l: the magic tent, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: The magic tent appears instantly on the plain after Ozma uses her wand. It is striped purple and white, bears the royal banner of Oz, and contains food, tableware, beds, chairs, and lamps before disappearing after the meal.

records.l: magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Magic can instantly provide food, shelter, beds, and other necessities through words, ceremonies, and a wand. Ozma explains that if everyone could fulfill every want by waving a wand, life would lose much of its interest and purpose.

records.l: fairy magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Fairy magic is distinct from sorcery and wizardry and does not make Ozma all-powerful. It allows Ozma to create the tent and its contents, while other fairies may possess different magical abilities.

records.l: hard work, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Hard work and careful thought make it possible to earn things that are longed for but difficult to obtain. Ozma says that the pleasure of earning such things would be lost if magic made everything easy.

records.l: happiness, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Ozma says that giving everyone the power to satisfy every want would bring weariness rather than happiness. She is happy because she can use her fairy powers to make others happy.

records.l: good deeds, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Four
records.s: Good deeds and helping those who are less fortunate are described by Ozma as what makes life worth while.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Dorothy and Ozma travel from their vanished fairy tent to the flat mountain, hoping to reach its summit and meet the Flatheads. They discover an invisible stone wall guarding the mountain entrance and find a way around it. Inside, they climb a winding stairway and passage designed to warn the Flatheads of intruders. At the summit, Dorothy and Ozma encounter a large group of armed Flatheads, whose unusual appearance and metal clothing are described.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Dorothy travels with Ozma toward the flat mountain and asks whether magic can provide a faster means of transportation. She helps search for a way through the mountain’s defenses, climbs the stairway, and becomes concerned when she learns that the Flatheads have been warned of their arrival.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Ozma explains that her magic cannot create a horse and wagon or an automobile, though she says Dorothy possesses the magical ability to win people’s hearts. She recognizes the purpose of the invisible wall, finds the way around it, and uses her silver wand to illuminate the dark passage. Ozma also hears the warning bell and the Flatheads’ alarmed voices before reaching the summit with Dorothy.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The Flatheads live on top of the flat mountain and use a guarded route to travel between the summit and the plain. They constructed an invisible stone wall and a winding stairway that warns them when intruders approach. They are described as bald people with flat-topped heads, large violet eyes, and metal clothing, and the men carry bows, arrows, and small steel axes.

records.l: the Enchanted Mountain of the Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The flat mountain is round, steep-sided, and topped by a flat surface where the Flatheads live. Its sides are difficult to climb, and an entrance cut into the rock provides access to a stairway leading upward.

records.l: the entrance, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The entrance is an arched opening cut into the mountain’s rock wall and leads to a short flight of stone stairs. Dorothy and Ozma can see it from outside, but an invisible stone wall initially prevents them from reaching it.

records.l: the invisible stone wall, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The invisible stone wall is made of solid stone held together with cement and stands a short distance before the entrance. It is intended to keep enemies from rushing up the stairs, while allowing the Flatheads to pass around its hidden end.

records.l: Stairway, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The mountain stairway repeatedly rises ten steps and descends five, with turns between the flights. Pressure on the tenth step causes a bell on the mountain’s summit to ring and warn the Flatheads of approaching intruders.

records.l: the mountain passage, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: The mountain passage is cut through the rock and is only wide enough for Dorothy and Ozma to walk abreast. It becomes dark inside the mountain, follows the repeated up-and-down stair pattern, and eventually leads to the summit.

records.l: magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Five
records.s: Magic cannot provide Ozma with a horse and wagon or an automobile, and no one is powerful enough to do everything. Ozma uses her magic to hear sounds from a great distance and uses a silver wand whose jewel produces green-tinted light.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Princess Ozma and Dorothy enter Flathead Mountain, where the Flatheads bring them before the Supreme Dictator. The Su-dic explains the Flatheads' dispute with the Skeezers over fishing in the Lake of the Skeezers and describes how Queen Coo-ee-oh transformed his wife, Rora Flathead, into a Golden Pig. Ozma proposes a settlement, but the Su-dic rejects it, declares war, and orders the girls imprisoned. Before the Flatheads can seize them, Ozma and Dorothy vanish.

records.l: the Enchanted Mountain of the Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Flathead Mountain has a saucer-shaped summit concealed from people below. Its rock-built houses, paths, walls, and central palace belong to the Flatheads.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Flatheads live on Flathead Mountain and use rock as their main building material. They carry canned brains supplied by fairies, and most serve as dictators or other office holders. They are in conflict with the Skeezers over fishing and prepare to fight them.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Skeezers forbid the Flatheads from fishing in their lake and guard its shore. Queen Coo-ee-oh, their ruler, transformed Rora Flathead into a Golden Pig, causing the Su-dic to declare war on them.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Princess Ozma identifies herself as the Ruler of Oz and tells the Su-dic that her laws apply to both the Flatheads and the Skeezers. She seeks to prevent war and proposes restoring Rora to human form with one can of brains while returning the other three cans to those Rora robbed. When the Su-dic orders her imprisoned, she vanishes with Dorothy.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Dorothy accompanies Princess Ozma into Flathead Mountain and questions the Su-dic about Flathead brains and Rora's transformation. She challenges the Su-dic's claims and vanishes with Ozma before the Flatheads can imprison them.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Land of Oz includes the territory of the Flatheads, and Princess Ozma rules all its peoples. The Su-dic denies that Ozma can compel him to obey her laws.

records.l: Su-dic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Supreme Dictator, called the Su-dic, is the elected ruler of the Flatheads and claims that his word is law. He says he counts the votes himself so that he is always elected, and he believes his three cans of brains make him a powerful sorcerer. He rejects Ozma's peace terms and orders her and Dorothy cast into the bronze prison.

records.l: Rora Flathead, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Rora Flathead was the Su-dic's wife and had four cans of brains, which made her a powerful witch. She tried to poison the fish in the Skeezers' lake after the Skeezers forbade Flathead fishing, but Queen Coo-ee-oh transformed her into a Golden Pig and took away her cans of brains.

records.l: Golden Pig, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Golden Pig is Rora Flathead after Queen Coo-ee-oh's transformation. It has a solid gold body, ruby eyes, and ivory teeth, and it grunts that the Flatheads should fight the Skeezers.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh is the young Skeezer Queen and a sorceress. She caught Rora Flathead attempting to poison the lake, transformed her into a Golden Pig, and removed Rora's four cans of brains.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Lake of the Skeezers contains fish that the Skeezers claim belong to them and place under their protection. The Flatheads want to fish there, but Ozma rules that the lake and its fish belong to the Skeezers.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Su-dic declares a war against the Skeezers in retaliation for Rora's transformation and because they prevent Flathead fishing. Ozma attempts to stop the war, but the Su-dic refuses her conditions and says he will fight even if many Ozmas oppose him.

records.l: Rora's transformation into the Golden Pig, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: Rora's transformation occurred when she tried to dump magic poison into the Lake of the Skeezers. Queen Coo-ee-oh transformed her into a Golden Pig and removed her four cans of brains; Ozma offers to restore Rora's human form but not all four cans.

records.l: Flathead fishing dispute, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Six
records.s: The Flatheads fish in the Lake of the Skeezers because they have no fish on their mountain, while the Skeezers forbid them to take fish from the lake. The dispute escalates after Rora attempts to poison the fish, leading to her transformation and the Su-dic's declaration of war.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Ozma uses her silver wand to make herself and Dorothy invisible, allowing them to escape the Su-dic and the Flatheads. The Su-dic and his soldiers pursue them but are delayed when the Golden Pig trips them. After reaching safety, Ozma and Dorothy decide to find the Lake of the Skeezers and warn its people about the Su-dic’s planned attack. They discover the lake and a beautiful island containing a large glass palace, but see no way to reach it.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Ozma makes herself and Dorothy invisible with her silver wand and leads Dorothy out of the Flatheads’ stronghold. After escaping, she decides to find the Lake of the Skeezers and help them resist the Flatheads. She believes the Flathead people may become peaceful if the Su-dic is removed from power and deprived of his unlawful magic.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Dorothy escapes with Ozma after Ozma makes them invisible, and she runs with her to safety. She agrees that they should find the Skeezers and hopes the Flatheads will be punished. She discovers the Lake of the Skeezers and the island palace with Ozma.

records.l: Su-dic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Su-dic pursues Ozma and Dorothy after they escape, but the Golden Pig trips him and his four soldiers. He realizes that he could have used his own knowledge of magic to make the girls visible, but he remembered this too late. He then prepares to march all his forces against the Skeezers.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Flatheads guard their mountain stronghold, but they fail to stop Ozma and Dorothy from escaping. The Su-dic intends to lead them in a war against the Skeezers. Ozma believes the Flathead people are not as responsible as the Su-dic and may become peaceful if he loses power.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Skeezers are described by Ozma as possibly good people and worthy of friendship. They are threatened by the Su-dic, who plans to attack them, so Ozma and Dorothy intend to warn and help them.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Lake of the Skeezers is a beautiful body of water about a mile from shore to shore, with blue, sparkling waves. A lovely island lies at its center, but no boats or signs of life are visible on either shore.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Magic Isle is located in the center of the Lake of the Skeezers. It is almost entirely covered by a large round glass building with a high glass dome, surrounded by polished white marble.

records.l: glass palace, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The glass palace stands on the Magic Isle and has glass walls and a high glass dome that shines in the sunlight. Dorothy and Ozma suspect the Skeezers are inside it, but they cannot find a way to reach them.

records.l: escape from the Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy escape from the Flatheads by becoming invisible with Ozma’s silver wand and running down the mountain stairway. The Su-dic and his soldiers chase them, but the Golden Pig trips the pursuers and gives the girls time to get away.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Seven
records.s: The Su-dic is determined to begin a war against the Skeezers and plans to march all his forces against them. Ozma and Dorothy cannot stop the war immediately, so they set out to warn the Skeezers and help them as much as possible.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Princess Ozma and Princess Dorothy reach Skeezer island by crossing a retractable steel bridge into the glass-domed village. Queen Coo-ee-oh receives them suspiciously, rejects Ozma's authority, and boasts that she is a powerful Krumbic Witch. Ozma tries to explain her rule and prevent war between the Skeezers and Flatheads, but Coo-ee-oh orders the girls kept as prisoners until the expected Flathead attack. Lady Aurex takes Ozma and Dorothy to her house, where they are allowed to wander under the Great Dome.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Princess Ozma signals the Skeezers with her handkerchief and crosses to Skeezer island with Princess Dorothy on a retractable steel bridge. She explains that she rules the Land of Oz under authority from the Fairy Queen Lurline and tries to persuade Queen Coo-ee-oh to avoid war with the Flatheads. Queen Coo-ee-oh rejects her authority and orders her kept prisoner until the battle is over.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Princess Dorothy crosses to Skeezer island with Princess Ozma and observes that the Skeezers appear unhappy despite their comfortable homes and ample food. She defends Ozma's authority, insults Queen Coo-ee-oh's pride, and is placed under the same imprisonment order as Ozma.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh is a proud and suspicious ruler who claims supreme authority over the Skeezers. She declares herself the only Krumbic Witch in the world and says her magic is greater than that of any fairy or Flathead. She refuses Ozma's claim to rule her and orders Ozma and Dorothy held as prisoners until the Flatheads are defeated.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: The Skeezers live on a glass-domed island containing a well-kept village of marble houses, streets, gardens, and parks. They are richly dressed and have comfortable lives, but they appear solemn, nervous, or irritated rather than happy. They are ruled by Queen Coo-ee-oh and are preparing to fight the Flatheads.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: The Flatheads are described as a neighboring people living on a barren mountain-top. Their Supreme Dictator is a Sorcerer, and they intend to attack the Skeezers.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: The Land of Oz includes the Skeezer island, according to Princess Dorothy and Princess Ozma. Ozma says it contains several countries and peoples with separate rulers who acknowledge her as supreme ruler and obey her laws.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Skeezer island is covered almost entirely by a great glass dome. It contains a marble village, gardens, parks, a central fountain, and Queen Coo-ee-oh's palace, and it can be reached from the shore by a steel bridge that extends from the palace and retracts with its passengers.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: A war between the Skeezers and Flatheads is expected because the Flatheads plan to attack the Skeezers. Princess Ozma comes to settle the dispute and prevent fighting, but Queen Coo-ee-oh intends to fight rather than make peace.

records.l: the Flatheads' attack, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh says that the Flatheads intend to attack the Skeezers tomorrow. She claims that the Skeezers are prepared and that the Flatheads will not return to their barren mountain-top.

records.l: Ozma and Dorothy's arrival on Skeezer island, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy signal the island and are brought across the water by a retractable steel bridge. They enter the glass-domed village, are escorted to the palace, and meet Queen Coo-ee-oh.

records.l: peace between the Skeezers and Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Princess Ozma seeks peace between the Skeezers and Flatheads because she dislikes wars and came to settle their dispute. Queen Coo-ee-oh rejects Ozma's intervention and shows no interest in avoiding the coming battle.

records.l: Ozma's rule over Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Princess Ozma says that the Fairy Queen Lurline gave her authority when Oz became a Fairyland. She rules the Emerald City and other countries whose people and rulers acknowledge her as the supreme ruler and obey her laws.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh's imprisonment of Ozma and Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eight
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh orders Ozma and Dorothy kept as prisoners on Skeezer island until the battle with the Flatheads is over. She assigns Lady Aurex to provide them with food and lodging, while allowing them to wander anywhere under the Great Dome.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Lady Aurex shelters Ozma and Dorothy in her house and explains why the Skeezers are unhappy under Queen Coo-ee-oh. She recounts how Coo-ee-oh stole the magic of three Adepts in Sorcery by transforming them into a gold fish, a silver fish, and a bronze fish, causing enmity between the Skeezers and the Flatheads. The coming war concerns control of the lake and the fishes, whose destruction would deprive Coo-ee-oh of her magic. Ozma promises to help, while Dorothy urges Ozma to remove the cruel rulers from power.

records.l: Lady Aurex, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Lady Aurex brings Ozma and Dorothy to her house and, after Ozma protects the house from Coo-ee-oh's hearing, tells them the history of the Skeezers and Flatheads. She explains that Coo-ee-oh's punishments and cruelty have made the Skeezers fearful and unhappy, and warns that war may begin the next day.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Ozma uses her silver wand to enchant Lady Aurex's house so that Queen Coo-ee-oh cannot hear anyone speaking within it. She gains Lady Aurex's trust, learns the history of the three fishes, and seeks to understand why the Skeezers are unhappy.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Dorothy defends Ozma's identity and declares that Ozma should remove the magic from Queen Coo-ee-oh and Su-dic and provide new rulers. She listens indignantly to Lady Aurex's account of Coo-ee-oh's cruelty and believes the Flatheads may attack the glass dome with bows and arrows.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh rules the Skeezers through fear, punishes remarks she dislikes, and can hear everything spoken on the island unless prevented by Ozma's enchantment. She stole the charms and magical instruments of the three Adepts in Sorcery, transformed them into fishes, and depends on those fishes remaining alive to retain her magic.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The Skeezers are described as peaceful people who do not seek quarrels or fights, but they obey Coo-ee-oh because they fear her punishments. They became enemies of the Flatheads after Coo-ee-oh transformed the three Adepts in Sorcery into fishes.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The Flatheads were once friendly with the Skeezers and were ruled by three benevolent Adepts in Sorcery. After the Adepts were lost, Su-dic and Rora became rulers, and the Flatheads now threaten war and seek to destroy one of the three fishes.

records.l: Su-dic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Su-dic and Rora became rulers of the Flatheads after the three Adepts in Sorcery were transformed. Su-dic stole canned brains from others to increase his power and came to the lake seeking to catch and destroy one of the three fishes.

records.l: Rora Flathead, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Rora seized some of the Adepts' magical tools and used them to become a witch. She tried to poison all the fishes in the lake, and Coo-ee-oh transformed her into a Golden Pig.

records.l: Adepts at Magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The three Adepts in Sorcery were beautiful girls who ruled the Flatheads and used magic only for good. They taught the Flatheads useful arts and helped the Skeezers, but Coo-ee-oh stole their magical instruments and transformed them into three fishes.

records.l: Land of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The Land of Oz is described as a fairyland where people do not grow old or die and do not change in appearance. Ozma is identified as its supreme and lawful Ruler.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The Magic Isle is the island where the Skeezers live beneath the great glass dome. Lady Aurex expects that the Flatheads may attack the Skeezers there.

records.l: lake, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The lake is where Coo-ee-oh cast the three transformed fishes after changing them from the Adepts. The Flatheads came to it to catch one of the fishes, and Rora later tried to poison all the fishes in it.

records.l: Great Dome, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The glass dome covers the Skeezers' village and was built for them by the three Adepts in Sorcery. Lady Aurex says the Flatheads cannot break it, although Dorothy believes they may try to shoot arrows at it.

records.l: gold fish, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The gold fish is one of the three fishes into which Coo-ee-oh transformed the Adepts in Sorcery. Its destruction would cause Coo-ee-oh to become shrivelled and helpless and would remove her stolen magic.

records.l: silver fish, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The silver fish is one of the three fishes into which Coo-ee-oh transformed the Adepts in Sorcery. The Flatheads sought to catch and destroy it, along with either of the other two fishes.

records.l: bronze fish, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The bronze fish is one of the three fishes into which Coo-ee-oh transformed the Adepts in Sorcery. Like the gold fish and silver fish, it is tied to Coo-ee-oh's continued possession of magic.

records.l: three transformed fishes, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The three transformed fishes are the three Adepts in Sorcery in altered forms. Their survival protects Coo-ee-oh's magic, while their destruction would weaken her and their restoration could allow the Adepts to return and punish Rora and Su-dic.

records.l: Golden Pig, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: The Golden Pig is the form Coo-ee-oh gave Rora after Rora tried to poison all the fishes in the lake.

records.l: magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Coo-ee-oh stole the magic of the three Adepts in Sorcery through their transformation into fishes, while Rora acquired magic through the Adepts' abandoned tools. The survival of the three fishes is necessary for Coo-ee-oh to keep her stolen magic.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: A war between the Skeezers and the Flatheads is expected because the Flatheads want to destroy the fishes and possibly conquer the Skeezers. Lady Aurex says Coo-ee-oh has been preparing for the conflict, while Ozma suspects the Flatheads will first attack the fishes rather than the island.

records.l: the transformation of the three Adepts into fishes, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Coo-ee-oh invited the three Adepts in Sorcery to a banquet, stole their charms and magical instruments, and transformed them into a gold fish, a silver fish, and a bronze fish. The transformation caused the Flatheads to turn against the Skeezers and made both peoples miserable.

records.l: attempt to poison the fishes, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Rora attempted to poison all the fishes in the lake. Coo-ee-oh transformed Rora into a Golden Pig, and the attempt frightened Coo-ee-oh because her safety depends on the fishes remaining alive.

records.l: punishments inflicted by Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Nine
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh punishes Skeezers who disobey her, displease her, or speak about her in their homes. She has offenders dragged to the whipping post in her palace and lashed with knotted cords, causing the Skeezers to fear her greatly.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Dorothy and Ozma remain prisoners in Lady Aurex's house while Queen Coo-ee-oh prepares the Skeezers' island for a Flathead attack. At daybreak, Coo-ee-oh submerges the island and its Great Dome beneath the lake, revealing the Skeezers' underwater defenses. The Su-dic arrives with armed Flatheads, two copper vessels, and poison intended to destroy the fish in the lake. Coo-ee-oh sends a submarine toward the Flatheads, but the Su-dic throws the contents of a copper vessel into her face before she can use her magic rope.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Dorothy remains a prisoner with Ozma in Lady Aurex's house but is treated considerately. She asks about the island's submergence and watches as a submarine approaches the Flatheads.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Ozma says she is glad to have learned about the Skeezers and Flatheads because her task is to liberate them and secure their freedom and happiness. She believes she and Dorothy are not in danger despite the island's submergence and the approaching conflict.

records.l: Lady Aurex, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Lady Aurex gives Dorothy and Ozma supper, provides them with a comfortable room, and explains the island's submergence and the Skeezers' defenses. She identifies the approaching underwater vessel as one of Queen Coo-ee-oh's submarines.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh orders the island submerged when the Flatheads approach and uses submarines to oppose them. She approaches the Su-dic in a submarine with a silver magic rope, but he throws the contents of a copper vessel into her face before she can throw it.

records.l: Su-dic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Su-dic leads armed Flatheads to the lake with two copper vessels, one of which contains enough poison to kill every fish in the lake. Seeking revenge because Coo-ee-oh transformed his wife into a Golden Pig, he attacks her by throwing a copper vessel's contents into her face.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Skeezers live on the island beneath the Great Dome and are ruled by Queen Coo-ee-oh. They possess underwater defenses, including submarines, and are threatened by the approaching Flatheads.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Flatheads approach the lake with armed followers under the Su-dic's leadership to attack the Skeezers. They do not know about the Skeezers' submarines and watch in surprise as one emerges from the submerged dome.

records.l: Great Dome, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Great Dome covers the Skeezers' village and is made of glass that does not leak when submerged. It descends beneath the lake's surface with the island, while its houses remain dimly visible through the water.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The island trembles, creaks, and sinks beneath the lake at Queen Coo-ee-oh's command. Once the top of the dome is underwater, the island stops sinking and remains stationary.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The lake surrounds the island and rises over the Great Dome when the island submerges. Its clear water reveals fish, swaying seaweed, the dome, and the distant shore.

records.l: submarine, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh keeps several enclosed submarines in rooms beneath the Skeezers' village. One travels from the submerged dome to the shore, rises to the surface, and carries armed Skeezers and the Queen.

records.l: the copper kettle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Su-dic brings two copper vessels to the lake. He uses one to throw its contents into Queen Coo-ee-oh's face when she approaches him in a submarine.

records.l: poison, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Su-dic has enough poison in one copper vessel to kill every fish in the lake. He does not release it into the lake before Coo-ee-oh confronts him.

records.l: magic rope, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh carries a silver magic rope while standing in the bow of the submarine. She draws back her arm to throw it at the Su-dic, but he acts first.

records.l: magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh stole magical knowledge and tools from the three Adepts in Sorcery after they were transformed into fishes. Lady Aurex says Coo-ee-oh has used that magic in ways the Adepts never would have.

records.l: the island's submergence, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh submerges the island to protect it from the approaching Flatheads and their attempt to attack or break the dome. The submergence requires considerable effort to operate the machinery, so she does not do it often.

records.l: the Flatheads' attack, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: The Flatheads come to attack the Skeezers after the island has been submerged. Their leader brings armed followers and poison, while Coo-ee-oh responds with a submarine.

records.l: Ozma and Dorothy's mission to prevent the war, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Ten
records.s: Ozma identifies her mission as liberating the Skeezers and Flatheads from leaders who are wild, lawless, unjust, and cruel. She intends to secure freedom and happiness for them and believes she can accomplish this in time.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh falls into the lake and is transformed into a Diamond Swan by the Su-dic, who claims this avenges Rora's transformation into a Golden Pig. The Su-dic loses the poison needed to kill the fishes and cannot make more because Rora has forgotten her magic. The Skeezers are left helpless in their submarine and unable to return to their village, while the Flatheads return to their mountain believing they have won the war. The Su-dic celebrates the conquest of the Skeezers with a feast.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh drops the rope, falls into the lake, and is transformed into a large Diamond Swan. She loses her powers of sorcery and warns the Su-dic that the three magic fishes will eventually destroy him.

records.l: Su-dic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The Su-dic transforms Queen Coo-ee-oh into a Diamond Swan and celebrates his revenge for Rora. He accidentally spills all of the poison he had to kill the fishes, orders his men to shoot the Swan, rejects the Skeezers' request for protection, and returns to his mountain to feast.

records.l: Golden Pig, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: Rora remains a Golden Pig after Queen Coo-ee-oh's earlier enchantment. Because she has become a Pig and forgotten her magic, the Su-dic says she cannot make more poison.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The Skeezers in the submarine are bewildered and unable to help Queen Coo-ee-oh after her transformation. They cannot operate the submarine or return to their village, and the Su-dic refuses to take them as prisoners or care for them.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The Flatheads march back to their mountain after the Su-dic declares that they have conquered the Skeezers. There, the Su-dic and some officers feast while the others are forced to serve them.

records.l: submarine, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The submarine is operated by mystic words spoken by Queen Coo-ee-oh rather than by machinery. After her transformation, the Skeezers cannot submerge it, restore its watertight shield, make it return to the castle, or put it back in its basement room.

records.l: lake, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The lake receives Queen Coo-ee-oh when she falls beneath its surface. After becoming a Diamond Swan, she swims across it to a place beyond the reach of the Flatheads' arrows and spears.

records.l: three transformed fishes, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The three magic fishes remain a threat to the Su-dic after Queen Coo-ee-oh's transformation. Queen Coo-ee-oh says that they will destroy him in time.

records.l: war between the Flatheads and the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The Su-dic declares that the Flatheads have won the war after Queen Coo-ee-oh is transformed and the Skeezers are left helpless. The Flatheads then return to their mountain.

records.l: conquest of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: The Su-dic calls the transformation of Queen Coo-ee-oh and the Skeezers' helplessness a conquest of the Skeezers. The Flatheads celebrate this claimed victory with a feast.

records.l: the transformation of Queen Coo-ee-oh into a Diamond Swan, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh is transformed when she falls into the water after dropping the rope. The Diamond Swan is large and white, covered with tiny diamonds, and has a polished-gold bill and amethyst eyes; her webbed feet and loss of sorcery leave her powerless.

records.l: Rora's transformation into the Golden Pig, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Eleven
records.s: Rora was transformed into a Golden Pig by Queen Coo-ee-oh before this unit. The Su-dic says that Rora's transformation avenged his wife but also left her unable to remember or perform her magic.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Coo-ee-oh is transformed into a Diamond Swan by Su-dic's magic and abandons the Skeezers, who remain trapped with their island beneath the Lake of the Skeezers. Ozma, Dorothy, and Lady Aurex recognize that only Coo-ee-oh knew how to raise the island, operate the under-water boats, and open the basement doors. The Skeezers accept Ozma as their Ruler, and she searches Coo-ee-oh's palace for a way to save them. Dorothy begins searching the lake for the three fishes that were once the Adept Witches, hoping Ozma can restore them and obtain their help.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: After being transformed into a Diamond Swan, Coo-ee-oh is absorbed in admiring her beauty and refuses or is unable to help Ervic and the other Skeezers return to the island. She has forgotten the magic she knew as a girl and swims away, unconcerned about her people or their plight.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Skeezers are left frightened and anxious after Coo-ee-oh's transformation, because they depended on her magic to defeat the Flatheads and raise their island. They accept Ozma as their Ruler and are told to remain patient and continue their daily tasks.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Ozma realizes that Coo-ee-oh's transformation has placed the Skeezers, their island, Dorothy, and herself in grave danger. She takes possession of Coo-ee-oh's palace, investigates the witchcraft room, and promises to study its contents in an attempt to save everyone.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Dorothy is glad that Coo-ee-oh has been punished but soon understands that the transformation has made escape and rescue more difficult. She suggests capturing the three transformed fishes so Ozma can restore the Adept Witches, then begins watching the lake for them.

records.l: Lady Aurex, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Lady Aurex explains that only Coo-ee-oh knew how to raise the island, operate the under-water boats, and open the basement doors. She helps advise Ozma and is invited to stay at Coo-ee-oh's palace because of her knowledge of the Skeezers and their island.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Lake of the Skeezers contains the submerged Skeezers' island and is filled with many kinds of fishes, shellfish, and colorful water foliage. Dorothy watches its clear waters in hopes of finding the gold, silver, and bronze fishes.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Skeezers' island lies at the bottom of the lake after Coo-ee-oh caused it to sink. Only Coo-ee-oh knew how to raise it, leaving the island and its inhabitants trapped underwater.

records.l: Great Dome, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The glass dome encloses the Skeezers and prevents them from escaping the bottom of the lake. Ozma, Dorothy, and Lady Aurex watch events outside through it, while Dorothy later observes the surrounding fish through its clear panes.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh's palace, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy are escorted to Coo-ee-oh's palace after the Skeezers accept Ozma as their Ruler. Ozma takes possession of it and finds a private room devoted to witchcraft.

records.l: under-water boats, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Skeezers possess other under-water boats that might reach the surface, but no one except Coo-ee-oh knows how to operate them. Their possible use therefore does not provide a known means of escape.

records.l: witchcraft, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Coo-ee-oh's magic is described as unlawful witchcraft rather than fairy magic. It controlled the island's machinery, the under-water boats, and the basement doors, but Coo-ee-oh's transformation caused her to forget it.

records.l: Coo-ee-oh's witchcraft tools and charms, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Coo-ee-oh's palace contains instruments, ointments, potions, strange machines, preserved animals, and books written in blood. Ozma cannot identify how to use them because Coo-ee-oh kept her secrets and the books are in a language Ozma does not know.

records.l: Adepts at Magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Adept Witches originally practiced good witchcraft intended to help their people, but Coo-ee-oh stole some of their tools. The Adept Witches have been transformed into fishes, and Ozma considers restoring them if they can be captured.

records.l: three transformed fishes, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The three transformed fishes are gold, silver, and bronze, and Dorothy believes they remain together as companions. She searches among the many fishes in the lake for them so Ozma can restore them to their proper forms.

records.l: the transformation of Queen Coo-ee-oh into a Diamond Swan, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Coo-ee-oh is suddenly transformed into a Diamond Swan after the Flatheads have gone away. The transformation punishes her but also removes the only person who knew how to control the island's magical mechanisms.

records.l: the Skeezers' imprisonment underwater, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: The Skeezers, their island, Ozma, Dorothy, and Lady Aurex are trapped beneath the lake in the glass dome. Opening the dome would flood it, and the available boats and doors cannot be used because only Coo-ee-oh knew their magic.

records.l: escape and rescue of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Twelve
records.s: Ozma seeks a way to rescue the Skeezers and escape the underwater prison, while Dorothy proposes finding the three transformed fishes for help. Ozma urges patience and begins studying Coo-ee-oh's palace and witchcraft materials.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Glinda, the Good, learns through her Great Book of Records and alarm bell that Ozma and Dorothy are prisoners in the submerged great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers. Queen Coo-ee-oh, the only one able to raise the island, has been transformed into a Diamond Swan by the Flathead Su-dic. Glinda cannot find or invent magic for raising the sunken island, so she travels to the Emerald City to seek help. She and the Scarecrow arrange for a Council of State to decide how to rescue Ozma and Dorothy.

records.l: Glinda, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Glinda studies sorcery, assists beasts, birds, and people, and checks the Great Book of Records for news of Ozma and Dorothy. After learning they are trapped beneath the lake, she experiments unsuccessfully with ways to raise a sunken island, then travels to the Emerald City and calls for a Council of State.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Ozma reaches the Enchanted Mountain of the Flatheads and escapes with Dorothy to the Magic Isle of the Skeezers. She is later reported to be a prisoner in the great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers beneath the lake.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Dorothy travels with Ozma to the Magic Isle of the Skeezers and uses the ring Glinda gave her to signal danger. She is imprisoned with Ozma in the great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers beneath the lake.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh submerges the Magic Isle of the Skeezers and is the only one able to command it to rise. She is transformed by the Flathead Su-dic into a Diamond Swan.

records.l: Scarecrow, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Scarecrow acts as Ruler of the Land of Oz while Ozma is away. After Glinda tells him about Ozma and Dorothy's imprisonment, he agrees to help and summons Ozma's counsellors for a Council of State.

records.l: Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Skeezers live on the Magic Isle of the Skeezers, which Queen Coo-ee-oh has submerged. Because Coo-ee-oh has forgotten her magic and has been transformed, none of the Skeezers knows how to raise the island.

records.l: Flatheads, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Flatheads come to the lake to poison the fishes. Their Supreme Dictator, the Flathead Su-dic, transforms Queen Coo-ee-oh into a Diamond Swan.

records.l: the Emerald City, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Emerald City is where Glinda travels to consult the Scarecrow and arrange a Council of State about rescuing Ozma and Dorothy.

records.l: Magic Isle, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Magic Isle of the Skeezers is submerged by Queen Coo-ee-oh and remains entirely under the lake's water. Ozma and Dorothy are trapped in its great Dome.

records.l: Lake of the Skeezers, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The lake surrounds and covers the submerged Magic Isle of the Skeezers. The Flatheads come to it to poison the fishes, and the transformed Queen Coo-ee-oh and the three fishes made from the Adepts of Magic are associated with it.

records.l: Glinda's Great Book of Records, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Great Book of Records tells Glinda that Ozma and Dorothy reach the Enchanted Mountain, escape to the Skeezers' island, and later become prisoners beneath the lake. It also records the submerging of the island and Queen Coo-ee-oh's transformation, though it initially gives few details.

records.l: Glinda's protective ring, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Glinda's alarm bell rings when Dorothy turns the ring Glinda gave her once to the right and once to the left. Its ringing tells Glinda that Ozma and Dorothy are in great danger.

records.l: Great Dome, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers is beneath the water of the lake. Ozma and Dorothy are imprisoned inside it.

records.l: the laws against unauthorized magic, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Glinda studies the magic of sorcery and searches her books and recipes for a way to raise a sunken island. She cannot find such a magic, and her experiments with a small submerged island fail.

records.l: raising the sunken island, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Raising the sunken island is necessary to free Ozma and Dorothy from the submerged dome. Glinda finds no known spell for doing it and cannot accomplish it through her initial experiments.

records.l: Queen Coo-ee-oh's imprisonment of Ozma and Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The danger threatening Ozma and Dorothy is that they are trapped as prisoners in the great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers, which lies beneath the lake. They can live there for a long time, but they cannot escape unless the island is raised.

records.l: Ozma and Dorothy's imprisonment, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Ozma and Dorothy's imprisonment takes place inside the great Dome of the Isle of the Skeezers beneath the lake. Glinda learns of it through her alarm bell and begins seeking a way to rescue them.

records.l: the transformation of Queen Coo-ee-oh into a Diamond Swan, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: Queen Coo-ee-oh's transformation is carried out by the Flathead Su-dic, who changes her into a Diamond Swan. Since she alone could command the island to rise, her transformation leaves the Skeezers unable to raise it.

records.l: the Council of State, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Thirteen
records.s: The Council of State is summoned by the Scarecrow at Glinda's request. Ozma's counsellors gather in the palace throne room to decide how best to rescue Ozma and Dorothy.

records.l: Glinda of Oz, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Princess Ozma's unusual council gathers in the Emerald City after Glinda explains the plight of Ozma and Dorothy. The counsellors decide that they must travel to the Skeezer country to investigate the sunken island and determine how to rescue them. Glinda the Good and the Wizard of Oz will lead the expedition because magic must meet magic, and the group plans to leave at sunrise. Glinda will send her stork chariot back to her castle, so the others will travel together on foot.

records.l: Ozma, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Princess Ozma has gathered a council of unusual but trustworthy advisers. She is in danger, and the council decides to travel to the Skeezer country to rescue her.

records.l: Dorothy, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Dorothy is in danger with Ozma, and Glinda tells the council about their plight. The council resolves to rescue both Dorothy and Ozma.

records.l: the Council of State, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Ozma's council includes the Tin Woodman, Scraps, the Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok, Jack Pumpkinhead, Cap'n Bill, Professor Wogglebug, the Frogman, Uncle Henry, the Wizard, the Scarecrow, and Glinda. It assembles in Ozma's throne room and decides to investigate the Skeezer country.

records.l: Tin Woodman, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: The Tin Woodman, whose name is Nick Chopper, is an adviser to Ozma and the Emperor of all the Winkies. He has a good mind, lacks much of a heart, and is careful not to be unkind; he joins the expedition to the Skeezer country.

records.l: the Patchwork Girl, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Scraps, the Patchwork Girl of Oz, is intelligent, playful, and often wise in her seemingly careless remarks. She suggests pumping the water out of the lake and decides to join the expedition.

records.l: Shaggy Man, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: The Shaggy Man is kind, gentle, and one of Ozma's most loyal supporters. He suggests raising the sunken island and agrees to go to the Skeezer country.

records.l: Tik-Tok, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Tik-Tok is a copper man moved, speaking, and thinking through three separate clockworks. His machinery is running well, and he says that the group will have to go to the Skeezer country.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead has a crude but durable wooden body and must replace his pumpkin head whenever it spoils. He suggests throwing a rope around the island and pulling it ashore, and he joins the expedition with a newly made pumpkin head.

records.l: Professor Wogglebug, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: Professor H. M. Wogglebug, T. E., is a highly magnified and thoroughly educated former bug who heads Ozma's Royal Athletic College. He suggests that the counsellors get under the island and lift it, and he agrees to travel to the Skeezer country.

records.l: Frogman, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: The Frogman is a man-sized frog from the Yip Country who is noted for wise sayings and dresses in splendid clothing. He asks how large the lake and island are, but no one can answer because they have not been there.

records.l: Scarecrow, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
records.s: The Scarecrow advises that the group go to the Skeezer country and examine it carefully. He joins the expedition and has recently been stuffed with fresh straw.

records.l: Glinda, Glinda of Oz, Chapter Fourteen
