At her palace party, she permits Professor Wogglebug to begin compiling the Royal Book and hears that her family tree is Oz’s oldest and most illustrious. Later, after learning that the Horners and Hoppers are at war again, she travels with Betsy Bobbin, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Wizard of Oz to settle it; with Glinda, she stops the war. She gives emerald collars to the A-B-Sea Serpent and Rattlesnakes. Finally, she welcomes Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Sir Hokus, and the animals back to Oz, seeks the Magic Belt’s help with the magic fan, and holds a celebration.

records.l: Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Oz is a marvelous, friendly Fairyland country on the Continent of Imagination, surrounded on every side by Oz's deadly desert. No one there grows old, all animals can talk, and animals and birds speak sensibly; adventures happen every day, so almost anything can happen. It is divided into four parts around the Emerald City at its center: Gillikin Country in the north, Quadling Country in the south, Munchkin Country in the east, and Winkie Country in the west. The Emerald City is both a destination and a home within Oz, and Oz is especially important as the Scarecrow's true, beloved home. While traveling and later ruling Silver Island, he repeatedly misses Oz, Ozma, Dorothy, and his friends. He remembers its games, dinners, and palace life, rejects doubt about Oz's existence, and prefers returning to Oz over remaining Emperor or becoming old. Dorothy likewise intends to return and tell Ozma what has happened, while the group hopes to reach Oz beyond the Deadly Desert. The journey unfolds as the Scarecrow searches for family traces, leaves or remains away from Oz, becomes homesick, and joins Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the animals in planning a return. He abdicates and seeks to go back with them, intending to send the Books of Oz to Happy Toko's grandsons and to remain connected to the Emperor's needs from Oz. In the end, Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Sir Hokus, the Comfortable Camel, and the Doubtful Dromedary return safely to a joyful celebration. The Scarecrow remains his old Ozish self in Oz, and Sir Hokus vows to serve it as its good Knight.

records.l: Emerald City, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Emerald City is Oz's capital, a city at the very center of Oz and in the Land of Oz. Called the most beautiful fairy city in the world, it shines with a soft green light for miles and has gemmed turrets, palace spires, and Ozma's palace. It is a seat of rule and help: the Scarecrow becomes its ruler, Ozma is expected to welcome visitors, and Dorothy seeks Ozma's Magic Picture and later Ozma's aid there. Professor Wogglebug travels there to present an idea. While the Scarecrow is missing, Dorothy and companions repeatedly make the city their destination, lose their way or find themselves farther from it, and seek roads back to it. It also hosts the A-B-Sea Serpent and Rattlesnakes, who tell stories there as Oz's celebrities gather to see them leave. At the end, a cyclone carries some companions toward the city, Dorothy and the Scarecrow fly to Ozma's garden, its people free Sir Hokus, and the returning travelers are welcomed.

records.l: old-fashioned Oz party, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Ozma's palace party gathers familiar Oz people, including Dorothy, for blind-man's-buff before Professor Wogglebug interrupts with genealogy questions.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead is a wooden person with a pumpkin head. He jokes that Professor Wogglebug lost his idea, misunderstands genealogy, worries his head is too ripe, then harnesses the Sawhorse to the red wagon and travels with Princess Ozma, Betsy Bobbin, and the Wizard of Oz.

records.l: Dorothy, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy is a real human little girl from Kansas who is also a Princess of Oz, a resident of Ozma's palace, an adventurer, and the Scarecrow's close friend. She is described as having discovered him at a Munchkin farm and as caring deeply about him, even becoming distressed when he may no longer be the Scarecrow in Oz. At Ozma's party, she hosts blind-man's-buff, catches him, and kindly dismisses worries about his ancestry. When the Scarecrow disappears, Dorothy searches for him and sets out with the Cowardly Lion. After being arrested in Pokes for moving too quickly, she meets Sir Hokus, accepts him as her knight, and escapes Pokes with him and the Lion by singing "Three Blind Mice." Their journey toward the Emerald City and the Scarecrow brings dangers and detours: Dorothy faces a storm, Bangladore, Fix City, a broken road, the Winkie Country, and the Deadly Desert. She is repeatedly rescued or assisted by companions, but she also encourages them, negotiates for the group, prevents Sir Hokus from entering the desert, and takes responsibility for their direction. Her wishes carry the company to Silver Island, where she reunites with and embraces the Scarecrow, learns he is Chang Wang Woe, and insists on returning for the Cowardly Lion when he is left behind. Given a magic fan and parasol, Dorothy becomes central to the escape: she accidentally flies with the parasol, helps end the crisis involving the Silver Princes, devises the return to Oz, and skillfully steers the parasol through a black passage and the beanstalk. Back in Oz, she follows the Scarecrow to rescue Sir Hokus, uses the Magic Belt to recover her fallen fan and bring airborne animals down safely, then tells Ozma the story and gives Ozma the magic fan and parasol. Her story unfolds as a determined search for her friend, ending in a safe return to Oz and the Emerald City.

records.l: Scraps, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scraps, a Patchwork Girl made of goods and brought to life by powder of life, jokes about genealogy, calling her family tree a clothes tree.

records.l: Tik-Tok, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Tik-Tok is a heavy copper clockwork man who, when wound, can think, walk, and talk; he asks Dorothy to wind him so he can consider Professor Wogglebug's proposal.

records.l: Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow is a straw-stuffed man and citizen of Oz, formerly its ruler and later ruler of the Silver Islands. He has very good magic brains given by the Wizard of Oz, needs neither food nor sleep, and can work with his head rather than his hands. Though he has no heart, he is troubled when Professor Wogglebug says he has no ancestors or family, only a bean pole as a family tree. Embarrassed and unhappy at being alone in Oz, he leaves the Emerald City to seek his family tree. At the Munchkin farm he investigates the bean pole, falls through it, pays the Middlings with an emerald, and lands in a silver palace. There he is hailed as Emperor Chang Wang Woe, receives imperial dress, fan, and parasol, and learns that he is considered to have a wife, three sons, and fifteen grandsons. He accepts the emperorship, appoints Happy Toko, befriends Tappy Oko, and faces demanding customs, a dragon-kite fall that requires straw and safety pins, and danger from the Golden Islands. He reforms the Silver Island and improves its prosperity, but misses Oz deeply. His sons are cold, his grandsons disbelieve in Oz, and he discovers his sons intend to remove him; after an attempted escape with Happy Toko, they capture him and bind him to the magic beanpole. He ultimately abandons the descent plan, decides to abdicate, gives Dorothy the magic fan and parasol, installs Happy Toko as Emperor, promises his grandsons the Books of Oz, and travels upward through the passage with Dorothy and the others toward Oz.

records.l: Nick Chopper, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Nick Chopper, a Tin Woodman and Royal Emperor of the Winkies, was transformed from a man of meat into tin. Identifying himself as a Tin Woodman, he asks Professor Wogglebug to record him as Smith, rejecting his meat connections.

records.l: Cowardly Lion, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Cowardly Lion is a cowardly lion and animal of Oz, marked by a golden mane, a loud voice, and frequent fear, hunger, sleepiness, and yet great valor in combat. He is Dorothy's companion and traveler, later Sir Hokus's fellow traveler and knight, and an old friend of the Scarecrow. His story begins when he follows Dorothy in search of the Scarecrow, agrees to be the Scarecrow's cousin under Dorothy's adoption plan, carries Dorothy toward the Emerald City, fears thunder, suffers a bump, and falls asleep at Pokes' gates. In Pokes, hunger and sleepiness nearly overcome him, but he helps persuade Sir Hokus to join the quest, is formally but jokingly announced as beknighted, and sings to stay awake. He creates his own song about being the Cowardly Lion of Oz and uses his especially loud voice and breath to keep the Pokes back and pull Dorothy and Sir Hokus through the gates, though it exhausts him. Though frightened, he repeatedly acts courageously: he attacks Bangladore with Sir Hokus, bites the giant's leg, endures his jaws being stuck by taffy, carries Dorothy, and controls his hunger in Fix City. On the purchased road, he clings on during its rapid movement and rescues both Dorothy and Sir Hokus from the stream; Sir Hokus then knights him, making him a knight. Through the Winkie Country and forest he scouts, warns of the Deadly Desert, carries Dorothy, and enjoys the camels' food. He recognizes Wish Way's power, restores the Comfortable Camel and Doubtful Dromedary by wishing them back to themselves, and warns against further wishes. At the reunion he recognizes the Scarecrow but is discouraged that the Scarecrow has a royal family. Unable to climb the beanstalk, he is left behind until the others return for him. He later judges the Princes deserving of becoming pigs, supports Happy Toko as ruler, and is tied to a magic parasol for the return. After surviving a haystack landing with a scratched hide, he is separated again when others rise away, then is blown by a cyclone toward the Emerald City with the two camels.

records.l: Wizard of Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Wizard of Oz is a wizard with magic abilities and a magic instrument. After Glinda's message, he joins Princess Ozma, Betsy Bobbin, and Jack Pumpkinhead on a journey to settle a war. Later he gathers others for Dorothy and the Scarecrow, explains the suspended animals, and makes Happy Toko's distant singing audible.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Betsy Bobbin, a little girl, reads with Princess Ozma, discusses Dorothy and Mer City visitors, then joins Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Wizard to help settle the Horners-Hoppers war.

records.l: Royal Book of Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Professor Wogglebug proposes the Royal Book of Oz to record names and histories of all Oz people; Ozma permits it, he gathers palace guests’ information, writes Chapter Twelve, and includes the Cowardly Lion’s knighting.

records.l: genealogy, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Professor Wogglebug presents genealogy as the study and recording of people's ancestors, family histories, and family trees. The subject confuses several guests, especially the Scarecrow, who has no known ancestors beyond the bean pole from which he was made.

records.l: the bean pole, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The bean pole is a magic beanstalk, also called the Scarecrow's family tree, growing from a crocus and reaching from the Silver Islands toward Oz. It is the Scarecrow's only claimed family tree and the support from which he first descended. When he digs beside it, he slides down its dark passage, clinging to it past the Middlings' kingdom until he lands in the silver palace. After he touches it on the other side of the world, Chang Wang Woe's spirit enters him and brings him to the Silver Islands. Bound to the tall pole there, the group considers its notches a climbable route home, though the Scarecrow judges descent too difficult and dangerous. It also helps guide Dorothy's parasol through the passage and gives her something to grasp during a fall. Finally, the party returns to Oz by climbing it, and its upper opening is covered.

records.l: family tree, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: In the Royal Book of Oz, family trees become a concern when Professor Wogglebug questions what guests descended from. Scraps claims a clothes tree, while the Scarecrow is said to have a bean pole; Wogglebug's remarks distress him and spur his search for his own family tree.

records.l: A-B-Sea Serpent, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A queer, huge serpent from Mer City is made entirely of alphabet blocks, with a serpent’s face and tape-measure tongue. It teaches Mer children their letters, has a large family but no memories, becomes a bridge across the Munchkin Country river for the Scarecrow, vacations yearly with Rattlesnake, can snap off its X block, and receives an emerald collar from Ozma.

records.l: Rattlesnake, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A small creature of rattles, wood, celluloid, and rubber amuses Mer children, vacations with A-B-Sea Serpent, befriends Scarecrow, tells riddles, following it toward Emerald City.

records.l: Munchkin River, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A broad blue river in Munchkin Country lacks a ferry, difficult to cross for the Scarecrow until the A-B-Sea Serpent forms a bridge.

records.l: Munchkin farm, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: contains cornfield (Munchkin farm's cornfield) The Munchkin farm is where Dorothy first discovered the Scarecrow and where the farmer who made him lives. The Scarecrow returns there to look for information about his history.

records.l: cornfield (Munchkin farm's cornfield), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: contains bean pole (Scarecrow's original support) [at its center] The cornfield contains the tall bean pole from which the Scarecrow originally descended. The Scarecrow clears away cornstalks and dried leaves there before digging around the pole.

records.l: the Scarecrow's family, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Scarecrow's family is a group he first believes does not exist, prompting him to seek traces of relatives at the Munchkin farm. It later arrives as three royal sons, the Princes, and fifteen grandsons. Their cold reception, apparent plotting, disbelief in Oz, reminders of his age, and the eldest son's binding him to a bean pole make the family a source of misery.

records.l: Scarecrow's search for his family, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow returns from the Emerald City along the yellow brick road to the Munchkin farm, seeking family traces by investigating and digging around his original bean pole.

records.l: the Scarecrow's discovery by Dorothy, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy discovers the Scarecrow at the Munchkin farm; he is made from a straw-stuffed suit and painted sack, with red boots, hat, and yellow gloves.

records.l: Scarecrow's fall down the bean pole, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow’s fall begins when digging around the bean pole makes its bottom give way. Clinging to a stout pole, he slides rapidly down through a deep black passage, passes the Middlings’ kingdom, then bursts through a silver palace roof and lands in its great hall.

records.l: the Middlings, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Middlings are underground mud-made people with dried grass hair, changing faces, root-like hands and feet, gold teeth, glowing eyes, and dried-mud coats. They dig mud and clay, sing the Middling National Air, travel deep black passages in parties, and demand tolls from travelers.

records.l: the King of the Middlings, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The King of the Middlings, monarch of the Middling Kingdom, wears a tall mud crown and stops the Scarecrow, takes an emerald toll, questions his work, then considers coating him in mud before Muddle releases him.

records.l: Muddle, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Muddle, a mud man and the King's attendant, confronts and insults the Scarecrow, helps restore the King's face, then makes him fall onward.

records.l: the Middling Kingdom, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Middling Kingdom is an underground realm in the middle of the earth, made of worm-rich mud and clay, where inhabitants dig all day and praise mud.

records.l: the cavern (Middlings' kingdom), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A dark, forbidding cavern houses thousands of Middlings, whose flashing red eyes light it as they dig with shovels and picks while one sings.

records.l: tube (inside the beanstalk), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A narrow, deep, black, chimney-like passage or tube links the Scarecrow’s fall downward with Dorothy’s party’s later upward flight. A board briefly stops the Scarecrow for questioning, then opens; later the party ascends for almost an hour, scraping its rough sides.

records.l: the silver palace, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A huge silver palace with halls, courtiers, and a throne room; a roof hole lets the Scarecrow fall inside.

records.l: the courtiers, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Gray-skinned inhabitants of the silver palace serve the Emperor. They mistake the Scarecrow of Oz for their returned Emperor and ancestor, prostrate themselves, carry him to the throne room, and spread news of his arrival.

records.l: the old courtier, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A very old, tottering courtier hobbles forward under a silk umbrella to greet the Scarecrow of Oz, reverently welcoming him as ancestor, father, emperor, and exalted sir.

records.l: Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow is a clever, gallant, and valiant straw man who is recognized by the silver palace’s inhabitants as Emperor and ruler of Silver Island. He has straw stuffing, excellent brains, a royal robe, and a little fan kept for Dorothy; through the fan’s magic, he wins a Silver Island victory despite having no plan. When the Imperial Army retreats, he urges the Silver Islanders to fight the King of the Golden Islands and helps defeat the Gnome King by outwitting him. Fireworks scorch his robe and stuffing, and after Happy Toko extinguishes him he is damp, dull-brained, lonely, and longing for Oz, Dorothy, and friends. Later he goes away to investigate his family tree, prompting Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion to seek him.

records.l: the magic fan, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The magic fan is a small object first found by the Scarecrow in his pocket after a bullet tears his hat. When opened and waved, it blows the King of the Golden Islands and his army upward; when closed, they fall into the sea. The Scarecrow plans to use it to protect the Silver Island, whose people fear it. Later it escapes Dorothy’s pocket, sends three animals airborne, and is closed and returned by the Magic Belt. Dorothy gives it to Ozma for safekeeping.

records.l: the magic parasol, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The magic parasol is a magical object attached to Dorothy’s wrist that opens when she throws up her hands. Though broken after being snapped off the beanstalk, it carries Dorothy through a broken skylight, helps redirect a silver vase, lifts the party from the Silver Island, and lets Dorothy and the Scarecrow fly after Sir Hokus. Dorothy finally gives it to Ozma for storage with Oz’s magic treasures.

records.l: Winkie Country, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Winkie Country is a yellow region bordered by the Deadly Desert. Dorothy recognizes it by yellow-clad little men near a stream; later she, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion cross its deserted woods, finding food, shelter, an ancient woodsman, and camels.

records.l: Scarecrow's golden tower, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow's golden tower in Winkie Country is a gorgeous residence shaped exactly like a huge ear of corn, surrounded by cornfields.

records.l: Pokes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Pokes is the Great Grand and Mighty Slow Kingdom, a strange gray city in Oz with a dimly lighted main gate, gloomy garden, castle, and a speed limit of one-quarter mile an hour. Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion reach it through a forest and sleep at its gate. Its strict ban on quick movement and sound leads to their arrest, but singing keeps them awake and lets them escape with Sir Hokus beyond the gates.

records.l: Magic Picture, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Ozma's Magic Picture in Ozma's palace shows Ozma or Dorothy any friend and what that person is doing; the Cowardly Lion suggests using it to find the Scarecrow.

records.l: the Scarecrow's disappearance, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Scarecrow's disappearance begins after the travelers leave the Emerald City, when he leaves without saying goodbye and does not return home. It causes Dorothy uneasiness; she and the Cowardly Lion search unsuccessfully, and Dorothy's account makes finding him Sir Hokus's new quest.

records.l: journey to find the Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy conducts a search for the Scarecrow, first seeking clues through the palace, gardens, servants, and his empty home with the Cowardly Lion. The travelers return toward the Emerald City to use the Magic Picture, then journey with Sir Hokus through deserted Winkie Country, avoid the Deadly Desert, gain two helpers, and continue on Wish Way.

records.l: adoption plan, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy proposes the adoption plan to give Scarecrow real relations, becoming his sister while Cowardly Lion becomes his cousin.

records.l: storm, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: has thunder [terrific and without rain] A storm begins while Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion travel back toward the Emerald City, bringing repeated crashes of thunder but no rain. The thunder frightens the Cowardly Lion, causes Dorothy to fall into the sandwich box, and contributes to their losing their way.

records.l: Sir Hokus, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Sir Hokus is a gentle, melancholy, brave knight of Pokes, also called a Knight Errant of Oz. He has been imprisoned in Pokes for centuries under a mysterious knight’s curse, sleeping so long that he has forgotten much of his past. Wearing stiff, rusty armor and carrying a sword, he joins Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion on the Quest for the Scarecrow after Dorothy declares him her knight. During the escape from Pokes, he sings an old English ballad and helps Dorothy when she tires, but is dragged over cobbles and left with badly battered armor. Though he thinks he has failed, Dorothy encourages him. He remains loyal to her colors and follows her through danger, even when his sword breaks against Bangladore or when he feels an easy victory is not a proper fight. As the journey continues, Sir Hokus grows especially concerned for the Scarecrow, helps the travelers in Fix City, helps buy a road, and is rescued from drowning by the Cowardly Lion after falling into a stream in heavy armor. In gratitude he knights the Lion. He cheers the company with songs, serves as the Comfortable Camel’s Karwan Bashi, and is treated as family by both camels. He is briefly transformed into a raven, then resumes his knightly role. He offers his sword and lance to the Scarecrow, supports the Scarecrow’s wish to remain himself, helps the party through the beanstalk adventure, kills the rheumatic dragon, and assists in restoring order on the Silver Island. Returning toward Oz, he cuts through the earth above the beanstalk. After eating a red bean, a branch grows from his shoulders and lifts him into the air, but Dorothy and the Scarecrow bring him safely to Oz, where the branch breaks away. He ends welcomed as Dorothy’s Knight Errant, promising to fight for Dorothy, Ozma, and Oz.

records.l: Pokes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Pokes are sleepy, slow-moving inhabitants of Pokes kingdom, ruled by the Chief Poker and unable to live outside it. They dislike noise and music, play croquet slowly, and arrest Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion. Sir Hokus's songs and later loud singing frighten them away; after a Poke puts Dorothy to sleep, the Cowardly Lion scatters them by dragging the travelers through the city gates.

records.l: the Quest for the Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Quest for the Scarecrow is undertaken and conducted by Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion. It begins when Sir Hokus joins Dorothy and the Lion in leaving Pokes; they sing to stay awake, travel toward the Emerald City, and seek information from King Fix It, who knows only a picture of the Scarecrow.

records.l: Three Blind Mice, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Three Blind Mice is the song Dorothy sings during the escape from Pokes. She returns to singing it after stumbling over a wicket and later begins singing it again after the Cowardly Lion has rescued her.

records.l: escape from Pokes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A successful escape rescues Dorothy and Sir Hokus from the Pokes after their singing prevents sleep; despite Dorothy's hokey pokey incapacitation, the Cowardly Lion ropes both through the gates to safety.

records.l: Glinda, the Good Sorceress of Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Glinda, the Good Sorceress of Oz, lives in a palace in Quadling Country, uses a Magic Record Book, and sends Ozma news of renewed war.

records.l: Silver Island, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Silver Island, also called the Silver Islands, is a flowery, bewilderingly beautiful realm surrounded by silver water and filled with silver houses, towers, temples, bridges, waterfalls, gardens, lanterns, and a royal palace. Its Imperial Palace overlooks the harbor, and its court includes an imperial silver throne room with a bean pole at the center of the hall. The Silver Islanders live there under rulers whose palace and court are richly furnished with silver, precious stones, rugs, flowers, flags, and chimes. After fifty years under the Grand Chew Chew, the Scarecrow is proclaimed Emperor Chang Wang Woe. The island fears invasion by the King of the Golden Islands, who attacks, but the Scarecrow saves it with the little fan, bringing victory and a great celebration. His reforms make the island more prosperous, though he misses Oz. Later Dorothy and her companions find him there, where royal authorities threaten their imprisonment as they try to escape. At the Ceremony of Restoration, the Islanders expect him to resume rule, but he seeks to leave for Oz. After the Princes become pigs, Happy Toko becomes Emperor. The Scarecrow departs while promising to watch over the island with the magic fan, and the Magic Picture later shows Happy Toko serving as Emperor before the former court.

records.l: forest road to the Emerald City, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A dim green woodland with two branching roads and a crooked, winding path that dwindles from road; sunlight barely penetrates its depths, where Bangladore bars smaller visitors until helping the travelers leave.

records.l: Chang Wang Woe, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Chang Wang Woe is the Great and Imperial ruler and Supreme Highness of the Silver Islands, said to have ruled fifty years earlier and defeated the King of the Golden Islands. Married to Tsing Tsing and father and grandfather within a royal family, he later abdicates his throne. By necromancy he becomes the crocus, and prophecy holds that his spirit enters the first being touching the magic beanstalk, returning as the Scarecrow. Revealed as the Scarecrow’s identity and under enchantment in that body, he dislikes being Emperor and fears the Gheewizard’s elixir making him old. He helps Dorothy save Sir Hokus, remains in Oz as a plain Scarecrow, and rules Silver Island through Happy Toko as Emperor.

records.l: Grand Chew Chew, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Grand Chew Chew is a Silverman and the aged grand, chief court official who ruled the Silver Islands for fifty years before the Scarecrow’s return. In Chapter 7, he proclaims the Scarecrow to be Emperor Chang Wang Woe returned, explains the prophecy, seeks relief from state cares, supplies royal clothing, and accompanies the Scarecrow through the realm. He then serves as prime minister and minister, advises the Scarecrow on imperial etiquette, objects to informal conduct, and warns of the Golden Islands’ king and the beanstalk prophecy. After the victory, he organizes a celebration and becomes more agreeable under the Scarecrow’s reforms. In Chapter 15, he publicly announces Chang Wang Woe’s promised restoration and secretly confers with General Mugwump.

records.l: Tsing Tsing, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Tsing Tsing, Silver Fisher’s daughter, was Emperor Chang Wang Woe’s wife and Empress of the Silver Islands. When he became a fading crocus, her tears kept it fresh three days. She died, returning to silver ancestors; after Scarecrow rescued her, she married him.

records.l: Happy Toko, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Happy Toko is a fat little, kind-hearted, jolly Silver Islander: the Scarecrow’s companion, faithful royal attendant, and Imperial Punster. As a small boy he attends the Scarecrow’s marriage, later accompanies him on walks, sings of his past, and tells how he met and married Tsing Tsing. At a kite-flying exhibition, he fears the Scarecrow has been killed after a fall and repairs him with straw and safety pins. During danger on the Silver Island, he alone follows the Scarecrow, carries a watering can, and extinguishes him when fireworks set him smoking. He remains beside the lonely Scarecrow, cheers him, welcomes his family, manages the grandsons, hears stories of Oz, and sings humorous songs. Suspicious of the Princes, he calls their whispering treason, scowls at them, and is captured and bound with the Scarecrow. He later prepares the throne room, warns of approaching Princes and the Grand Gheewizard, takes a language pill that lets him speak and understand Ozish instead of Silver Islandish, and climbs the bean pole. Newly appointed Emperor, he accepts the throne and the Silver Islanders’ allegiance despite sadness at the Scarecrow’s departure.

records.l: Silver Islanders, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Silver Islanders, or Silvermen, are the people of the Silver Islands, described as an older race than their Chinese cousins and as people of the stars. They inhabit and live on Silver Island, eat its cuisine, and serve the Emperor through elaborate court ceremonies. They are portrayed as quarrelsome and too stupid to appreciate their country’s beauty. They watch a kite exhibition, panic at the approach of the King of the Golden Islands, and flee during the invasion, cheering faintly for Chang Wang Woe. After the Scarecrow defeats the invaders, they return, celebrate with speeches, a banquet, and fireworks, and carry him to the palace. They love him as their honorable little Father and resist his abdication, but ultimately pledge allegiance to Happy Toko as Emperor.

records.l: Golden Islands, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Golden Islands are associated with the fleet and the king who threatens the Silver Islands with fire and enslavement.

records.l: prophecy of the beanstalk, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The prophecy of the beanstalk foretells that Emperor Chang Wang Woe’s spirit will enter the first being to touch the magic beanstalk on the other side of the world and return fifty years later to save his people. When the Scarecrow arrives, the Grand Chew Chew declares it fulfilled and demands he face the danger to save the Silver Islanders.

records.l: magic fan, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A magical fan, produced by the Scarecrow and given to Dorothy, is secured with the Cowardly Lion’s hair for defending Oz against conquest.

records.l: the Scarecrow's transformation into his old Imperial self, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Gheewizard’s elixir transforms the lively Scarecrow into his old Imperial self, an old Emperor. Fearing loss of his Scarecrow identity and, at eighty-five, inability to return to Oz, he is bound by the eldest Prince so the change can proceed.

records.l: Chang Wang Woe's transformation into a crocus, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_caused_by necromancy [performed by a magician employed by the King of the Golden Islands] Fifty years earlier, a magician working for the King of the Golden Islands entered Chang Wang Woe's sleeping chamber and used necromancy to transform him into a crocus. Tsing Tsing preserved the fading crocus with her tears until it became the source of the magic beanstalk.

records.l: the return of Chang Wang Woe's spirit, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_prophesied_by the prophecy of the magic beanstalk [after fifty years] Chang Wang Woe's spirit is said to have returned when the Scarecrow touched the magic beanstalk. The Silvermen therefore identify the Scarecrow as their former Emperor, although he retains the Scarecrow's body and memories rather than remembering a life as Chang Wang Woe.

records.l: King of the Golden Islands, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: King of the Golden Islands rules the Golden Islands, commands an army, and has a sister, Princess Orange Blossom, proposed as a bride. He threatens to conquer, burn, and enslave the Silver Islands, sends a fleet, and leads an invasion, but the little fan drops him into the sea, forcing retreat.

records.l: Golden Islands fleet, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Golden Islands fleet, the king's fleet, sails singular silken-sailed vessels into the harbor, causing the court to fear an attack as the Scarecrow watches.

records.l: dragon kite, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A dragon-shaped kite with a tail hook catches the Scarecrow, carries him toward the clouds, then shakes him until he falls onto rocks.

records.l: kites, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: are favorite sport [in the Silver Islands] The kites at the exhibition take many forms, including huge fish, silver paper dragons, and birds. They are flown by Silver Islanders while a large crowd watches.

records.l: kite-flying exhibition, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: has kites [of many shapes and kinds] The kite-flying exhibition draws a great throng of boys, girls, and adults. The disguised Scarecrow attends with Tappy Oko, but the event becomes dangerous when the dragon kite carries him away.

records.l: Golden Islands invasion, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: threatens Silver Islands [under the King of the Golden Islands] The threatened Golden Islands invasion is represented by the fleet entering the harbor. The Grand Chew Chew says the attack will burn the Silver Islands and enslave their people.

records.l: Imperial Army, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Imperial Army, stationed in Silver Island caves, retreats there rather than confront invaders; its General credits the retreat for victory, after which the army receives decorations.

records.l: King of the Golden Islands' army, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_defeated_by little fan [the fan lifts them into the air and drops them into the sea] The King of the Golden Islands' army lands on Silver Island in small boats and fires at the Scarecrow. The little fan sends the soldiers high into the air and then plunges them into the sea, after which they climb back into their boats and sail away.

records.l: magic, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_in little fan [the fan controls the enemy's elevation] The magic comes from the little fan the Scarecrow has been saving for Dorothy. It lifts the enemy army into the air when opened or waved and drops them into the sea when closed.

records.l: watering can, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_used_to_extinguish Scarecrow [when his straw stuffing catches fire] The Scarecrow asks Happy Toko to bring a watering can in case he catches fire. Happy later uses a giant silver watering can to put out the Scarecrow's smoking straw stuffing during the fireworks.

records.l: fireworks, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: ignite Scarecrow's straw stuffing [during the Silver Island celebration] The Silver Islanders set off elaborate fireworks to celebrate their victory. Sparks land in the Scarecrow's lap and set his straw stuffing smoking, forcing Happy Toko to extinguish him.

records.l: Scarecrow's victory over the king of the Golden Islands, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_won_with little fan [by the Scarecrow] The Silver Island victory is achieved when the Scarecrow uses the magic of the little fan to defeat and drive away the King of the Golden Islands' army. The Imperial Army claims partial responsibility because it had left the field, and the victory is followed by decorations, a banquet, and fireworks.

records.l: Horners, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Horners are quarrelsome folk living in the Quadling mountains, described as being at war with the Hoppers again.

records.l: Hoppers, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Hoppers are quarrelsome people in the Quadling mountains, again at war with the Horners.

records.l: war between the Horners and Hoppers, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a war [recurring conflict] The Horners and Hoppers are at war again. Princess Ozma, Betsy Bobbin, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Wizard of Oz travel to help settle the conflict.

records.l: Bangladore, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Bangladore is a candy giant with taffy legs, a peppermint collar, sourball eyes, a chocolate coat, and huge marshmallow buttons. He bars smaller beings from his forest and sings of humans as food, threatens travelers, then falls under attack and meekly carries them out after promising silence.

records.l: candy giant encounter, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion confront candy-bodied Bangladore after his song; Dorothy secures their safe removal and his marshmallow vest buttons by promising secrecy.

records.l: escape from the forest, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Bangladore lifts Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion from the forest, drops them in a daisy field in the Winkie Country, and they follow a road seeking the Scarecrow.

records.l: Fix City, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Fix City is a strange gated city inhabited by the Fixes, or Fix Its. It has one long street and circles for each resident or occupant. Its broad-faced, long-footed people stand motionless in chalked circles and use bells to summon moving furniture. From the entrance, King Fix sends Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion to buy a road at the street’s end.

records.l: King Fix It, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: King Fix It is the king of Fix City, resembling its inhabitants except for his crown. He rules by handling one question at a time, hosts travelers, explains the people’s stillness preserves furniture, and knows Scarecrows only from a picture.

records.l: the Fixes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Fixes are inhabitants of Fix City with large round heads and unusually long flat feet. Alike in simple gendered clothing, they stand in chalked circles while furniture moves, then sit to eat and stare at Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion as unusual runabouts.

records.l: the travelers' journey to Fix City, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion journey through deserted country, rest at a stream and pear orchard, then reach Fix City at night for food and transport by walking beds.

records.l: road (purchased in Fix City), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A five-mile road purchased by Dorothy and her companions, lined with trees, unrolls rapidly to carry travelers to a stream in the Winkie Country, then winds up after throwing them into the air.

records.l: stream (in the Winkie Country), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a broad stream of water [muddy] The stream is where Dorothy and Sir Hokus land after falling from the road. Dorothy nearly drowns in its muddy water, while the Cowardly Lion swims in and pulls both travelers to safety.

records.l: knighting of the Cowardly Lion, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_performed_by Sir Hokus [after the Lion saves his life] After the Cowardly Lion saves Sir Hokus from the stream, Sir Hokus declares that the Lion shall be knighted. He strikes the Lion on the shoulder and calls him Sir Cowardly Lion before collapsing to sleep.

records.l: rescue of Dorothy and Sir Hokus, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_performed_by Cowardly Lion [from the stream] Dorothy is not helped by Memo, who says that he only saves lives on Monday, while Ran attempts to reach her but cannot swim fast enough. The Cowardly Lion rescues Dorothy and then returns to retrieve Sir Hokus from the stream.

records.l: three Silver Princes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The three Silver Princes are the Scarecrow's haughty, overbearing royal sons and fathers of fifteen grandsons. They plot to kill the Scarecrow and succeed him, first considering throwing him into the silver river. They feign affection while making him feel old, seek the Grand Gheewizard's help to restore Chang Wang Woe's original form, and promote plans concerning succession and marriage. Resenting the Scarecrow's friends from Oz, they insist on continuing the Ceremony of Restoration. When the silver vase bursts over them, two become silver pigs and the eldest becomes a weasel, and they flee into the gardens.

records.l: eldest Silver Prince, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Scarecrow’s eldest son announces marriage to Princess Orange Blossom to celebrate the Scarecrow’s restoration, then has the Scarecrow and Happy Toko bound to the beanstalk under the Grand Gheewizard’s formula, hoping to become Emperor after his father’s death.

records.l: fifteen little Princes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Fifteen little Princes, the Scarecrow’s solemn grandsons and sons of three Princes, formally greet him, deny Oz exists because it is absent from their map, and are returned by Happy Toko to the royal nursery.

records.l: Deadly Desert, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Deadly Desert is a poisonous barrier ahead of the travelers, keeping intruders from Oz by destroying every living thing that enters.

records.l: Grand Gheewizard, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Grand Gheewizard is a wizard of the Silver Island who lives in a dark cave in a silver mountain with a rheumatic dragon. He discovers a formula to break the Scarecrow's enchantment and prepares an elixir, consulting a yellow book and waiting for it to boil. Later he brings a sealed silver vase against the Scarecrow, but Dorothy's interference transforms the three Princes, and he is seized and taken to his cave.

records.l: dragon, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A rheumatic, silver-scaled dragon belonging to the Grand Gheewizard is chained in his dark cave, follows him into the throne room, and is killed by Sir Hokus.

records.l: Princess Orange Blossom, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Princess Orange Blossom, a richly clad, cross-looking elderly Princess and sister of the King of the Golden Islands, is proposed as bride for the eldest Prince. She arrives to marry the Emperor, persists after the ceremony is disrupted, swoons when the Cowardly Lion attacks her palanquin, and is carried away by order of the Scarecrow, whom she intends to marry.

records.l: family tree (the beanstalk), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a family tree [belonging to the Scarecrow's family] The magic beanpole is the Scarecrow's family tree, and the eldest Prince orders the Scarecrow tied to it as part of the Grand Gheewizard's formula.

records.l: the magic formula, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: breaks the enchantment [freeing Chang Wang Woe from the Scarecrow body] The Grand Gheewizard's magic formula is said to restore Chang Wang Woe to his original shape and free him from the Scarecrow body. The eldest Prince identifies tying the Scarecrow to the beanstalk as part of the formula.

records.l: Gheewizard’s elixir, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: restores Chang Wang Woe's restoration to his original form [after boiling one more night] The Grand Gheewizard prepares an elixir in a large kettle in his cave. He tells the youngest Prince that it must boil for one more night before it is ready.

records.l: the enchantment, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: affects Chang Wang Woe [keeping him in the Scarecrow body] The Grand Chew Chew says that the Grand Gheewizard's discovery will break the enchantment that has left Chang Wang Woe in the Scarecrow's body.

records.l: Chang Wang Woe's restoration to his original form, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_announced_by the Grand Chew Chew [as occurring tomorrow] Chang Wang Woe's restoration is announced as an event to take place the next day. The Scarecrow understands that this restoration would leave him in his old Imperial self, at eighty-five years old.

records.l: the proposed marriage of the eldest Prince and Orange Blossom, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_intended_to_celebrate Chang Wang Woe's restoration to his original form [according to the eldest Prince] The eldest Prince announces the proposed marriage to make the celebration of the Scarecrow's restoration complete. The Scarecrow is alarmed when he sees Orange Blossom and realizes that she is an elderly Princess rather than the youthful bride he expected.

records.l: Comfortable Camel, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Comfortable Camel is a comfortable, happy camel of Oz and friend of the Doubtful Dromedary. Separated from its caravan and absent Karwan Bashi by a sandstorm, it arrives carrying meal supplies, cushions, a tent, and other goods, feeds the travelers, and accepts Sir Hokus as Karwan Bashi. When the Dromedary disappears, it cries, causing Sir Hokus to fall, then melts into air; the Cowardly Lion wishes it back, reuniting it with both companions. Returning to Oz, it is welcomed as family, grieves when the others vanish upward, and is blown toward the Emerald City with the Lion and Dromedary.

records.l: Doubtful Dromedary, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The Doubtful Dromedary is a habitually doubtful dromedary of Oz and friend of the Comfortable Camel, carrying goods, silk cushions, and a tent. It travels with the Camel and other travelers onto Wish Way, repeatedly doubting what it hears. It disappears into a big yellow butterfly, is restored by the Cowardly Lion’s wish, and doubts it wanted the change. Later it fears rejection in Oz and Sir Hokus’s loss before a cyclone carries it toward the Emerald City.

records.l: caravan, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A caravan begins with Comfortable Camel and Doubtful Dromedary, loses its Karwan Bashi in a sandstorm, then travels with Dorothy, Sir Hokus, and the Cowardly Lion.

records.l: Wish Way, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Wish Way is a narrow, tree-lined road marked by a sign. The travelers follow it rather than turn back and learn that every wish made there comes true. Dorothy wishes to be with the Scarecrow, causing her and the others to fall to Silver Island.

records.l: road, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: has_name Wish Way [shown on a sign] Dorothy and her companions spend three days looking for a road leading back to the Emerald City. They eventually find a narrow, tree-lined road marked Wish Way.

records.l: magic, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: causes_transformations living beings Magic causes the characters to transform: Sir Hokus becomes a raven, the Comfortable Camel melts into air, and the Doubtful Dromedary becomes a butterfly. Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion recognize that magic transformations may happen to them as well.

records.l: wishing, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a particular work [according to Dorothy] Wishing on Wish Way is powerful and precise, as shown when wishes transform and restore the characters. Dorothy's wish that everyone stop wishing makes the group unable to speak, and her final eight-word wish opens the earth and swallows everyone.

records.l: Dorothy's company, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Dorothy's party is fastened to a parasol by ropes of varying lengths, flies upward through a passage, crashes and tumbles, returns to Oz, then is swallowed by earth after Dorothy's final wish.

records.l: Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow is in an excellent body on Silver Island, where he is treated as Emperor and temporarily speaks Silver Islandish. Though he has the Emperor’s sons, grandsons, and bride, and is identified there as Chang Wang Woe, he prefers being himself and considers Oz his true home. After recognizing his friends, he explains that he is better suited to being a Scarecrow, gives Happy Toko a language pill, and proposes using the family-tree bean pole to reach Oz. He announces his abdication in favor of his eldest son, keeps his current body, confronts the Grand Gheewizard’s magic, orders the Grand Gheewizard seized, and dismisses the Silver Islanders and Princess Orange Blossom. Back in Oz, he helps cover the bean-pole opening, vows never to leave Oz, and follows Dorothy upward to help Sir Hokus before being carried toward the sky.

records.l: the wish to reunite with the Scarecrow, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: causes the fall to Silver Island [immediately] Dorothy's wish to be with the Scarecrow transports her and her companions from Wish Way to Silver Island. Instead of bringing them directly to the Scarecrow in Oz, it causes them to fall through the darkness into his throne room.

records.l: the fall to Silver Island, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: causes Silver Island [by a wish] Dorothy, the Cowardly Lion, Sir Hokus of Pokes, the Comfortable Camel, and the Doubtful Dromedary fall repeatedly before landing in the Scarecrow's throne room on Silver Island. The Comfortable Camel and Doubtful Dromedary describe the fall as going on and on.

records.l: being oneself, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_important best self [rather than former identity] The Scarecrow decides that he wants to be himself rather than choose between being an Emperor and being a Scarecrow. He and Dorothy conclude that being one's best self matters more than what one was, and he identifies himself as a better Scarecrow than an Emperor.

records.l: parasol, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The parasol, plucked from a beanstalk and fitted with a handle, enables flight when opened. It carries Dorothy's party upward, partly closes and drops them after a crash, then is reopened; later it slows descent and helps Dorothy and the Scarecrow pursue Sir Hokus.

records.l: Scarecrow's abdication, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow's proposed abdication is his planned means of returning to Oz. He intends to give a farewell speech, abdicate in favor of his eldest son, keep his body, and leave with the others. Fearing Gheewizard's magic, the group prepares to flee; the Silver Islanders reject the abdication and demand he remain Emperor.

records.l: magic, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a power [capable of transforming beings] Magic is central to the attempted restoration and transformation, and the characters fear the Grand Gheewizard's power. The Scarecrow calls magic a serious matter to meddle with after the elixir transforms the Princes, and the Grand Gheewizard is removed because of his dangerous actions.

records.l: Ceremony of Restoration, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A ceremony to restore the Scarecrow's proper body and authority as Emperor proceeds despite his attempt to stop it, until Dorothy's parasol and a misdirected silver vase disrupt it.

records.l: slaying of the dragon, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a slaying [performed by Sir Hokus] The slaying of the dragon is carried out by Sir Hokus when he sees the Grand Gheewizard's rheumatic dragon. It causes an explosion, fills the hall with smoke, enrages the Grand Gheewizard, and adds to the confusion surrounding the ceremony.

records.l: transformation of the Princes, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_a transformation [into their true shapes] The transformation of the Princes occurs when the magic elixir from the silver vase lands on them instead of the Scarecrow. Two become silver pigs and the eldest becomes a weasel, revealing their true shapes.

records.l: silver vase, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: contains magic elixir [sealed inside the vase] The Grand Gheewizard holds the sealed silver vase above his head and throws it at the Scarecrow while reciting an incantation. Dorothy's returning parasol knocks it off course, causing it to burst over the three Silver Princes.

records.l: magic elixir, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: causes_transformation three Silver Princes [into their true shapes] The magic elixir is contained in the silver vase and is intended to restore the Scarecrow's original body. Instead, it touches the three Silver Princes and changes them into two silver pigs and a weasel.

records.l: the escape from the Silver Island, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: uses the magic parasol The escape from the Silver Island is carried out when Dorothy opens the magic parasol after everyone is securely tied to it. The entire party floats gently upward and disappears from the sight of the astonished Silver Islanders.

records.l: the journey back to Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: is_planned_by Dorothy The journey back to Oz is planned by Dorothy and undertaken by the Scarecrow, Dorothy, Sir Hokus, the Cowardly Lion, the Doubtful Dromedary, and the Comfortable Camel. They fasten ropes around themselves and the animals and attach them to the magic parasol for flight.

records.l: the coronation and installation of Happy Toko, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Happy Toko is crowned and installed as Emperor in the throne room after receiving the Imperial hat, accepting Silver Islanders’ allegiance, speaking, and taking his place as the party departs.

records.l: flight through the passage, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: has_duration hours The flight carries Dorothy's party upward through pitch darkness. It includes a crash that makes the parasol partly close and sends the party falling, followed by a faster ascent after Dorothy reopens the parasol.

records.l: green branch (growing from Sir Hokus), The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A green branch suddenly sprouts from Sir Hokus’s shoulders after he eats a red bean, attaches firmly to the bean pole, and carries him upward out of sight.

records.l: cyclone, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: A cyclone whistles through trees, blows the Cowardly Lion, Comfortable Camel, and Doubtful Dromedary high into the air, and sends them toward the Emerald City.

records.l: return to Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: brings Dorothy [back to the Munchkin landscape] The party returns to Oz by emerging through the beanstalk and landing on a haystack near the bean pole. They celebrate being home and prepare to travel to the Emerald City.

records.l: Scarecrow's rescue and return to Oz, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow's rescue and return to Oz is an event experienced by Dorothy. After Dorothy's adventures with Sir Hokus, the Comfortable Camel, and the Doubtful Dromedary, Dorothy and Sir Hokus rescue the Scarecrow and return with him to Oz, where he explains his royal identity, is welcomed by friends, and vows never to leave them again.

records.l: magic beanstalk, The Royal Book of Oz
records.s: The magic beanstalk grows from a red bean swallowed by Sir Hokus, rooted in his back and carrying him toward the clouds, then stops, snaps off, and disappears.

The document is a fantasy adventure centered on two linked crises in Oz. At Prince Pompadore’s eighteenth birthday feast in Pumperdink, a magical cake explodes and a scroll warns that the kingdom will disappear unless Pompadore marries the Proper Fairy Princess in time. King Pompus tries to force him to marry the ancient Princess Faleero, but Kabumpo, the Elegant Elephant, spirits Pompadore away to seek Ozma, whom they hope is the required princess. Their journey brings them through Rith Metic, where Pompadore escapes the Figure Heads, and Illumi Nation, before they reach the Emerald City. Meanwhile, Ruggedo, the former Gnome King, finds Glegg’s Box of Mixed Magic in his underground cavern. He enlarges Peg Amy, a wooden doll, and Wag, his rabbit servant; reanimates Peg; then expands himself into a giant and carries Ozma’s palace on his head into Ev. The palace’s inhabitants, including Ozma, Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Scraps, Sir Hokus, and Tik Tok, endure the upheaval. They temporarily restrain Ruggedo by threatening him with eggs, but the Sand Man’s silver sand puts nearly all of them to sleep. Glinda learns of Ruggedo’s attack and seeks a remedy. Kabumpo and Pompadore join Peg Amy and Wag, who are traveling to correct Ruggedo’s magic, and the four journey toward Ev. They fight the Twigs, are carried across the Deadly Desert by the Runaway Country, and finally find Ruggedo with the palace on his head. Glinda uses Trick Tea to make him return and shrink. Pompadore proposes to Ozma, but she refuses and learns through the Question Box that he must marry the Princess of Sun Top Mountain. The travelers return to the Winkie Country and reach a golden castle on Sun Top Mountain. A magic mirror reveals Peg Amy to be the Princess of Sun Top Mountain and the Proper Princess, changing her from a wooden doll into a living princess. Uncle Tozzyfog explains that Glegg had enchanted her after she refused to marry him; Pompadore and Wag helped free her by recognizing her as a princess. Pompadore and Peg Amy marry, saving Pumperdink. In the conclusion, Ozma banishes Ruggedo and the Runaway Country to the Nonestic Ocean as Ruggedo’s Island, defeats Glegg with his own Triple Trick Tea, and restores order to the palace.

King Pompus is the proud, fat, old King of Pumperdink, husband of Queen Pozy and father of Prince Pompadore. He rules through the dipping punishment, rewarding right conduct and punishing wrongdoing. After a birthday cake explodes, he orders footmen dipped and learns that Pompadore must marry the Proper Fairy Princess or Pumperdink will disappear. Fearing this fate, he chooses Princess Faleero as the Proper Princess, orders their wedding, and has the castle watched for disappearance.
Queen Pozy of Pumperdink, loveliest of the royal family and King Pompus’s wife, attends a birthday feast, repeatedly faints after an explosion and marriage condition.

Prince Pompadore is the handsome Prince of Pumperdink, son of King Pompus and his queen, whose eighteenth birthday reveals a condition that he must marry a Proper Princess or Pumperdink and its people will disappear. He initially rejects marriage and is ordered to marry Princess Faleero, but, distressed by Queen Pozy's tears and his duty to save the kingdom, he agrees to seek a solution. Kabumpo secretly carries him from the palace, and the two travel toward the Emerald City, with Pompadore resolving to consider every princess they meet. Their journey brings trials and setbacks: Pompadore escapes Rith Metic by doing somersaults, falls into the Illumi Nation and loses his golden hair, and survives other dangers. In the Emerald City, he mistakes Glinda for Ozma, then believes rescuing Ozma from a giant in Ev may let him marry her and save Pumperdink. Joined by Peg Amy and Wag, he fights the Twigs, is injured and separated from supplies by the Runaway Country, and continues toward Ozma. When Ozma is found, Pompadore proposes, but she refuses. The Question Box reveals that he must marry the Princess of Sun Top Mountain. Though gloomy and reluctant to marry an unknown princess, he realizes at the gold castle that he would rather return to Pumperdink with Peg Amy. He then learns that Peg Amy is the Proper Princess, helps free her by recognizing and believing she is a princess, and marries her. Afterward, he travels with Peg Amy to the Emerald City and Pumperdink and is expected to visit Ozma and the others.

Kabumpo is Pumperdink’s only elephant, its Elegant Elephant, and a favored member of the royal family. Splendidly dressed in robes, pearls, and jewels, he has royal quarters, an attendant named Spezzle, and deep devotion to Prince Pompadore, whom he loves, advises, guards, and carries. Mischievous as well as formidable, he steals feast food, blows out birthday candles and explodes the cake, frightens enemies with his trumpet, and can be impatient, proud, and easily angered by indignity. Kabumpo fiercely opposes Pompadore’s arranged marriage to Faleero, whom he considers unsuitable, and insists that Ozma is the Proper Princess. He helps Pompadore flee Pumperdink through a secret entrance, taking jewels, a magic mirror, and a gold door knob. Their journey leads through Rith Metic, where Kabumpo helps Pompadore escape and anxiously follows him; the Illumi Nation, where he damages his robe and tail but returns them safely to the surface; and the Soup Sea and Emerald City. Learning that Ozma has been taken to Ev, he urges her rescue and travels onward with Pompadore. Along the way Kabumpo meets Peg Amy and Wag. Though he first laughs at Peg Amy and quarrels with Wag, he becomes protective and caring, comforts Peg Amy, gives her a pearl necklace, promises to help her gain a Court position, and fights to protect the travelers from Twigs. Captured by the Runaway Country, he refuses to be used as a laborer and demands proper food. He helps seek Ozma and confront Ruggedo’s threat, while also trying to arrange a chance for Pompadore to ask Ozma to marry him. Ozma refuses Pompadore, disappointing Kabumpo, but he continues with his friends. He safeguards the magic mirror and gold door knob, refuses to proceed without Peg Amy, helps enter the gold castle, and rejoices when the mirror reveals Peg Amy’s identity. By the end, Peg Amy recognizes him as one of the friends who helped free her, and Kabumpo travels on with Pompadore.
The courtiers attend Prince Pompadore's eighteenth birthday feast, endure fifteen speeches, are scattered or unconscious after the cake explodes, then emerge and anxiously hear the scroll read.

Pumperdink is a cozy, old-fashioned, ancient and honorable kingdom, also called a country, in the northern Gilliken Country of Oz. It has a palace and a courtyard well: inhabitants who do wrong are lowered into the stone well and dipped. It is ruled by Pompus and Pozy Pink, while Prince Pompadore is its prince and regards it as his homeland. Its central crisis is a magic scroll’s warning that Pumperdink and everyone in it will disappear unless Pompadore marries a Proper Princess, or Proper Fairy Princess, within the stated time, described as seven days. Fear of this danger darkens and secures the palace, and Pompadore and Kabumpo leave Pumperdink to seek help and continue a marriage quest. The Question Box later confirms that it has not disappeared, although it is subsequently described as having disappeared and still needing rescue. After Pompadore learns that Peg Amy is the proper princess, he considers returning with her. Their marriage saves Pumperdink; news is carried to the kingdom, and the couple visits its King and Queen.

records.l: the palace of Pumperdink, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The palace of Pumperdink contains a banquet hall and golden door bolts; though anxiously barred and dark, Kabumpo secretly carries Pompadore out.

records.l: the Gilliken country of Oz, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Purple northern part of Oz containing Illumi Nation and Pumperdink, where a scroll threatens Pumperdink’s disappearance unless a royal marriage condition is met.

records.l: the royal birthday cake, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The royal birthday cake is Hashem’s great, gorgeous pink masterpiece, made for Prince Pompadore. It disappears from the pantry table, reappears for his birthday feast, and is suspected of containing magic after a mysterious scroll and other objects appear. When Kabumpo blows out its candles, it explodes as the cake explosion.

records.l: the eighteen birthday candles, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Eighteen candles on Prince Pompadore’s royal birthday cake resist ordinary blowing by Pompadore and others until Kabumpo extinguishes them with one powerful breath.

records.l: the threatening scroll, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The scroll appears upright in a tumbler after the cake explosion and bears the signature J. G. It states that Prince Pompadore must marry the Proper Fairy Princess within the proper span of time or Pumperdink will disappear forever and even longer from the Gilliken country of Oz.

records.l: Prince Pompadore's eighteenth birthday, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Prince Pompadore's eighteenth birthday is a celebration with a feast, speeches, music, and a large pink cake. The cake explodes, and a mysterious scroll announces the royal marriage condition. At the party, Pompadore learns of the cake, gold mirror, and door knob for his Proper Princess search.

records.l: the cake explosion, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: causes the courtiers [half are thrown under the table and the rest are knocked unconscious] The cake explosion occurs after Kabumpo blows out the eighteen candles. It flings half the courtiers under the table, knocks others unconscious, scatters icing and tableware, damages the royal clothing, and leads Pompus to order several palace servants dipped.

records.l: the royal marriage condition, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The royal marriage condition requires Prince Pompadore to wed a Proper Fairy Princess within a proper time or Pumperdink will disappear from the Gilliken country of Oz. The scroll starts his quest, and the Question Box redirects him from Ozma to the Princess of Sun Top Mountain.

records.l: the disappearance of Pumperdink, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The disappearance of Pumperdink is an imminent threatened event, conditioned on Prince Pompadore failing to meet the royal marriage condition in time. According to the scroll, Pumperdink would vanish forever from the Gilliken country of Oz, affecting everybody. The threat alarms King Pompus, who orders guards to watch for signs as small as a missing fence paling, while the palace repeatedly checks that it still exists. Kabumpo prepares to disappear elegantly but leaves with Pompadore, taking him to seek a Proper Princess. Though Pompadore wants to return and save his parents and kingdom, Kabumpo presses onward. The danger remains unresolved while Pompa seeks a princess whose marriage may save Pumperdink.

Princess Faleero, a thousand-year-old, unattractive royal fairy princess, lives in a small Follensby forest hut near Pumperdink and gathers faggots. She gladly accepts Prince Pompadore and agrees to marry him the next morning.

Ozma is the little fairy Princess, Queen, and Fairy Ruler of Oz, ruling from her royal Emerald City palace. She is described as the loveliest, beautiful, lovely, and good; she has lived almost a thousand years, is unharmed by dangers because she is a fairy, and is regarded by Kabumpo as the Proper Princess. As ruler, she welcomes Trot and Betsy Bobbin to remain in Oz, directs Scraps to live in the Emerald City, and is someone Sir Hokus seeks permission from before his quest. Her palace, with Ozma and its important occupants, is carried away when Ruggedo becomes a giant, creating her disappearance from the Emerald City and terrifying Oz. In Ev, she is pinned beneath a collapsed bed but is freed by the Scarecrow and Scraps, helps tend the injured, marks a warning sign with her name and Oz's Royal seal, and prevents Sir Hokus from killing Ruggedo because his fall could destroy the palace. The Sand Man then puts her into enchanted sleep. Glinda brings her down after the Question Box reveals a rescue plan; Ozma tries Trick Tea and refuses Prince Pompadore's proposal. She nevertheless helps Pompadore's party, uses the Question Box and magic spinning to stop the Runaway Country, intends to banish Ruggedo there, and sends the party to the Winkie Country. Learning Ruggedo's confession, she uses her Magic Belt to transport him. She also takes and keeps Glegg's Question Box and Mixed Magic, uses the Belt to bring Glegg to the Emerald City, and follows the Box's instruction that Glegg drink Triple Trick Tea.

Oz is a huge oblong country and Fairyland ruled by Ozma, where Dorothy lives as a Princess. It is divided by cardinal direction into the purple Gilliken country, blue Munchkin country, red Quadling lands, and yellow Winkie country, and includes many small kingdoms, such as Pumperdink, that Ozma has not explored. Its magical terrain and lack of railway or steamship lines make travel difficult. Oz’s gentle, kindly people usually obey orders, and its law forbids sorcery except when Glinda and the Wizard practice magic for the people’s good. Though generally delightful and happy, Oz is threatened when Ruggedo, secretly planning conquest, uses Mixed Magic: he grows huge, his footsteps shake the country, and Ozma’s castle disappears. Peg Amy and Wag travel west through Oz seeking Ruggedo and the missing castle, while Prince Pompadore hopes to become King by marrying the Proper Princess. The story culminates in a rescue in Oz, with Ozma remaining its little Ruler.

Emerald City is the city at the center of Oz and its capital. It contains the royal palace, later Ozma’s palace, and is where Ozma lives. It is also home to Sir Hokus and the gathering place for Dorothy’s friends. Its green parks, emerald-studded houses, and shining marble streets impress Prince Pompadore when he and Kabumpo arrive at dawn seeking Ozma. Ruggedo is ordered to live above ground there but secretly uses a cave to store objects he steals from inhabitants; he hopes to conquer the city and turn its people into mouldy muffins. Panic follows when the palace vanishes, until Glinda directs the inhabitants to resume their work and play. After Ruggedo returns to his cave, the palace reaches the city and settles on its old foundations, and Ozma plans to return.

records.l: the mysterious scroll, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The mysterious scroll is found in the birthday cake after it explodes and contains seven-day magic. It warns that the Kingdom of Pumperdink will disappear forever unless Prince Pompadore marries the Proper Fairy Princess within the proper time. The warning makes the King wonder where she is and when Pompadore should marry her, alarms others, and remains puzzling because of unexplained initials and links to a gold door knob and gold mirror.

records.l: gold door knob, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: A round, shiny gold door knob marked P. A. comes from the birthday cake, flies through the air to strike King Pompus, and remains mysteriously connected to the scroll. Kabumpo later carries it from Pumperdink, fits it to the gold castle door, and opens the glittering gold court room.

Magic Mirror is a truthful gold mirror found under a window. It displays descriptions of those who look into it, calling Kabumpo an Elegant Elephant, King Pompus a Fat Old King, Queen Pozy a Lovely Queen, and Prince Pompadore a Charming Prince. Later it identifies a woman on a golden bench as Glinda, the Good Sorceress of Oz, helping Prince Pompadore decide whether to ask her to marry. Finally, it reveals Peg Amy as Princess of Sun Top Mountain and the Proper Princess, followed by her transformation from a wooden doll into a living princess.

The Proper Princess is the fairy princess Prince Pompadore must marry within the proper time to prevent Pumperdink and its people from disappearing. King Pompus identifies Princess Faleero because she is the only known fairy princess, while Kabumpo favors Ozma and Wag notes that the magic scroll names no one. Pompadore searches among princesses, increasingly worried his quest will fail after losing most of his hair.

records.l: Pompadore and Faleero's wedding, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: is_scheduled_for tomorrow morning [after Faleero accepts] King Pompus orders Pompadore and Princess Faleero to marry, and Faleero accepts with pleasure. The wedding is set for the following morning, although Pompadore is dismal and Kabumpo strongly opposes it.

records.l: the scroll's appearance in the cake, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Queen Pozy believes the scroll flew out when the birthday cake exploded, but Eejabo reports that the cake had disappeared before the party and later returned. The text does not establish exactly how the scroll entered or emerged from the cake, and it does not identify J.G.

The Curious Cottabus is a large, luxurious, cat-shaped curious beast with bulging eyes and a fan-ended tail, as large as a pony. Living on other people’s affairs, it requires fifty questions daily and questions Pompadore and Kabumpo before helping. It follows them to Rith Metic, offers a cryptic chant, falls from a fence, then corrects “wintersault” to “summersault,” accidentally providing their escape clue.

occupies the West of Oz [yellow country] The Winkie Country contains the Kingdom of Sun Top Mountain. Ozma directs the Runaway Country to carry Pompadore's party across the Deadly Desert and set them down there.

records.l: the Emerald City palace, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The Emerald City palace is a gorgeous, emerald-studded royal palace of Oz, normally located in the Emerald City above a cave. It contains Ozma, most of the Courtiers, Dorothy and her friends, a sitting-room, and the Magic Picture in one of Ozma’s rooms. Its crisis begins when it shivers, its lights fail, furniture falls, and the whole castle seems to rise into the air. It then disappears, leaving a deep palace-shaped hole in the gardens and a giant footprint nearby. The cause is tied to Glegg’s tunnel beneath the palace and the Mixed Magic he buried there: Ruggedo becomes a giant, bursts through the cave ceiling, and the palace is impaled on the spikes of his gray head. Carried across the country to Ev with its occupants, the palace is violently shaken, tilted, and damaged; twenty windows are shaken to bits. High among the clouds, it is mistaken for an air castle by the Sand Man, whose silver sand leaves nearly everyone inside asleep. The occupants are endangered whenever Ruggedo moves, while others seek the giant and the one responsible. The Question Box says the palace will settle firmly on its foundations when Ruggedo returns to the Emerald City. Afterward, Ozma and the others set the topsy-turvy palace right.

records.l: Pompa and Kabumpo’s journey to the Emerald City, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Pompa and Kabumpo travel south from Pumperdink toward the Emerald City, beginning through a dim forest and planning a two-day trip. They encounter the Curious Cottabus and a huge black flag, later cross the Soup Sea by night and a sleeping Gilliken village, reach the city at dawn, seek Princess Ozma, and leave to rescue her in Ev.

records.l: the scroll's seven-day magic, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: A seven-day deadline requires Prince Pompadore to marry Ozma, the Proper Princess, before it takes effect; with two days gone, he must hurry or Pumperdink will disappear.

records.l: wedding (Pompa and the Princess), Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: is_intended_by Pompa [as a means of saving Pumperdink] Marriage to a Proper Princess is presented as the condition for preserving the Kingdom of Pumperdink. Pompadore is supposed to marry such a Princess within the time specified by the scroll, and Kabumpo takes him to the Emerald City to seek Ozma's hand.

records.l: the Figure Heads, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: The Figure Heads are strange, thin inhabitants of Rith Metic with figure-shaped heads who form arithmetic problems in its streets, force travelers to solve them, then flee confused when Pompadore turns somersaults.

Rith Metic is a dry, choky kingdom ruled by the King of the Figure Heads, with arithmetic-book houses, sign-marked streets including Minus Alley, and inhabitants who require travelers to solve problems to pass.

records.l: the King of the Figure Heads, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: An enormous wooden school ruler with arms, legs, and a square head, the King rules Rith Metic from a solid wooden throne and directs travelers to begin simple additions.

records.l: Count It Up, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: Count It Up, a tall thin pencil-like person in Rith Metic, takes charge of Kabumpo and Pompadore, assigning arithmetic from addition to fractions and predicting Pompadore’s journey. When Pompadore somersaults, Count It Up is knocked down and his point breaks.

Scarecrow is a stuffed straw person and clever Straw Man, adviser to Ozma, made of straw yet unbreakable, with excellent mixed brains given by the Wizard of Oz. Though he has never slept and lacks an ordinary brain, he can think. He lives at the Corn-Ear residence and guards Ozma’s palace with Scraps, committed to his post to the end. In the Emerald City, he helps Ozma count royal emeralds, aids companions during the palace’s upheaval, discovers Ruggedo is carrying the palace, helps free Ozma, and paints a warning. Awake through the crisis, he patrols and prepares for attack. After falling from the palace, he helps the group escape the Runaway Country, proposes sending Ruggedo away on it, and returns toward the Emerald City with Ozma and Glinda.

are_used_to make_examples_of_travelers [by the rulers of Rith Metic] Arithmetic problems are used in Rith Metic to trap and test travelers. The Figure Heads form themselves into sums, and Count It Up threatens to place Kabumpo and Pompadore in a problem and make an example of them.

is_a arithmetic problem [formed by Figure Heads] Addition is the first kind of arithmetic problem assigned to Kabumpo and Pompadore. Pompadore calculates the figures while Kabumpo carries the figures physically, but the process is slow and difficult.
Somersaulting becomes the travelers’ unexpected method of escaping arithmetic problems. When Pompadore repeatedly turns somersaults, Count It Up and all the Figure Heads panic and flee.

records.l: the travelers' escape from Rith Metic, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: ends_at the gate [the black iron gate at the other end of the city] The travelers escape from Rith Metic after Pompadore turns repeated somersaults and drives away the Figure Heads. Kabumpo then carries Pompadore through the deserted streets, breaks through the black iron gate, and runs miles away from the city.

records.l: the disappearance of Pompadore, Kabumpo in Oz
records.s: occurs_at the white marble slab [after Pompadore strikes or falls through it] After the escape, Pompadore finds nuts and begins cracking them on a white marble slab. He suddenly falls through it and disappears, leaving Kabumpo to find only the words, “Please Knock Before You Fall In.”

Ruggedo is an old gnome and former Gnome King, once the wicked ruler of the Kingdom of the Gnomes. After banishment, Ozma orders him to live as a common gnome and gives him a cottage in the Emerald City. He pretends to live there but secretly occupies an underground cavern reached through passages beneath his cellar and Ozma’s castle. Although one record calls him formerly wicked and now good, the later account repeatedly presents him as wicked, bad-tempered, thieving, and intent on renewed power. In the cavern, Ruggedo keeps precious stones, an accordion, and stolen goods; steals from the Emerald City and from Wag; mistreats and steals Peg Amy while she is an unalive wooden doll; and carves his History of Ruggedo in Six Rocks. He plans to conquer the Emerald City, regain the Magic Belt, and seek conquest of Oz. His most important discovery is Glegg’s Box of Mixed Magic, found in a concealed opening in the cavern floor. He struggles to open it, then uses it to enlarge Peg Amy and Wag and to bring Peg Amy to life with Re-animating Rays. When Peg Amy and Wag pursue him, Ruggedo tries to escape by pouring Expanding Fluid over himself. He becomes a giant three-quarters of a mile high; his expansion makes a terrific bang, destroys the cave’s top, and leaves Ozma’s palace impaled on his spiked hair and carried on his head. He ends in Ev, on a mountain, frightened of the threat of ten thousand eggs, since eggs cause gnomes to shrivel and disappear.
