records.s: The underground lake catches Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, and Bill after their fall. Its water is initially cool enough for swimming but becomes steaming hot as it carries them toward Fire Island.

records.l: Gorba's medicine, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The wizard’s medicine saves Tatters and Grampa from drowning when each takes a mouthful. It also protects the travelers from burns, scalds, and heat stroke, allowing them to cross Fire Island safely for a time.

records.l: King Fumbo's head, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: King Fumbo’s head remains missing. Prince Forge John the First has not seen it, and finding it is one of the reasons the travelers continue their journey.

records.l: the fortune, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The fortune is still being sought by Tatters, and Bill repeatedly announces that they have reached it when they arrive at the golden-looking Fire Island. Prince Forge John the First offers Tatters a different way to make a fortune through fireworks.
The Princess is named by Bill as one of the people or things the travelers are seeking. This unit provides no further information about her.

records.l: Fire Island voyage to Blazes, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Prince Forge John the First orders an iron boat and has Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, and Bill taken across the waters surrounding Fire Island. Two Fire Islanders row them toward Blazes, while the travelers remain uncertain about what will happen.

records.l: fall into the underground lake, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The group’s fall ends when Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, and Bill plunge into a deep underground lake with a great splash. They survive the fall but are then carried by the water toward the burning Fire Island.

records.l: arrival on Fire Island, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The travelers are washed up on the burning sands of Fire Island after the medicine protects them from the heat. They meet Prince Forge John the First and the flame-like Fire Islanders, who show them the island before sending them onward.

records.l: burning up, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Grampa, Tatters, and the others fear that they will burn up when the wizard’s medicine wears off. Prince Forge John the First warns that the medicine may soon fail, prompting the travelers’ departure toward Blazes.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, and Bill are sent from Fire Island through a dark tower and into a volcano. Blazes erupts them from the volcano, and Gorba's medicine protects them from the boiling lava as it forms a flying island beneath them. They land in the Nonestic Ocean, spend the night on the floating island, and reach a snowy shore marked as the Illustrious Island of Isa Poso. A sign warns them to beware of the dragon.

Grampa and his companions are taken through the dark tower and sent up through a volcano. He survives the eruption because of Gorba's medicine, helps care for Urtha, eats toasted bread and butter, keeps his spirits up, and leads the group ashore on the Illustrious Island of Isa Poso.

Tatters travels with Grampa, Urtha, and Bill through the dark tower and volcano. He survives the eruption, explains the stars to Urtha, helps make her a pillow from the thread bear's skin, and reaches the snowy shore with the others.

Urtha is frightened while entering the dark tower and volcano but survives the eruption without crushing any of her posies. She delights in seeing the stars for the first time, falls asleep while counting them, and reaches the snowy land with Grampa and Tatters.

Bill rides on Grampa's shoulder, survives the volcanic eruption, and keeps watch while the others sleep. At sunrise he crows loudly, announces that land is ahead, and flies after the others to the ice-covered shore.

records.l: Fire Island, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Fire Island is visible from the dark tower, whose moss soaks up its rays. The rowers from Fire Island leave Grampa and his companions at the tower and row back to the island.
The volcano contains a boiling lake of lava and is tended by Blazes. It erupts Grampa and his companions high above the earth and sends them toward the Nonestic Ocean.

records.l: Kingdom of Ev, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: The volcano is located in the Kingdom of Ev, on the other side of the Deadly Desert.

records.l: Nonestic Ocean, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: The eruption throws Grampa and his companions into the Nonestic Ocean, a great body of water far to the Northwest. Their hardened lava island bobs across its waves until it reaches a snowy shore.

records.l: Isa Poso, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: The Illustrious Island of Isa Poso is a cold, ice-bound land with snowy shores and ice-covered trees. A sign identifies it and warns visitors to beware of the dragon.

records.l: flying island, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: A flying island forms when the liquid lava surrounding Grampa and his companions hardens after the eruption. It carries them above the earth and later bobs across the Nonestic Ocean.

The lava in the volcano boils and churns in a lake below Blazes. It catches Grampa and his companions during the eruption, but Gorba's medicine prevents it from injuring them; the surrounding lava then hardens into a flying island.
The eruption is noisy, smothering, and terrifying, hurling Grampa and his companions from the middle of the earth to a point above its surface. It sends them into the Nonestic Ocean.

records.l: Gorba's medicine, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Gorba's medicine keeps Grampa and his companions safe from the boiling lava during the eruption. Without it, they would have been blown clear out of the story.
A sign at the Illustrious Island of Isa Poso warns visitors to beware of the dragon. Urtha does not know what a dragon is when she asks about it.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, and Bill travel across the frozen island of Isa Poso to find and slay the dragon Enorma, hoping to claim half the kingdom and Princess Poso. Grampa defeats Enorma by throwing snuff in her face, causing her to sneeze, lose her teeth, and flee into an icy stream, where she is put out. The travelers find Enorma’s cave, eat her stored meat, and then encounter King Chin Chilly the Third and his snow-men subjects. Grampa claims the reward for Prince Tatters of Ragbad, and Chin Chilly leads them toward the island’s kingdom, while Tatters begins to worry about the princess.

Tatters travels with Grampa, Urtha, and Bill across the frozen land of Isa Poso. He helps pursue Enorma, comforts Urtha after the dragon is put out, and shares the meat from her cave. When Grampa claims the reward for him, Tatters begins to have misgivings about the Princess of Isa Poso.

Grampa decides to slay Enorma so that Tatters can claim half the kingdom and Princess Poso. He defeats the dragon with snuff, helps secure her body as proof of their valor, finds food and shelter in her cave, and then claims the reward before King Chin Chilly the Third.

Urtha travels with the others and warms the frozen land wherever her feet touch it, causing flowers to grow in the snow. Her flowers and footprints anger the islanders, but Grampa defends her when Chin Chilly objects to her presence. She weeps after Enorma is put out and is comforted by Tatters.

Enorma is a fire-breathing dragon who lives on Isa Poso and keeps a large fire and stores of frozen meat in her cave. Grampa throws snuff in her face, causing violent sneezing and revealing that she is toothless. She flees and plunges into an icy stream, where she is put out and floats like a log with only a puff of smoke remaining.

records.l: Chin Chilly the Third, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Chin Chilly the Third is the King of Isa Poso and offers half the kingdom and Princess Poso to whoever slays Enorma. He initially objects to Urtha’s flowers and footprints, but becomes pleased when he learns that Tatters has slain the dragon. He then leads Grampa and the others toward the kingdom.

records.l: Isa Poso, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Isa Poso is a frozen island ruled by Chin Chilly the Third. Its snow-covered land is inhabited by towering snow men, and Enorma’s presence makes the surrounding people melt. The island contains Enorma’s fire-lit cave and a palace or kingdom that Grampa and the others seek.
Ragbad is the kingdom associated with Prince Tatters. Grampa claims the reward in Tatters’s name and hopes that the reward will help them return to Ragbad after finding the King’s head.

records.l: dragon-slaying reward, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The dragon-slaying reward offered by Chin Chilly the Third is half the kingdom and the hand of Princess Poso. Grampa claims it for Prince Tatters after Enorma is put out, and Chin Chilly accepts the claim after seeing the dragon’s body.

records.l: slaying of Enorma, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The slaying of Enorma is accomplished when Grampa uses snuff to make her sneeze and lose her teeth, after which she flees and plunges into an icy stream. Grampa and Tatters moor her body to a tree as proof of their valor before claiming the reward.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Prince Tatters and his companions are stranded on an iceberg after Chin Chilly tricks them with the Princess of Isa Poso and cuts away the connecting land. The wizard's medicine protects Tatters and Grampa from the cold, and Urtha's flowers make the iceberg cheerful as it drifts east toward Oz. Grampa later smokes tobacco from a pouch, causing Bill to vanish and Tatters, Urtha, and Grampa to transform into crows. The adventurers then begin flying east toward Oz, led by the invisible Bill.

Prince Tatters is stranded with Grampa, Urtha, and Bill on an iceberg after Chin Chilly cuts away its connection to Isa Poso. He takes the wizard's medicine, becomes protected from the cold, dances with Urtha, and later transforms into a great black crow. He joins the flight east toward Oz.

Grampa is horrified by the Princess of Isa Poso and angered when Chin Chilly tricks the party. He takes the wizard's medicine, helps keep the others cheerful, and later smokes the tobacco that transforms him into an old crow with a game leg. He flies after Bill toward Oz.

Urtha warns Tatters and Grampa to run from the Princess of Isa Poso and reminds them about the wizard's medicine. Her flowers blossom across the iceberg, and she dances and plays scrum with Tatters. After the tobacco is smoked, she becomes a crow with vari-colored feathers and flies toward Oz.

Bill arrives just after the party is stranded and asks about the golden ship and the diamonds. When Grampa smokes the tobacco, Bill vanishes and remains only as an unseen cock's crow. He leads the others east by crowing and fluttering his invisible iron wings.

records.l: Chin Chilly the Third, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Chin Chilly brings the Princess of Isa Poso to Tatters and insists on keeping his word. He snaps off his daughter's hand, drags her back to Isa Poso, and has the snow men chop away the land connecting the iceberg to the island.

records.l: Princess of Isa Poso, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The Princess of Isa Poso is a maiden of ice who treats Tatters with cold disdain. She seizes his hand, but Chin Chilly snaps off her hand and takes her back to Isa Poso; she immediately grows another hand.

records.l: the adventurers, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The adventurers are stranded on a desolate iceberg after losing the connection to Isa Poso. The wizard's medicine makes them warm and frost proof, and the tobacco transforms them into birds or, in Bill's case, an unseen crowing sound. They then fly east across the Nonestic Ocean toward Oz.

records.l: Isa Poso, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Isa Poso is the island from which Chin Chilly and the Princess are separated from the adventurers. The connecting strip of land is chopped away, leaving the party marooned on the iceberg and moving away from Isa Poso.

records.l: the iceberg, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The iceberg is connected to Isa Poso by a narrow strip of land until Chin Chilly's snow men chop the strip away. After the wizard's medicine is used, it carries the party east through the choppy waters and becomes covered with flowers before the adventurers fly away.

records.l: Nonestic Ocean, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The Nonestic Ocean separates the iceberg from Isa Poso after the connecting land is destroyed. The iceberg travels across its choppy waters, and the transformed adventurers begin flying over it toward Oz.

Ragbad is Tatters' home, which he misses while stranded on the iceberg. He talks to Urtha about its pigeons, the Redsmith, Pudge's tower, the old castle, and Mrs Sew-and-Sew's garden, and hopes to return there with Grampa.

Oz lies east of the adventurers, and Grampa is encouraged that traveling east takes them farther from Isa Poso. Tatters, Grampa, Urtha, and the invisible Bill begin flying toward the Emerald City in Oz.

records.l: the fortune, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The fortune remains undiscovered after the party finds no golden ship or diamonds at Isa Poso. Bill insists that they must continue looking for it, and Grampa agrees that they should not give up because Oz contains fortunes and other Princesses.

records.l: wizard's medicine, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The wizard's medicine is found in the bottle after Urtha reminds the party about it. Grampa gives four drops to Tatters, and the mixture makes them warm and frost proof, allowing them to remain cheerful on the iceberg.

records.l: the Princess's hand, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The Princess's hand is snapped off by Chin Chilly when she seizes Tatters. Tatters throws the hand away, while Chin Chilly claims that possessing it is Tatters' half of the Kingdom.

records.l: the magic tobacco, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The tobacco is in the blue pouch that Grampa took from Vaga and had forgotten inside his game leg. Grampa smokes it without realizing its source, and its magic causes Bill to vanish and the others to transform.

records.l: Grampa's pipe, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Grampa takes up Grampa's pipe during a peaceful moment on the iceberg and fills it with tobacco from the blue pouch. After he smokes it, Bill vanishes and Grampa, Tatters, and Urtha undergo the crow transformation.

records.l: the magical crow transformation, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The crow transformation occurs when Grampa smokes the tobacco. Bill becomes an unseen cock's crow, Tatters becomes a great black crow, Urtha becomes a crow with vari-colored feathers, and Grampa becomes an old crow with a game leg.

records.l: the flight to Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The flight to Oz begins after the crow transformation. Bill leads the way east, while Grampa, Tatters, and Urtha follow through the air over the Nonestic Ocean, with the iceberg shrinking to a tiny speck below.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Dorothy, Percy Vere, and Toto spend the night in the forest and continue toward the Emerald City. They find a woodcutter’s cabin, eat breakfast, and leave a poem and Dorothy’s gold ring as payment. While climbing a mountain, they are attacked by wild wash women and discover that it is Monday Mountain. The Tubbies capture Dorothy and Percy after Percy refuses to marry the Princess of Monday Mountain.

Dorothy travels with Percy Vere and Toto toward the Emerald City. She prepares breakfast in a woodcutter’s cabin, leaves her gold ring as payment, and later helps Percy face the wild wash women. She explains that they are searching for a Princess, but the Tubbies carry her away with Percy.

records.l: Percy Vere, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Percy Vere spends the night in the forest, makes breakfast in a woodcutter’s cabin, and leaves a poem as payment. He climbs the mountain with Dorothy and is struck by a cake of soap before fighting back against the wild wash women. The Princess of Monday Mountain asks to marry him, but he refuses, and the Tubbies seize him.

Toto wakes early because he wants breakfast and travels with Dorothy and Percy Vere. He hides from Percy’s strange poetry and from the approaching wash women, but later growls fiercely at them and unexpectedly tells them to stop shouting. He follows Dorothy and Percy when the Tubbies carry them away.

records.l: Monday Mountain, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Monday Mountain is a steep, blue mountain covered by clouds of vapor. It is inhabited by wild wash women, the Tubbies, and herds of clothes horses. The Tubbies take Dorothy and Percy to its top.

records.l: the Tubbies, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The wild wash women attack Dorothy and Percy Vere with soap, blueing, clothes props, wash boards, tubs, and baskets. They complain about the travelers’ shabby clothes and threaten to wash their faces, wring their necks, and hang them up to dry. They capture Dorothy and Percy and carry them to the top of Monday Mountain.

The Tubbies are the tribe of wild wash women living on Monday Mountain. They become excited when Dorothy says the travelers are searching for a Princess, but turn hostile when Percy refuses to marry their Princess. They carry Dorothy and Percy away to the wash tubs.

records.l: Queen of the Tubbies, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The Queen of the Tubbies leads the wild wash women and angrily orders that Dorothy and Percy be taken to the wash tubs after Percy refuses to marry her daughter. She announces that her daughter is a Princess of the Tubbies.

records.l: Princess of Monday Mountain, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The Princess of Monday Mountain is the Queen’s enormous daughter. She takes an immediate interest in Percy Vere and asks whether she may have him and marry him. Percy refuses, causing the Tubbies to become furious.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Grampa, Urtha, Tatters, and Invisi-Bill cross the Nonestic Ocean, Ev, and the great desert to reach the Winkie country, but their magical crow transformation ends before they reach the Emerald City. A storm carries them and the red umbrella into the sky, where they meet Maribella and find King Fumbo's head among nearly a hundred heads in the clouds. They place King Fumbo's head in Maribella's pink knitting bag and return by traveling down a rainbow with Polychrome. The search for the Princess and the fortune remains unfinished.

Grampa leads the journey across the Nonestic Ocean, Ev, and the great desert toward the Emerald City. He discovers why the company became crows, loses his pipe, helps find King Fumbo's head, and carries on the search for the Princess and the fortune. He travels down the rainbow with the others and decides that he needs an anchor because he is tired of flying and falling.

Urtha flies as a crow with the company and notices the gun sticking through Grampa's feathers before the transformation ends. In the sky, she skips over the clouds, causing flowers to spring up, and meets Maribella. She travels down the rainbow with Polychrome and the others.

Tatters becomes partly human and partly crow before the transformation ends, then eats plums and dried bear steak with Grampa. He meets Maribella, asks about the stars, and recognizes King Fumbo as his father. Tatters begs Fumbo to return and later carries his father's head and the red umbrella down the rainbow.

Invisi-Bill flies with the company across the ocean, Ev, and the desert, calling out directions and warning them when the magical crow transformation is ending. He predicts the storm and suggests that King Fumbo's head might be found in a storm because it was lost in one. He identifies Fumbo's head when the company finds it and travels down the rainbow balanced on Grampa's shoulder.

records.l: King Fumbo, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: King Fumbo's head is found among the heads resting on the pink clouds. He explains that a storm blew off his head while he wore a wing collar, which carried him to the clouds. He agrees to return after Tatters promises to tell him about the company's adventures, although he complains about being carried in a bag and thrown about.

records.l: King Fumbo's head, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: King Fumbo's head is discovered almost first among nearly a hundred heads in the sky, where it is talking with the head of an inventor of market baskets with legs. Grampa puts it into Maribella's pink knitting bag so it can be taken back to its body. During the rainbow journey it is jostled inside the bag and complains that it may be cracked.

Maribella is a sky shepherdess who tends the baby stars and keeps them from falling out of the Milky Way. She tells the company that there are many heads in the clouds and leads them to King Fumbo's head. She lends them her pink knitting bag and shows them the rainbow they can use to descend.

Polychrome, the Rain King's daughter, appears on the rainbow after the storm. She welcomes the travelers, insists on kissing them, and teaches them how to travel down the rainbow. She leaves them to attend her father's birthday party in the sky.

records.l: the three crows and Invisi-Bill, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The three crows and Invisi-Bill fly for an hour over the Nonestic Ocean, cross Ev and the great desert, and reach the Winkie country. The three crows change back into Grampa, Urtha, and Tatters when the magic tobacco's three-hour effect ends, and the company then continues on foot and by the red umbrella.

records.l: Nonestic Ocean, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The Nonestic Ocean is crossed by the three crows and Invisi-Bill during their flight toward Oz. They fly over it for about an hour before reaching the rocky shores of Ev.
Ev is reached after the company crosses the Nonestic Ocean. The travelers fly over the country and continue toward the great desert.

records.l: Deadly Desert, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The great desert surrounds the magic Kingdom of Oz and is described as deadly. Grampa orders the company to fly high above it, and they cross it quickly before reaching the Winkie country.
The magic Kingdom of Oz lies beyond the great desert. The company travels toward it, aiming to reach the Emerald City.

records.l: Emerald City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The Emerald City is the company's intended destination after crossing the Nonestic Ocean, Ev, and the great desert. Grampa expects the company could reach it by noon, but the journey is diverted by the storm and the sky journey.

records.l: the sky, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The sky contains pink cloud meadows, a sky shepherdess named Maribella, many heads, and a rainbow leading downward. The company is carried into the sky by the red umbrella and later descends from it by the rainbow.

records.l: the storm near Chicago, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: A storm is forecast by Invisi-Bill and soon arrives with strong wind, thunder, rain, and scattered camp materials. Its gale lifts the red umbrella and carries Grampa, Urtha, Tatters, and Invisi-Bill above the storm area into the sky. The storm also explains how King Fumbo's head was blown away.

records.l: the rainbow journey, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The rainbow journey begins when Maribella points out a rainbow extending from the cloud's edge. Polychrome teaches Grampa, Urtha, Tatters, and Invisi-Bill to travel down it, but the steepening rainbow makes them slide rapidly until they tumble off in the Winkie country.

records.l: the search for the Princess and the fortune, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The search for the Princess and the fortune leads the company to question Maribella and investigate the heads in the clouds. They find King Fumbo's head, but no Princess or fortune is found in this unit. Grampa refuses to give up and says there is always a fortune at the end of the rainbow.

records.l: the magical crow transformation, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The magical crow transformation changes Grampa, Urtha, and Tatters into crows for three hours. It ends at the minute because Grampa smoked three puffs of the magic tobacco, and the company changes back while descending over the Winkie country.

records.l: the blue tobacco pouch, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The blue tobacco pouch belongs to Vaga, the bandit, and contains instructions explaining how its tobacco turns people into crows. Grampa finds the pouch in his pocket after the transformation and learns that three puffs caused the company's three-hour crow state.

records.l: the magic tobacco, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The magic tobacco turns a company of captives into crows, with each puff lasting for one hour. Grampa accidentally smokes it instead of his own tobacco, using three puffs and causing the company to remain crows for three hours.

records.l: red umbrella, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The red umbrella belongs to Tatters and is carried during the journey. The storm lifts it into the sky with Grampa, Urtha, and Tatters clinging to it, and Tatters later carries it down the rainbow.

records.l: the pink knitting bag, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The pink knitting bag is used by Maribella before she lends it to the company. Grampa places King Fumbo's head inside it for the return journey, and the head complains after the group tumbles off the rainbow.

records.l: the fortune, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The fortune remains undiscovered while the company finds King Fumbo's head instead. Grampa continues to believe that a fortune is waiting at the end of the rainbow, while Tatters says they can be happy without one.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Dorothy, Toto, and Percy Vere are held prisoner on Monday Mountain and forced by the Queen of the Tubbies to work at the wash tubs. Percy Vere discovers the word that stops the running white fence and helps Dorothy and Toto escape through its gate. The Tubbies overturn their wash tubs, sending hot soapy water down the mountain and causing the prisoners to slide to the bottom. After fleeing, they meet Bill, who hears Percy call Dorothy a princess and flies away shouting about the princess.

Dorothy is held prisoner on Monday Mountain and forced to work at the wash tubs with Percy Vere and the wild wash women tribe. She refuses to let Percy marry Pearl Borax and escapes with Percy and Toto through the gate in the running white fence.

Toto is tied to Dorothy's wash tub while they are prisoners and growls at the wash women, whom he loathes. He escapes with Dorothy and Percy, slides down the mountain in the hot soapy water, and later rests beneath a tulip tree trying to catch his breath.

records.l: Percy Vere, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Percy Vere is forced to wash clothes on Monday Mountain and tries to keep Dorothy cheerful with rhymes. He figures out the word that stops the running white fence, opens its gate, and leads Dorothy and Toto to escape.

records.l: Queen of the Tubbies, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The Queen of the Tubbies keeps Dorothy, Toto, and Percy Vere prisoner and sentences Dorothy and Percy to work at the wash tubs. She calls from Monday Mountain that Percy should marry Pearl Borax and is expected to be furious when the prisoners escape.

records.l: the Tubbies, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The Tubbies are a wild wash women tribe whose wash tubs surround the top of Monday Mountain. After Dorothy, Toto, and Percy Vere escape, the Tubbies overturn the tubs and send hot soapy water cascading down the mountain.

records.l: Monday Mountain, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Monday Mountain is where Dorothy, Toto, and Percy Vere are held prisoner, with washing required from morning until night and potatoes and cabbage served for dinner. The three escape by sliding down its side after the Tubbies overturn their wash tubs.

records.l: the running white fence, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The running white fence circles Monday Mountain a few feet below the wash tubs. It is tall, spiked, and too high to jump, but Percy Vere discovers how to command it to stop so that the prisoners can pass through.

records.l: the fence gate, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The fence gate comes opposite Dorothy and Percy Vere only once a day. Percy Vere stops the running white fence when the gate is in front of them, opens it, and pulls Dorothy and Toto through.

records.l: wash tubs, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The wash tubs are arranged in a circle around the top of Monday Mountain, where Dorothy and Percy Vere are forced to wash clothes. The Tubbies overturn them during the escape, releasing a torrent of hot soapy water.

records.l: the escape from Monday Mountain, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The escape from Monday Mountain begins when Percy Vere tells Dorothy how to stop the running white fence and they dash through its gate with Toto. The Tubbies cannot follow immediately because the fence starts spinning again, and the fugitives slide down the mountain before running away.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Dorothy and Percy Vere meet Grampa, Tatters, Urtha, Bill, and the disembodied head of King Fumbo beneath a tulip tree. The travelers recognize Dorothy as a Princess of Oz and learn that Tatters is the Prince of Ragbad, while both groups explain their journeys and their searches for missing princesses. Grampa decides that the combined party should search for the Princess of Perhaps City and the prophet Abrog. They make camp, eat supper, share stories, and spend the evening together before resting.

Dorothy meets Grampa's party and is recognized by King Fumbo as Princess Dorothy of Oz. She explains that she and Percy Vere have had a difficult journey and agrees to help search for the Princess of Perhaps City.

records.l: Percy Vere, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Percy Vere initially mistakes Tatters for a ragged non-Prince and recites a mocking verse about him. He tells the party about Abrog's prophecy, the disappearance of the Princess of Perhaps City and Abrog, and his adventures with Dorothy, then helps Tatters gather wood for camp.

records.l: Prince of Ragbad, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Tatters is identified as the Prince of Ragbad, although his ragged appearance and untidy hair initially cause Percy Vere to doubt his identity. He carries King Fumbo's detached head in a knitting bag and agrees to help Dorothy and Percy Vere rescue the Princess.

Urtha helps settle the disagreement by proposing that the group believe Dorothy is a Princess if Dorothy's companions believe Tatters is a Prince. She happily welcomes the new friends, gathers berries for supper, and joins Dorothy, Tatters, and Percy Vere in a game of scrum.

Grampa initially insists that Dorothy is only a country girl and not a Princess, but he is embarrassed when King Fumbo identifies her. He tells the story of his party's adventures, decides to join the search for the Princess of Perhaps City, and orders the group to make camp for the night.

records.l: King Fumbo, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: King Fumbo appears as a talking head that Tatters carries in a knitting bag because his head blew off from his body. He recognizes Dorothy, confirms Tatters's princely identity, hears both groups' stories, and supports finding the Princess of Perhaps City as a suitable match for his son.

Bill identifies Dorothy as the Princess when Grampa's party arrives, though Grampa initially dismisses his claim. He explains that the group followed directions on a bottle and traveled by falling, swimming, exploding, sailing, and flying, and he continues to insist that they must find the Princess and the fortune.

records.l: Urtha, Princess of Perhaps City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: The Princess of Perhaps City has disappeared along with Abrog, and Percy Vere has been searching for her. Grampa's party decides to join Dorothy and Percy Vere in looking for her.

Oz is the country in which the events occur, including Ragbad, Perhaps City, Maybe Mountain, and the surrounding locations. Dorothy is known as a Princess of Oz, and King Fumbo says that Peer Haps is a monarch in Oz.
Ragbad is the country associated with Tatters and King Fumbo. Grampa's party traveled from Ragbad, and King Fumbo promises that Bill will receive a perch on Ragbad's highest tower.

records.l: Perhaps City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Perhaps City is the place ruled by Peer Haps and is the home of the missing Princess whom Percy Vere seeks. Its Princess disappeared at the same time as Abrog.

records.l: Abrog’s prophecy, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Abrog's prophecy concerned a monster and was connected to the disappearance of the Princess of Perhaps City and Abrog himself. Grampa distrusts the prophet and suspects that Abrog ran away with the Princess.

records.l: the search for the Princess, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: The search concerns both Dorothy's effort to find the missing Princess of Perhaps City and Grampa's party's search for a Princess. The groups combine their efforts, planning to pursue Abrog the following day with weapons and supplies.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Grampa's army continues its march toward the Emerald City but is diverted into the play grounds of the Play Fellows. The Play Fellows forcibly make Grampa, Percy Vere, Dorothy, Tatters, and Urtha participate in exhausting games, while Toto hides and Bill watches helplessly. Urtha escapes through a wicket gate, and Grampa escapes using a croquet mallet after discovering that his game leg has been stolen. Tatters follows Urtha's trail of daisies and forget-me-nots to search for her.

Grampa leads the army toward the Emerald City and tries to control the march while Percy Vere makes jokes and poems. The Play Fellows force him through repeated amusements, and after he falls asleep under a checker bush, they run off with his game leg. He escapes by using a long-handled croquet mallet as a crutch, with Percy Vere and Dorothy helping him.

records.l: Percy Vere, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Percy Vere marches with Grampa's army and entertains himself by making riddles, puns, and poems. The Play Fellows drag him through games, including running him around the mulberry bush, until he escapes and rolls under a tree, exhausted.

Dorothy travels with Grampa's army toward the Emerald City and suggests knocking at the gate of the fenced park. The Play Fellows rush her to the swings and force her to play; she later helps Grampa escape by running beside him and carrying the red umbrella.

records.l: Prince of Ragbad, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The Prince of Ragbad marches with the company while carrying his father's head and the red umbrella. The Play Fellows force him onto the high wooden slide repeatedly, leaving him black and blue; after Urtha disappears, he drops the head and umbrella and sets out to search for her.

records.l: Urtha, Princess of Perhaps City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Urtha dances along during the march and is treated roughly by the Play Fellows, who snatch flowers from her hair and pull her from place to place. She escapes by running through a wicket gate and continues running until she is lost.

Bill jokes about his name while marching and warns the company about trouble ahead. He avoids being captured by the Play Fellows, circles anxiously over the park, helps locate Grampa, and directs the others toward an exit.

records.l: King Capers, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: King Capers is the King of Play, dressed like a court jester and carrying a belled, beribboned scepter. He opens the gates to the play grounds and repeatedly orders the Play Fellows to play, directing them from group to group.

records.l: Play Fellows, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The Play Fellows are a large company of Pierrettes and Pierrots who invite Grampa's army into their park and then carry the travelers away to different amusements. They force the visitors to play noisily and relentlessly, treat Urtha roughly, and steal Grampa's game leg while he sleeps.

records.l: Grampa's little army, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Grampa's army sets out toward the Emerald City to use Ozma's magic picture to find Abrog and the lost Princess of Perhaps City. The army enters the play grounds and is separated and exhausted by forced games before escaping through the exits; afterward, Tatters leaves to search for Urtha.

records.l: play grounds, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The play grounds are a huge fenced-in park entered through a gate marked "Play!" and "No trespassing!" They contain amusements and unusual features such as swings, merry-go-rounds, slides, bubble fountains, balloon vines, top trees, and checker bushes.

records.l: Grampa's game leg, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Grampa's game leg is taken by the Play Fellows while he sleeps under a checker bush. He cannot walk normally after discovering it is missing and escapes by using a croquet mallet as a crutch.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Grampa's army begins another march to the Emerald City so they can learn from Ozma's magic picture where Abrog and the lost Princess of Perhaps City are. The march is interrupted when the company enters the fenced play grounds.

records.l: forced play, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The Play Fellows force Grampa's army to ride merry-go-rounds, use swings and slides, run around the mulberry bush, play tag, and join other amusements. The travelers conclude that playing by choice and being forced to play are entirely different.

records.l: Urtha's escape, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Urtha watches for an opportunity and runs away from the Play Fellows across the gardens. Because she is a fairy, she quickly outdistances them, passes through a wicket gate, and continues running until she becomes lost.

records.l: Tatters's search for Urtha, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: When Tatters learns that Urtha is missing, he drops the King's head and the red umbrella and rushes after her. He follows a trail marked by daisies and forget-me-nots, ignoring rocks, sticks, brambles, and thorns in his determination to find and comfort her.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Peer Haps finds his missing daughter, the Princess of Perhaps City, climbing Maybe Mountain, but she is cloaked and apparently bewitched. He hastily arranges for the arriving Prince of Ragbad to marry her, believing the marriage will protect her from the prophesied monster. Tatters is confused and distressed, while the Forgetful Poet, Percy Vere, Dorothy, and Grampa arrive and expose the mix-up. Abrog then declares that Tatters has married a two-headed monster, but Tatters seizes Abrog and removes the cloak, revealing the frightened Princess herself.

records.l: Peer Haps, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Peer Haps anxiously watches Maybe Mountain while waiting for news of the Forgetful Poet and fearing the monster. When he recognizes his lost daughter, he carries her to the palace and tries to arrange her immediate marriage to protect her. He mistakenly marries her, while cloaked and apparently bewitched, to the arriving Prince of Ragbad.

records.l: Lord High Humpus, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The Lord High Humpus, who is also Chief Justice and handles state weddings, helps Peer Haps seek a groom for the Princess. He notices Tatters at the city gates, helps bring him into the palace, and mistakenly congratulates him on his marriage. He flees when Fumbo's disembodied voice frightens him.

records.l: Forgetful Poet, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The Forgetful Poet follows the flower trail and Tatters's footprints to Maybe Mountain with Percy Vere, Dorothy, and Grampa. He is delighted to reach familiar ground and warmly greets Peer Haps, but his excitement causes him to drop Fumbo's head.

records.l: Percy Vere, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Percy Vere arrives at Peer Haps's palace with the Forgetful Poet, Dorothy, and Grampa after following the trails. He tells Tatters that marrying the Princess fulfills the purpose for which Tatters had been searching for a princess and fortune, and he tries to reassure him.

Dorothy arrives with the Forgetful Poet, Percy Vere, and Grampa after following the trails to Maybe Mountain. She runs to Tatters when she sees him distressed and urges that he be allowed to explain what happened.

Grampa reaches the throne room with the others and angrily questions Tatters about marrying a Princess he has never seen. He insists on seeing the Princess, tries to defend Tatters when Abrog calls him a monster, and seizes Abrog by the beard.

Abrog enters the throne room and calls Peer Haps an idiot for marrying his daughter to a monster. He places Fumbo's head on Tatters's shoulders to make Tatters appear to have two heads, then tries to reach the Princess and snatches away her cloak. Tatters catches him after he reveals the Princess.

records.l: Maybe Mountain, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Maybe Mountain is the route by which the Princess returns to Peer Haps's castle and the place where the Prince of Ragbad follows the flower trail. Its summit is covered with wild flowers, making it impossible for Tatters to trace the fairy's footsteps farther.

records.l: Perhaps City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Perhaps City is where Peer Haps's palace stands and where the young and single noblemen hide after hearing that the Princess has mysteriously changed. The Prince of Ragbad reaches its gates while searching for the fairy.

records.l: the monster, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The monster is the feared creature from Abrog's prophecy, expected to carry off the Princess on the fourth day. It does not appear in this unit, although Peer Haps believes the hasty marriage will prevent it from taking her.

records.l: the Princess's enchantment, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The Princess appears changed and is described by Peer Haps as bewitched, so he keeps her covered and says she cannot yet be seen. The text does not explain the enchantment, but removing the cloak reveals her as the Princess herself.

records.l: the Princess's marriage to Tatters, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Peer Haps and the Lord High Humpus hastily arrange the Princess's marriage to Tatters after Tatters arrives at the city gates. Tatters is tricked into the marriage without seeing her, and the marriage is later shown to involve the cloaked Princess rather than the monster Abrog claims.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Dorothy discovers that the flower maiden is Urtha, the lost Princess of Perhaps City, and that Abrog is responsible for bewitching her. Abrog confesses that he intended to turn Urtha into mud so the monster would not marry her, but his magic transformed her into a flower fairy instead. Dorothy interprets the prophecy as describing Tatters rather than a monster. Grampa uses the wizard's medicine to punish Abrog, transforming him into a mouse, but the group then realizes that no one knows how to restore Urtha.

Grampa learns that the flower maiden is Urtha, the lost Princess, and helps expose Abrog's deception. He uses the wizard's medicine to determine Abrog's punishment and breaks a saucer of the mixture over Abrog's head.

Urtha insists that her name is Urtha and is revealed to be the lost Princess of Perhaps City. Abrog's spell changed her into a flower fairy instead of turning her into mud, and the company realizes afterward that she still needs to be unbewitched.

Dorothy organizes the questioning of Abrog and identifies him as being at the bottom of the affair. She recognizes that “Gorba” is “Abrog” spelled backwards, interprets the prophecy, and realizes that Tatters is the youth it describes.

records.l: Peer Haps, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Peer Haps is astonished to learn that the flower maiden is Urtha, although he initially insists that his daughter's name is Pretty Good. He warns Abrog that Dorothy can have him punished and later points angrily at Abrog when the supposed monster is shown not to exist.

Abrog confesses that he bewitched Urtha because he wanted to save Pretty Good from the monster and marry her himself. He intended to change Urtha into mud, but the spell made her a flower fairy; he is later punished and transformed into a mouse.
Gorba is revealed to be Abrog's name spelled backwards. The label on the wizard's medicine bears the name “Gorba,” helping Dorothy identify Abrog as the wizard.

Tatters confirms Urtha's identity as Urtha, and Dorothy identifies him as the youth described in the prophecy. The prophecy therefore indicates that Tatters, rather than a monster, will marry the Princess of Perhaps City.

records.l: Perhaps City, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Perhaps City is identified as the home of Urtha, its Princess. The prophecy concerns the marriage of its Princess.
The supposed monster is revealed not to exist. Abrog had used the threat of the monster as part of his plan to prevent Pretty Good from marrying Urtha.

records.l: Abrog’s prophecy, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The prophecy says that a youth wrapped in the skin of an old bear, with two heads upon his shoulders and carrying a red umbrella, will marry the Princess of Perhaps City. Dorothy and the others determine that it describes Tatters, not a monster.

records.l: wizard's medicine, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The wizard's medicine is kept in a bottle labeled “Gorba” and causes Abrog to become frightened and desperate when he sees it. Its instructions prescribe breaking a saucer of the mixture over a sorcerer's head.

records.l: the Princess's enchantment, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Abrog carried Urtha to the hidden garden to bewitch her and change her into mud. Because Urtha was sweet, lovely, and good, the spell instead transformed her into a bewitching little flower fairy.

records.l: the disappearance from the throne room, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Abrog is punished after he confesses his scheme and is identified as the wizard. Grampa follows the medicine's instructions by breaking a saucer of the mixture over Abrog's head.

records.l: Abrog's transformation into a mouse, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: When the saucer breaks over Abrog's head, he disappears and a little brown mouse scurries across the room. Grampa concludes that Abrog will not do much harm in that shape.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Urtha is cured of her enchantment and transformed from a little flower fairy back into a lovely Princess. Peer Haps learns the adventurers' full story and welcomes Fumbo as the King of Ragbad, while Grampa recovers his lost leg with Bill's help. Peer Haps gives Tatters the yellow hen so he can receive a fortune of a thousand gold bricks. Just as everyone celebrates, a blinding flash makes everyone in the throne room disappear.

Urtha has forgotten her former existence as the Princess of Perhaps City because of the Prophet's spell. After Grampa applies the cure for enchantment, she becomes a Princess again, and Peer Haps joyfully embraces her.
Tatters whispers cozily with Urtha about Ragbad and other important matters. He receives the yellow hen so that he can obtain its fortune.
Grampa uses the wizard's bottle to cure Urtha's enchantment, then listens as the adventurers' story is retold. When Bill returns his lost leg, Grampa joyfully buckles it on and dances a jig.
Dorothy discovers the cure for enchantment on the wizard's bottle. She watches with Grampa, Percy Vere, and Peer Haps as the cure is applied to Urtha.

records.l: Peer Haps, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peer Haps is relieved and happy when Urtha is restored, and he listens to the full account of the adventurers' experiences. He welcomes Fumbo as the King of Ragbad and gives Tatters the yellow hen to provide a fortune.

Bill returns from the playground carrying Grampa's lost leg, which he rescued from King Capers and two Pierrettes. He is celebrated by everyone and is present when the yellow hen produces a gold brick and when the throne room disappears in a flash.

records.l: yellow hen, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peer Haps gives the yellow hen to Tatters as the source of a fortune. When Bill calls it only a bunch of feathers, the yellow hen flies up and lays a gold brick on the table.
Ragbad is mentioned while Tatters and Urtha whisper about important matters. Peer Haps welcomes Fumbo as the King of Ragbad.

records.l: the Princess's enchantment, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Urtha's enchantment has caused her to lose all memory of her former existence as Princess of Perhaps City. It is removed when three drops of the cure are placed on her head.

records.l: wizard's medicine, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: The wizard's bottle contains a cure for enchantment, though Grampa has poured nearly all of it over Abrog. He shakes out three remaining drops onto Urtha's head.

records.l: cure for enchantment, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: The cure for enchantment requires three drops on the head. When the three drops fall onto Urtha, she melts into a rainbow mist and emerges as a Princess.

records.l: Grampa's game leg, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Grampa's lost leg is taken from the playground by Bill, who snatches it away from King Capers and two Pierrettes. Grampa joyfully buckles it on when Bill returns it.

records.l: the fortune, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peer Haps intends Tatters to receive a fortune as a reward, consisting of a thousand gold bricks. The yellow hen begins providing the fortune by laying one gold brick.

records.l: gold brick, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: The yellow hen lays a gold brick upon the table after Bill questions whether it can provide a fortune. The brick astonishes Bill and delights the others.

records.l: Urtha's transformation, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Urtha's transformation begins when the cure makes the little flower fairy melt into a rainbow mist. She emerges as a Princess whose eyes, cheeks, skin, colors, and fragrance retain the beauty of flowers.

records.l: the blinding flash, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: A blinding flash occurs while everyone is laughing over the yellow hen's gold brick. It causes every person and creature in the throne room to disappear.

records.l: the disappearance from the throne room, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: The yellow hen, Bill, Toto, Peer Haps, and every other person in the throne room disappear after the blinding flash. The text says they are gone completely.

records.l: Grampa in Oz, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Ozma uses her magic belt to transport Dorothy, Peer Haps, the Forgetful Poet, and their companions to Ragbad, where they reunite with Mrs Sew-and-Sew, Tatters, Urtha, Fumbo, Pudge, and Grampa. Fumbo’s head is permanently restored, and everyone celebrates with a feast and the Ragbad Quadrille. Dorothy, Toto, Peer Haps, and the Forgetful Poet later return home, while Ragbad becomes prosperous through the gold bricks produced by the yellow hen. Mrs Sew-and-Sew becomes Queen of Ragbad again, and Tatters and Urtha remain happy.

Ragbad receives Dorothy and her companions after Ozma transports them there. The kingdom becomes prosperous when the twenty-four rustic laborers sell the gold bricks produced by the yellow hen, and Mrs Sew-and-Sew becomes Queen of Ragbad again.

records.l: old red castle, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The old red castle is where the reunited group gathers in its shabby ballroom. Mrs Sew-and-Sew holds a great feast there, followed by dancing that lasts into the night.

Ozma follows Dorothy’s adventures through a magic picture and hears the story with the Wizard of Oz’s radio. Using her magic belt and the wizard’s magic, she transports the group safely to Ragbad, restores Fumbo’s head permanently, and later sends Dorothy, Toto, Peer Haps, and the Forgetful Poet home.
Dorothy arrives in Ragbad with her companions and joins the celebrations there. She dances the Ragbad Quadrille, then returns home with Toto after promising to visit Ozma in the Emerald City.

records.l: Peer Haps, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Peer Haps is transported to Ragbad with Dorothy and the Forgetful Poet so he can meet Mrs Sew-and-Sew and Tatters’s other friends. He attends the feast and dance before being transported home with Dorothy and the Forgetful Poet.

records.l: Forgetful Poet, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The Forgetful Poet is taken to Ragbad with Dorothy and Peer Haps to meet Mrs Sew-and-Sew and the others. He joins the feast and Ragbad Quadrille, then returns home with Dorothy and Peer Haps.

records.l: Mrs Sew-and-Sew, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Mrs Sew-and-Sew is overjoyed to find Tatters and Urtha reunited with her and repeatedly kisses them to make sure they are real. She prepares a lavish feast, later removes her thimble and becomes Queen of Ragbad again.
Tatters is reunited with Mrs Sew-and-Sew in Ragbad and dances with Urtha during the celebrations. He and Grampa later have record crops, and he remains happy with Urtha.
Urtha is reunited with Mrs Sew-and-Sew and joins the festivities in Ragbad. She leads off the Ragbad Quadrille with the Prince and is later described as happy with Tatters.

records.l: King Fumbo, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Fumbo welcomes Dorothy, Peer Haps, and the Forgetful Poet to Ragbad after Ozma restores his head. He joins the feast and dance with Pudge and the others.
Grampa plays the spirited music for the Ragbad Quadrille. He and Tatters achieve record crops after Ragbad gains the means to obtain supplies.

records.l: yellow hen, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The yellow hen lays gold bricks, which the twenty-four rustic laborers sell. Its production helps provide Ragbad with money for supplies and care of the linens and lawns.

records.l: the twenty-four rustic laborers, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The twenty-four rustic laborers are summoned by Pudge to join the gathering and fill in the lines for the Ragbad Quadrille. Afterward, they sell the gold bricks laid by the yellow hen as fast as they are produced.

records.l: Prince of Ragbad, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The Prince of Ragbad is celebrated with the Princess during the party, which ends with a hundred cheers for them. The text identifies Tatters as happy with Urtha but does not explicitly name him as the Prince.

records.l: Fumbo's head, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Ozma, aided by the wizard’s magic, wishes Fumbo’s head firmly and permanently back upon his body. Fumbo then possesses and welcomes others with his restored head.

records.l: gold brick, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The gold bricks are laid by the yellow hen and sold by the twenty-four rustic laborers. Their sale supplies Ragbad with enough money to buy supplies and care for the linens and lawns.

records.l: the Ragbad quadrille, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: The Ragbad Quadrille is danced in the old red castle’s ballroom after the feast. Grampa plays the music, and the group dances until the crows of Bill announce sunrise.
Ozma follows Dorothy and her companions’ adventures through a magic picture and decides that they have had enough adventures. She therefore sends them safely home after bringing them to Ragbad.

records.l: prosperity of Ragbad, Grampa in Oz, CHAPTER 22
records.s: Ragbad’s prosperity follows the sale of the gold bricks laid by the yellow hen. The kingdom gains money for supplies and maintenance, while Grampa and Tatters produce record crops.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Kinda Jolly and Rosa Merry rule the cheerful kingdom of Kimbaloo from a cozy button-covered castle in the Gilliken country of Oz. The Kimbles earn their living by selling bouquets and buttons gathered from the bouquet bush and button wood. Mombi, an old Gilliken witch who lost her magic powers, serves as the castle cook while secretly attempting to recover her magic. After Mombi tries to transform Kinda Jolly into a collar button, a talking goose accuses her of having done something to the King.

records.l: Kinda Jolly, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Kinda Jolly is the kind and jolly King of Kimbaloo, where he made a fortune in buttons. He lives in the button-covered castle with Rosa Merry, oversees the button boys, and is seen calmly walking under the button trees after Mombi attempts a transformation.

records.l: Rosa Merry, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Rosa Merry is the quaint, merry Queen of Kimbaloo and keeps the castle spick and spandy with flowers. She manages the bouquet bush and gives bouquets to the flower girls to sell.

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Mombi is an ugly, ill-tempered old Gilliken witch who lost her magic powers through her wicked transformations. She works as Kinda Jolly's cook, secretly tries to recover her magic, and reacts angrily when her formulas fail.

records.l: goose (Kinda Jolly's dinner goose), The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The goose bought by Kinda Jolly for dinner is a talking white bird brought to the castle in a wooden crate. It recognizes Mombi and demands to know what she has done with the King.

records.l: Kimbaloo, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Kimbaloo is a cheerful kingdom in the Gilliken country with about five hundred inhabitants. Its people live comfortably through the sale of buttons and bouquets, and everyone is happy except Mombi.

records.l: Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Oz contains Kimbaloo and is described as having no stores, allowing the button boys and flower girls to sell their wares directly to residents.

records.l: castle (Kinda Jolly and Rosa Merry's castle), The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The castle stands in the center of a thick button wood and has many chimneys and windows. It is built of dark purple button wood, covered with bright buttons, and kept cozy and flower-filled by Rosa Merry.

records.l: button wood, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The button wood surrounds Kinda Jolly and Rosa Merry's castle and produces the buttons sold by the button boys. Kinda Jolly and the boys gather a crop of buttons there each morning.

records.l: Kimbles, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The Kimbles are the two hundred and fifty girls and boys who live in tiny cottages beneath the trees of Kimbaloo. The girls work for Rosa Merry and the boys work for Kinda Jolly.

records.l: button boys, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The button boys gather buttons in the button wood with Kinda Jolly, fill their button boxes, and sell the buttons along the King's Highway. They return by noon with coins and spend the rest of the day playing.

records.l: bouquet bush, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The bouquet bush grows in the castle garden and produces an enormous, continually renewing supply of many kinds of bouquets. Rosa Merry uses it to fill the flower girls' arms each morning.

records.l: buttons, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Buttons are the source of Kinda Jolly's fortune and are harvested from the button wood. They decorate the castle and the clothing and crowns of Kinda Jolly and Rosa Merry, while collar buttons are especially easy for the button boys to sell.

records.l: bouquets, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Bouquets of many kinds grow on the bouquet bush, including violets, roses, daisies, daffodils, pinks, and larkspur. The flower girls sell them along the Queen's Highway and return with heavy pockets.

records.l: Mombi's search for a cook's position, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: After losing her magic powers, Mombi closed her hut near the Gilliken mountains and traveled with her crooked stick to find work as a castle cook. Most castles rejected her, but Kinda Jolly allowed her to remain in Kimbaloo.

records.l: Mombi's attempted transformation of the King, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Mombi secretly mutters formulas and mixes ingredients in an effort to restore her magic. She chants that the King shall become a collar button, but the magic fails, and Kinda Jolly remains unchanged.

records.l: the goose's accusation of Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: After Mombi opens its crate and grabs it by the feathers, the goose recognizes her and cries out, asking what she has done with the King. Its accusation frightens Snip because it suggests that Mombi may have harmed or transformed Kinda Jolly.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Snip overhears Mombi and Pajuka reveal that Pajuka is a transformed goose and that Mombi has forgotten what she did with King Kinda Jolly. Mombi tries to silence Snip, but Pajuka protects him and persuades Mombi to search for the missing King. After learning that Mombi is the witch who transformed Ozma and Pajuka, Snip is forced to accompany them into the forest. Mombi makes Snip carry their supplies as they leave Kimbaloo.

records.l: Snip, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Snip hides on a narrow window sill and overhears Mombi and Pajuka discussing the King. After falling into Mombi's arms, he is threatened with being put into the soup kettle, but Pajuka protects him. Mombi then forces Snip to carry a basket and drags him into the forest.

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Mombi is revealed as a witch who transformed Pajuka into a goose and Ozma into a boy named Tip. She has forgotten her witchcraft and does not remember what she did with King Kinda Jolly. She agrees to search for the King and leaves Kimbaloo with Pajuka and Snip.

records.l: Pajuka, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Pajuka is a Prime Minister who has been transformed into a great white goose by Mombi. He resists being cooked, protects Snip from Mombi, and persuades her to help find King Kinda Jolly. He claims that he could recognize the King in any shape.

records.l: Kinda Jolly, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: King Kinda Jolly is identified as Ozma's father and the rightful ruler of Oz. Mombi says she has forgotten what she did with him, while Pajuka insists that he is still alive in some transformed shape and has been searching for him.

records.l: Ozma, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Ozma is the little girl ruler of Oz and the daughter of King Kinda Jolly. Mombi had transformed her into a boy named Tip, but Glinda forced Mombi to disenchant her, after which Ozma was proclaimed Queen of Oz.

records.l: Kimbaloo, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Kimbaloo is a kingdom in the Gilliken country of northern Oz. Mombi enjoys special privileges there as a cook, but she fears being exposed as a witch and expelled. Snip leaves Kimbaloo sadly with Mombi and Pajuka.

records.l: Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Oz is described as an oblong kingdom divided into the Gilliken, Winkie, Quadling, and Munchkin countries, with the Emerald City at its center. Ozma rules it as Queen, while King Kinda Jolly is described as its rightful ruler. Its history includes rule by the Wizard, the Scarecrow, and briefly Jinjur.

records.l: Mombi's magic powers, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Mombi has lost or forgotten her witchcraft and says that she would not still be a cook if she retained her magic powers. Her loss of magic prevents her from restoring Pajuka to his proper form and leaves her unable to remember the King's transformation.

records.l: Mombi's transformations, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Mombi transformed Pajuka from an elegant man into a goose and transformed Ozma into the boy Tip. She also transformed King Kinda Jolly, although neither she nor Pajuka knows what form he now has.

records.l: King Kinda Jolly's disappearance, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Mombi admits that she does not remember what she did with King Kinda Jolly. Pajuka has spent years searching for him and believes that he remains alive in some form, so Mombi and Pajuka begin a search to locate him.

records.l: Snip's journey, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Snip is taken against his will from Kimbaloo by Mombi and Pajuka. Mombi leads them through the kitchen garden into a gloomy forest, while Snip carries a basket of food, spices, and other supplies and mourns leaving his friends and the castle.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Kinda Jolly and Rosa Merry learn that Mombi, the goose intended for dinner, and Snip have disappeared from Kimbaloo. General Whiffenpuff leaves to search for them, while the palace mourns and then settles down to a picnic supper. The King decides to send for an invisible cook, and Rosa offers to cook in the meantime. Hah Hoh comforts Kinda Jolly by revealing his "funny bone."

records.l: Kinda Jolly, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Kinda Jolly happily discusses dinner with Rosa Merry, expecting to eat a large roast goose that cost a thousand gold buttons. He becomes distressed when Mombi, the goose, and Snip are found to be gone, but agrees to send for an invisible cook and later laughs with Hah Hoh.

records.l: Rosa Merry, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Rosa Merry sews a button onto Kinda Jolly's suspenders and guesses at the riddle about dinner. After Mombi and the dinner disappear, she comforts Kinda, sends for the Town Crier, and offers to cook while they seek an invisible cook.

records.l: General Whiffenpuff, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: General Whiffenpuff checks the pantry and reports that the dinner, goose, and Mombi are gone. He is upset by Snip's disappearance, then takes his gun and boldly leaves to search for Mombi, the goose, Snip, and an invisible cook.

records.l: Hah Hoh, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Hah Hoh jokes about the dinner guesses and tries to make Kinda Jolly laugh after the losses. He reassures Kinda that he has something up his sleeve, then reveals his left elbow as his "funny bone."

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Mombi disappears along with the dinner and the goose. Hah Hoh describes her as an evil-appearing old woman, and General Whiffenpuff goes to search for her.

records.l: Snip, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Snip disappears from the palace. Kinda Jolly calls him the brightest boy in Kimbaloo and his best button picker, and the palace is deeply upset by his loss.

records.l: Town Crier, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: The Town Crier is summoned after the dinner, goose, and cook disappear and cries for seven minutes for the goose and three minutes for Mombi. He later guesses that the replacement dinner will be an omelet and helps maintain the Kingdom's customary mourning through tears.

records.l: the Invisible Cook, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: An invisible cook who reportedly lives near a sixteenth cousin of Hah Hoh's is proposed as a replacement for Mombi. Kinda Jolly decides to send for her, while Rosa Merry offers to cook in the meantime.

records.l: Kimbaloo, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Kimbaloo is a merry Kingdom with both a Town Crier and a Town Laugher, because its people do not ordinarily shed tears. It has two hundred and forty-nine little button boys and two hundred and fifty little flower girls serving around the palace.

records.l: goose (Kinda Jolly's dinner goose), The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Kinda Jolly's dinner goose is described as the finest and fattest goose he has ever seen and as having cost a thousand gold buttons. It disappears before it can be served, and General Whiffenpuff searches for it.

records.l: dinner (Kinda Jolly's dinner), The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Kinda Jolly's planned dinner is roast goose and apple sauce. It disappears along with the goose and Mombi, leaving the King disappointed and causing the palace to arrange a picnic supper from the ice box.

records.l: loss of the dinner, goose, and cook, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: The dinner, the goose, and the cook Mombi are discovered to be gone at the same time. Their disappearance shocks Kinda Jolly, prompts the Town Crier's official crying, and leads to a search and a plan to obtain an invisible cook.

records.l: Whiffenpuff's search, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: General Whiffenpuff's search begins when he takes his gun and plunges into the night to find Mombi, the goose, Snip, and an invisible cook. The search gives Kinda Jolly confidence that the missing people and things may be recovered.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi drags Snip through the Purple Forest while Pajuka helps watch him, and Snip decides to stay with them rather than face the forest alone. Pajuka explains that Mombi changed him into a goose and that they are searching for the King, whom Mombi cannot remember where she hid. Mombi concludes that green magic transformed the King and plans to go to the Emerald City, steal Ozma's magic belt, restore the King, and take revenge. After supper, Snip and Pajuka fall asleep while Mombi unsuccessfully experiments with her black frying pan.

records.l: Snip, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Snip is dragged through the Purple Forest by Mombi and helps gather wood for a fire. He becomes friendly with Pajuka, learns about the search for the King, and sleeps beside the fire after watching Mombi's failed magical experiments.

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi takes Snip and Pajuka into the Purple Forest while searching for the King. She remembers that green magic may have been used to transform the King and decides to go to the Emerald City, where she plans to steal Ozma's magic and take revenge.

records.l: Pajuka, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Pajuka helps Mombi keep watch over Snip and tells him that he has searched all over Oz for Mombi and the King. He explains that Mombi changed him into a goose and says that, despite some advantages of being a goose, he most misses having pockets and being himself.

records.l: Humpy, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: The King was transformed by Mombi and hidden somewhere, but Mombi cannot remember where she put him. Mombi believes green magic can restore him and plans to find him near the Emerald City.

records.l: Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Pajuka says he has searched everywhere in Oz for Mombi and the King. Mombi and Pajuka were once in a small greenwood near where the Emerald City now stands.

records.l: Purple Forest, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: The Purple Forest is where Mombi, Pajuka, and Snip stop for the night. It has purple pines, lengthening shadows, and a grim, forbidding appearance in the twilight.

records.l: Emerald City, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi decides to travel to the Emerald City because she believes green magic works only in and around it. She expects to remember more about the King's transformation once she arrives there.

records.l: the map of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi carries a small purple scroll containing a map of Oz. She studies it in the failing light while trying to remember where she hid the King.

records.l: green magic, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi concludes that she used green magic when she transformed the King. She believes green magic can take effect only in and around the Emerald City and can therefore restore him.

records.l: Mombi's magic powers, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi's magic powers are gone, so Pajuka says she cannot turn Snip into a muffin and eat him. Mombi nevertheless plans to steal Ozma's magic belt and use its magic to restore the King and transform others.

records.l: the transformation of Pajuka into a goose, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi changed Pajuka into a goose in a small greenwood near where the Emerald City now stands. Pajuka was driven away immediately afterward and spent years searching for Mombi and the King.

records.l: the King's transformation, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi cannot remember what kind of magic she used or where she hid the King after transforming him. Pajuka's recollection that the transformation occurred near the Emerald City leads Mombi to identify green magic as the likely cause.

records.l: the black frying pan, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Mombi uses the old black frying pan for endless magical experiments after supper. Her incantations produce only dense smoke, and nothing emerges from the pan.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi travel southwest through the Gilliken country toward the Emerald City. They survive an attack by a weenix using Mombi's purple pepper, then meet the Hoopers, who roll over them in their park. Snip defeats several Hoopers with Mombi's crooked stick, angering their king, Rollo the Royal. When Mombi is identified as a witch, Rollo and the Hoopers flee, and the travelers continue toward the Corners.

records.l: Snip, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snip travels with Pajuka and Mombi toward the Emerald City, planning to escape from Mombi there and tell Ozma the whole story. He helps drive off the Hoopers by striking them with Mombi's crooked stick and then continues along the path.

records.l: Pajuka, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Pajuka brings Snip grapes and a sugar bun for breakfast and travels with him and Mombi toward the Emerald City. He explains that the King of Oz was kind, gentle, tall, and absent-minded, and that he misses him greatly.

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Mombi plans to disguise herself as a market woman in the Emerald City and have Pajuka steal some of Ozma's magic. She protects the travelers from a weenix with purple pepper, but later hides in a bonnet bush while Snip fights the Hoopers.

records.l: Humpy, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Pajuka says that the King of Oz was a kind and gentle ruler who never punished anyone and would believe evil of no one. Mombi transformed him in a little wood, and Pajuka hopes to find him and restore him.

records.l: Ozma, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snip intends to tell Ozma the entire story so that she can use her magic to help Pajuka find the King. Pajuka calls Ozma a pretender, while Snip notes that she does not know her father is alive.

records.l: Rollo the Royal, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Rollo the Royal is the king of the Hoopers. He demands that Snip and the others bow to him and orders them to leave the park, but flees with his subjects after learning that Mombi is a witch.

records.l: the Hoopers, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Hoopers are tall, thin, flat people who can bend over, seize their toes, and roll like hoops. They attack Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi, but Snip knocks several of them away with Mombi's crooked stick before they flee with Rollo the Royal.

records.l: Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Oz is described as having once been ruled by the King of Oz, before Ozma became queen. Its northern Gilliken country is purple, and it contains unusual plants, creatures, and peoples such as the Hoopers.

records.l: Emerald City, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Emerald City is the destination toward which Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi travel. Mombi plans to disguise herself there, while Snip plans to reach Ozma and ask for help.

records.l: the Hoopers' park, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Hoopers' park is a large pleasant park with dazzling white paths and a surrounding fence. Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi are attacked there, and they leave it through a small gate after Rollo and the Hoopers flee.

records.l: Mombi's magic powers, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Mombi says that she has forgotten her magic and wants to steal some of Ozma's magic so that she can remember it. She still knows practical tricks, including using purple pepper to repel a weenix.

records.l: Mombi's crooked stick, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snip takes Mombi's crooked stick when the Hoopers attack. He uses it to knock several Hoopers away and rolls two of them like hoops.

records.l: the Hoopers' attack, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Hoopers' attack begins when six of them roll at Snip and Mombi at full speed, knocking them onto their backs. Snip fights back with Mombi's crooked stick, and the attack ends when the Hoopers retreat after Mombi is called a witch.

records.l: the King's transformation, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Pajuka says that Mombi transformed the King of Oz in a little wood. The travelers hope to find the King and undo or remedy the transformation, but the King has not yet been found.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The journey to the Emerald City takes Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi through the Gilliken forest and countryside. They face a dangerous weenix and the Hoopers, then continue along a zig-zag path toward the Corners.

records.l: The Lost King of Oz, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Snip, Pajuka, and Mombi reach an inland sea, which Mombi jellies with a purple can of gelatin so they can cross it. They then enter Catty Corners, a city inhabited by cats, where the cats welcome Mombi but capture Snip and Pajuka. The Maltese cat queen, called the Imperial and Puissant Pussy, declares that Mombi may stay, Snip will be chased and scratched, and Pajuka will be eaten. Snip tries to protect Pajuka, but cat guards take them away as a threatened dinner and prisoner.

records.l: Snip, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Snip travels with Pajuka and Mombi, encounters laughing willows, and reaches an inland sea. He crosses the jellied sea, enters Catty Corners, and is seized by cat guards. The cat queen orders that he be publicly chased and scratched, but Snip tries to stop the cats from eating Pajuka.

records.l: Pajuka, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Pajuka travels with Snip and Mombi while searching for the King, and he says he is homesick for his slippers, castle, and pipe. He crosses the jellied sea, is captured by cat guards in Catty Corners, and is selected as the cat queen's dinner. He warns that he is bad for cats and will give them fits if they eat him.

records.l: Mombi, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Mombi uses a small purple can of powerful gelatin to turn the inland sea solid enough to cross. She is welcomed by the cats of Catty Corners because she is a witch and happily sits under a catsup tree with kittens. When the queen condemns Snip and Pajuka, Mombi ignores Pajuka's plea and says that he deserves it.

records.l: inland sea, The Lost King of Oz, CHAPTER 6
