records.l: Rash army, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The Rash army advances in response to Irashi's whistle. Reddy's giant appearance, together with the attacks of his companions, terrifies the soldiers into fleeing, and they surrender their swords as they escape.

records.l: Rash rubies, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The Rash rubies protect Reddy when Irashi's scimiter strikes him and when Ippty's coffee pot is thrown at his head. Reddy displays the three rubies to Fizzenpop, who recognizes their importance with great delight and astonishment.

records.l: Princess Elma's big wig, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Reddy puts on the giant's wig when the Rash army rushes at him, causing him to shoot skyward and terrifying the soldiers. He later puts it on again to ensure that Irashi and Ippty cannot escape while they are being bound.

records.l: crown of Rash, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Reddy snatches the crown of Rash from Irashi and tosses it to Betsy Bobbin for safekeeping. After the victory, Reddy wears the crown while presiding over the feast as the restored ruler.

records.l: proclamation of Evered's restoration, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Fizzenpop reads a proclamation from the pink balcony announcing that Evered, the Scarlet Prince, has returned. It states that the rule of Irashi the Rough is over forever.

records.l: Reddy's conquest of Rash, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Reddy's conquest of Rash is carried out with help from Carter Green, Atmos, Betsy Bobbin, Ozma, the Hungry Tiger, the Rash rubies, and the giant's wig. He captures Irashi and Ippty, routs the Rash army, and is restored as the rightful ruler without any broken bones being reported.

records.l: The Hungry Tiger of Oz, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Atmos Fere takes Ippty and Irashi into the sky to use them as proof that people live at the bottom of the air, intending to abandon them on a lonely island after his lecture. Ozma and her companions must find another way across the Deadly Desert, and Fizzenpop provides Rash hurry-canes that carry them safely back to the Emerald City. Reddy joins the travellers, keeping the Rash rubies while giving the giant wig to Fizzenpop. The travellers receive a joyful welcome in the Emerald City, while the Hungry Tiger learns that heart-ache is worse than a stomach-ache and loses his desire to eat a live man.

records.l: Ozma, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Ozma tries to stop Atmos Fere from leaving because he had promised to carry her and the others across the desert and back to Oz. After he departs with Ippty and Irashi, she worries about crossing the Deadly Desert, but she returns safely to the Emerald City on a Rash hurry-cane.

records.l: Atmos, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Atmos Fere takes Ippty and Irashi into the sky, planning to use them as proof that people live at the bottom of the air. He says he will drop them on a lonely island after his lecture and then disappears above the clouds in his iron boots.

records.l: Ippty, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Ippty is carried into the sky by Atmos Fere as a specimen to support his claim about people living at the bottom of the air. Atmos Fere plans to abandon Ippty on a lonely island after his lecture.

records.l: Irashi, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Irashi is carried into the sky by Atmos Fere as a specimen to support his claim about people living at the bottom of the air. Atmos Fere plans to abandon Irashi on a lonely island after his lecture.

records.l: Carter Green, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Carter Green suggests that a Rash ruby might protect the travellers from the burning sands, recalling that he had possessed it when they first crossed the desert. In the Emerald City, he is so frequently invited and sought after that he could not have taken root even if he had wanted to.

records.l: Hungry Tiger, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Hungry Tiger celebrates that Atmos Fere will keep his secret by taking Ippty and Irashi away. He is relieved not to be a kitten, and his heart-ache from missing his friends in Rash cures him of wanting to eat a live man.

records.l: Reddy, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Reddy repeatedly urges Ozma and the others to stay in Rash, but eventually joins them on their journey to the Emerald City. He keeps the Rash rubies, gives the giant wig to Fizzenpop, and promises to return to Rash in a month.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Betsy Bobbin suggests that Dorothy or the Wizard might see the travellers in the Magic Picture. She returns with the others to the Emerald City, where her adventures are celebrated in feasts, processions, story tellings, and parties.

records.l: Fizzenpop, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Fizzenpop proposes using the marvelous Rash hurry-canes to cross the Deadly Desert safely. He brings five hurry-canes from the umbrella stand, and in Rash he later uses a telescope to look for Ippty and Irashi on clear nights.

records.l: Rash, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Rash is left peaceful under Reddy's rule after Ippty and Irashi are removed. Its pink palace displays Atmos Fere's iron boots, and its people have the Rash hurry-canes and rubies as notable magical possessions.

records.l: Emerald City, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Emerald City receives the travellers with feasts, processions, story tellings, and parties. The adventures of Betsy Bobbin and Ozma are widely discussed there, and Evered later visits the castle with his big wig to entertain the Scarecrow.

records.l: Deadly Desert, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Deadly Desert initially seems impossible for Ozma and the others to cross after Atmos Fere leaves. Fizzenpop's Rash hurry-canes carry the travellers safely across it and back to Oz.

records.l: iron boots (Atmos Fere's boots), The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Atmos Fere removes his iron boots before soaring into the air, dropping one boot with a crash as he departs. The boots remain on display in the pink palace of Rash as proof that an airman visited the country.

records.l: Rash rubies, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Rash rubies are discussed as possible protection from the burning sands, though it is uncertain whether they would work on the desert. Reddy keeps the rubies when he travels to the Emerald City, while the giant wig is given to Fizzenpop.

records.l: hurry-cane, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Rash hurry-canes are described as having a patent action that is triply guaranteed to protect travellers while crossing the Deadly Desert. Five of them carry Ozma, Reddy, and the others from Rash to the Emerald City in five furious flashes.

records.l: the travellers' return to Oz, The Hungry Tiger of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The travellers return to Oz on five Rash hurry-canes, arriving in the Emerald City five minutes after setting out. They are shocked and breathless at first, then receive a joyful welcome filled with feasts, processions, story tellings, and parties.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: Queen Cross Patch, the Sixth, goes to pieces while ruling the patch-work Kingdom of Patch in Oz. Prime Piecer and Chief Scrapper put her scraps away and begin the required search for a new ruler, using the Royal Spool of Succession. The spool leads them out of Patch, through the Winkie Country, and eventually to the Emerald City. A magical foot-path carries the two Quilties rapidly to the city gates, where they continue following the spool.

records.l: Queen Cross Patch, the Sixth, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: Queen Cross Patch, the Sixth, rules Patch and watches her subjects work from her castle window. She is extremely cross and patchy, has a patch over one eye from fine sewing, and goes to pieces while sorting patches at her sewing table.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: Patch is a busy but unpleasant little Kingdom in the Winkie Country of Oz. Its people grow and work different-colored cotton patches, make and repair quilts, and live among cross roads and patched, shabby houses; it will go to pieces if no new ruler is found within four days.

records.l: Quilties, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Quilties are the magically constructed people of Patch, who gather cotton patches, make quilts, and do mending and darning. They cannot die, but when they wear out they go to pieces, after which their scraps are stored in a scrap-bag for about ten years before they return.

records.l: Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: Oz contains the Kingdoms that use and appreciate patch-work quilts, and Patch lies in its Winkie Country. The Emerald City is identified as the capital of Oz.

records.l: Piecer, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Prime Piecer rushes to the Queen after hearing that she has gone to pieces, then helps prepare for the search for a new ruler. He carries the Royal dust-pan and a large rag-bag, follows the Royal Spool of Succession with Chief Scrapper, and repeatedly urges that they return when the journey becomes difficult.

records.l: Scrapper, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Chief Scrapper reacts crossly to the Queen's going to pieces and says that finding a new ruler will interrupt the busiest season. He helps sweep up and store the Queen, carries the gold shears, cuts the golden spool from its tree, recites the succession command, and follows the spool toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Scissor Bird, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Scissor Bird sleeps on a perch in the Queen's chamber until the Queen goes to pieces. It cries out for help and then flies out of the window to announce the news to the patchworking population.

records.l: the royal Spool of Succession, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Royal Spool of Succession grows as one golden spool on the central tree in Patch and is meant to lead to the next ruler. After Chief Scrapper cuts it free and commands it to unwind, it rolls far beyond Patch, leads the ministers through difficult terrain, enters the Emerald City, and continues ahead of them.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz. A sign in the forest identifies it as thirty-five miles away, and the Royal Spool of Succession leads Prime Piecer and Chief Scrapper to its gates.

records.l: foot-path to the Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The foot-path to the Emerald City has a hundred broad feet and suddenly rises and rushes through the forest. A notice says that it runs straight to the Emerald City, belongs to the Wizard of Oz, and forbids stamping or kicking; it carries the two ministers to the city gates in less than a minute before coiling up beneath a lime drop tree.

records.l: Queen Cross Patch's going to pieces, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: Queen Cross Patch's going to pieces begins with a shrill scream as she flings patches into the air, topples from her three-legged throne, and breaks into extremely small pieces. Prime Piecer and Chief Scrapper sweep up the scraps and hang them in a closet, treating the event as a normal consequence of a Quilty wearing out.

records.l: selection of a new ruler of Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: The selection of a new ruler of Patch is required whenever a ruler goes to pieces and must follow the method in the Imperial Scrap Book. Prime Piecer and Chief Scrapper cut the golden spool from the royal spool-cotton tree and follow it because Patch will go to pieces if no ruler is found within four days.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 1 Queen Cross Patch Flits
records.s: During the Emerald City foot-path journey, Prime Piecer and Chief Scrapper cling to the railing and to each other as the path carries them rapidly through the gloomy forest. After reading that the path runs straight to the Emerald City, they learn that they are not going to pieces and arrive at the city's gates in less than a minute.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Scrapper and Piecer follow the Spool of Succession into the Emerald City and find the Patchwork Girl, Scraps, whom they mistake as the future ruler of Patch. They kidnap Scraps in a rag bag and use the foot-path to carry her back to the Quilty Kingdom. The Quilties enthusiastically accept Scraps as their queen, and she is crowned Queen of Patch with a sewing basket as her coronet and old spools as her crown jewels.

records.l: Scrapper, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Scrapper follows the Spool of Succession with Piecer into the Emerald City and recognizes the Patchwork Girl as a possible queen. He helps seize Scraps, carry her in the rag bag, direct the foot-path to Patch, and present her to the Quilties.

records.l: Piecer, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Piecer follows Scrapper into the Emerald City and is delighted by the Patchwork Girl. He helps kidnap Scraps, carries the rag bag, and announces her as Queen Scraps of Patch before handing her into the royal rolling chair.

records.l: Quilties, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The Quilties await the return of Scrapper and Piecer and demand to see their ruler. They enthusiastically accept Scraps after seeing her anger, cheer for her, crown her Queen of Patch, and lead her into the palace.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Patch is the seven hundred and fifth smaller country among the countries of Oz. It is the Quilty Kingdom to which Scrapper and Piecer return with Scraps, who is crowned its queen.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Scraps is the Patchwork Girl, made from an old crazy quilt and stuffed with cotton, with silver suspender-button eyes, a red-velvet tongue, and unruly yarn hair. Scrapper and Piecer mistake her for their future sovereign, kidnap her in a rag bag, and bring her to Patch, where she accepts the attention and is crowned Queen.

records.l: Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Oz is a magical, oblong fairyland divided into four large countries and many smaller countries, including Patch. It is ruled by Queen Ozma, and its capital is the Emerald City.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz and lies at the center of the kingdom. Scrapper and Piecer enter it while following the Spool of Succession, find Scraps in the palace garden, and escape with her using the foot-path.

records.l: Ozma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Ozma is the little girl fairy who rules Oz and is described as its wisest and gentlest sovereign. She is in the palace with Dorothy discussing curtains when Scraps's scream is heard, but she does not see the kidnapping.

records.l: the royal Spool of Succession, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The Spool of Succession leads Scrapper and Piecer through the Emerald City to the palace garden, where it stops at Scraps's feet. It helps them locate the Patchwork Girl they believe should rule Patch.

records.l: foot-path to the Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The foot-path is a mischievous piece of property that has been left untied and is running wild. It carries Scrapper and Piecer out of the Emerald City with Scraps in the rag bag, follows Scrapper's written direction to Patch, then kicks Piecer and departs.

records.l: rag bag, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The rag bag is placed over Scraps's head and used to carry her away from the Emerald City. Scraps struggles and screams inside it until Scrapper opens it in Patch.

records.l: Queen of the Quilties, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The title is given to Scraps when Scrapper and Piecer identify her as the ruler they have found. The Quilties cheer for her and treat her as their queen after she emerges from the rag bag.

records.l: kidnapping of Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: The kidnapping of Scraps occurs when Scrapper and Piecer seize her in the palace garden, cover her with the rag bag, and carry her toward the gates. The foot-path enables them to escape the Emerald City and transport her to Patch.

records.l: Scraps's coronation, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 2 The New Queen Of the Quilties
records.s: Scraps's coronation takes place at the patched palace after the Quilties welcome her as their ruler. She receives a coronet made from a round sewing basket and crown jewels made from a string of old spools, then enters the castle amid cheers.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Scraps, newly made Queen of Patch, refuses to perform the extensive household and administrative duties assigned to her. Piecer and Scrapper use the Scissor Bird to threaten her, forcing her to work all day while the bird pursues her. That night, Scraps discovers Grumpy, a small brown bear who had been the late Queen Cross Patch’s pet, and tells him she intends to escape and return to the Emerald City. A violent disturbance at the palace door ends the chapter as Grumpy hides in a chest.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Scraps is made Queen of Patch against her will and refuses to perform the duties assigned to her. The Scissor Bird forces her to sweep, wash, scrub, and complete other tasks by threatening to cut off her head. She later meets Grumpy, tells him she plans to return to the Emerald City, and hopes Ozma will find her through the Magic Picture.

records.l: Scrapper, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Scrapper tells Scraps that the Queen must do all the work in the palace and explains that the royal Spool of Succession chose her. He encourages her anger, saying that Patch’s queens must be good scolders, and helps Piecer force her to work.

records.l: Piecer, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Piecer reads Scraps the long list of the Queen’s duties, including preparing breakfast, cleaning, sorting patches, feeding the Scissor Bird, and scolding the Patch-workers. He brings in the Scissor Bird and suggests that it cut off Scraps’s head if she refuses to clean the castle.

records.l: Scissor Bird, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The Scissor Bird threatens Scraps by swooping at her and snipping off an inch of her yarn hair. It relentlessly pursues her from one task to another throughout the day and ignores her complaints.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Grumpy is a small brown bear who had been the late Queen Cross Patch’s pet and helped her with grumbling and growling. He warns Scraps that the Scissor Bird would cut off her head if she tried to escape, and he hides in a chest when someone violently approaches the palace door.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Patch is the country ruled by the Queen of Patch. Its queens are expected to be cross, scold the Patch-workers, and perform all the work in the palace.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The Emerald City is where Scraps says she belongs and where she wants to return. She tells Grumpy that she is a free subject of Ozma of Oz and expects that Ozma might send for her.

records.l: Ozma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Ozma of Oz is Scraps’s ruler, and Scraps identifies herself as one of Ozma’s free subjects. Scraps believes Ozma may locate her by looking in the Magic Picture.

records.l: Emerald Palace, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The palace is the residence where Scraps is crowned and required to perform the Queen’s duties. Its sitting-room has barred windows, locked doors, needle-books, pin-cushions, cross-stitched mottoes, and a chest containing Grumpy.

records.l: the Magic Picture, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The Magic Picture hangs in Ozma’s palace and can show where any of Ozma’s subjects are and what they are doing when Ozma commands it. Scraps expects Ozma to use it to locate her in Patch.

records.l: the royal Spool of Succession, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The royal Spool of Succession chose Scraps to rule Patch. Scrapper says that the golden spool led him and Piecer to the Emerald City in search of a new queen after the former queen went to pieces.

records.l: the Queen of Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The Queen of Patch is expected to prepare food, clean the palace, manage sewing-related supplies, feed the Scissor Bird, help with pin-cushions, and scold the Patch-workers. Scraps becomes Queen of Patch but rejects the role and its duties.

records.l: the Queen's duties, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: The Queen’s duties include preparing breakfast, making beds, sweeping floors, dusting furniture, scrubbing steps, washing windows, sorting patches, counting cotton spools, preparing old clothes for mending, feeding the Scissor Bird, helping pick tomato pin-cushions, and scolding the Patch-workers.

records.l: escape from Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Scraps declares that she intends to escape from Patch and return to the Emerald City, whether or not Ozma finds her first. She remains locked inside the palace sitting-room, and Grumpy warns that the Scissor Bird would cut off her head if she tried to get away.

records.l: the Scissor Bird's threat to cut off Scraps's head, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 3 Duties Of the Quilty Queen
records.s: Piecer tells Scraps that the Scissor Bird will cut off her head if she refuses to clean the castle. The threat frightens Scraps into taking the broom and completing her work, and Grumpy later says the bird would make the same threat if she tried to escape.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Peter leaves his Philadelphia home to buy a balloon and is carried into the sky by a green balloon that transforms into a talking balloon bird. The bird tells Peter that he is being taken to Balloon Island as a present for Queen Luna from Sandaroo, but Peter lets go and falls into the Nonestic Ocean. He swims to a small island, where he meets Ruggedo, the exiled Gnome King, who claims to rule five hundred thousand gnomes. As Peter and Ruggedo discuss escaping the island, the Nonestic Ocean suddenly boils and rises into a terrifying wave.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Peter buys a green balloon in Philadelphia and is carried high into the sky when it transforms into a balloon bird. He learns that he is supposedly being taken to Balloon Island as an airrend boy for Queen Luna, but he lets go of the bird, falls into the ocean, swims to a small island, and meets Ruggedo. Peter decides to try to catch fish and later discusses building a boat or raft to escape.

records.l: Lord High Bouncer of Balloona, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: The balloon merchant is revealed to be Lord High Bouncer of Balloona. He gives Peter the green balloon that carries him toward Balloon Island.

records.l: the balloon bird, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: The green balloon changes into a plump, talking balloon bird with a stiff leg that carries Peter through the sky. It says Peter is being taken to Balloon Island and warns that Queen Luna plans to cut a hole in his back and blow him up so he can float. Peter lets go of its leg while it is passing through a black cloud.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Ruggedo, the Gnome King, lives alone in a cave on a small island and angrily objects when Peter sits on his chimney. He says he is the Metal Monarch, ruler of five hundred thousand gnomes, and that he has been banished from his kingdom for trying to recover his magic belt from Ozma of Oz. Although he initially threatens and insults Peter, he eventually agrees to consider helping him escape and offers to make him the richest boy in the world.

records.l: Gnomes, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: The gnomes are described as underground elves who mine precious stones. Ruggedo claims to rule five hundred thousand gnomes, but says he has been separated from them while imprisoned on the island.

records.l: Balloona, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Balloona is associated with the balloon merchant, who is identified as its Lord High Bouncer. The unit provides no further description of Balloona.

records.l: Balloon Island, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Balloon Island is the destination to which the balloon bird says it is taking Peter. The bird says Peter is being sent there as a present to Queen Luna from Sandaroo.

records.l: Nonestic Ocean, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: The Nonestic Ocean surrounds the island where Peter lands and is described by Ruggedo as lying between Peter and Oz. Its waters suddenly boil and churn, rising into a huge green wall that crashes down with a deafening roar.

records.l: Peter's balloon, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Peter's bright green balloon is sold to him by the mysterious balloon merchant for twenty-five cents. It expands into a plump green balloon bird, allowing Peter to rise over Philadelphia and travel through the clouds.

records.l: Ruggedo’s island, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: The island is small, straggly, rocky, and only slightly larger than the public square near Peter's home. It has about a dozen trees, no visible houses or people, and contains Ruggedo's cave. Peter reaches it after falling into the ocean and begins searching for food and a way to leave.

records.l: Peter's flight to Balloon Island, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Peter's flight begins when his green balloon carries him over Philadelphia and upward through the clouds. The balloon bird says the flight is taking him to Balloon Island, but Peter abandons it before they arrive.

records.l: Peter's fall into the ocean, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 4 Peter Flies With An Odd Bird
records.s: Peter releases the balloon bird's leg after his arms ache and he becomes frightened by the plan to cut and inflate him. He falls several miles through clouds and air, strikes the ocean with great force, hits a clam shell at the bottom, and then swims to a nearby island.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Peter and Ruggedo flee Ruggedo’s island when a sea quake turns the sea upside down and exposes the sea bottom. They cross the strange exposed seabed, find the wrecked pirate ship Blunderoo, and climb aboard just before another quake sends the seabed back underwater and throws the ship into the air. The ship survives but has no rudder, usable masts, or sails, so they drift on the Nonestic Ocean while Ruggedo plans to regain his kingdom and Peter hopes to return to Philadelphia. Peter feeds himself with small fish, and Ruggedo tells him about his magic belt, Ozma, and his past banishment.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Peter sees the sea bottom exposed when the sea turns upside down and follows Ruggedo across it. He helps discover and board the pirate ship Blunderoo, cooks three small fish for dinner, and later falls asleep while drifting with Ruggedo.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Ruggedo urges Peter to cross the exposed seabed, hoping it may lead to Ev. After boarding Blunderoo, he plans to regain his kingdom, recover his magic belt, take revenge on Ozma and Dorothy, and destroy the Emerald City of Oz; he also promises to make Peter a general.

records.l: Ruggedo’s island, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Ruggedo’s island is almost touched by the exposed stretch of sea bottom. Peter and Ruggedo leave it by jumping across a small stretch of water.

records.l: the sea bottom, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The sea bottom rises and lies on top of the waves near Ruggedo’s island, displaying crystal caverns, coral walls, castles, and sea creatures. It later quivers and crashes back into the depths.

records.l: Nonestic Ocean, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The Nonestic Ocean covers the place where the sea bottom had appeared after it sinks again. Its strong tides carry Peter, Ruggedo, and the damaged ship toward the shores of Ev.

records.l: Ev, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Ev lies beyond the Nonestic Ocean and is the location of Ruggedo’s vast dominions beneath its surface. Ruggedo hopes the ship will reach its shores so he can return to his kingdom.

records.l: Blunderoo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: Blunderoo is identified by Peter as the name of the battered old ship resting beside a green sea cavern. Peter and Ruggedo board it after seeing its pirate markings and hoping to find useful things and treasure.

records.l: the pirate ship Blunderoo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The pirate ship Blunderoo has water-soaked, rotten planks and is covered with rust, decay, sea moss, and barnacles. After the sea quake throws it into the air, it strikes the water, rocks violently, and rights itself, but its rudder, masts, and sails are gone.

records.l: the upside-down sea, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The upside-down sea leaves a long stretch of gleaming sea bottom lying on top of the waves and nearly touching Ruggedo’s island. Sea creatures rush toward the edges, while fish, a mermaid, and other creatures struggle to return to the water.

records.l: the sea quake, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The sea quake first exposes the sea bottom and later sends it crashing back underwater. The second shock also dislodges the pirate wreck, hurls it high into the air, and nearly sends Peter and Ruggedo to the bottom of the sea.

records.l: the ship’s wrecking and resurfacing, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 5 Sea Tips Upside Down In Quake
records.s: The old wreck is dislodged from the sea bottom by the second sea quake, hurled into the air, and slammed back onto the churning water. It rocks backward and forward before righting itself, allowing Peter and Ruggedo to survive and drift onward.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Peter awakens aboard the Blunderoo and discovers a pirate treasure hold containing gold, silver, jewels, and a diary. The diary leads him to the magic casket of Soob, which contains the Flying Cloak of Invisibility, an emerald, and two mysterious onions. Ruggedo tries to use the cloak to reach the Emerald City, but it fails because it is torn, so he plans to have it mended and steal back his magic belt from Ozma. The Blunderoo reaches the shores of Ev, which Ruggedo identifies as his country, while Peter continues hoping to return to Philadelphia.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Peter discovers the pirate treasure aboard the Blunderoo and imagines using the gold to build a clubhouse, buy vehicles and animals, and help his grandfather. He finds the pirate chief's diary and the magic casket of Soob, but Ruggedo takes the Flying Cloak of Invisibility from him. Peter realizes that the cloak is torn and plans to use it to warn Ozma if he reaches Ev and the cloak is repaired.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Ruggedo discovers the pirate jewels and greedily claims them, while allowing Peter to have the gold pieces. He tries to use the Flying Cloak of Invisibility to reach the Emerald City, but it does not work because it is torn. Ruggedo plans to have his gnomes mend it, steal back his magic belt, and imprison Ozma and others in cages.

records.l: Blunderoo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The Blunderoo carries Peter and Ruggedo with the current while they explore its wrecked interior and find the pirate treasure. It eventually drifts toward a shallow beach on the coast of Ev and is likely to go aground.

records.l: treasure, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The pirate treasure fills the Blunderoo's hold with old sea chests, boxes, and rotting sacks containing gold and silver coins and jewels. Peter finds the treasure and the diary of Polacky, the Plunderer, while Ruggedo focuses on the jewels.

records.l: magic casket of Soob, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The magic casket of Soob was taken by Polacky, the Plunderer, from the Island of Ashangabad and hidden beneath a raised plank in the treasure room. It contains the Flying Cloak of Invisibility, a small uncut emerald, and an ivory box containing two onion-like objects with instructions to plant them in extreme danger.

records.l: Flying Cloak of Invisibility, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The Flying Cloak of Invisibility is described as making its wearer invisible and taking the wearer wherever desired. Ruggedo seizes it from Peter and attempts to travel to the Emerald City, but it does nothing because a large hole and a long tear run through it.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The Emerald City is Ruggedo's intended destination because he wants to enter Ozma's palace undetected and recover his magic belt. Peter also hopes to reach it so that Ozma can send him back to Philadelphia.

records.l: Ozma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Ozma is in the Emerald City and possesses or has custody of Ruggedo's magic belt. Ruggedo threatens to steal the belt, turn Ozma into a canary, and imprison her in a gold cage.

records.l: magic belt, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The magic belt is the object Ruggedo intends to recover from the Emerald City. Peter hopes that once he reaches Ozma, she will use the magic belt to send him back to Philadelphia.

records.l: Ev, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Ev is the country whose shore the Blunderoo approaches at the end of the unit. Ruggedo identifies it as his country and describes it as containing underground caverns, caves, and labyrinths.

records.l: Philadelphia, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: Philadelphia is Peter's home, and he repeatedly thinks about returning there and about his grandfather's worry over his absence. Peter imagines the excitement that his return and his adventures will cause in Philadelphia.

records.l: invisibility and magical transport, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 6 Ruggedo Discovers Pirate’s Treasure
records.s: The Flying Cloak of Invisibility is said to provide both invisibility and magical transport to any desired location. Its powers cannot be tested successfully because the cloak is torn, and Peter and Ruggedo conclude that it must be mended first.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Peter and Ruggedo reach the shores of Ev aboard the battered Blunderoo and return to the underground Kingdom of Gnomes. Ruggedo reclaims his crown from Kaliko, resumes rule, and orders the treasure unloaded, but learns that gnome magic cannot repair the magic cloak. They discover that the cloak must be mended in the Kingdom of Patch, then use the magic bulbs to cross the Deadly Desert and arrive in a peach orchard in Oz. Ruggedo and Peter head toward a yellow cottage to ask the way to Patch while planning to reach the Emerald City.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Peter helps Ruggedo swim from the Blunderoo to the shores of Ev and follows him into the Kingdom of Gnomes. He plans to take the repaired magic cloak and fly to the Emerald City, but instead uses the magic bulbs with Ruggedo to cross the Deadly Desert. He arrives in Oz, enjoys the peach orchard, and decides to tell the Wizard of Oz about the elevator plants.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Ruggedo returns to the Kingdom of Gnomes, takes back his crown from Kaliko, and resumes his position as Gnome King. He orders lunch, new suits, the unloading of the treasure, and the repair of the magic cloak, but admits that he lacks enough magic to cross the desert. He urges Peter to plant the magic bulbs, crosses the Deadly Desert with him, and heads toward a cottage in Oz.

records.l: Kaliko, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Kaliko has been ruling as King of the Gnomes in Ruggedo’s absence. When Ruggedo returns, Kaliko gives him the crown and becomes Royal Chamberlain again. He obeys Ruggedo’s orders, including unloading the treasure, preparing food, and bringing a new suit.

records.l: Blunderoo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The battered old Blunderoo reaches the shore of Ev, grounds its nose in the sand, and comes to a creaky stop. Its treasure is later unloaded by the gnomes.

records.l: Ev, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Ev is described as a barren land of sand and cactus with hills near Ruggedo’s caverns. Peter and Ruggedo land on its shores before traveling to the edge of the Deadly Desert.

records.l: the Kingdom of Gnomes, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The Kingdom of Gnomes lies underground beneath Ev and contains passageways, jewel-filled caverns, mines, and Ruggedo’s throne room. Ruggedo returns there and reclaims his rule from Kaliko. Its gnomes mine gems and unload the treasure from the Blunderoo.

records.l: Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Oz is surrounded by the Deadly Desert, which is intended to keep people out. Peter and Ruggedo cross the desert and arrive in a sunny peach orchard in Oz.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Peter intends to fly to the Emerald City with the magic cloak and hopes Ozma can transport the treasure there with him. After the cloak cannot be repaired in the Kingdom of Gnomes, Peter and Ruggedo continue toward the Emerald City by way of the Kingdom of Patch.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The Kingdom of Patch is in the Winkie Country of Oz, just below the Kingdom of Ann of Oogaboo. Potaroo says the magic cloak cannot be properly repaired anywhere else, so Ruggedo and Peter travel toward it.

records.l: the Deadly Desert, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The Deadly Desert surrounds the whole country of Oz and is dangerous enough that a person can go up like a puff of smoke upon stepping onto its sand. Peter and Ruggedo cross it using the magic bulbs, which grow into elevator plants that carry them over the desert.

records.l: Gnomes, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Thousands of gnomes work in the underground caverns, using pick axes to dig out jewels. They accept Ruggedo’s return without described resistance, unload the treasure from the Blunderoo, and serve Ruggedo and Peter food.

records.l: Flying Cloak of Invisibility, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The magic cloak is carried by Ruggedo after he returns to the Kingdom of Gnomes. Potaroo determines that gnome magic cannot mend it and says it must be repaired in the Kingdom of Patch.

records.l: Silence Stone, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The sorcerer’s stone is a strangely marked emerald found in the casket. Peter commands it to carry him and Ruggedo across the desert, but nothing happens.

records.l: magic onions, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The magic bulbs are accompanied by instructions to plant them in case of extreme danger. When Peter plants them, they produce enormous green plants with plush seats that carry Peter and Ruggedo across the Deadly Desert.

records.l: elevator plants, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The elevator plants grow rapidly from the planted magic bulbs, rise high into the air, arch over the desert, and deposit Peter and Ruggedo in a peach orchard. Peter thinks the Wizard of Oz would be interested in them.

records.l: treasure, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: The treasure is aboard the Blunderoo when it reaches Ev. Ruggedo orders Kaliko to have the treasure unloaded and stored in the silver grotto.

records.l: crown, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Ruggedo demands the crown from Kaliko and takes it back, placing it jauntily on the back of his head. Its return marks Ruggedo’s resumption of rule as King of the Gnomes.

records.l: magic, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Ruggedo boasts that he has magic stronger than Ozma’s and claims it enabled him to leave the island, but he later admits he does not know how to cross the desert. Potaroo says gnome magic cannot repair the magic cloak.

records.l: crossing the Deadly Desert, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 7 Kaliko Falls As King of Gnomes
records.s: Peter and Ruggedo initially do not know how to cross the Deadly Desert. They accomplish the crossing by planting the magic bulbs, riding the resulting elevator plants high into the air, and landing in a peach orchard in Oz.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Peter and Ruggedo visit Kuma Party, a Winkie whose hands, feet, head, and arms can separate from his body. Kuma explains his come-apartishness and offers them shelter, but Ruggedo insists they continue toward Patch. Kuma lends them an umbrella, lantern, and guiding hand, which leads them through rain, woods, and a cotton field to Patch’s castle. At the castle, Kuma’s hand leaves Peter a note and escapes, while Ruggedo claims that his cloak needs mending so they can enter.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Peter meets Kuma Party and is astonished and frightened by his separate-moving body parts. He wants to stay and ask Kuma more questions, but follows Ruggedo toward Patch; along the way he objects when Ruggedo suggests stealing Kuma’s hand and is excited by the hand’s assistance.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Ruggedo is kicked into a gooseberry bush by Kuma Party’s foot and is frightened by Kuma’s detached parts. He refuses Kuma’s hospitality, leads Peter onward, and plans to seize Kuma’s guiding hand so that the magic belt can make it work for him. At Patch’s castle, he claims that his cloak needs mending in order to gain entry.

records.l: Kuma Party, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Kuma Party is a pleasant old Winkie who can separate and control his hands, feet, head, arms, and other body parts. He says that his father was a wizard in the Zamagoochie Country and that he has possessed this gift since childhood. He warns Peter about traveling with a gnome and helps Peter and Ruggedo reach Patch.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Patch is the place Peter asks how to reach, and Kuma says it is near his cottage, just below the Kingdom of Queen Ann of Oogaboo. Peter and Ruggedo eventually reach a castle there after crossing a wood and a broad cotton field.

records.l: Kuma Party's cottage, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Kuma Party’s cottage is a little yellow house with a neat pebble path and a cozy sitting room. Kuma invites Peter and Ruggedo to stay there during the rain, but Ruggedo insists that they leave.

records.l: Kuma Party's come-apartishness, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Kuma Party’s come-apartishness allows his body parts to move independently and perform tasks while he rests. His hands can gather fruit, his head can seek news, and his parts can assist others; his arm carries an umbrella and lantern for Peter and Ruggedo and guides them to Patch.

records.l: magic belt, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: The magic belt is something Ruggedo intends to get after reaching Patch. He wants to use it to make Kuma Party’s captured hand work for him.

records.l: Flying Cloak of Invisibility, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Ruggedo waves a cloak over his head when he sees Patch’s castle and boasts that he will soon rule the realm. He later tells Scrapper that he has a cloak to be mended, using this claim to enter the castle.

records.l: umbrella, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Kuma Party lends Peter and Ruggedo a large umbrella for their journey. His detached arm holds it over them through the rain without letting a drop fall on them, then carries it to Patch’s castle and uses it to knock on the door.

records.l: Peter and Ruggedo's journey to Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Peter and Ruggedo leave Kuma Party’s cottage in the rain, following Kuma’s arm with its umbrella and lantern. They pass tidy farms and orchards, travel through a wood and across a cotton field, and arrive at a castle in Patch. Kuma’s hand leaves them after greeting Scrapper, patting Peter, placing a note in Peter’s pocket, and warning Ruggedo.

records.l: Peter's meeting with Kuma Party, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Peter first encounters Kuma when a detached hand pulls him into the cottage and a foot kicks Ruggedo into a gooseberry bush. He learns about Kuma’s unusual gift and enjoys Kuma’s kindness, but Ruggedo prevents him from staying to hear more. Peter remains especially excited by Kuma’s hand and its helpful actions during their journey.

records.l: Kuma Party's assistance, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 8 Peter Meets Kuma Party
records.s: Kuma Party offers Peter and Ruggedo shelter, supper, directions, an umbrella, and a lantern. His detached arm protects them from the rain and guides them toward Patch, while his hand later pats Peter approvingly, gives him a small note, and warns Ruggedo before departing.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Scraps is astonished to find Ruggedo, the former King of the Gnomes, in the Patchwork castle seeking to have his magic cloak mended. Scrapper allows the cloak to be repaired and accepts Peter as payment after Ruggedo falsely identifies him as a slave. Once the cloak is mended, Ruggedo uses it to vanish, despite Peter’s attempt to send him to Zamagoochie. Scraps, Peter, and Grumpy then discuss Ruggedo’s threat to Ozma and the Emerald City and begin considering how to escape from the castle.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Scraps is astonished and alarmed to find Ruggedo outside Runaway Island, since she knows he was banished and has repeatedly tried to capture Oz. She warns Scrapper about Ruggedo, promises to help Peter, and tells him about her life and forced work in the castle. After Ruggedo disappears, she joins Peter in considering how they can escape and reach the Emerald City.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Ruggedo arrives with Peter to have his magic cloak mended and is disconcerted to discover that Scraps is the Queen of Patch. He falsely agrees that Peter is his slave so that Scrapper will accept the boy as payment, then puts on the repaired cloak and vanishes. Scraps fears that he will use the cloak to reach and threaten the Emerald City.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Peter tries to conceal the truth about himself and Ruggedo because he needs the magic cloak repaired so he can warn Ozma. Ruggedo causes him to be offered as a slave, but Scraps assures him that she will help. Peter unsuccessfully tries to seize the cloak before Ruggedo disappears, then tells Scraps and Grumpy how he came to Oz and resolves to escape with Scraps.

records.l: Scrapper, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Scrapper brings Peter and Ruggedo to the old Quilty woman so that Ruggedo’s cloak can be mended. He treats Ruggedo as an honored customer, ignores Scraps’s warnings, and accepts Peter as payment after Ruggedo calls him a slave. After Ruggedo vanishes, Scrapper becomes upset but still leaves Peter locked in the room.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Grumpy is found hiding in a chest and comments on the argument in the room. He listens eagerly to Peter’s story, urges Peter to tell Scraps about him and Scraps, and reminds them that they must first escape from the castle. He advises Peter to go to sleep when they do not know what to do, and Peter falls asleep resting on his shoulder.

records.l: Ozma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Ozma is identified as being in danger from Ruggedo’s plans. Peter wants the repaired magic cloak so he can reach the Emerald City and warn her, and he later dreams of defending her.

records.l: Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Ruggedo is described as having tried to capture Oz at least a dozen times. Scraps warns that he is mean, cruel, and dangerous and may ruin Oz and everyone there.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Peter hopes to reach the Emerald City to warn Ozma about Ruggedo. After Ruggedo escapes with the magic cloak, Scraps fears that Peter and she may never reach the Emerald City before him.

records.l: Flying Cloak of Invisibility, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: The magic cloak is brought to the Quilty castle to be repaired because it can take its wearer wherever he wants to go. Once the old Quilty woman mends it, Ruggedo puts it on and becomes invisible except for a blue patch before disappearing completely.

records.l: mending the cloak, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: An old Quilty woman is summoned late at night to mend Ruggedo’s cloak. She repairs it rapidly with a needle, and Scrapper seeks payment; Ruggedo offers Peter as payment by falsely claiming that he is the boy’s master.

records.l: Ruggedo's disappearance, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: After the cloak is mended, Ruggedo puts it on and vanishes from sight, leaving only the blue patch visible for a moment. Peter cries out, "Take him to Zamagoochie!", but Ruggedo and the blue patch disappear, leaving Peter angry and Scrapper distressed.

records.l: escape from Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 9 Queen Scraps Meets Peter
records.s: Peter and Scraps decide that they must escape from the castle and try to reach the Emerald City ahead of Ruggedo. Grumpy points out that escaping is their immediate problem, while Scraps begins planning after the candle goes out and Peter falls asleep.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy plan to escape the castle in Patch after Peter reads Kuma's note promising help. They discover the Sandman's Nap Sack, use it to put the Scissor Bird to sleep, and summon Kuma's hand to unlock the doors and fight off the Quilties. Kuma's hand carries them out of Patch and helps them reach a maple grove, where it leaves them to continue toward the Emerald City. Scraps declares that she will no longer be Queen of Patch, even though Grumpy says the kingdom will fall apart in four days without her.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Peter reads Kuma's note and realizes that Kuma will lend them a hand. He helps prepare breakfast, discovers the Sandman's Nap Sack with Scraps, summons Kuma's hand, and escapes Patch with Scraps and Grumpy.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Scraps urges Peter to use Kuma's help to escape and worries about reaching the Emerald City before Ruggedo. She discovers the Sandman's Nap Sack, helps Peter carry out the escape, and declares that she abdicates as Queen of Patch.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Grumpy offers to help Peter and Scraps and washes the dishes while wearing a gingham apron. During the escape, he sends one of the pursuing Quilties flying into a ditch and travels with Peter and Scraps toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Kuma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Kuma promises in a note to send a helping hand whenever Peter needs one. Kuma's assistance enables Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy to escape from Patch.

records.l: Kuma Party’s hand, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Kuma's right arm and hand smashes through the castle door, unlocks the way out, and uses a club to strike the Quilties pursuing the fugitives. It opens gates, removes obstacles, carries Peter and Grumpy when they become tired, and then leaves them in a maple grove several miles from Patch.

records.l: Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Patch is the little kingdom where Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy are held as prisoners and forced to work. After their escape, Grumpy says that Patch will go to pieces in four days without Scraps as its Queen.

records.l: Quilties, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: The Quilties keep Peter and Scraps imprisoned and make them perform household work. Several Quilties chase the escaping group, but Kuma's hand, the Sandman's Nap Sack, and Grumpy drive them back.

records.l: Scissor Bird, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: The Scissor Bird supervises Peter and Scraps, drives Scraps toward the kitchen, and repeatedly snips at them with its bill. Peter throws the Sandman's Nap Sack over its head, causing it to fall asleep and snore loudly.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital toward which Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy travel after escaping Patch. Scraps believes they can reach it that night, and she wants to arrive before Ruggedo.

records.l: Kuma's note, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Kuma's note says that Peter can write directions on it and toss it into the air whenever he needs a helping hand. Peter writes a request for help escaping the palace of Patch, and the note disappears before Kuma's hand arrives.

records.l: Sandman’s Nap Sack, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: The Sandman's Nap Sack is an old grey sack labeled as putting its wearer to sleep at once. Peter uses it first on the Scissor Bird and later on a pursuing Quilty.

records.l: escape from Patch, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy escape from Patch after Peter summons Kuma's hand. Kuma's hand helps them break out of the castle, defeat or evade their pursuers, and reach the edge of the kingdom.

records.l: Kuma Party's assistance, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 10 Escape From Patch At Last
records.s: Kuma's assistance comes through the summoned hand, which unlocks the castle, protects the fugitives with a club, clears their path, and carries Peter and Grumpy when they tire. After bringing them safely beyond Patch, the hand departs without leaving another note.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy continue their journey to the Emerald City and accidentally slide down Soap Mountain into a village made entirely of soap. The Suds take them to their ruler, Shampoozle, the Sultan of Suds, who plans to turn them into soap products. They escape by jumping from a window and run along the shore of a lake. Peter discovers that soap floats, so they build a raft from a large soap slab and sail away.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Peter travels with Scraps and Grumpy toward the Emerald City, hoping Ozma can send him back to Philadelphia in time to pitch in his game. He is captured by the Suds, escapes from Shampoozle's palace by jumping from a window, and discovers that soap floats, allowing the group to cross the lake on a soap raft.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Scraps leads the group onward and slides with Peter and Grumpy down Soap Mountain into the soap village. She refuses to salaam to Shampoozle and is forcibly salaamed by his slaves, but escapes with the others and helps launch the soap raft.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Grumpy guides the travelers by climbing trees and insists that he will never leave Oz because he can be both a bear and a person there. After sliding down Soap Mountain, he is threatened with being made into a bath mat, but escapes with Peter and Scraps on the soap raft.

records.l: Sultan of Suds, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Shampoozle is the green-soap Sultan of Suds, ruling from an ivory soap throne. He orders Scraps to be salaamed and plans to turn Grumpy into a bath mat, Scraps into washcloths, and Peter into soap fat, but the three escape through a window.

records.l: the Suds, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: The Suds are soap villagers who skate through their village and bring Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy to Shampoozle. They are made of soap, wear turbans and robes of Turkish toweling, and come in pink, green, white, and violet.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: The Emerald City is the destination toward which Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy are traveling. Scraps believes they can capture Ruggedo even if he has reached the Emerald City.

records.l: Soap Mountain, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Soap Mountain is a slippery mountainside covered in yellow soap. Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy slide down it and cannot climb back up.

records.l: the soap village, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: The soap village has houses, walks, gardens, fountains, trees, bushes, and snow made from or associated with soap. Its inhabitants are the Suds, who skate over the slippery streets and take the travelers to Shampoozle.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy continue their journey through the pleasant land of the Winkies, following roads and traveling under banana trees. Their route is interrupted when they slide into the soap village, but they resume their escape by crossing its lake.

records.l: the escape from the Sultan of Suds, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Peter notices an open window in Shampoozle's throne room and signals Scraps to flee. Scraps jumps first, followed by Peter and Grumpy, and they run along the lake shore until they find materials for a raft.

records.l: the soap raft, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: The soap raft is made from a large slab of soap taken from an abandoned soap building. Peter pushes it into the lake with a bar of green soap as a pole, and he, Scraps, and Grumpy float away from the Sultan of Suds.

records.l: soap, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 11 Scraps Meets Sultan Of Suds
records.s: Soap covers the mountain, buildings, streets, trees, plants, snow, and lake shore in this land. The soap is slippery, produces lather and bubbles, and floats well enough to serve as a raft.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy cross the Sudsy lake and become lost in the Bewilderness, where trees, rocks, bushes, and sand move around them. They meet Ozwold, an Oztrich guarding his enormous egg, and persuade him to carry them toward the Emerald City while they transport the egg. Peter considers using the egg to frighten Ruggedo, but promises to keep it safe. At the Emerald City’s yellow wall, Scraps plays an upright piano blocking the opening, causing it to fall backward and then snap upright after they pass through.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Peter crosses the sudsy lake with Scraps and Grumpy, then becomes lost with them in the Bewilderness. He helps find Ozwold, carries Ozwold's egg during the journey, and considers threatening Ruggedo with it. He reaches the Emerald City with the others after Scraps opens a passage through the yellow wall.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Scraps travels with Peter and Grumpy through the Bewilderness and is repeatedly tripped by the shifting landscape. She helps persuade Ozwold to carry them and his egg to the Emerald City. At the yellow wall, she plays the Grand March of Oz on an upright piano, causing it to fall backward and allowing them to pass.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Grumpy crosses the lake with Peter and Scraps and becomes dizzy and confused in the Bewilderness. He helps identify Ozwold as a living creature and suggests that the Oztrich's egg could be endangered by the moving rocks. He rides on Ozwold's back to the Emerald City, bouncing and gasping during the journey.

records.l: Bewilderness, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: The Bewilderness is a barren, shifting desert where trees, rocks, bushes, and sand move unpredictably. Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy struggle to travel through it until Ozwold carries them out.

records.l: Oztrich, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: An Oztrich resembles an ostrich but has green feathers and blue eyes. The Oztrich encountered by Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy is guarding an enormous egg and agrees to carry them toward the Emerald City if they transport the egg.

records.l: Ozwold, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Ozwold is the Oztrich whom Peter, Scraps, and Grumpy meet in the Bewilderness. He initially stays to guard his egg, but agrees to carry the travelers after they offer to take the egg with them. He carries them rapidly out of the Bewilderness and to the yellow wall of the Emerald City.

records.l: oztrich egg, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Ozwold's egg is enormous and lies beside him in the sand. Peter carefully carries it on Ozwold's back, and he and Scraps discuss using it to frighten Ruggedo, though Peter decides to keep it safe for Ozwold.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: The Emerald City is the destination toward which Peter, Scraps, Grumpy, and Ozwold travel. Its outskirts are enclosed by a high yellow wall with an opening blocked by an upright piano.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: Ruggedo is the person Peter and his companions are trying to catch. Peter believes that if Ruggedo is afraid of hen's eggs, Ozwold's much larger egg might frighten him.

records.l: upright piano, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 12 Friend Oztrich Offers To Help
records.s: An upright piano is wedged into an opening in the high yellow wall near the Emerald City. When Scraps plays the Grand March of Oz, it falls backward, allowing the travelers to pass, and then snaps back upright.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Scraps, Peter, Grumpy, and Ozwold fall into Tune Town, where the bandmaster explains that everyone must sing, dance, and obey the town’s musical laws. They meet Queen Jazzma, perform songs, and visit the Viol Inn, but find that its food consists of leather music rolls rather than dinner. Scraps discovers that the travelers can escape by singing out of tune, so their discordant “Ah” causes the inhabitants to flee and sends them outside the town. The travelers then choose the center road and continue onward, still hungry.

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Scraps falls into Tune Town with the others and adapts enthusiastically to its rules of singing and dancing. She sings with Queen Jazzma, refuses the offer to become a maid of waiting, tries to obtain food at the Viol Inn, and devises the plan to escape by singing “Ah” in different keys.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Peter enters Tune Town with Scraps, Grumpy, and Ozwold while carrying the oztrich egg. He struggles with the law against speaking, becomes hungry at the Viol Inn, and helps produce the discord that gets the travelers out of Tune Town.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Grumpy enters Tune Town riding the oztrich and suggests that he and the others present themselves as a quartet. He dances and shuffles along with the music, cannot eat the leather music rolls at the Viol Inn, and joins the others in the discordant scream that leads to their escape.

records.l: Oztrich, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Ozwold says that he cannot sing despite being a bird, so the bandmaster advises him to keep quiet and dance. He dances through Tune Town, makes a song about running away, rejects the leather music rolls, and joins the others in singing out of tune.

records.l: bandmaster, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: The bandmaster explains that Tune Town’s gates are locked with piano keys and that the travelers entered when they struck the opening chords. He warns them to sing rather than speak, tests whether they are in tune, and tells them they may go where they wish as long as they keep step and sing.

records.l: Tune Town, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Tune Town requires its inhabitants and visitors to sing instead of talking and dance instead of walking. Its dwellings, streets, trees, and activities are marked or shaped around music, and the travelers eventually escape it by creating a terrible discord.

records.l: Queen Jazzma, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: Queen Jazzma arrives dancing with a tom-tom cat and questions the travelers. She invites Scraps to become her maid in waiting, permits the travelers to eat at the Viol Inn, and takes part in the musical life of Tune Town.

records.l: band, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: The band begins a lively march that makes the population of Tune Town dance and carry out daily activities to music. When Peter speaks against the law, its members rush at the travelers with their instruments, but they flee after the travelers produce a discordant “Ah.”

records.l: Viol Inn, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: The Viol Inn is kept by Daddy Linn, who demands payment in musical harmony before the travelers may eat. Instead of food, he gives them leather music rolls and offers a grand piano, so the hungry travelers leave disappointed.

records.l: Tune Town escape, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: The travelers escape Tune Town after Scraps has them all scream “Ah” in different keys. The resulting discord frightens the band, Queen Jazzma, and the Tunesters away and leaves the four travelers outside the town without knowing exactly how they crossed the wall.

records.l: singing and dancing in Tune Town, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 13 Tune Town Sings The Wanderers Onward
records.s: In Tune Town, singing replaces speech and dancing replaces walking, and the inhabitants perform ordinary tasks to the music. Scraps, Peter, Grumpy, and Ozwold attempt to follow these rules until their deliberately discordant singing provides a way out.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Peter, Grumpy, Scraps, and Ozwold travel rapidly toward the Emerald City after learning that Ruggedo has escaped and plans to steal all the Oz magic and rule Oz. Along the way, Peter and Grumpy eat umbrella melons, and Ozwold worries about protecting his egg child. Ozwold runs over a bookman, who offers them stories but does not know the way to the Emerald City. Scraps eventually spots the yellow brick road and directs Ozwold toward the Emerald City’s golden gate.

records.l: Peter, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Peter travels with Grumpy, Scraps, and Ozwold toward the Emerald City. He eats an umbrella melon, carries Ozwold’s egg child, helps the bookman after Ozwold runs him over, and continues onward when Scraps finds the yellow brick road.

records.l: Grumpy, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Grumpy complains hungrily about the lack of biscuit bushes and carrot trees, then catches and eats an umbrella melon. He falls into a ditch when Ozwold stops suddenly and later rides behind Peter while urging Ozwold to say “whum” instead of “whoa.”

records.l: Scraps, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Scraps dances, performs cartwheels, and rides on Ozwold during the journey. She welcomes the bookman with a verse and promises to read him in the Emerald City, then spots the yellow brick road and urges Ozwold to hurry toward the city.

records.l: Ozwold, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ozwold carries Peter, Grumpy, and Scraps toward the Emerald City and eats cobblestones along the way. After hearing about Ruggedo’s escape and plan, he becomes alarmed and races forward, accidentally running over the bookman. He is impatient with the group’s delay and then follows Scraps onto the yellow brick road.

records.l: baby oztrich (Ozwold's child), The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ozwold’s egg child is his wife’s favorite egg. Peter carries it during the journey, and Ozwold worries that it might hatch before they reach the Emerald City; it remains safe after falling onto soft sand.

records.l: bookman, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: The bookman is a living book with a round, jolly face, floppy dog ears, thin limbs, and a book body. Ozwold runs him over, but he is not seriously hurt and offers the travelers animal tales, verse, and other stories. He cannot give directions to the Emerald City because he is not a guide book.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ruggedo has escaped and has a flying cloak. Ozwold fears that Ruggedo may already have reached the Emerald City and captured everyone.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: The Emerald City is the travelers’ destination, and Scraps says the yellow brick road leads to its golden gate. The group hopes to reach it before Ruggedo can threaten the kingdom, though Ozwold fears it may already have been destroyed.

records.l: Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Oz is the realm whose kingdom is in danger from Ruggedo. Scraps tells the travelers about its capital and its delightful people.

records.l: yellow brick road, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: The yellow brick road is found between pear trees by Scraps. She identifies it as the road leading to the Emerald City’s golden gate.

records.l: Oz magic, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ruggedo’s stated plan is to steal all the Oz magic. The threat to the Oz magic is part of the danger that drives the travelers toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Ruggedo's escape, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ruggedo’s escape is described to Ozwold during the journey. After hearing about it, Ozwold worries that Ruggedo may already have used his flying cloak to reach and capture the Emerald City.

records.l: Ruggedo's plan to rule Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 14 Ozwold And His Friends Rush On
records.s: Ruggedo plans to steal all the Oz magic and make himself ruler of Oz. Ozwold reacts with alarm and races toward the Emerald City to help save the kingdom.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Wumbo the Wonder Worker lives in a crystal cavern in the Zamagoochie Country and secretly studies magic after Ozma forbids its practice. He uses a speech-giving chant on his furniture and discovers that an invisible Ruggedo is trapped in his arm-chair. Wumbo makes Ruggedo visible and learns that he plans to go to the Emerald City, though Ruggedo claims he is going there to report a treasure ship. Wumbo falls asleep before he can warn Ozma, allowing Ruggedo to use his magic cloak and escape toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Wumbo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Wumbo lives comfortably in a crystal cavern and secretly studies sorcery. He uses chants to speak with his furniture, makes Ruggedo visible, and tries to keep him prisoner until he can warn Ozma, but he falls asleep and Ruggedo escapes.

records.l: Ruggedo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo is revealed as the invisible visitor trapped in Wumbo’s arm-chair. He says he wants to reach the Emerald City to report a treasure ship, but Wumbo considers him wicked and untrustworthy; after four hours, Ruggedo uses his magic cloak to escape.

records.l: Emerald City, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo intends to travel to the Emerald City and says he will have Ozma transport the treasure ship’s jewels and gold pieces to her castle. After escaping, he flies toward the Emerald City and sees its flashing spires below.

records.l: magic, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Magic practice has been forbidden by Ozma for everyone except Glinda and the Wizard of Oz, so Wumbo studies it secretly. Wumbo explains that two magic charms cannot work at the same time and that his chant will last four hours.

records.l: arm-chair, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Wumbo’s arm-chair has real arms and can clasp a person tightly. It holds the invisible Ruggedo, scolds him, and squeezes him whenever he struggles or puts his feet on its rungs, but its enchantment ends after four hours.

records.l: Flying Cloak of Invisibility, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo wears a magic cloak that makes him invisible. When Wumbo’s chant wears off, Ruggedo whispers a command and the cloak lifts him out of the arm-chair’s grasp and carries him away.

records.l: Blunderoo, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo says he is going to the Emerald City to report the discovery of a treasure ship. He claims that he will give its jewels and gold pieces to Ozma.

records.l: discovery of a treasure ship, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo claims that the discovery of a treasure ship is the reason he must reach the Emerald City. He says he intends to report it to Ozma and have the treasure transported to her castle, though Wumbo determines that Ruggedo’s account is not true.

records.l: Ruggedo's escape, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 15 Wumbo, Wonder Worker, At Home
records.s: Ruggedo escapes after four hours, when the magic of Wumbo’s chant has completely worn off. Using his magic cloak, he flies over the mountains, hills, and valleys toward the Emerald City.

records.l: The Gnome King of Oz, The Gnome King of Oz, CHAPTER 16 Kuma’s Hand Is At Work Again
records.s: Wumbo awakens to discover that Ruggedo has escaped and sends a message to Kuma Party for help.
