records.s: Quiberon’s cave is a great cave between jeweled cliffs, with sapphire formations, jeweled rocks, a stream, and a waterfall leading to further, incompletely known caves. Akbad brings Trot there to serve Quiberon and says he carried a mortal maiden there; searchers find neither her nor Quiberon. Trot and companions later escape by an explosion and reach the mainland.

records.l: Quiberon, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Quiberon is Mombi's gigantic sea monster: a dragon-headed fear-fish with dragon scales and talons, fiery nostrils, horns, a silver lock of hair, and eight red tusks. He occupies the Lake of Orizon and its cave, where his head rises above the water. Sent by Mombi, he pitilessly destroys Orizon's sea horses, terrifies the Ozure Islanders, prevents them from leaving, and demands a mortal maiden to serve him. He threatens the Ozure Isles with destruction unless they comply, and his menace is also linked to the threatened destruction of Philador's father's Kingdom. He imprisons Orpah after Orpah defends the sea horses and seeks to make Trot his servant, assigning her tasks in his cave. While chasing Trot and her companions, he loses his tusks biting Benny and becomes trapped in a narrow passageway. He later escapes or reaches the lake, attacks Queen Orin's boat, pursues Akbad, repeatedly assaults the sapphire castle, and is transported to the gardens of the Castle of Cheeriobed. There, before he can attack again, the Wizard uses black magic to petrify him into a glittering dragon of silver and bronze. His great figure is finally moved to the mouth of his cave, remaining there for all to see.

records.l: Tattypoo, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Tattypoo is the Good Witch of the North, an old, happy, good and powerful witch who rules the Gilliken Country wisely from her hut in the purple forest. She uses magic only for good, settles disputes, helps all who visit, defeated Mombi, and is the only witch of consequence in Oz. She owns a staff and believes magic for personal benefit would be wrong, yet cannot remember her youth or life before reaching the forest. After looking through her witch's window, she screams, leaps out, and disappears with her staff, cap, and spectacles. Her absence leaves the Gilliken Country without a ruler and vulnerable, prompting Ozma and others to seek her. Orin later reveals that Tattypoo was originally the Princess of the North, daughter of King Gil, wife of Cheeriobed, and mother of Philador. Mombi carried her from the Ozure Isles on a huge black eagle. Having lived as Tattypoo, she regains her true identity, returns to the Ozure Isles, and reunites with Cheeriobed and Philador.

records.l: Joe King, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Joe King is King of the Uplanders and Up Town, ruling a mountain-top kingdom. Though he came down from ruling to work and have fun, using his ax in the mountains, he owns the horse High Boy. He aids Philador and Herby, welcomes them to Up Town, tells Queen Hyacinth their story, hosts a feast, gives umbrellas, and seeks High Boy to speed their journey to the capital.

records.l: Cave City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Cave City is a dim, damp underground cavern beyond a narrowing sapphire passage, entered by paying three rocks and making its door open with laughter. Its shadow inhabitants imprison Orpah and take the travelers to King Silly the Second. Orpah escapes it, and the travelers are carried out after an explosion in Quiberon’s cave.

records.l: the Round-abouties, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Round-abouties are pudgy little people living in a round house, with rubber-soled, tennis-ball-like hands and feet. They continually circle through opposing moving, singing circles, draw Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny onto a merry-go-round, then chase them up tower stairs.

records.l: the Shutter Faces, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Shutter Town inhabitants use blue shutters to block sight and hearing, hiding from travelers as their King refuses to believe anyone crossed the wall.

records.l: Queen of the Ozure Isles, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Queen of the Ozure Isles, also Queen Orin and the Good Witch of the North, was abducted by Mombi when Prince Philador was two and remained missing for a long time. Her disappearance raised hopes that King Cheeriobed would seek her, while Trot and companions planned to ask Ozma for help. She returns crowned and young-looking, survives Quiberon's attack through Akbad's rescue, reunites with Philador, and reveals her identity.

records.l: Ozma, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Ozma is a little fairy and the Queen and ruler of Oz, the Emerald City, and the royal court. She is presented as a beneficent authority whose subjects expect her help: Philador is directed to seek her, and the Scarecrow warns that she may come with her army for important subjects in danger. Before she appears, Akbad predicts that she will travel to the Ozure Isles, destroy Quiberon, and restore Cheeriobed's Queen, while others await her arrival. In the Emerald City, she welcomes Philador and his companions, hears their troubles, uses the magic picture to see Quiberon, and orders the Wizard to take the group to the Ozure Isles. There she listens even to Akbad, favors pardoning him because he helped save Queen Orin and suffered, and permits removal of his golden wings. She secretly works with the Wizard to restore the sea horses and persuades the King, Queen, and little Prince to return to the Emerald City. At her castle, she hosts a banquet, establishes Cheeriobed and Orin as King and Queen of the East, appoints Joe and Hyacinth as rulers of the North, and adds Benny and Herby to her court.

records.l: Orizon, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Orizon is a remote, deep, salt, turbulent inland sea in the Munchkin Mountains, surrounding the Ozure Isles and forgotten on modern Oz maps. After an explosion carries Trot, Benny, the Scarecrow, and Orpah across its bottom, they emerge from its waters. Later it lies beside the palace, carries Queen Orin’s return route, and becomes the setting for Orpah’s crossing and Quiberon’s attack.

records.l: Sapphire City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Sapphire City is a city in Oz and the capital of the East, with glittering spires, jeweled sands and rocks, blue waters, and the Castle of Cheeriobed. The Wizard brings Ozma, Philador, Trot, and others there, where Quiberon is petrified. Cheeriobed and the royal party tour it, and King Orin and Queen Cheeriobed declare it the eastern capital.

records.l: the Ozure Islanders, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Ozure Islanders are one thousand and seven tall, fair-haired Munchkins, virtual prisoners inhabiting the Ozure Isles and subjects of Cheeriobed; they include the Guards. They cheer Ozma's promised arrival, send bold Guards toward Quiberon's cave, welcome Queen Orin, then retreat to the sapphire castle and bar it against Quiberon's attack.

records.l: Munchkin Country, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Munchkin Country contains Lost Lake of Orizon and a blue farm house; Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny land there and head toward a road to Jinjur's door.

records.l: Gillikens, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Gillikens, ruled by Tattypoo after thanking her for defeating Mombi, live peacefully and prosperously.

records.l: Mombi, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Mombi is an old, ugly witch and former wicked ruler of the North, credited with the strength of ten men and with powerful magic tools and enchantments. She steals and abducts queens and mothers, including the young Queen of Cheeriobed and Philador's mother, and hides Philador's royal mother while causing his troubles. When Philador is two, she carries off the Queen of the Ozure Isles. After seeing Cheeriobed's intended wedding to Orin, Mombi falls in love with him, transforms herself into a young maiden, and seeks to marry him. Rejected, she abducts Orin and tries to turn her into a witch, but Orin drives her from the forest. Mombi also utterly destroys Cheeriobed's father, the good King of the Munchkins. Tattypoo captures and conquers her, taking her magic tools; later Ozma orders her put out. Her absence leaves some of her damage beyond remedy.

records.l: Akbad, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Akbad is a court soothsayer from the Ozure Isles who possesses magic wings and a descriptionary. Rejecting Cheeriobed's inaction, he decides to obtain a mortal maiden for Quiberon. He plucks the golden pear from the sacred tree, which becomes golden wings that carry him to the Emerald City of Oz. There, appearing as a great ugly bird-man, he uses a picture to identify Trot, seizes her, and carries her away despite Benny's resistance. He transports Trot, Benny, and the Scarecrow to the Ozure Isles, tells Trot she was chosen to save the islands by serving Quiberon, and leaves. Back in the King's garden, he lies about carrying Philador and leaving a maiden for Quiberon. The wings cannot be removed and allow him to fly only as far as the shore. Later, hiding because he cannot explain Ozma's absence and the Prince's disappearance, he overcomes fear when Quiberon attacks Queen Orin, rescues her, and carries her to the sapphire castle. Philador exposes Akbad's lies; Akbad is dismissed from court, pardoned, and given a cottage.

records.l: sea horses of Orizon, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: White sea horses, a herd once belonging to Cheeriobed and reunited with Orpah, are restored by the Wizard from bones; they race shoreward, greeted by High Boy, caressed by Orpah, and one carries the little Prince.

records.l: Quiberon's demand for a mortal maiden, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a threatening demand [requires a mortal maiden to wait upon Quiberon] Quiberon sends a smoke-written message ordering the Ozurians to send a mortal maiden to wait upon him. His demand alarms Cheeriobed and his subjects, who have no apparent way to obtain one or protect her.

records.l: Quiberon's threatened destruction of the Ozure Isles, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Quiberon threatens to destroy the Kingdom and Ozure Isles within three days unless he receives a mortal maiden, while preventing anyone from leaving. The threat terrifies the castle and islands and drives Philador, Cheeriobed, and Akbad to consider aid, the golden pear, the Good Witch of the North, or finding a maiden. With two days left, Philador begins toward the Emerald City; on the final day, Quiberon attacks Queen Orin and the sapphire castle.

records.l: Quiberon's imprisonment of the Ozurians, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a imprisonment [Quiberon keeps the King and his subjects on the islands] Quiberon has made Cheeriobed and the Ozurians virtual prisoners on the islands by guarding the waters of Orizon and destroying their sea horses. The inhabitants can venture to the shore only when Quiberon is sleeping, and they have no ordinary way to leave the islands.

records.l: the Castle of Cheeriobed, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Castle of Cheeriobed is a blue sapphire castle on the Ozure Isles and the royal residence of Cheeriobed and Queen Orin. After Akbad brings Orin there, Quiberon repeatedly attacks until the Wizard petrifies it in the gardens, and Cheeriobed admits Ozma’s party.

records.l: the blue gull, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Mo-gull is a giant blue gull, twice Philador’s size, with crown-like feathers and rule over land and sea birds; it carries Philador away for kindness and gentleness to its subjects.

records.l: Ozure Isles, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Ozure Isles are a kingdom ruled by King Cheeriobed, with Sapphire City as their radiant capital. They include Philador’s father’s kingdom and are home to the Queen, Prince Philador, and the Ozure Islanders. Their blue waters, Orizon, jeweled caverns, sea horses, and past mainland riders are notable. The kingdom faces almost certain destruction when Quiberon demands a mortal maiden and threatens to destroy it. Cheeriobed refuses to harm a mortal, while Akbad seeks a solution and Philador travels to save his mother and his father’s kingdom. Mombi had abducted the Queen, attacked the sea horses, imprisoned Orpah, and earlier carried Orin away; Orin later returned after recovering her identity. As destruction nears, Cheeriobed and his advisors await Ozma. The royal family eventually returns from the Emerald City to Sapphire City, where Cheeriobed makes Trot a Princess of the Ozure Isles.

records.l: the enchanted tree, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: An emerald tree in the King's gardens always bears one golden fruit; Akbad breaks the golden pear from its sacred bough.

records.l: the golden wings, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The golden wings emerge when the golden pear bursts open, fasten to Akbad's shoulders, and carry him swiftly south toward the capital. They later lift Akbad, Trot, and Benny, despite Benny's great stone weight. After Akbad picks the pear, they attach again but refuse his commands or removal, allowing flight only to the island's shore.

records.l: the rescue of the mortal maiden, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: King Cheeriobed, joined by a dozen Guards, seeks the mortal maiden at Quiberon’s cave after her reported abduction, but finds neither her nor Quiberon.

records.l: Akbad's flight to the Emerald City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_enabled_by the golden wings Akbad's flight begins after he plucks the golden pear and it becomes wings attached to his shoulders. Although he is frightened and initially hangs helplessly above the emerald tree, he eventually tells the wings to take him to the Emerald City of Oz, and they carry him south.

records.l: Philador's flight from the Ozure Isles, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Philador's flight begins in a seaside cave as he climbs onto the giant blue Mo-gull, which carries him from the Ozure Isles toward the Good Witch of the North.

records.l: the little black book, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The little black book contains closely written strange words; when Danny reads from it, its mysterious force apparently brings the Public Benefactor to life.

records.l: the yellow brick road, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The yellow brick highway crosses green fields, leading to Emerald City as Benny and the Scarecrow begin traveling it together.

records.l: Scarecrow, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Scarecrow is a cheerful, jolly, living straw-stuffed straw man and tolerated inhabitant of the fairy Kingdom of Oz. Created to frighten crows from a cornfield, he has hay in his shirt front, a cotton finger, magic brains in his head, and an unusual freedom from discomfort when his neck is wrung. Though recorded as not a real person, he advises Benny to act like one; he is also described as a Munchkin, a former real person, a celebrity, a traveler, Ozma of Oz's subject, and formerly Emperor of the Emerald City. He is now an emperor of the Land of Oz, has a castle in the Winkie Country, and lives and spends most of his time in the Emerald City. He meets Benny in Oz, names a statue Benny, explains Oz's monarchy, offers an introduction to the Queen, recognizes Trot, and recounts his creation, journey with Dorothy, and receipt of brains from the Wizard of Oz. Traveling with Trot and Benny toward the Emerald City, he shows fear of Akbad, Quiberon's fire, and High Boy's appetite, yet repeatedly helps the group: devising entry to Cave City, questioning and threatening its rulers, warning King Silly the Second of Ozma's response, and surviving an explosion, soaking, and a shadow transformation attempt. He then leads the companions through the Roundabout Way, escapes the Round-abouties, and reaches the Emerald City. There he introduces the arrivals, praises Benny's courage, and joins the journey to the Ozure Isles.

records.l: the Emerald City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz, containing the Emerald City castle; it was conquered by Jinjur in the past. It is a destination for travelers: the Scarecrow offers to take Benny there to meet the Queen, while Trot, Benny, and the Scarecrow approach its tall towers and flashing castle spires for a party. Philador and Herby travel there seeking Ozma’s help, and Trot’s party heads there to find the Queen of the Ozure Isles and stop Quiberon. At the end, inhabitants welcome Trot, the Scarecrow, and High Boy with a torchlit procession before the party leaves by the Wizard’s transport spell.

records.l: the transformation into a real person, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: This topic is Benny's wish to become a real person. After becoming alive, he is told that acting like a real person can make him one. He wants laughter, song, dance, and happiness despite the hardships of a different form. He expects the Wizard of Oz to help, but begins finding happiness by helping everyone.

records.l: Benny's coming to life, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Benny’s coming to life is caused by Danny reading strange, mysterious words from the little black book, changing the Public Benefactor from a statue into a living being. Benny leaves his pedestal, frightens and confuses people in Boston, then falls into Oz and gradually learns to behave like a person.

records.l: bird-man, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Akbad is a great, ugly bird-man with golden wings, first frightening the Scarecrow and Benny from above, then landing, confronting them, and carrying Benny to the Ozure Isles.

records.l: the Wizard of Oz, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Wizard of Oz, a native of Omaha, came to Oz in a circus balloon, became Royal Wizard, and ruled for many years before Ozma’s accession. He possesses a black bag of magic and famous, powerful wishing pills. He records problems involving Queen Orin, Tattypoo, Mombi’s mischief, Quiberon, and Benny; transports his group to the Sapphire City and petrifies Quiberon. He restores sea horses, moves Quiberon’s figure to its cave, and travels to the Emerald City. There he explains his past, finds the magic picture unchanged, concludes Mombi destroyed Cheeriobed’s father, and offers to make Benny real.

records.l: the picture (Akbad's picture), The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: comes_from the history of Oz Akbad uses a picture torn from his history of Oz to identify the kind of maiden he is seeking. After seeing Trot with the others, he declares that she is one of them and abducts her.

records.l: Akbad's abduction of Trot, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: has_destination the Ozure Isles Akbad suddenly seizes Trot after deciding that she is the maiden shown in his picture. The Scarecrow grabs her hand and Benny catches Akbad's ankles, but Akbad's magic wings carry Trot away toward the Ozure Isles.

records.l: Quiberon's cavern, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: contains the waterfall [a sparkling silver waterfall] The cave is a jeweled grotto with sapphire icicles, gems on the floor, and water rushing through its center. Trot, Benny, and the Scarecrow run through it while Quiberon pursues them.

records.l: the waterfall, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: leads_to the cave [another cave beyond it] A silver waterfall falls from the top of the cave and conceals a passage into another cave. Benny passes through it first, and Trot and the Scarecrow follow while Quiberon later plunges through after them.

records.l: Orpah, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Orpah is an old mer-man from the Ozure Isles, formerly the faithful keeper of King Cheeriobed’s sea horses. Made lame and given golden crutches by Cheeriobed, he was captured after escaping Quiberon’s cave and spent nearly twenty years imprisoned and enslaved in Cave City, where he guarded its entrance. He guides travelers through the city, recounts Mombi’s wickedness and the attacks on his people, then rescues Trot and aids Benny and the Scarecrow after the blue-ray explosion. Escaping at last, he returns to Cheeriobed as a messenger with news of the travelers and swims toward Queen Orin’s boat.

records.l: the monster's servitude, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_imposed_on Trot [by Quiberon] Quiberon requires Trot to serve him by polishing his scales, combing his hair, sweeping the cave, telling him stories, and singing him to sleep. Trot agrees to try serving him temporarily so that she and her companions may find a way to escape.

records.l: the travelers' escape from Quiberon's cave, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: An escape through a hidden waterfall passage: Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny flee Quiberon’s cave while he pursues. Benny stops him by breaking his tusks, and Quiberon becomes wedged in the narrowing passage.

records.l: Akbad's deception, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Akbad deceives Cheeriobed, falsely claiming Philador is safe in the Emerald City, Ozma will rescue the Ozure Isles, and he left Trot in Quiberon's cave.

records.l: Philador's disappearance, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: concerns Philador Philador's disappearance causes Cheeriobed and the courtiers to search urgently for him. Akbad uses the disappearance to invent his false account of having carried Philador to the Emerald City.

records.l: Agnes, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Agnes is Tattypoo’s small, amiable, good-tempered pet dragon and Orin’s maid-in-waiting, living with Tattypoo since Mombi’s conquest. Though non-destructive, she longs for grandeur, beauty, and a better home; she persuades Tattypoo to use a witch’s window, then falls after her.

records.l: North, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_ruled_by Joe [with Hyacinth as co-ruler] Ozma appoints Joe and Hyacinth as rulers of the North because the Gillikens are without a sovereign. High Boy leaves to announce the appointment to Joe.

records.l: the purple forest, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The purple forest is a deep, impenetrable yet beautiful purple-toned place around the good witch's cottage, rich in roots, herbs, vines, flowers, streams, and lavender fragrance; Philador and Herby enter it and emerge at a rushing torrent.

records.l: Good Witch's hut, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Good Witch's hut is a small, plainly and poorly furnished home, always unbolted and welcoming seekers of help or advice. Tattypoo lives there with Agnes and the two-tailed cat; Orin occupies it while under Mombi's spell. After Tattypoo and Agnes disappear, Philador stays, searches, and finds its shed workshop and enormous bottle.

records.l: the witch's window, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The witch's window is a dormer in the attic of the good witch's hut, with blue and pink leaded panes showing past and future; Tattypoo looks through it, jumps out, and Agnes follows.

records.l: magic, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_governed_by the law against using magic for personal benefit Tattypoo uses magic to help others, including freeing a forest maiden from an evil spell and sending her home on a fast wish. She refuses to use magic for her own benefit because she believes doing so is against the law.

records.l: youth and beauty, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_desired_by Agnes [for Tattypoo] Agnes suggests that Tattypoo could regain youth and beauty, or at least discover how she once looked. Tattypoo cannot remember whether she was ever young or pretty and insists that using magic for herself would not be right.

records.l: Tattypoo's disappearance, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Tattypoo's disappearance is triggered when she looks through the witch's window, screams, and jumps out with her belongings; Agnes falls after her. It leaves Philador distressed about saving the Kingdom, prompts the magic slate to direct him to the Emerald City, and alarms Ozma and her advisers, who plan to search using the magic picture.

records.l: Philador, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Philador is a little prince of the Ozure Isles and prince of his father's Kingdom. When Tattypoo disappears, he follows a magic slate's advice to seek Ozma of Oz's help, frees Herby from an enormous bottle, and travels toward the Emerald City carrying a thinking cap and a magic jumping rope. He is welcomed in Up Town, survives a storm that carries him down a mountain, and reunites with High Boy. He helps the travelers cross a river with his rope, shares food and pills, and continues guiding the journey. At the Emerald City, he is sad to part from his friend Trot, returns with the King, Queen, and little Prince, and invites Trot to the Ozure Isles, offering sea-horse rides, his crown, and a request that she become a Princess.

records.l: Philador's father's Kingdom, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Philador's father's Kingdom, linked to the Ozure Isles, is threatened with destruction by Quiberon and a monster; Philador leaves for the Emerald City seeking help to save it.

records.l: the magic slate, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: gives_guidance the journey to the Emerald City [through written messages] The magic slate first announces that the good witch of the North will never return. It then instructs Philador to go to the Emerald City, where Ozma of Oz will help him.

records.l: the enormous bottle, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: contains Herby [in liquid form for thirty years] The enormous bottle falls from a shelf when Philador is startled by a winking blue box. It breaks into three pieces, and the thick brown liquid inside forms Herby.

records.l: Good Witch's thinking cap, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Good Witch of the North's thinking cap is an object that reveals the direction to the Emerald City when asked. Philador and Herby take it and use it to travel through the forest and toward the mountains, though they forget to consult it at the river. A storm carries it away, leaving Herby to mourn it and resolve to think for themselves.

records.l: the jumping rope, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: A magical rope enables users to skip over a raging river; Philador and Herby cross safely, then return it to the witch's basket.

records.l: the bottle man's release, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_caused_by Philador [when he broke the bottle] Philador accidentally releases the bottle man when the enormous bottle breaks and its liquid forms Herby. Herby is grateful and promises to repay Philador by helping him.

records.l: the journey to the Emerald City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The journey to the Emerald City is undertaken by Philador with Herby. After preparing provisions and using a thinking cap to find the direction, they travel through a forest, cross a rushing river with a jumping rope, are separated from the castle by a storm, and are carried over purple mountains toward the capital by High Boy, joined by Joe King.

records.l: Philador's mother, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Philador's mother was stolen long ago by Mombi. Queen Hyacinth learns about her disappearance during Joe King's account of the travelers' adventures.

records.l: Kingdom of the Uplanders, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The Kingdom of the Uplanders is Joe King's kingdom, located at the top of the mountain. Joe King offers Philador half of it.

records.l: Up Town, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a mountain city Up Town is a strange mountain city with narrow, steep streets, tall towered houses, gardens, and very tall grass. Its castle stands majestically above the city amid purple haze and clouds.

records.l: the purple mountains, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: are_a mountain range [between the travelers and the Emerald City] The purple mountains lie beyond the river and lead toward a purple city and castle high in the clouds. Philador and Herby begin climbing them before Joe King and High Boy carry them toward the top.

records.l: the castle at Up Town, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_located_on Joe King's mountain [at the top] The castle of Up Town is the residence of Joe King and Queen Hyacinth. It contains a sumptuous dressing room, a dining hall, and a balcony overlooking the courtyard.

records.l: the witch's basket, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: contains the jumping rope [the rope is magical] The witch's basket contains the jumping rope. Its sudden rattling alerts Philador and Herby to the rope, which helps them cross the river.

records.l: Herby's medicine chest, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: contains pill boxes [multiple] Herby's medicine chest contains pills and lozenges, including medicine to prevent crossness and laugh lozenges that stop someone from laughing at the wrong time. Herby carries it up the mountain, worrying that the bottles may be smashed while riding High Boy.

records.l: the destruction of Philador's kingdom, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_caused_by the monster threatening the Ozure Isles [if the travelers fail to reach the Emerald City] The destruction of Philador's kingdom is the danger Philador is trying to prevent. Herby says the kingdom will be utterly destroyed by a monster unless they reach the Emerald City that night.

records.l: Queen Hyacinth, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Queen Hyacinth, ruler of Up Town and later the North, wears an amethyst crown and lavender lace dress, warmly aids Philador and Herby with food, then is appointed with Joe.

records.l: Joe King's mountain, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: contains Up Town Joe King's mountain is so tall that its top is hidden by storm clouds when Philador and Herby land at the bottom. High Boy searches across the mountain for them after the storm.

records.l: storm, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a weather phenomenon [sudden and furious] A sudden, violent storm strikes while Philador and Herby are walking near the castle. The wind carries them down the mountain because they do not know that Uplanders put their umbrellas down and jump into them during storms.

records.l: the royal feast, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a feast [prepared for the travelers] The royal feast includes chicken and waffles, sweet potatoes, hot biscuits, cream cake, custard pie, and lavender ices. Philador and Herby eat so much that they declare they cannot eat another bite.

records.l: umbrella, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a protective covering [used during storms] Joe King gives Philador and Herby umbrellas in case a storm comes up. The wind carries them away because they hold the umbrellas open, while High Boy explains that an Uplander should put an umbrella down and jump into it.

records.l: King Silly the Second, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: King Silly the Second, one-eyed king of Cave City, rules from the King's cavern and orders Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny melted into shadows while seeking the blue ray.

records.l: Cave Men, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Cave Men are living, mobile silhouettes of Cave City, armed with shadow weapons, serving King Silly the Second as subjects and guards who surround and forcibly escort visitors to him.

records.l: blue ray, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The blue ray, carried as a flaming blue torch by King Silly the Second, destroys exposed bodies and transforms them into shadows, producing a sparkle, flash, roar, and grinding sound when turned upon Benny.

records.l: shadow transformation, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a transformation into shadows King Silly the Second intends to transform Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny from bodies into useful silhouettes. The transformation is about to begin with Benny when the blue ray flashes and roars.

records.l: Mombi's abduction of the Queen, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Mombi abducts the Queen of the Ozure Isles when the little Prince is two, snatching her up and flying away; according to Orpah, it coincides with and causes Quiberon's attack.

records.l: Quiberon's attack on the Ozure Islanders, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Quiberon crossed the lake, devoured the Ozure Islanders' sea horses, depriving them of rides to the mainland, and seized Orpah after Orpah defended them.

records.l: Roundabout Way, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a road [possibly the longest route home] Roundabout Way is a narrow blue road entered through a blue turnstile. It curves repeatedly through bushy trees and leads to a huge round wooden house with a swiftly revolving door.

records.l: the round house, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The round house has a sawdust-covered floor, a revolving door, moving circles, and a central merry-go-round. A round tower rises to its wooden roof, where a spiral stairway reaches a trap door; Trot, the Scarecrow, and Benny escape from the roof across a forest.

records.l: the blue ray, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Operated by Ozeerus, the blue ray is turned higher when Benny refuses to melt, explodes through a cave, and carries mainland and companions across Lake Orizon’s bottom.

records.l: the explosion in Quiberon's cave, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: carries the mainland [by propelling the travelers to the lake bottom] The explosion in Quiberon's cave follows Ozeerus's increasing the blue ray. It blows out the cave's side and sends the travelers across the bottom of Lake Orizon to the mainland.

records.l: the escape from Cave City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The escape from Cave City frees Orpah, Benny, and the Scarecrow when a blue-ray explosion carries them and Trot out; Orpah tells Cheeriobed.

records.l: ring leader, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The ring leader is a Round-abouty leading the Round-abouties, marked by merry-go-round rings and a large silver bell. Around a round table, he orders Trot to make him laugh and the travelers kept circling; after Trot escapes, he rings the bell to direct pursuit.

records.l: merry-go-round, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: An immense, splendid carrousel stands at the exact center of the round house, with wooden zebra, tiger, and elephant riders and a round table in its hollow center. Its motion is scarcely noticeable until the ring leader’s bell stops it so Round-abouties can change riders.

records.l: Out Keeper, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Out Keeper is Shutter Town’s gate keeper, refusing entry while hiding a pale, flat face behind bolted blue shutters. He hears but cannot see through their slats. High Boy carries him over the wall and drops him in pickle bushes; afterward he warns the town about the travelers and flees, shouting for everyone to shut up.

records.l: Philador's quest, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: seeks Tattypoo [his royal mother] Philador's quest is to find his missing royal mother and save his father's Kingdom from Quiberon's threat. He travels with Herby toward the Emerald City after learning that Trot's experiences may be connected to the danger facing the Ozure Isles.

records.l: Shutter Town, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Shutter Town is a gloomy place of dingy blue-shuttered houses, box hedges, and stiff gardens; as High Boy passes through, hedges and flowers shut their lids, and the travelers see no Shutter Face.

records.l: travelers, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: reach Emerald City [at night after crossing the river] The travelers pass through Shutter Town despite the town's attempts to shut itself off, then cross a river safely on High Boy. They become tired and hungry during the journey, but Herby's pills keep some of them awake until they reach the Emerald City.

records.l: Joe, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a ruler [of the North] Ozma appoints Joe and Hyacinth rulers of the North. High Boy leaves the banquet hall intending to tell Joe the news.

records.l: shutters, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The shutters hide the Shutter Faces' eyes and faces, though the Out Keeper says he can hear through their slats. They can be fastened with bolts, opened to hear, or shut tightly so their owners neither see nor listen.

records.l: arrival at the Emerald City, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: occurs_at Emerald City [after less than an hour of travel from the green glow] After crossing the river and traveling through the night, the travelers see the green glow of the Emerald City's tower lights. High Boy speeds over hills and fields, and in less than an hour they reach the shimmering capital.

records.l: Queen Orin's return, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_a return [of the lost Queen to the Ozure Isles] Queen Orin's return occurs unexpectedly when she arrives in a fisherman's dory rather than with Ozma. Her welcome is interrupted by Quiberon's attack, and Akbad saves her from the monster.

records.l: Akbad's rescue of Queen Orin, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Akbad’s rescue of Queen Orin is a rescue from Quiberon’s attack. When Quiberon lunges at Orin’s boat, Akbad flies at the monster, snatches her from its jaws, and carries her beyond the islands with his magic wings. Cheeriobed credits him with the rescue, though another account about seeking help is unconfirmed.

records.l: the magic picture, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The magic picture, a powerful treasure in Oz, shows requested people where they are; at the Wizard’s command, it displays Quiberon attacking the sapphire castle.

records.l: Mombi's enchantments, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Mombi's enchantments cause the good witch's disappearance, bewitch Agnes, and drive Prince Philador's troubles. Her magic changes her appearance, abducts Orin on a black eagle, and tries to make Orin an old witch, but instead makes her a good, powerful witch. Orin's recognition through the blue window breaks the spell, and the Wizard plans to undo the damage.

records.l: the transport to the Ozure Isles, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: The transport to the Ozure Isles is ordered by Ozma after the magic picture reveals Quiberon attacking the royal castle. The Wizard uses his wishing pills to move the hand-holding company instantly to the gardens of the Castle of Cheeriobed.

records.l: Quiberon's petrification, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: transforms Quiberon [into a glittering dragon of silver and bronze] Quiberon's petrification occurs when the Wizard blows black powder into the air and stamps three times with his left foot. The monster freezes in midair and becomes a glittering dragon of silver and bronze.

records.l: Munchkins, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: are_ruled_by Cheeriobed [from the Sapphire City] The Munchkins are placed under the rule of Cheeriobed and Orin. The Scarecrow says that he is a Munchkin and promises to be their loyal friend and subject.

records.l: Orin's transformation into a witch, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Orin’s transformation occurs when Mombi imprisons her and uses magic to make her an old, ugly witch; retaining goodness and surpassing Mombi, Orin takes Mombi’s hut and rules the North as Tattypoo.

records.l: Orin's restoration to her true form, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Agnes leads Orin to Mombi's blue window; seeing Cheeriobed and Philador restores her memory, and jumping through the window breaks the spell, restoring Queen Orin's identity.

records.l: Akbad's punishment and pardon, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: Akbad's punishment and pardon is an event in which Cheeriobed confronts Akbad's deceit, threatens punishment, then pardons and dismisses him after Ozma, Trot, and Orin plead, giving him a cottage while the Wizard removes his heavy golden wings.

records.l: East, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_ruled_by Cheeriobed [with Orin as queen] Cheeriobed and Orin are appointed King and Queen of the East. Their rule includes all of the Munchkins, and Sapphire City is named their capital.

records.l: grand banquet, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: is_held_at Ozma's castle [to welcome the returning company] The grand banquet is held in the Emerald City to celebrate the returning company. Celebrities and palace animals attend, speeches are made, and the company drinks the health of the new sovereigns in pale pink lemonade.

records.l: homecoming celebration, The Giant Horse of Oz
records.s: includes Oz orchestra [playing at the welcome] The homecoming celebration begins with dancing in the gardens and continues with a royal banquet. After the announcements and speeches, the company goes into the garden to play blind-man's buff.

records.l: appointment of the rulers of the East, The Giant Horse of Oz

records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead possesses Red Jinn's bell (in his pocket)
records.q: Finally Jack grew so hoarse he could shout no more and, holding his head in both hands, he tried to think of some way to reach the Emerald City. "If the Scarecrow were only here," sighed Jack dolefully, "he would be sure to hit upon some clever plan, but I am only a poor stupid pumpkin head with only a few dried seeds for brains." Realizing that the whole fate of the Kingdom of Oz depended upon him, poor Jack pressed his head with his wooden hands and thought so hard that the seeds inside skipped about like corn in a corn popper. And one must have been a seed of thought, for presently Jack gave a little bounce and feeling in his pocket drew out the Red Jinn's bell.

records.q: Are you not Mogodore the Mighty, slayer of an hundred bears, subduer of an hundred barons and Lord of this mountain?

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Peter, stuck indoors by rain, finds a gold piece in one of the pirate's sacks and wishes to return to Oz. The coin transports him to a pumpkin-shaped cottage, where he meets Jack Pumpkinhead and learns more about Jack's history and Ozma's transformation from Tip. Peter and Jack set out for the Emerald City, but a red brick wall blocks their expected route. Peter opens a black door marked "Enter Here" and steps through it.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Peter becomes frustrated when rain cancels baseball practice, then finds a small gold piece in one of the pirate's sacks. After wishing to return to Oz, he is transported to a pumpkin field, meets Jack Pumpkinhead, and follows him toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The Land of Oz is described as an enchanted kingdom divided into four colored countries, with the Emerald City at its center. Peter returns there and arrives in the yellow Winkie Country before being confronted by a red wall and door.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Ozma is the little girl ruler of Oz and Peter hopes to see her again. Jack explains that Ozma was once a boy named Tip, who was transformed back into Ozma by Glinda after Mombi had enchanted him.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The two coarse sacks once held gold from a pirate ship that Peter discovered in Oz. One sack's gold was spent on various improvements and purchases, while the other was exchanged for United States dollars and placed in a bank; Peter later finds a remaining gold piece in one of them.

records.l: magic coin, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The magic coin is a small, thin gold piece Peter finds in a pirate's sack. When Peter wishes to be in Oz while flipping it into the air, the coin transports him there, and Jack calls it a piece of change because Peter wished to come to Oz for a change.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead catches Peter's attention by accidentally losing his head, which Peter replaces on his body. Jack does not remember Peter because he has had several heads, tells Peter the history of Ozma and his own creation, and guides him toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz, located at the center of its four countries. Peter wants to visit Ozma and Dorothy there, but he and Jack do not reach it because their road ends at a high red brick wall.

records.l: Peter's return to Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 1
records.s: Peter's return to Oz occurs when he wishes over the gold piece found in the pirate's sack. He arrives in a pumpkin field, reunites with Jack Pumpkinhead, and begins traveling toward the Emerald City before entering an unexplained door in a red wall.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead fall down a chimney into Chimneyville, where the Smokies and Chimney-villains attack them with smoke. Peter uses a candle end inside Jack's head as a lantern, allowing them to escape through another chimney into a quiet wood. They continue toward the Emerald City and visit the Goody Shop, where Peter receives bird seed labeled a good breakfast and Jack receives advice to keep his mouth shut.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Peter falls with Jack Pumpkinhead into Chimneyville and is surrounded and nearly suffocated by the Smokies. He lights the candle end inside Jack's head, uses the lantern light to escape, and then continues toward the Emerald City. At the Goody Shop, he receives bird seed labeled a good breakfast and jokes about Jack's advice.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead falls down a chimney with Peter and is attacked by the Smokies, whose smoke does not affect him. Peter lights a candle inside Jack's head, and Jack helps guide them through Chimneyville; afterward, Jack says he feels brighter when lit. At the Goody Shop, he chooses good advice but rejects the instruction to keep his mouth shut because his mouth is carved open.

records.l: Smokies, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The Smokies emerge from the chimneys in Chimneyville as smoky figures with spark-like eyes. They surround Peter and Jack, threaten to throw them down the chimneys, and fill the square with a suffocating cloud, but they cannot overpower the travelers and are confused by Jack's lantern light.

records.l: Chimney-villains, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The Chimney-villains are the smoky inhabitants of Chimneyville. They try to smoke Peter and Jack out, lift them into the air, and force them toward the chimneys, but Peter and Jack escape.

records.l: Chimneyville, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Chimneyville is a place filled with red chimneys and inhabited by the Smokies and Chimney-villains. Its citizens invite Peter and Jack to visit their Sooty and attack them when they refuse.

records.l: Soot City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Soot City is the place Peter and Jack identify with the disagreeable citizens behind the chimney wall. From the outside, its red wall shows no chimneys or smoke to warn travelers about the Smokies.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Peter and Jack intend to continue their journey to the Emerald City after escaping Chimneyville. Peter takes a northward direction through the Quadling Country toward the capitol.

records.l: Goody Shop, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The Goody Shop is a small red cottage in a clearing with shelves of goods such as good advice, good excuses, and good breakfasts. The shop sells wordplay-based goods rather than the ordinary food Peter expects.

records.l: old lady (shopkeeper at the Goody Shop), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The old lady runs the Goody Shop and offers Peter and Jack a choice of goods. She gives Peter a box labeled a good breakfast and Jack a red envelope containing good advice, then sends them out of the shop.

records.l: chimney square (in Chimneyville), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The chimney square is paved with red flags and is crowded with red chimneys of many shapes and sizes. The Smokies attack Peter and Jack there, filling the square with smoke until the travelers escape through a chimney.

records.l: chimneys (in Chimneyville), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: The chimneys in Chimneyville stand close together across the red square and appear without houses. Smokies spiral out of them, and Peter and Jack use one chimney to enter and another to escape into the wood.

records.l: candle end, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Peter finds a small candle end in his pocket while he and Jack are trapped in darkness. He lights it, places it inside Jack's hollow head, and uses it to help them see through the smoke and escape.

records.l: Jack's lantern light, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: Jack's lantern light comes from the candle end Peter places inside his head. The bobbing light helps Peter and Jack see through the Smokies' cloud and puzzles their enemies while they flee.

records.l: Peter and Jack's journey to the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 2
records.s: After leaving Chimneyville, Peter and Jack resume their journey to the Emerald City. They travel north through a little wood in the Quadling Country and stop at the Goody Shop.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead encounter a walking Christmas Tree in the Quadling Country, which attacks them with grasping hands and thrown ornaments. They escape through a hidden rock door and discover that a silver bell summons a magically appearing dinner. After eating, they continue through a frightening corridor and arrive at the gates of Scare City.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Peter travels with Jack Pumpkinhead and encounters an aggressive Christmas Tree. He escapes the tree, eats the dinner summoned by the Red Djinn's dinner bell, and proceeds with Jack to Scare City.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead travels with Peter and is pursued by the Christmas Tree, which tries to take his pumpkin head. He picks up the Red Djinn's dinner bell, uses it to summon dinner, and continues with Peter toward Scare City.

records.l: Christmas Tree, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: The Christmas Tree is a green, walking tree searching for last year's ornaments. It attacks Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead with hands extending from its branches and throws its ornaments at them, but they escape through a rock door.

records.l: Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: The Red Djinn's dinner bell is a silver magic bell with its name carved on it. When Jack Pumpkinhead rings it, a black slave appears with a tray of dinner, and the bell later vanishes with the tray before Jack keeps it.

records.l: dinner, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: The dinner appears on a silver tray after the Red Djinn's dinner bell is rung. It includes roast duck, mashed potatoes, hot rolls, and apple sauce, and Peter eats it before the tray, dishes, and silverware disappear.

records.l: Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 3
records.s: Scare City is reached through a dark corridor filled with frightening goblin lanterns and noises. Its red, spiked gates bear scare heads and open while a voice welcomes Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead enter Scare City, where the Chief Scarer and the Scares try to frighten them into trembling, running, or screaming. Jack uses the magic dinner bell, allowing Peter to throw dinners and dishes at the attacking Scares. When the pirate sack opens, it swallows Harum Scarum, the Scares, and the Fraid Cats, but Peter and Jack remain trapped inside the city. A red stone griffin then comes to life and asks them, "Who? What? Whither? Why?"

records.l: Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Scare City is a grim cliff city with jagged rocks, carved dwellings and steps, frightening drawings, goblin lanterns, and bluish green smoke. After the Scares disappear, Peter and Jack cannot open the gate or find another way out, leaving them trapped in the silent city.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Peter is insulted by the Chief Scarer and responds by scowling and sticking out his tongue. He tries not to run or scream, throws food and dishes from the magic dinner bell at the Scares, and uses the pirate sack when the food runs out. After the sack swallows the Scares, Peter ties it shut and searches unsuccessfully for a way out of Scare City.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead trembles before the Scares and turns his head around so he will not have to see their frightening faces. He remembers the magic dinner bell and rings it repeatedly so Peter can throw food and dishes at the attackers. Afterward, he helps search for a way out and worries that the pirate sack may swallow them.

records.l: Scares, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: The Scares rush from the rock dwellings, order Peter and Jack to tremble before the King, and try to frighten and attack them. Peter throws food and dishes at them, after which the pirate sack swallows Harum Scarum and all the Scares.

records.l: Fraid Cats, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: Fraid Cats are singular two-headed creatures with a head at each end instead of a tail. They run among the Scares, and the pirate sack eventually swallows every Fraid Cat in the courtyard.

records.l: Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: When Jack Pumpkinhead rings the magic dinner bell, a little slave appears and sets down a tray of food before disappearing. It provides five dinners in less than five minutes, but on the fifth ringing it produces only a small bowl of soup.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 4
records.s: The pirate sack opens when Peter swings it and flies through the air, swallowing Harum Scarum, the Scares, and the Fraid Cats. It then returns to Peter and collapses at his feet, appearing empty; Peter ties it shut and decides to take it to the Emerald City to show the Wizard.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead meet Snif, an Iffin who was formerly a griffin imprisoned in Scare City. After Peter frees Snif from his chain, Snif briefly flies away but returns and agrees to carry them toward the Emerald City. Snif explains that he was held captive for five years and offers to serve Peter and Jack for seven years. He then flies with them over the wall into the Land of the Barons and lands in a peaceful valley.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Peter meets Snif, learns that he is an Iffin, and frees him from his chain with a gold key. He and Jack ride on Snif's back toward the Emerald City, and Peter is pleased that their escape from Scare City led to their meeting with Snif.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Jack questions whether Snif is carnivorous before Peter releases him and later rides in front of Peter on Snif's back. He helps carry the dinner bell and is warned to hold onto his head during the flight.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snif is an Iffin who lost his growl after being captured and imprisoned in Scare City for five years. Peter frees him, and after briefly testing his wings, Snif agrees to carry Peter and Jack and serve them faithfully for seven years. He flies them over the wall into the Land of the Barons and lands in a peaceful valley.

records.l: Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Scare City is a red cliff city filled with horrors, goblin lanterns, sulphurous air, and prisoners who have been frightened into statues or Fraid Cats. After Peter and Jack's conquest, they leave the city with Snif by flying over its wall.

records.l: Scares, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Scares are defeated and swallowed by the pirate's sack during Peter and Jack's battle in Scare City. They had captured Snif, chained him to a pillar, and wanted him to devour travellers.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Peter asks Snif to take him and Jack to the Emerald City. Snif is unsure of the way but plans to fly into the Land of the Barons, where they hope to find someone who can direct them.

records.l: Land of the Barons, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The Land of the Barons lies beyond Scare City's wall and contains rolling hills, trees, and castles with red towers and flags. Its barons are of various kinds and are often fighting, and Snif brings Peter and Jack down into a peaceful valley there.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The pirate's sack swallows the entire company of horrors during the battle for Scare City. Peter carries it when he and Jack leave the city, tightening its cord before they ride with Snif.

records.l: the battle for Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: The battle has ended before Peter and Jack meet Snif. Peter and Jack have conquered the city, using the Red Jinn's dinner bell and the pirate's sack to defeat and remove the Scares.

records.l: Peter and Jack's conquest of Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Peter and Jack's conquest causes the Scares to vanish and frees Snif from his imprisonment. Their victory allows them to leave Scare City, although they initially fear being stranded when Snif flies away before returning.

records.l: Snif's flight to the Land of the Barons, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 5
records.s: Snif carries Peter and Jack over the wall and flies across a bright red forest toward the Land of the Barons. He pauses to show them the castles below, then lands gently with them in a peaceful valley.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif travel from Scare City through the Quadling Country toward the Emerald City. They meet Belfaygor of Bourne, whose beard has grown uncontrollably after he was mesmerized and now prevents him from rescuing Princess Shirley Sunshine. Belfaygor explains that Mogodore the Mighty has stolen Shirley Sunshine, and Peter and Snif offer to help recover her.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Peter rests and eats wild strawberries while traveling with Jack Pumpkinhead and Snif. He praises Snif's abilities, learns about Belfaygor's troubles, and asks the baron to explain who Mogodore the Mighty is and what happened to Shirley Sunshine.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead travels with Peter on Snif's back and suggests that Belfaygor throw his beard over his shoulder so it will grow away from his feet. Belfaygor appoints Jack the Royal Bearer of the beard, but Jack says he cannot take the beard with him to the Emerald City.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Snif carries Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead toward the Emerald City, stopping to eat geraniums and then waddling because he is too full to fly. He recognizes Belfaygor as one of the good barons and offers to help rescue Shirley Sunshine with his wings and a magic sack.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Belfaygor of Bourne is introduced as the lord of the lands and a good baron. He has been abandoned by his men because of his enormous beard, and he cannot rescue the princess he was to marry because the beard trips him. He appoints Jack Pumpkinhead Royal Bearer of the beard after Jack suggests throwing it over one shoulder.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Shirley Sunshine is the princess whom Belfaygor was to marry. Mogodore the Mighty has stolen her, and Belfaygor fears that she needs to be rescued.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Mogodore the Mighty has stolen Shirley Sunshine, the princess Belfaygor was to marry. No further details about Mogodore are given in this unit.

records.l: Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Scare City is the place Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead have recently left. After experiencing it, they find the quiet valley and surrounding country especially beautiful.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Oz is the land in which the Quadling Country, Belfaygor's lands, and the Emerald City are located. Jack Pumpkinhead identifies himself as a subject of Ozma of Oz.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: The Emerald City is Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead's destination. They plan to ask one of the barons for directions to it, and later continue traveling toward it with Snif.

records.l: Peter and Jack's journey to the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Peter and Jack Pumpkinhead travel with Snif after leaving Scare City. They cross a flower-filled valley and open country containing hills, parks, castles, and red mountains, while intending to reach the Emerald City.

records.l: Belfaygor's mesmerizing, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Belfaygor's mesmerizing was performed by his servant, a miserable mesmerizer who rushes away in distress. Afterward, Belfaygor's beard grows continuously, and the baron identifies the practice as forbidden by Ozma.

records.l: the kidnapping of Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: The kidnapping of Shirley Sunshine is attributed to Mogodore the Mighty. It leaves Belfaygor distressed and unable to pursue or rescue her because his runaway beard trips him.

records.l: Belfaygor's beard, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 6
records.s: Belfaygor's beard grows in a steady torrent from his chin, flowing down his breast and around his feet. He tries desperately to cut it, but throwing it over one shoulder is the first useful solution offered, after which Jack Pumpkinhead is appointed to bear it.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Belfaygor tells Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif how a beard-growing enchantment caused his red beard to grow uncontrollably while Mogodore abducted Shirley Sunshine. Peter, Jack, and Snif agree to help rescue Shirley Sunshine from Baffleburg, using the pirate's sack and the magic dinner bell. They fly to the chasm outside Baffleburg and plan to enter Mogodore's castle at night, but Snif accidentally eats shrinking violets and becomes no bigger than a squirrel.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Belfaygor explains that his beard-growing enchantment caused his red beard to grow uncontrollably, forcing him to escape his palace with shears. He joins Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif on their journey to Baffleburg, but loses confidence when they reach Mogodore's mountain.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Peter promises to help Belfaygor rescue Shirley Sunshine and proposes flying into Baffleburg at night, dropping into Mogodore's castle courtyard, and using the pirate's sack against Mogodore and his fighting men. After Snif shrinks, Peter tries to comfort him.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead praises Peter's past victories and joins the plan to rescue Shirley Sunshine. He uses the magic dinner bell to summon meals and later cuts Belfaygor's growing beard while Peter comforts the shrunken Snif.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Snif carries Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Belfaygor toward Baffleburg and helps them reach the ground outside the chasm. After eating the shrinking violets, Snif shrinks to a creature no bigger than a squirrel.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Mogodore abducts Shirley Sunshine and carries her unconscious to his castle in Baffleburg. He is said to rule from a grim red castle on Mogodore's mountain and to have a formidable fighting force.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Shirley Sunshine is Belfaygor's intended bride. Mogodore abducts her while she is unconscious and takes her to his castle in Baffleburg.

records.l: Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Baffleburg is a fortified city built into a red mountain, surrounded by a chasm and defended by warriors, forts, and city walls. No one is said to have entered the city or returned alive from Mogodore's mountain.

records.l: Mogodore's mountain, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Mogodore's mountain contains Baffleburg and Mogodore's castle, with a chasm and towered fortress at its foot. Belfaygor regards the mountain and the rescue mission as extremely dangerous.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Peter is in Oz and recalls that he previously saved the Emerald City from the Gnome King. Belfaygor promises to knight Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif.

records.l: Mogodore's castle, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Mogodore's castle is a grim red castle clinging to the rocks halfway up the mountain. Peter believes Shirley Sunshine is locked in its tallest tower and plans to enter its courtyard.

records.l: Belfaygor's beard, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The red beard grows continuously after the enchantment, filling Belfaygor's palace and later streaming behind him during flight. Belfaygor must repeatedly cut it with shears, while Jack Pumpkinhead cuts it after they stop outside Baffleburg.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The pirate's sack is a magical object carried by Peter. Peter plans to open it inside Mogodore's castle so it will swallow Mogodore and his fighting men.

records.l: Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The magic dinner bell summons a little black slave carrying food on a silver tray. Jack Pumpkinhead rings it to provide meals for Peter and Belfaygor while they wait for night.

records.l: shrinking violets, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The shrinking violets cause Snif to shrink after Peter gives them to him as food. Snif becomes no bigger than a squirrel and worries that he is no longer useful for carrying the others.

records.l: Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine's wedding, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The marriage of Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine has been satisfactorily arranged, and Belfaygor has prepared his palace and retainers for the wedding. The marriage is threatened when Mogodore abducts Shirley Sunshine.

records.l: the kidnapping of Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: Shirley Sunshine's abduction occurs when Mogodore and his armed riders carry her unconscious from the next hillside to Baffleburg. Two riders boast that Mogodore will marry her the following morning.

records.l: the beard-growing enchantment, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The beard-growing enchantment is performed by Belfaygor's chief mesmerizer to improve his appearance before the wedding. The beard continues growing despite the mesmerizer's incantations and magic powders, eventually filling the palace.

records.l: the plan to infiltrate Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 7
records.s: The plan to infiltrate Baffleburg is to fly into the city under cover of darkness, drop into Mogodore's castle courtyard, and use the pirate's sack on Mogodore and his fighting men. Peter expects to find Shirley Sunshine locked in the castle tower and escape with her afterward.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, Snif, and Belfaygor must find a way to cross the chasm and reach Mogodore's city to rescue Shirley Sunshine. Snif, who has shrunk after eating violets, proposes using Belfaygor's beard as a bridge, with Snif flying it across and fastening it to a tree. The group plans to climb to the city gates in daylight, where the Baffleburghers may capture them and take them to Mogodore. They spend the night in a cave, using cut lengths of Belfaygor's beard as mattresses while Jack stands guard.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Peter reassures Snif that the Wizard of Oz can make him large again and helps plan how to reach the Emerald City. He agrees to Snif's beard-crossing plan and spends the night asleep in the cave with Snif curled in his arm.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead helps tend Belfaygor's beard by snipping it and later offers to stand guard while the others sleep. He worries about crossing the chasm and about the Baffleburghers impaling the group.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Snif explains that he shrank after eating violets, but he remains able to think and make verses. He devises the plan to use Belfaygor's beard as a bridge and expects the Baffleburghers to seize the travelers and take them to Mogodore.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Belfaygor agrees to lend his beard for the crossing, even though cutting it will hurt, because he wants to save Shirley Sunshine. He sleeps with his head outside the cave while Jack trims the beard to keep it from blocking the entrance.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Shirley Sunshine is locked in a dismal tower and is the reason the group is trying to reach Mogodore's city. Belfaygor is willing to sacrifice part of his beard to help rescue her.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Mogodore is associated with the mountain and the grim city on the rocks. Snif expects the Baffleburghers to take the travelers to Mogodore, where Peter can open the sack.

records.l: Baffleburghers, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The Baffleburghers are the guards at the city gates. The group fears they may impale the travelers, though Snif guesses they will instead seize them and carry them to Mogodore.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The Emerald City is the group's intended destination, where Peter hopes the Wizard of Oz can restore Snif's size.

records.l: chasm (between the cave and castle), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The chasm separates the travelers from Mogodore's city and appears too wide to cross by jumping. The group must find another way across it before climbing to the city gates.

records.l: shrinking violets, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The violets were eaten by Snif, apparently unintentionally, and caused him to shrink.

records.l: Belfaygor's beard, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Belfaygor's beard is proposed as a bridge across the chasm. Snif will carry its end across and fasten it to a tree, after which Peter and Jack can cross and Belfaygor can cut the beard near his chin and follow.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Peter is expected to open the sack once the group is brought before Mogodore. Snif believes the sack will swallow everyone, allowing the group to find Shirley Sunshine and return to the capitol on foot.

records.l: shrinking, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: Shrinking is what happened to Snif after he ate the violets, leaving him small enough to fit in Peter's pocket. Peter hopes the Wizard of Oz will make Snif large again.

records.l: crossing the chasm, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The group cannot cross the chasm by ordinary means and postpones the attempt until morning because the climb to the city would be impossible at night. They intend to use Belfaygor's beard to cross.

records.l: beard-crossing plan, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The beard-crossing plan requires Belfaygor to walk three times around a tree so his beard will be held fast, while Snif flies the beard's end across the chasm and ties it to a tree. Peter and Jack will cross first, and Belfaygor will cut himself free and cross afterward.

records.l: rescue of Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 8
records.s: The rescue of Shirley Sunshine requires the group to reach Mogodore's city and enter the tower where she is imprisoned. Belfaygor agrees to endure the loss of his beard to help accomplish the rescue.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: In Baffleburg, Baron Mogodore the Mighty worries about the secret of the forbidden flagon while preparing to marry the captive Princess Shirley Sunshine. Shirley refuses to marry him but manipulates his vanity by suggesting he should become a king, prompting him to plan an invasion of Oz and the Emerald City. Wagarag warns that Ozma and the Wizard may defeat him, but Mogodore orders preparations for the expedition and intends to open the flagon once he is king.

records.l: Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Baffleburg is Mogodore's mountain domain, where he rules as baron. Wagarag argues that Mogodore should remain there, where he is known and powerful, rather than attempt to conquer Oz.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Mogodore is a vain and cruel baron who has captured Shirley Sunshine and intends to force her to marry him. After Shirley flatters his strength, he decides to conquer Oz, become King Mogodore the First of Oz, and eventually open the forbidden flagon.

records.l: Wagarag, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Wagarag, Mogodore's chief steward and Major Domo, repeatedly urges him to stop worrying about the forbidden flagon and abandon his plan to invade Oz. Mogodore appoints him Royal Chancellor of Oz and orders him to accompany the expedition, despite his gloomy warnings.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: The forbidden flagon is a sealed container whose contents and purpose are unknown to Mogodore. The Book of Baffleburg warns that disturbing its seal or spilling even one drop will cause a dreadful disaster, and Mogodore plans to open it after becoming king of Oz.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Shirley Sunshine is held captive in a tower by Mogodore and refuses to marry him. Hoping to delay the wedding and secure her freedom, she flatters his ambition by suggesting that he conquer other countries and become a king, but this causes him to plan an invasion of Oz.

records.l: Mogodore's planned marriage to Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Mogodore intends to force the Princess to marry him, although she refuses and threatens that her father and Belfaygor will destroy him. After Shirley prompts his ambition, he declares that she will accompany him to the Emerald City, where they will marry and she will be crowned with Ozma's crown.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Mogodore plans to march across the Red Mountains, capture the Emerald City, depose Ozma, and proclaim himself king. Shirley becomes terrified that his planned attack will lay waste to the city's parks and palaces and enslave its inhabitants.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Mogodore intends to conquer Oz and become its king, believing his strength will overcome Ozma and the Wizard. Wagarag warns that many have tried to conquer the Kingdom of Oz without succeeding.

records.l: Mogodore's invasion and capture of the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 9
records.s: Mogodore decides to begin his conquest the following morning, ordering Wagarag to rouse his fighting men at daybreak. He plans to cross the Red Mountains, capture the Emerald City, depose Ozma, and use his new position to open the forbidden flagon.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Peter, Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Belfaygor travel toward Baffleburg to confront Mogodore. They cross a deep chasm and scale a steep cliff using Belfaygor's growing beard, then pass through a treacherous tunnel into a courtyard outside the city gates. Baffleburg's tilting towers fire golden spears at them, but Belfaygor enters a tower and lowers his beard so the others can climb inside. The adventurers begin descending a spiral stairway within the tower.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Peter encourages Snif by reminding him that he can think and is free. He crosses the chasm and helps Jack Pumpkinhead survive the dangerous crossing, then leads the group through the tilting tunnel and into the courtyard outside Baffleburg. After climbing Belfaygor's beard into a tower, Peter eagerly begins descending its spiral stairway.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Snif practices his growls and worries about being too small to fight, but he remains cheerful and helps the others. He flies Belfaygor's beard across the chasm, assists in scaling the cliff, rescues Jack's head during the tunnel accident, and later climbs into the Baffleburg tower by flying. Snif initially considers flying over the city walls to open the gates.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead cuts Belfaygor's beard and rakes the clippings into a huge mound. He reluctantly crosses the chasm and follows the others through the dangerous tunnel, where his head comes off and rolls into a hollow before Peter replaces it. He helps climb into the Baffleburg tower but complains about the many steps.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Belfaygor uses his beard as a rope to cross the chasm and scale the cliff. He enters Baffleburg by plunging headfirst through a low tower window while the towers are firing spears, then anchors his beard to the window sill so the others can climb up. He follows Peter down the tower's spiral stairway.

records.l: Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Baffleburg is a fortified city with high gray walls, buttressed towers, wooden-backed gates, and a large bell over the entrance. Its defenses include four towers that tilt downward and shoot golden spears into the courtyard. The adventurers reach a tower inside the city walls but have not yet explored the city itself.

records.l: Belfaygor's beard, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Belfaygor's beard grows long enough to form a swinging cable across the chasm and later serves as a rope for scaling the cliff. It catches on a rock and saves Belfaygor when the tunnel tips, and it then grows down from a Baffleburg tower window so Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif can enter. Belfaygor clips portions of it whenever it is no longer needed.

records.l: the tunnel to Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The tunnel is dark, clammy, and rough underfoot, and it unexpectedly tips downward, throwing the adventurers toward the precipice. On a second attempt, Peter and the others hold onto one another and Peter grips the iron ring until the tunnel rights itself. Peter then opens the wooden door at its end, leading into a cobblestone courtyard.

records.l: the cliff and chasm, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The adventurers must cross a deep chasm and climb a steep rock wall before reaching Baffleburg. The chasm is crossed with Belfaygor's beard, while the cliff is scaled by fastening sections of the beard to trees, boulders, and saplings. They complete both dangerous obstacles without losing any member of the group.

records.l: the tilting-tower spear defense, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Four towers on Baffleburg's walls tilt downward and fire showers of golden spears into the courtyard.
