The adventurers avoid injury by lying flat and crawling close to the walls, but the defense stops after Belfaygor jumps through a tower window. Its interruption leaves a possible route into the city through Belfaygor's beard.

records.l: crossing the chasm, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: Belfaygor grows his beard long enough to stretch across the deep chasm and fastens its ends to trees on opposite sides. Peter crosses by swinging along it, Snif helps rescue Jack when Jack nearly loses his hold, and Belfaygor crosses after clipping his beard close to his chin.

records.l: scaling the cliff, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The group scales the steep cliff by using Belfaygor's beard as a movable rope. Snif flies each section upward and secures it around a sturdy boulder or sapling, after which Belfaygor clips his end and climbs while Peter and Jack follow.

records.l: entering Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 10
records.s: The adventurers pass through the tunnel into a courtyard outside Baffleburg's gates, but the gates do not open when Peter rings the bell. After the spear defense stops, Belfaygor enters a low tower window and lowers his beard so the others can climb inside. They then begin descending the tower's spiral stairway.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Peter, Snif, Belfaygor of Bourne, and Jack Pumpkinhead enter Baffleburg pretending to be magicians so they can be captured and learn where Princess Shirley Sunshine is held. Mogodore recognizes Belfaygor, declares that Shirley will marry him, and orders the travelers imprisoned after their attempted magical tricks fail. Jack Pumpkinhead is beheaded, Peter loses the pirate's sack, and Belfaygor and Peter are locked in separate dungeons. Mogodore then marches toward the Emerald City intending to conquer Oz, marry Shirley, and become its king.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Peter enters Baffleburg with Snif, Belfaygor, and Jack Pumpkinhead, intending to get captured so they can reach Princess Shirley Sunshine. He tries to use the pirate's sack, but a spearman seizes him before he can open it; he is imprisoned in the North tower after dropping the sack. Peter worries that Mogodore will conquer Oz and wishes he could escape to warn Ozma.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Snif flies ahead, rests on Peter's shoulder, and pretends to threaten the mounted men with magic. He helps Peter during the capture attempt, bites and scratches the guards, and remains imprisoned with Peter because he cannot fit through the dungeon bars.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Belfaygor demands that Mogodore reveal what he has done with Princess Shirley Sunshine and declares that she should be released. Mogodore identifies him despite his false whiskers and says Belfaygor will not marry Shirley. Belfaygor is seized and locked in a dungeon higher in the tower.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead confronts Mogodore and claims that Peter and Snif are powerful magicians. He rings the Red Jinn's bell, causing the little slave, Biggen, and Little to disappear, but Mogodore's men capture him. Jack is thrown across the table and beheaded, and his pumpkin head rolls through a curtained doorway.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore, Baron of Baffleburg, is found studying a map of Oz and planning an attack on its capitol. He recognizes Belfaygor, announces that he will marry Princess Shirley Sunshine, orders Peter, Belfaygor, and Jack punished, and begins a march toward the Emerald City. He intends to return as King of Oz.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Princess Shirley Sunshine is being held by Mogodore, who says she is to marry him rather than Belfaygor. Mogodore orders that she be readied while he marches toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Ozma is in the Emerald City and may not know that Mogodore is coming. Peter fears that without warning, Ozma and the Wizard will not have time to begin their magic before Mogodore captures them.

records.l: Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Baffleburg is a steep mountain town with red stone cottages, a narrow cobbled street, and a castle reached through red gates. Its mounted men capture Peter's group and bring them to Mogodore.

records.l: Castle of Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: The castle contains a large baronial hall decorated with jeweled swords and armor. Mogodore uses the hall to study an old map of Oz, confront the travelers, and order their imprisonment in the North tower.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore plans to attack and conquer Oz, believing he can become its king. Peter fears that the Emerald City and its inhabitants will be captured and the whole city destroyed if Ozma is not warned.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore and his forces march toward the Emerald City after leaving Baffleburg. He intends to marry Princess Shirley Sunshine there and be crowned King of Oz before nightfall.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Peter carries the pirate's sack into Mogodore's hall and prepares to open it when the discussion becomes dangerous. A spearman seizes Peter before he can use it, and Peter drops the sack during the struggle.

records.l: Mogodore's invasion and capture of the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore's invasion begins when he sends his forces toward the Emerald City after declaring that he will conquer Oz. Peter believes the city may soon be taken because only one Knight and one soldier are in the palace, and the soldier cannot fight.

records.l: Mogodore's planned marriage to Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore declares that Princess Shirley Sunshine will marry him instead of Belfaygor. He plans to marry her in the capitol after reaching the Emerald City.

records.l: Mogodore's planned coronation, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore boasts that he will be crowned King of Oz before nightfall. He intends to achieve this after conquering the Emerald City and marrying Shirley Sunshine.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead's beheading, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 11
records.s: Mogodore orders Jack Pumpkinhead beheaded after the travelers' supposed magic causes alarm. A guard throws Jack across the table and strikes off his head, sending the pumpkin rolling through a tapestry-curtained door.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Peter and Snif escape their dungeon when the shrinking violets wear off and Snif returns to his full size, freeing Belfaygor from the tower as well. They find Jack's head and the pirate's sack in Mogodore's castle, but Jack tells them about a forbidden flagon guarded beneath the castle. Believing the flagon may destroy Mogodore's power, Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor enter the lost labyrinth while Jack remains behind. They plan to find the enchanted cavern and obtain the flagon before Mogodore reaches the Emerald City and captures it from Ozma.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Peter escapes the dungeon when Snif expands to his former size and tears away the bars. He frees Belfaygor, helps recover Jack's head and the pirate's sack, and reluctantly agrees to search the lost labyrinth for the forbidden flagon before going to the Emerald City.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Snif returns to his full size and strength after the shrinking violets wear off, breaking the dungeon bars and overpowering the guards. He helps Peter and Belfaygor escape Mogodore's castle and joins the search for the forbidden flagon.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Belfaygor is freed from the tower after Peter and Snif reach his cell by following his enchanted beard. He accompanies them through Mogodore's castle and into the lost labyrinth, planning to use his beard to guide them back.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Jack's head is recovered in a cellar after rolling down a spiraling passage. Jack tells Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor about the guarded forbidden flagon and remains behind while they enter the lost labyrinth.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Mogodore has gone to capture the Emerald City and make himself a king. The characters believe that the forbidden flagon may contain something capable of destroying his power.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Ozma is in danger because Mogodore is going to the Emerald City to capture it. Peter and his companions intend to warn or save her.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The Emerald City is Mogodore's intended target, and he plans to capture it and make himself king. Peter, Snif, Belfaygor, and Jack discuss flying there to warn Ozma, but first decide to seek the forbidden flagon.

records.l: Mogodore's castle, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor escape from the dungeons of Mogodore's castle. They search the castle for Jack's head and the pirate's sack, then discover a passage leading downward toward the lost labyrinth.

records.l: tower (in Mogodore's castle), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The tower contains the dungeon where Snif and Peter are imprisoned and the higher cell where Belfaygor is held. Snif's return to full size breaks the dungeon bars, allowing the prisoners to escape.

records.l: lost labyrinth, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The lost labyrinth lies below the castle and leads toward the enchanted cavern. Jack says that travelers must turn left at every opportunity, and Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor enter it to search for the forbidden flagon.

records.l: enchanted cavern, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The enchanted cavern is reached through the lost labyrinth and contains the forbidden flagon. Guards say that only someone who knows the tricks of the labyrinth can find it.

records.l: shrinking violets, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The effect of the shrinking violets finally wears off, causing Snif to expand rapidly to his former size and strength. His expansion tears the dungeon door from its hinges and bends the bars outward.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Snif finds the pirate's sack behind a screen in Mogodore's castle. Peter takes it from Snif before they slide down the passage in search of Jack's head.

records.l: Jack's head, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Jack's head rolls down a sloping, spiraling passage and is found in a dark cellar. Peter retrieves it and carries it back to Jack's body, but Jack stays behind while the others seek the forbidden flagon.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The forbidden flagon is guarded in or near the enchanted cavern beyond the lost labyrinth. Jack learns from overheard guards that one tip of it may be important in opposing Mogodore, so Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor go to find it.

records.l: the escape from the tower, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The escape from the tower begins when Snif regains his full size and breaks through the dungeon bars. Peter frees himself and Snif, and they then release Belfaygor before searching the castle for Jack's head and the pirate's sack.

records.l: Mogodore's invasion and capture of the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: Mogodore's attack on the Emerald City is imminent: he has gone to capture the city and make himself king. Peter and his companions consider flying there immediately, but delay in order to seek the forbidden flagon.

records.l: the forbidden flagon's power to destroy Mogodore's power, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 12
records.s: The forbidden flagon's power is not explained directly. Jack infers from an armed guard's conversation and gesture that one tip of the flagon may contain something capable of destroying Mogodore's power.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor follow the labyrinth to an enchanted cavern, where magic mirrors make them believe it is filled with Ugly Muglies. They find the Forbidden Flagon in a fire fountain and retrieve it using a piece of Belfaygor's beard, after which they return through the labyrinth. Back at Mogodore's palace, they reunite Jack's Pumpkinhead with his body and prepare to leave with the flagon, the pirate's sack, the dinner bell, and the sauce box. They then depart toward the Emerald City on Snif's back.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Peter follows Belfaygor through the labyrinth and helps discover that the apparent Ugly Muglies are reflections in magic mirrors. He retrieves the Forbidden Flagon by using a piece of Belfaygor's beard to knock it from the fire fountain, then carries it back to Mogodore's palace. He reunites Jack's Pumpkinhead with his body and prepares to travel toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Snif panics at the apparent Ugly Muglies and charges into the magic mirrors, discovering that the monsters are only reflections. He helps Peter and Belfaygor return with the Forbidden Flagon, joins Jack and Peter for the departure, and nearly chokes after swallowing a geranium when the sauce box threatens them.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Belfaygor leads Peter and Snif through the labyrinth by always turning left, then captures the enchanted cavern's guard by wrapping him in his red beard. He gives Peter his shears so a piece of the beard can pull the Forbidden Flagon from the fire fountain. Afterward, he cuts his beard shorter and travels with the others toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Jack's Pumpkinhead waits above the cellarway and welcomes Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor when they return with the Forbidden Flagon. Peter places Jack's head back on his body, and Jack dances before preparing to leave with the group. He carries the dinner bell and rides on Snif's back.

records.l: Ugly Muglies, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The Ugly Muglies appear to surround the enchanted cavern and frighten Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor. They are revealed to be distorted reflections created by the magic mirrors rather than actual creatures.

records.l: enchanted cavern, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The enchanted cavern contains walls made of magic mirrors and an opening into a smaller grotto. The smaller cave holds the Forbidden Flagon in a fire fountain, guarded by a sleeping guard. Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor retrieve the flagon and leave through the labyrinth.

records.l: lost labyrinth, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The labyrinth lies at the foot of the ladder and branches repeatedly into multiple tunnels. Belfaygor leads the group into the enchanted cavern by always turning left, and they return by turning right until reaching the ladder and cellarway.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The group plans to carry the Forbidden Flagon to the Emerald City. Peter says they are close to reaching it when they leave Mogodore's palace.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The Forbidden Flagon is a small black flask hidden in the middle of a fountain of fire. Its label says that each successive Baron of Baffleburg must guard it and that breaking its seal or spilling its red contents will bring woe to Baffleburg and disaster to the person responsible. Peter retrieves it, carries it back to the palace, and keeps it in his pocket.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Peter opens the pirate's sack when the group first sees the apparent Ugly Muglies, but it cannot swallow them because they are only reflections. He closes the sack and carries it with him when the group leaves the palace.

records.l: magic mirrors, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The walls of the enchanted cavern are magic mirrors that multiply and distort the people standing before them. They create the illusion of fifty frightening Ugly Muglies and cause Snif to knock himself down.

records.l: fire fountain, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The fire fountain rises from the center of a deep green grotto and contains the Forbidden Flagon in its flames. Peter tests it with paper and learns that the fire is real. Using Belfaygor's beard, Peter and Belfaygor knock the flagon from its stand and let it roll into a dark corner.

records.l: guard (enchanted cavern), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The guard sleeps beside the fire fountain until Peter enters the grotto. Belfaygor seizes the guard's spear, wraps the guard in his beard, and drags him out of the way, leaving him helpless and still bound when the group departs.

records.l: sauce box, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The sauce box suddenly speaks in a threatening voice, warning the group that they will be boiled, stewed, or fried. A hunting dog carries it to Peter, who closes its lid and stops the threats. Jack advises them to take it along because it may frighten others.

records.l: Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: Jack checks that the famous dinner bell is safe before the group leaves Mogodore's palace. It remains one of the magical objects they carry with them.

records.l: rescue of Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 13
records.s: The rescue mission involves Peter, Snif, Belfaygor, and Jack's Pumpkinhead retrieving the Forbidden Flagon and reuniting Jack's head with his body. After completing these tasks, they prepare to leave Mogodore's palace and continue toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Peter, Belfaygor, Snif, and Jack Pumpkinhead travel toward the Emerald City on Snif while carrying the pirate's sack, the forbidden flagon, and Mogodore's magic bell. They are intercepted in Swing City, where Hi-Swinger, Tip Toppsy the Tenth, and the Swingers toss them among the swings and trapezes. Mogodore's sauce box falls from Peter's pocket and frightens the Swingers into dropping them into a safety net. The travelers escape to the ground with the sack, flagon, and bell still in their possession, then continue pursuing Mogodore.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Peter travels with Belfaygor, Snif, and Jack Pumpkinhead toward the Emerald City. In Swing City, the Swingers toss him between swings and trapezes until Mogodore's sauce box falls from his pocket and causes them to drop him into a net. He helps Jack recover and continues the pursuit of Mogodore with the pirate's sack, flagon, and magic bell.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Belfaygor wants to attack Mogodore before the pirate's sack is opened and hopes the Wizard of Oz can repair his growing beard. In Swing City, the Swingers stretch his beard between swings and use it as a tightrope, while he is held by the citizens. After escaping, he cuts a hole in the net and follows the others to the ground.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Snif carries Peter and the others toward the capitol and provides them with food during the flight. In Swing City, he tries to rescue Peter and Belfaygor but is buffeted by the aerialists, and he later catches Jack's head as it falls. He helps the group escape the net and resumes the journey.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead travels with Peter, Belfaygor, and Snif and jokes about opening the sack and using the forbidden objects against Mogodore. In Swing City, the acrobats toss his head around like a ball, and he later needs help placing it back on his body. He escapes the net and continues toward the Emerald City.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Mogodore is the baron whom Peter and his companions are pursuing toward the Emerald City. His bodyguards, Biggen and Little, deliver dinner in the air, and he possesses the sauce box that falls from Peter's pocket during the struggle in Swing City.

records.l: Hi-Swinger, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Hi-Swinger is the king and highest Swinger of Swing City. He catches and tosses Peter, introduces him to Tip Toppsy the Tenth, and orders the Swingers to drop Peter and his companions when the sauce box frightens them.

records.l: Tip Toppsy the Tenth, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Tip Toppsy the Tenth is the queen of Swing City. She catches Peter in midair, swings him gently, fusses over his appearance, and discusses dressing him in pink or blue.

records.l: Swing City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: Swing City is a strange aerial city filled with swings, trapezes, ropes, and citizens who move through the air. Its people seize Peter and his companions and subject them to dangerous acrobatic tossing before dropping them into a large net beneath the city.

records.l: Swingers, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The Swingers are the aerial citizens of Swing City. They toss Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the others from swing to swing, stretch Belfaygor's beard into a tightrope, and are frightened into releasing their captives by the screams from Mogodore's sauce box.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The pirate's sack remains in Peter and his companions' possession throughout the events in Swing City. Peter still intends to open it when they reach Mogodore.

records.l: sauce box, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 14
records.s: The sauce box belongs to Mogodore and falls from Peter's pocket during the struggle in Swing City. When it opens, its screams, threats, and brazen screeches frighten the Swingers and enable Peter and his companions to escape, although the sauce box is lost afterward.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, Belfaygor, and Snif pursue Mogodore and his army after escaping Swing City's net. When Peter tries to open the pirate's sack over Mogodore, a gust of wind carries it upward and then sends it falling onto the rescuers, capturing Peter and Belfaygor while Snif disappears into it. Jack escapes the sack's fall with the flagon but breaks his wooden leg, retrieves the sack, and tries to summon help with the Red Jinn's bell. The summoned slave vanishes, and Jack disappears with him, leaving the pink hay field empty.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Peter travels with Jack Pumpkinhead, Belfaygor, and Snif to intercept Mogodore. He unties the pirate's sack and tries to hold it over Mogodore's army, but a gust of wind carries it away before it captures the enemy. The falling sack captures Peter and Belfaygor.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead escapes the falling pirate's sack by diving to earth with the flagon, but his wooden left leg breaks off at the knee. Believing Peter, Belfaygor, and Snif are trapped in the sack, he retrieves it and resolves to take it to the Wizard of Oz. He summons the Red Jinn's slave with the silver bell, but vanishes when the slave disappears.

records.l: Belfaygor, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Belfaygor travels with Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Snif while pursuing Mogodore. He urges Peter to throw the flagon, but the falling pirate's sack captures him along with Peter.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Snif flies Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Belfaygor toward Mogodore and identifies Mogodore and his men below. He warns the others when the pirate's sack flies toward them. Snif disappears into the fathomless depths of the sack.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Mogodore rides out of a forest with his army, and Peter's group attempts to intercept him. He escapes when the pirate's sack misses him and falls onto the rescuers. Jack believes Mogodore will march to the capitol, enslave the inhabitants, and seize the magic treasures.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The Emerald City is threatened by Mogodore, who Jack believes will march to its capitol and attack its unsuspecting inhabitants.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The fate of the Kingdom of Oz depends on Jack Pumpkinhead after Peter, Belfaygor, and Snif are captured or lost and Mogodore escapes.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Peter unties the pirate's sack and prepares to open it over Mogodore's army. A gust of wind tears it from his hands, sends it upward, and then brings it crashing down onto Peter, Belfaygor, and Snif. Jack retrieves the sack and intends to take it to the Wizard of Oz.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: Peter is about to give the flagon to Belfaygor when Snif warns that the pirate's sack is approaching. Jack snatches the flagon and dives from Snif, keeping hold of it during the fall. He later places it in his coat pocket.

records.l: the sack's fall, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: The pirate's sack, blown upward like a balloon, comes hurling down with its mouth open after Mogodore's army clears the area. It captures Peter, Belfaygor, and Snif, while Jack escapes by jumping away. The sack settles against a pink hay stack.

records.l: Jack's disappearance, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 15
records.s: After ringing the Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead seizes the summoned slave and begs it to help him. The slave vanishes, and Jack vanishes as well, leaving only a pink rabbit in the hay field.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead arrives at the glittering red glass Palace of the Red Jinn after being carried by the magic dinner bell. The Red Jinn laughs at Jack's appearance but repairs his broken leg and listens to his account of the pirate's sack, which contains the little boy, the baron, and the flying red monster. The Red Jinn begins devising a rescue and return to Oz, but Jack suddenly vanishes through another magic before the plan can be carried out.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead arrives at the Palace of the Red Jinn carrying his broken leg under his arm and is struck on the head by visitors as part of their greeting custom. He asks the Red Jinn for help rescuing his friends and saving Oz, and the Red Jinn magically restores his leg. Jack then suddenly disappears from the palace before he can be sent back to Oz.

records.l: the Red Jinn, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The Red Jinn rules the red glass palace and initially treats Jack Pumpkinhead as a source of amusement. After hearing Jack's story, he repairs Jack's broken leg and considers using his magic looking-glass, umbrella, and Jinrickasha to help rescue the prisoners and return Jack to Oz. He becomes frustrated when Jack vanishes through magic not caused by him.

records.l: Ginger, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Ginger, the little black slave of the bell, escorts Jack Pumpkinhead into the Red Jinn's palace and explains the local greeting custom. He encourages Jack to speak to the Red Jinn and is present when Jack suddenly vanishes.

records.l: Palace of the Red Jinn, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The Palace of the Red Jinn is a glittering red glass palace beside a green glass sea with a dangerous beach of glass splinters. Its throne room contains red glass furnishings, musical glass curtains, incense, and the Red Jinn's glass throne.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Oz is Jack Pumpkinhead's country, which Jack says is in danger of destruction. Jack seeks the Red Jinn's help in returning there and protecting it.

records.l: Red Jinn's bell, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The magic dinner bell brought Jack Pumpkinhead to the Palace of the Red Jinn. Although the bell belongs to the Red Jinn, he does not want it returned and says that its theft has connected him with the outside world and brought him two extra slaves.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The pirate's sack contains the little boy, the baron, and the flying red monster. Jack shows the sack to the Red Jinn and asks for help releasing its prisoners.

records.l: little boy (inside the pirate's sack), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The little boy is one of the prisoners inside the pirate's sack. Jack asks the Red Jinn to help release him.

records.l: Belfaygor of Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The baron is one of the prisoners inside the pirate's sack. Jack asks the Red Jinn to help release him.

records.l: flying red monster (inside the pirate's sack), Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: The flying red monster is one of the prisoners inside the pirate's sack. Jack asks the Red Jinn to help release it.

records.l: Jack's arrival at the Red Jinn's palace, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Jack's arrival occurs after about three whirls and one spiral, bringing him to the steps of the glittering red glass palace. Ginger guides him inside while Jack carries his broken leg under his arm.

records.l: Jack's disappearance from the palace, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 16
records.s: Jack disappears suddenly just as the Red Jinn is arranging to send him to Oz in the Jinrickasha. The Red Jinn says the disappearance was caused by meddlesome magic rather than his own magic, and its source is not identified.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Mogodore arrives in the Emerald City with his army and captures the city and Ozma's palace while Ozma and her companions are playing blind-man's buff. His soldiers bind Ozma, Dorothy, Scraps, and the other celebrities and courtiers, while Mogodore declares himself the future King of Oz and announces his intention to marry Ozma. Betsy Bobbin hides in a butterfly bush and considers reaching the magic belt, but Mogodore finds it first. When Mogodore uses the belt to transform Scraps into a bird, Scraps escapes with Ozma's crown and flies away to spread the alarm.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Ozma plays blind-man's buff with her friends and courtiers in the garden of Ozma's palace. Mogodore's soldiers capture and bind her to a tree, but she remains composed, tells her people to be patient and brave, and warns Mogodore that her Wizard and Army will destroy him. Mogodore declares that he intends to marry her.

records.l: Dorothy, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Dorothy plays blind-man's buff in the garden and is captured and tied to a tree by Mogodore's soldiers. She worries that the magic belt may be found and tries to reassure the Scarecrow while they are prisoners.

records.l: Betsy Bobbin, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Betsy Bobbin hides in the center of an enormous butterfly bush during the game. She discovers that Mogodore's army has captured the others and considers slipping out to get the magic belt, but ultimately remains hidden in the bush.

records.l: Scraps, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Scraps is captured and chained to a tree with the other inhabitants of the palace. When Mogodore uses the magic belt to command her to become a bird, she changes into a patchwork bird, escapes her chains, steals Ozma's crown, and flies away to spread the alarm.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Mogodore leads his army into the Emerald City and captures it with little opposition. He binds Ozma and her companions, claims he will be King of Oz, and announces that he will marry Ozma. After finding the magic belt, he transforms Scraps into a bird, but becomes confused when she escapes with Ozma's crown and retreats into the castle.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Oz is the country Mogodore seeks to rule after capturing its capital. Mogodore proclaims himself the future King of Oz and boasts that the magic belt could enable him to destroy the entire country.

records.l: Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: The Emerald City is captured by Mogodore's forces, causing its peaceful inhabitants to flee into their houses. Mogodore leaves five hundred soldiers to hold the city while he leads another five hundred against Ozma's palace.

records.l: Ozma's palace, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Ozma's palace has a garden where Ozma, Dorothy, Betsy, Scraps, and the other residents gather for games. Mogodore's soldiers storm the palace, overpower its servants, search it for the magic belt, and occupy it after capturing the garden.

records.l: Mogodore's invasion and capture of the Emerald City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Mogodore's invasion captures the Emerald City without opposition because the city has no visible defenses, army, or guards. His forces seize the palace, bind Ozma and the celebrities, imprison the servants, and leave soldiers to control the city.

records.l: magic belt, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: The magic belt has the power to transform anyone into any shape. Mogodore finds it in the palace and fastens it around his arm because it is too small for his waist, then uses it to transform Scraps into a bird.

records.l: Mogodore's army, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: Mogodore's army enters the Emerald City and drives its inhabitants into their homes. Five hundred soldiers remain to hold the city, while five hundred accompany Mogodore to attack the palace; they capture and chain the palace's inhabitants and imprison its servants.

records.l: transformation magic, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 17
records.s: The transformation magic of the belt can change a person into any desired shape. Mogodore uses it successfully to turn Scraps into a bird, although he is too inexperienced to stop her from escaping.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore forces Ozma to join him at a feast and declares that he intends to marry her and rule Oz. While the prisoners remain guarded outside, Mogodore tries to use the magic belt to bring the forbidden flagon to the castle. Jack Pumpkinhead arrives with the flagon, breaks it against Mogodore's nose, and releases its thin red liquid. Ozma hopes that Scraps and Glinda will come to her aid.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore brings Ozma to the banquet and announces that he has chosen to marry her instead of Shirley Sunshine. He claims to be King of Oz by seizure and conquest, refuses to marry until he is ready, and commands the forbidden flagon to appear. Jack Pumpkinhead then breaks the flagon against Mogodore's nose, causing its red liquid to run down his face.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Ozma is released from her chains and escorted into the banquet hall, where Mogodore forces her to sit beside him and declares that she will be his bride. She is frightened and distressed by the soldiers' behavior, hopes Scraps and Glinda will help, and rushes forward when Jack Pumpkinhead appears.

records.l: Scraps, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Scraps is free, and Ozma tells Trot that Scraps will find a way to help them. Ozma hopes that Scraps has reached Glinda's castle, but no assistance arrives during the feast.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead arrives through a window, carried to the castle by the magic belt while holding the forbidden flagon. He removes his head, sets it on a chair, and throws the flagon at Mogodore, breaking it against the baron's nose.

records.l: spearmen, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The spearmen guard the prisoners, escort Ozma into the palace, and celebrate Mogodore's intended marriage. They complain that the conflict has brought them no hangings, bonfires, or killings, and urge Mogodore to marry Ozma so they can resume killing.

records.l: prisoners, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The prisoners remain tied in the garden while food is served to the soldiers and none is offered to them. They wait in fear for Mogodore's next move, while Betsy Bobbin remains hidden in a butterfly bush without an opportunity to escape.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore claims that he is already King of Oz by right of seizure and conquest. Wagarag insists that he will not be the lawful King until he marries Ozma.

records.l: magic belt, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: The magic belt carries Jack Pumpkinhead and the forbidden flagon from the Red Jinn's palace to Mogodore's castle.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore commands the forbidden flagon and its guard to appear before him. The flagon arrives in Jack Pumpkinhead's hand and is shattered against Mogodore's nose, releasing a thin red liquid and revealing what happens when its seal is broken.

records.l: Mogodore's planned wedding to Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore announces that he intends to marry Ozma, but he refuses to hold the wedding immediately. His spearmen urge him to marry her at once so they can continue with the killings.

records.l: forbidden flagon's mystery, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 18
records.s: Mogodore wants to discover what is inside the forbidden flagon and why it is forbidden. When Jack Pumpkinhead breaks its seal, a thin red liquid pours over Mogodore, and the event answers the question of what will happen.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead returns to the banquet hall and uses the forbidden flagon to shrink Mogodore the Mighty and his midget followers. Toto drives the frightened invaders into a corner while Ozma, Jack, and Shirley Sunshine realize the others imprisoned in the garden must be freed. Scraps reaches Glinda the Good, who releases the captives, and the company returns to the hall. Ozma is restored to her place, the prisoners are guarded, and Jack prepares to explain what happened and release three enchanted comrades.

records.l: The Forbidden Flagon Acts, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The forbidden flagon shrinks Mogodore the Mighty and his band of invaders. Its use allows Jack Pumpkinhead to rescue Ozma and the others from the invasion.

records.l: banquet hall, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The banquet hall becomes quiet and seemingly deserted while the invaders shrink and hide under tables and chairs. After the captives are freed, the company returns there, restores Ozma to her place, and gathers to hear Jack Pumpkinhead's account.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Ozma is rescued after the forbidden flagon shrinks Mogodore and his followers. Betsy fastens the magic belt around her waist, Scraps places the emerald crown on her head, and the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman conduct her back to her rightful place at the head of the table.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead returns in time to use the forbidden flagon against Mogodore the Mighty and his forces. He explains that he must tell a long story, then prepares to release three brave comrades from enchantment by following the Red Jinn's advice.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Mogodore the Mighty is shrunk by the forbidden flagon along with his retainers. He tries to quiet his frightened followers, flees from Toto, and is guarded as a prisoner by the Soldier with the Green Whiskers.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The forbidden flagon shrinks Mogodore the Mighty and the men serving him. Jack Pumpkinhead identifies it as the cause of the invaders' sudden reduction.

records.l: Scraps, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Scraps is immediately restored to her cheerful self by Glinda the Good. She reaches Glinda's castle, helping bring Glinda to the rescue, and later places the emerald crown on Ozma's head.

records.l: Glinda, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Glinda the Good comes after Scraps reaches her castle and releases the company imprisoned in the garden. She arrives in her red robes and head-dress, ready to use her strongest magic.

records.l: Dorothy, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: Dorothy returns to the banquet hall with the rescued company and asks Ozma what happened. She reports that the spearmen in the garden suddenly disappeared and asks how Mogodore became so tiny.

records.l: garden, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 19
records.s: The garden holds the imprisoned company and the spearmen during the invasion. The captives are released after Scraps reaches Glinda the Good, and the spearmen suddenly disappear.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor arrive at Ozma's banquet after Jack Pumpkinhead shakes the pirate sack, but the sack first releases a horde of Scares that attack the banquet. Ozma commands the Scares to return to Scare City, and Jack explains how he, Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor escaped their adventures involving the forbidden flagon, Baffleburg, and the sack. The rescuers are celebrated for saving the Kingdom of Oz, while Mogodore and his tiny army are captured. The company then holds a wedding feast for Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine, and celebrates until daybreak.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Ozma commands the Scares to return to Scare City, and they obey at once. After hearing the rescuers' story, she declares that Jack Pumpkinhead, Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor have saved the Kingdom of Oz.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead shakes the pirate sack to release its prisoners, accidentally filling the banquet room with Scares before shaking it again and producing Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor. He explains that the Red Jinn advised him to remove his head before throwing the forbidden flagon and to turn the sack inside out and shake it three times.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Peter emerges from the pirate sack with Snif and Belfaygor and identifies the intruders as Scares. He helps the Oz folk understand what has happened and is celebrated as one of the four rescuers who saved the Kingdom of Oz.

records.l: Snif, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Snif, an Iffin or Griffin, emerges from the pirate sack with Peter and Belfaygor and helps fight the Scares. He participates in the celebration, entertains the company with Scraps through rhymes, and is given eight geranium plants and an Easter lily.

records.l: Belfaygor of Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Belfaygor emerges from the pirate sack after being reduced to a midget by the forbidden flagon, and his enchanted beard has disappeared into the sack. He is reunited with Shirley Sunshine, marries her at the wedding feast, and is toasted and showered with gifts.

records.l: Shirley Sunshine, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Shirley Sunshine arrives with Belfaygor after he has escaped his adventures. She is introduced to the company and marries Belfaygor during the wedding feast.

records.l: Mogodore, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Mogodore and his men remain captured in the banquet hall after being reduced to midgets by the forbidden flagon. They are later locked in the pantry for safety along with the rest of the tiny army.

records.l: Scare City, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Scare City is the place to which Ozma sends the Scares after they attack the banquet. The Scares return there immediately on Ozma's command.

records.l: Baffleburg, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Baffleburg is part of the route in Jack Pumpkinhead's account of the journey from Scare City to Baffleburg and then to Swing City. The story also concerns Belfaygor's escape from Baffleburg.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Oz celebrates the return of Peter and the arrival of the rescuers with a wedding feast. The rescuers are praised for saving the Kingdom of Oz, and Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine's wedding is solemnized by the highest judge in Ozma's court.

records.l: Emerald City's inhabitants, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Oz folk initially fight the Scares and then listen closely as Jack explains the strange events. They celebrate Peter's return, honor the rescuers, and enjoy the wedding feast until daybreak.

records.l: Scares, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Scares spill from the pirate sack and attack the banquet hall, frightening and struggling with the Oz folk. Ozma commands them to return to Scare City, and they all obey.

records.l: pirate's sack, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The pirate sack swallows Peter, Snif, Belfaygor, and others during the adventure. Jack turns it inside out and shakes it three times, releasing Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor but initially unleashing the Scares as well.

records.l: Forbidden Flagon, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The forbidden flagon reduces Mogodore, his men, and Belfaygor to midgets after its seal is broken. The Red Jinn tells Jack that removing his head before throwing it will avoid the disaster promised by its label.

records.l: the wedding feast, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Dorothy proposes that the dinner become a wedding feast for Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine. It becomes a merry celebration with food, music, rhymes, gifts, emeralds, and Ozade.

records.l: Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine's wedding, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Belfaygor and Shirley Sunshine's wedding is solemnized by the highest judge in Ozma's court during the feast. They are toasted in tall tumblers of Ozade and showered with emeralds and other gifts.

records.l: the Scares' attack on the banquet, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: The Scares' attack begins when Jack shakes the pirate sack and fills the banquet room with screaming, groaning, and struggling Scares. The Oz folk try to protect Ozma, but Ozma ends the attack by commanding the Scares to return to Scare City.

records.l: the rescue of the Kingdom of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 20
records.s: Jack Pumpkinhead, Peter, Snif, and Belfaygor are credited with saving the Kingdom of Oz. Ozma announces their achievement, and the company responds with cheers.

records.l: Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peter spends the day in Oz before asking Ozma to send him back to Philadelphia. Glinda explains that Mogodore and his followers were reddies whose great size had been sustained by the red liquid in the forbidden flagon, and Ozma sends them back to their now-tiny city. Peter returns to his grandfather, tells him about his adventures in Oz, and becomes convinced that his grandfather is his best chum and bravest adventurer. His grandfather agrees that they should try flying together.

records.l: Peter, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peter says goodbye to his friends in Oz and asks Ozma to send him back to Philadelphia because his companions and grandfather depend on him. After returning home, he excitedly tells his grandfather about flying and all that happened in Baffleburg and elsewhere in Oz.

records.l: Ozma, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Ozma explains that Mogodore and his followers are now too small to harm anyone and sends them back to their tiny red city in Baffleburg. She says goodbye to Peter and invites him to return to Oz soon and often.

records.l: Peter's grandfather, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peter's grandfather calmly accepts Peter's account of having been to Oz and agrees that they should try flying together. Peter decides that his grandfather is his best chum and bravest adventurer.

records.l: Philadelphia, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Philadelphia is Peter's home, where he returns after asking Ozma to send him back from Oz. He arrives in the dim library of his own house.

records.l: Oz, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Oz is where Peter spends the day with his friends before returning home. The Wizard's magic releases the Fraid Cats and Statues from Scare City, while Ozma sends Mogodore and his followers back to Baffleburg and Peter back to Philadelphia.

records.l: Peter's return to Philadelphia, Jack Pumpkinhead of Oz, CHAPTER 21
records.s: Peter's return to Philadelphia takes place when Ozma uses her magic belt to send him home. He appears in the dim library of his house and immediately tells his grandfather about his latest adventures in Oz.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: The Yellow Knight of Oz is a 1930 book by Ruth Plumly Thompson, founded on and continuing the Oz stories by L. Frank Baum and illustrated by John R. Neill. Its introduction announces a quest by Sir Hokus of Pokes involving a strange Yellow Knight and his horse, Stampedro. The contents list adventures involving Queen Marcia, Ploppa, a camel, Tuzzle, a golden princess, and the restoration of Corumbia, culminating in the Yellow Knight's return and the marriage of Marygolden.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: The Yellow Knight of Oz is a 1930 book by Ruth Plumly Thompson, illustrated by John R. Neill and published by The Reilly & Lee Co. It continues the famous Oz stories by L. Frank Baum and tells of the quest of Sir Hokus of Pokes, a strange Yellow Knight, and Stampedro.

records.l: Ruth Plumly Thompson, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: Ruth Plumly Thompson wrote The Yellow Knight of Oz in 1930. In her introductory poem, she invites readers to enjoy the tale of Sir Hokus of Pokes, the Yellow Knight, Stampedro, and their adventures.

records.l: Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: Oz is the setting and continuing story-world identified in the book's title and subtitle. The book is presented as continuing the famous Oz stories by L. Frank Baum.

records.l: Sir Hokus of Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: Sir Hokus of Pokes undertakes a quest that is announced in the introductory poem and listed in the contents. His adventures include meeting the Yellow Knight, escaping with Ploppa, and encountering an old friend.

records.l: Yellow Knight, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: The Yellow Knight is described as strange and is central to the book's announced tale. The contents include his return and a later event concerning the hand of a princess.

records.l: Stampedro, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: Stampedro is the horse of the Yellow Knight. He is named in the introductory poem as part of the adventures told in the book.

records.l: Sir Hokus's quest, The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz
records.s: Sir Hokus's quest is the main adventure announced for The Yellow Knight of Oz. It involves a strange Yellow Knight, Stampedro, a wicked old Shah, and a princess.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Sir Hokus of Pokes announces that he intends to go on a quest, and Dorothy agrees to accompany him on Monday. Scraps spreads the news, causing nearly everyone in the Emerald City and Ozma's palace to prepare to join the adventure. Overwhelmed by the prospect of traveling with an entire army, Sir Hokus secretly leaves the palace at night with his battle-axe and second-best helmet. The nature of the quest has not yet been revealed.

records.l: Sir Hokus of Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Sir Hokus announces his intention to go on a quest. He becomes distressed when the people and animals of the Emerald City prepare to accompany him, fearing that such a large group will prevent him from rescuing a damsel, slaying a dragon, or challenging a giant. Three days before the planned departure, he secretly leaves the palace at night carrying his battle-axe and second-best helmet.

records.l: Scraps, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Scraps enthusiastically questions Sir Hokus about his quest and says that she will go with him. She spreads the news throughout the castle, prompting widespread preparations for the adventure.

records.l: Dorothy, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Dorothy is spending the evening with Sir Hokus and others in her apartment and agrees to accompany him on the quest on Monday. She warns Scraps not to damage the furniture while celebrating and later discusses preparations for the journey.

records.l: Ozma, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Ozma is described as the powerful and important fairy ruler of Oz, governing its four countries wisely and keeping its people contented and happy. Her palace houses many celebrated subjects, including Dorothy, Bettsy, and Trot, and Ozma's people become involved in the preparations for Sir Hokus's quest.

records.l: Emerald City, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: The Emerald City is described as a sparkling capital whose streets, towers, and castle shine with emeralds. News of Sir Hokus's quest spreads quickly through the city, and its courtiers, servants, animals, and other residents prepare to accompany him.

records.l: Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Oz is described as a happy, informal, and magical kingdom ruled by Ozma. It contains four great countries and many unusual inhabitants, including wizards, witches, fabulous monsters, talking animals, and celebrated subjects who live or gather in the Emerald City.

records.l: Ozma's palace, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: Ozma's palace is the setting for the evening gathering where Sir Hokus announces his plan. Its residents quickly learn about the quest, and courtiers, servants, animals, and other inhabitants begin preparing to join it.

records.l: Sir Hokus's quest, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER ONE
records.s: The quest is planned to begin on Monday, with Dorothy accompanying Sir Hokus. Its purpose and destination remain unspecified, though Sir Hokus imagines that it might involve rescuing a damsel, slaying a dragon, or challenging a giant.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Sir Hokus leaves the Emerald City and travels east toward the Winkie Country to learn more about his lost past. After an unhelpful encounter with a night owl, he meets Getsom and Gotsom, Mud Guards of Queen Marcia of Marshland, who offer him kingship and marriage to their one-eyed queen. Sir Hokus refuses, escapes into a dangerous marsh, and is nearly dragged under by frog goblins. A giant mud turtle named Ploppa rescues him and carries him across the swamp.

records.l: Sir Hokus of Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Sir Hokus travels east from the Emerald City into the Winkie Country, hoping to learn about his forgotten history. He refuses an offer to marry Queen Marcia and become monarch, escapes from Getsom and Gotsom, fights frog goblins in a marsh, and is carried to safety by Ploppa.

records.l: Winkie Country, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: The Winkie Country lies east of the Emerald City and is ruled by the Tin Woodman. Sir Hokus chooses to travel there because Dorothy first discovered him in that country and he hopes to learn about his former history.

records.l: Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Sir Hokus was imprisoned in Pokes for five centuries after a black Knight transported him there. He escaped from Pokes with Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion, but remembers little of his earlier life.

records.l: the Knight's first adventure, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: The Knight's first adventure in this unit begins when Sir Hokus leaves the Emerald City seeking a maiden, monarch, or monster to assist or fight. It leads him through a forest and into Marshland, where he battles frog goblins and is rescued by a giant mud turtle.

records.l: Sir Hokus's quest, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Sir Hokus's quest is to find adventure, including a distressed maiden, a monarch in need, or a dangerous monster. He also hopes his journey east will reveal something about his lost identity and early history.

records.l: monster, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Sir Hokus expects to find a monster to fight and identifies the giant mud turtle as one when it approaches him in the swamp. The turtle does not attack him and instead treats him as a fellow turtle man.

records.l: Marshland, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Marshland is a wild, desolate swamp reached after the forest. Its treacherous bog nearly swallows Sir Hokus, and it is ruled by Queen Marcia.

records.l: Getsom, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Getsom is one of Queen Marcia's Mud Guards. He and Gotsom stop Sir Hokus, explain that the queen has sworn to marry the first stranger entering the kingdom, and are knocked unconscious when they try to seize him.

records.l: Gotsom, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Gotsom is one of Queen Marcia's Mud Guards and warns Getsom to treat Sir Hokus carefully because he believes Sir Hokus is the King. He offers Sir Hokus marriage to Queen Marcia and is felled by Sir Hokus's battle-axe.

records.l: Mud Guards, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: The Mud Guards are Getsom and Gotsom, servants of Queen Marcia of Marshland. They are covered in mud, wear swamp grass skirts, and attempt to take Sir Hokus to their queen after offering him kingship.

records.l: Queen Marcia, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Queen Marcia rules Marshland and has sworn to marry the first stranger who enters her kingdom. Getsom says that she has one wonderful eye, while Sir Hokus refuses the proposed marriage.

records.l: frog goblins, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Frog goblins rise from bubbles in the marsh and try to pull Sir Hokus into the mire. He strikes at them with his sword, but they attack in such numbers that he is nearly overwhelmed before they suddenly dive away.

records.l: giant mud turtle, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: The giant mud turtle appears after the frog goblins disappear and is as large as an elephant flattened out. It mistakes Sir Hokus for a fellow turtle man, offers him food, and carries him through the marsh.

records.l: Ploppa, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: Ploppa is the giant mud turtle that rescues Sir Hokus from the marsh. Sir Hokus climbs onto Ploppa's shell and tells it to proceed toward the edge of the swamp.

records.l: marsh, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER TWO
records.s: The marsh is filled with deep, watery mud that traps Sir Hokus up to his waist and threatens to swallow him. Frog goblins attack him there, but a giant mud turtle carries him onward.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Sir Hokus and Ploppa travel through Marshland, where the Marshlanders use stilts and live in mud-thatched houses high in the trees. They arrive at the Royal Hut of Queen Marcia, whose Mud Guards seize Sir Hokus and proclaim him King. Queen Marcia declares that she will marry Sir Hokus, while her sister Mira also claims him. Sir Hokus eats the royal duck, is locked in a room, and escapes through a barred window with Ploppa's help beginning to take shape.

records.l: Sir Hokus of Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Sir Hokus rides cross-legged on Ploppa through Marshland and studies the Marshlanders, their houses, and their use of stilts. He is captured by Queen Marcia's Mud Guards, is declared King, and is told he must marry the Queen. After eating the royal duck, he calls to Ploppa from his locked room and asks him to break the window bars so they can escape.

records.l: Ploppa, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Ploppa carries Sir Hokus through the marsh and explains that the Stick-in-the-Muds use stilts to keep out of the mud. He brings Sir Hokus to Queen Marcia's hut, later listens to his call for help, and bends apart the barred window with his claws.

records.l: Queen Marcia, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Queen Marcia sits in the Royal Hut eating marshmallows when Sir Hokus is brought before her. She declares that she has sworn to marry the first stranger who enters her Kingdom, orders him to be treated as King, and has him conducted to an apartment after ordering that he be served royal duck.

records.l: Stick-in-the-Muds, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: The Marshlanders have bodies no larger than Sir Hokus's but use long, stick-like stilts to cross the marsh. They live in tiny mud-thatched houses built high in the trees, with each dwelling level with the occupants' feet.

records.l: Marshland, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Marshland is a muddy region inhabited by Stick-in-the-Muds and frog goblins. It contains higher, dryer patches of ground, tree-top dwellings, and Queen Marcia's Royal Hut.

records.l: the Royal Hut of Queen Marcia, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: The Royal Hut of Queen Marcia stands on a higher, dryer clearing in the center of Marshland and is larger and more pretentious than the other Marshlanders' dwellings. Sir Hokus is dragged inside it by the Mud Guards and later locked in a small room at the back.

records.l: Mud Guards, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Six Mud Guards stand before Queen Marcia's hut when Sir Hokus arrives, then seize him and drag him inside while proclaiming him King. Ten Mud Guards later replace them and threaten Sir Hokus with their stilts when he considers escaping.

records.l: stilts, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: The Marshlanders use stilts to keep out of the mud and to travel across Marshland. They leave them standing against their houses when they go inside, and the Mud Guards brandish them threateningly.

records.l: Sir Hokus's quest, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Sir Hokus says that a knight must avoid comfort, seek danger, and undertake curious quests in search of adventure. He explains that his quest requires him to fight, though he later says that fighting with ladies is not seemly for a knight.

records.l: the proposed marriage of Queen Marcia and Sir Hokus, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER THREE
records.s: Queen Marcia proposes to marry Sir Hokus because he is the first stranger to enter her Kingdom. Sir Hokus objects and tries to leave, while Mira also claims him; he plans to escape rather than accept the marriage.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Sir Hokus is held in the Queen of the Marshes' hut while preparations for his unwanted wedding to Marcia proceed. When Marcia attacks him with her bouquet, three calls from the window signal Ploppa, allowing Sir Hokus to escape through the window onto the turtle's shell. Ploppa has knocked down the nearby stilts, preventing the Stick-in-the-Muds from pursuing them. Sir Hokus leaves the Marshes to seek adventure, while Ploppa returns sadly to the mud.

records.l: Yellow Knight, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Sir Hokus anxiously awaits Ploppa while imprisoned in the hut and rejects Marcia as his bride. He escapes through the window onto Ploppa's shell, then continues onward because he is determined to save a maiden, serve a monarch, destroy a monster, and seek adventure.

records.l: Ploppa, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Ploppa arrives in time to help Sir Hokus escape and knocks down the stilts for miles around. He asks Sir Hokus to remain in the Marshes, but when Sir Hokus chooses to continue, Ploppa sadly carries him to the edge of a wide yellow plain and returns to the mud.

records.l: Queen Marcia, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Marcia enters with marsh maidens and a bouquet of tiger lilies and cat-tails, intending to have Sir Hokus salute her as Queen. Angered by his rejection, she attacks him with the bouquet, but he escapes through the window.

records.l: Stick-in-the-Muds, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: The Stick-in-the-Muds attend Marcia and shout and scold as Sir Hokus escapes. With their stilts knocked into the mire, they are unable to pursue or stop him.

records.l: Marshland, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: The Marshes contain Queen Marcia's hut, tree-houses, mud, fog, frog goblins, and tree-dwelling Stick-in-the-Muds. Sir Hokus leaves the Marshes and crosses a wide yellow plain toward a strange castle.

records.l: wedding, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Preparations for Sir Hokus's wedding to Marcia proceed while he is held in the hut. Sir Hokus expects no cake, castle, music, or dance and wants no part in the wedding.

records.l: escape, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Sir Hokus's escape begins when three calls sound at the window. He dives through it onto Ploppa, who carries him through the swamp after disabling the nearby stilts.

records.l: stilts, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Ploppa knocks down the stilts for miles around and tramps them into the mire. This leaves Marcia, her court, and the Stick-in-the-Muds unable to pursue Sir Hokus.

records.l: mud, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Mud fills the swamp and is essential to Ploppa, who says he cannot live without plenty of thick, wet mud. Ploppa settles back into the mud after carrying Sir Hokus to the edge of the next country.

records.l: Sir Hokus's adventure, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FOUR
records.s: Sir Hokus says that he must have adventure, along with the glitter and glory of strange, glamorous places. His desire for adventure leads him to leave Ploppa and cross the plain toward a strange, tall castle.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Sultan of Samandra is desperate to recover his lost favorite camel, which the Seer Chinda reveals is in the Emerald City at the Royal Stable of Queen Ozma of Oz. The Sultan sends his Grand Vizier, Tuzzle, with the Royal Sampan and twenty slaves down the Winkie River to retrieve the camel using a golden halter. The Sultan secretly wants the package hidden in the camel's left hand saddle sack rather than the camel itself. Tuzzle's party reaches the outskirts of the Emerald City on the second evening.

records.l: Sultan of Samandra, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Sultan anxiously learns from Chinda that his lost camel is in the Emerald City and orders Tuzzle to bring it back. He reveals to Confido that his true concern is the package in the camel's left hand saddle sack, whose recovery he believes is essential to him.

records.l: Tuzzle, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: Tuzzle serves as Grand Vizier and carries out the Sultan's orders to prepare the Royal Sampan and travel to Oz. He demands elaborate clothing and servants, then departs with twenty slaves and reaches the outskirts of the Emerald City on the second evening.

records.l: Chinda, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: Chinda, the Seer and Prophet of Samandra, explains that he has searched for the camel for ten years. Using a new lens in his magic telescope, he sees the camel in the Emerald City and is promoted by the Sultan to Magician Extraordinary and Grand Bozzywoz of the Realm.

records.l: the Comfortable Camel, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The camel was the Sultan's favorite and is described as an exceptionally valuable and beautiful beast. It was lost in a sand storm, and Chinda reports that it is now in the Royal Stable of Queen Ozma of Oz in the Emerald City.

records.l: Samandra, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: Samandra is a very old kingdom in the northern part of the Winkie Country, bordered by the Deadly Desert and the Winkie River. It contains golden deserts, fertile valleys, orange groves, date palms, and fig trees, and has been ruled by the Sultan for five hundred years.

records.l: Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: Oz is the wonderful kingdom in which Samandra lies. The Royal Sampan travels toward Oz's capital, the Emerald City, to recover the camel.

records.l: Emerald City, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Emerald City is the capital of Oz and the destination of Tuzzle's recovery party. Chinda sees the lost camel there through his magic telescope, and Tuzzle's party arrives at the city's outskirts on the second evening.

records.l: Ozma, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: Queen Ozma of Oz is identified as the ruler whose Royal Stable in the Emerald City contains the lost camel. Tuzzle also carries embroidered shawls intended as gifts for her.

records.l: Royal Stable of Queen Ozma of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Royal Stable of Queen Ozma of Oz in the Emerald City is where Chinda sees the lost camel through his magic telescope.

records.l: Winkie River, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Winkie River borders Samandra on the south and winds through the Great Empire of the East to the outskirts of the Emerald City. Tuzzle and the slaves travel down it in the Royal Sampan.

records.l: Royal Sampan, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Royal Sampan is loaded with supplies, gifts, servants, a golden halter, and equipment for the journey. It sails at dawn down the Winkie River and carries Tuzzle and his twenty slaves to the outskirts of the Emerald City.

records.l: the package in the camel's left hand saddle sack, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The package in the camel's left hand saddle sack is the Sultan's real reason for wanting the camel recovered. He says that without it he is lost, ruined, and done for, and plans to hide it again once it is returned.

records.l: the great sand storm, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: A sudden sand storm caused the camel to disappear. Chinda states that the storm was not his doing because he is a Seer rather than a weather prophet.

records.l: the camel-recovery mission, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER FIVE
records.s: The Sultan assigns the camel-recovery mission to Tuzzle, who must sail to the Emerald City, use a golden halter, and ensure that the camel still wears its original harness and saddle sacks. The mission reaches the Emerald City's outskirts after traveling for two evenings.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Tuzzle brings greetings from the Sultan of Samandra to Ozma and asks for the return of the Comfortable Camel, which he claims was lost from the Sultan's herd ten years earlier. Ozma and her companions discover that the camel and Sir Hokus are missing from the Royal Stables and the palace, so Tuzzle returns to Samandra without receiving the camel. The magic picture, which could have located them, is also missing. The Wizard offers to find them with a new searchlight if they do not soon return.

records.l: Tuzzle, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Tuzzle arrives in the Emerald City as the Grand Vizier of Samandra, leading a procession of slaves bearing orange branches and embroidered shawls. He asks Ozma to return the Comfortable Camel to the Sultan of Samandra, but leaves when the camel cannot be found, giving Ozma the shawls as a gift.

records.l: Dorothy, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Dorothy recognizes Tuzzle and explains that the camel must be the Comfortable Camel Sir Hokus brought to the Emerald City. She joins Ozma and the others in searching for the camel and later helps inspect the missing magic picture.

records.l: Bettsy Bobbin, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Bettsy Bobbin watches Tuzzle's procession with Dorothy and helps announce the visitors to Ozma. She suggests using the magic picture to find the Sultan, Sir Hokus, and the Comfortable Camel.

records.l: Ozma, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Ozma receives Tuzzle courteously and agrees that the Comfortable Camel may return to the Sultan if it belongs to him and wishes to go. After discovering that the camel and Sir Hokus are missing, she uses the magic picture, only to find that it too has disappeared.

records.l: Sultan of Samandra, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Sultan sends Tuzzle to Ozma with greetings and twenty embroidered shawls, asking for the return of a camel lost from his royal herd ten years earlier. The camel is described as his favorite mount and as a source of great comfort to him.

records.l: Samandra, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Samandra is ruled by the Sultan and sends a grand delegation to the Emerald City. The Wizard later learns some information about Samandra, its ruler, and its customs from the encyclopedia of Oz.

records.l: Emerald City, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Emerald City amazes Tuzzle because its beauty and magnificence surpass every place he has seen. Tuzzle's procession travels through its jewelled streets to Ozma's castle.

records.l: Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Oz is the land whose encyclopedia contains information about Samandra. The Wizard proposes using a new searchlight to locate missing people and objects anywhere in Oz.

records.l: the Comfortable Camel, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Comfortable Camel was brought to the Emerald City by Sir Hokus and is believed to be the camel lost from the Sultan of Samandra's royal herd. It is missing from the Royal Stables, and neither the stable staff nor the Doubtful Dromedary knows where it has gone.

records.l: Sir Hokus of Pokes, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Sir Hokus of Pokes is missing along with the Comfortable Camel. The Wizard and Ozma learn that he had started upon his quest, but they cannot determine his whereabouts.

records.l: the little Wizard of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Wizard cannot explain the disappearance of the Comfortable Camel, Sir Hokus, or the magic picture. He says he is nearly finished with a powerful searchlight that can locate missing people and objects throughout Oz.

records.l: the Royal Stables, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Royal Stables are searched for the Comfortable Camel, but the camel's stall is empty. Grooms and stable boys are sent in every direction without finding any trace of it.

records.l: the magic picture, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The magic picture normally shows the exact location of a person when Ozma asks about them. When Ozma asks it to show the Comfortable Camel, it is found to be missing from its place on the wall.

records.l: the Wizard's searchlight, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The Wizard's searchlight is a new invention that he is almost finished perfecting. Fired like a shell from a cannon, it is intended to travel throughout Oz, find whatever it is sent for, and return with its exact location.

records.l: Sir Hokus's quest, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: Sir Hokus's quest has already begun when the others discover that he and the Comfortable Camel are missing. The palace inhabitants had been preparing to accompany him and therefore had not noticed his departure.

records.l: the camel's disappearance, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SIX
records.s: The camel's disappearance is discovered when the Royal Stables are searched at Tuzzle's request. No one at the palace knows where the Comfortable Camel has gone, and the missing magic picture provides no help in locating it.

records.l: The Yellow Knight of Oz, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: Speedy and his Uncle Billy attempt to travel to Mars in the Skyrocket, but the craft launches before Uncle Billy can board. Speedy turns the Skyrocket back toward Earth, causing it to crash through the ground and travel deep into the Underworld. The craft stops in Subterranea, where the Shah orders Speedy to repair the hole he made in the underground sky or face being thrown to the fire fish in Lava Lake. Zunda tells Speedy about the Underworld's nine levels and warns him that his execution is scheduled for the next morning.

records.l: Speedy, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: Speedy is a ten-year-old orphan named Bill who lives with Uncle Billy and is known for his quickness in sports. He accidentally launches the Skyrocket without Uncle Billy, steers it back toward Earth, and crashes into the Underworld. In Subterranea, he explains what happened but is ordered to mend the hole in the sky or be thrown to the fire fish in Lava Lake.

records.l: Uncle Billy, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: Uncle Billy is a great scientist who invents the Skyrocket and intends to travel with Speedy to Mars. He fails to get into the craft before it launches and is left behind on Earth.

records.l: Skyrocket, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: The Skyrocket is a flying torpedo designed to carry Uncle Billy and Speedy through the sky to Mars. It launches before Uncle Billy boards, is turned downward by Speedy, crashes through the earth, and eventually stops in the public square of Subterranea.

records.l: Subterranea, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: Subterranea is an underground kingdom at one of the lowest levels of the Underworld. Its city has a public square, blue stone ceilings, radium stars, and tiled passageways decorated with precious stones.

records.l: Shah of Subterranea, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
records.s: The Shah is the ruler of Subterranea and travels on a giant blue earthworm with attendants. After seeing the hole made by the Skyrocket, he doubts Speedy's explanation and orders that the sky be repaired or that Speedy face consequences.

records.l: Rhomba, the Rhymer, The Yellow Knight of Oz, CHAPTER SEVEN
